# A Psalm
Of David. Lord, who shall dwell in Your tent? Who shall dwell on Your holy mountain? He who walks uprightly and works righteousness, and speaks the truth in his heart. He does not slander with his tongue, nor does he do evil to his neighbor, nor does he take up a reproach against his relative. In whose eyes a vile person is despised, but he honors those who fear the Lord; he who swears to his own hurt and does not change. He does not put out his money at interest, nor does he take a bribe against the innocent. He who does these things shall never be moved.

# For the Leader

"The fool has said in his heart"—this refers to Sennacherib <note>The Assyrian King who besieged Jerusalem in the time of King Hezekiah</note>... regarding the language of mocking. The phrase "For the Leader, a Psalm" refers to the heart's intent to destroy Israel and the Holy Temple... The word "corrupted" implies that their actions were an abomination. "There is none who does good"—this refers to those who lived without a good nature, all of them dreamed of their own deeds, acting only for their own bellies. For they thought there was no Judge and no Justice... The Lord looked down from heaven to see the vision of every soul... even if they were to repent. And so too in the future. "There they were in fear"—they will return and say that in the place of their greatness, they shall fear again and know that God is in the generation of the righteous, helping them. "You would put to shame the counsel of the poor"—you mock them because the Lord is their refuge; you think their counsel is worthless because they are oppressed, asking "where is their God that He may comfort them?" "O that out of Zion"—since it is written that God dwells in Israel, the salvation must come from Zion. It says "Who will give," meaning "Who will provide the salvation?" "When the Lord returns the captivity of His people," then Jacob will rejoice. Currently, they are in grief and mourning in exile, but when the captives return from their suffering, they will find joy.

# A Psalm

"Lord, who shall dwell"—the beginning of the book of the upright. This psalm describes the qualities of those who are pure. "Your holy mountain" refers to the chosen place, which is the Holy Temple, for it is the most honored place on earth. "Who shall dwell"—this refers to the upper soul, the actions of the intellect, and those who merit life in the world to come in the presence of the Throne of Glory. "He who walks uprightly"—the word "upright" (Tamim) is an adjective. It means one who walks in a perfect way, not following the impulses of the heart but walking in simplicity... "Works righteousness"—in all his deeds, he acts with justice. "Speaks the truth in his heart"—this refers to the three levels of human expression: action, speech, and thought. He does not say one thing with his mouth and another in his heart; his speech is a direct result of the thoughts in his heart. Even if he only thought of doing something good, he fulfills it as if he had spoken it. Our Sages also noted that this refers to being truthful even in one's private thoughts, such as in business dealings. "He does not slander with his tongue"—this verse lists the prohibitions of speech and action. One might think it unnecessary to mention this after saying he "speaks truth," but the text emphasizes that even if his thoughts are truthful, he must not use his tongue to peddle gossip <note>original: "rekhilut"</note>, which kindles anger and evil. "Nor does he do evil to his neighbor"—"neighbor" here includes relatives. The Torah forbids harming any person, but emphasizes the neighbor or relative because those are the people one is most frequently in contact with. "In whose eyes a vile person is despised"—this is another good quality. Even though he himself is upright and righteous, he remains humble in his own eyes and considers himself small, thinking that he has not yet done enough to honor his Creator. But he honors others who fear the Lord, considering them greater than himself. "He who swears to his own hurt and does not change"—this means even if a vow causes him physical or financial loss, he fulfills it. He binds his physical desires with an oath so that his "evil inclination" does not lead him astray. "He does not put out his money at interest"—he does not take advantage of his neighbor's need. Even if a person pays interest willingly, it is forbidden because the borrower only does so out of necessity. Therefore, the Torah is very strict regarding interest, grouping it with the most severe sins. Our Sages explained that David is describing the ideal person who follows the spirit of the law, even in dealings with those where interest might technically be permitted by letter of the law, but he refrains out of piety. "Nor does he take a bribe against the innocent"—this refers to a judge or a witness who refuses any compensation that might tilt the scales of justice, even if he intended to rule correctly regardless.

->He who does these things shall never be moved: Even if he slips occasionally, he will not fall forever, for he will be restored time and again to his place of honor.<-

->Of David: We have already written regarding this in the previous psalms. Michtam: Our sages explained in the Gemara <note>The Talmud</note> that it refers to one who is humble and perfect <note>a wordplay on 'mach' (humble) and 'tam' (perfect)</note>.<-

# Michtam
<margin>According to my palate</margin>
His voice goes out and becomes publicized: "So I have hoped and not in Your profane things." "You have said to the Lord, You are my Master": To serve Him and remember Him, and so it is right for you to pray to Him as well. "My goodness is not upon You": This is explained as a debt—"Pay me what is owed." It is not incumbent upon You to pay me, for the debt is already paid; rather, everything is a kindness from Your hand. That is to say, my merit is not upon You, for it is not possible that I could give anything to You. "To the holy ones who are in the earth": This refers to the righteous. Through them, all my delight is found. I prefer to join with the holy ones and noble ones rather than with the wicked who hasten after other gods. My goodness and my portion are found among the scholars. And it is my opinion that the phrase "to the holy ones" connects back to the beginning: I said to the Lord, "You are my goodness, but it is also for the holy ones who are on the earth." This means my merit is counted for them. David says this to the pious, his companions, the wise men. "Hasten" <note>Hebrew: 'maharu'</note>: This refers to those who move quickly toward vanity. It may also be related to a marriage dowry, as if they have wed themselves to another god. "I will not pour out their libations of blood": I will not join in the rituals of those who offer blood. I will not even mention the names of their idols. "The Lord is the portion of my inheritance": I have no desire for worldly pleasures; rather, the Lord is my portion. "You maintain my lot": You support me and help me to choose the good. "The lines have fallen to me": My lot in life has been pleasant. "I will bless the Lord who has advised me": For giving me this good portion. "Even in the nights my kidneys instruct me": In the quiet of the night, when one is free from the business of the world, the heart and mind reflect on the ways of God. "I have set the Lord always before me": In all my ways, I keep His path before my eyes. "Because He is at my right hand": He supports my right hand so that I do not slip. "Therefore my heart is glad": Because I stand in His ways. "My glory rejoices": Referring to the soul, which is the glory of the body. Even after death, the soul clings to its Creator and the flesh dwells in safety, for the soul's merit protects the body from the worm. "For You will not abandon my soul to the grave": You will show me the path to eternal life. "In Your presence is fullness of joy": This refers to the delight of the soul in the afterlife, which is permanent and has no end.

<note>Beginning of the commentary on Psalm 17</note>
This is a prayer, and it is said with a humble spirit. For one who prays sometimes cries out in a loud voice and sometimes in a whisper. "From Your presence let my judgment come": I seek judgment from You because I know my heart is pure. "Let Your eyes behold uprightness": See the integrity of my actions. "You have tested my heart": You have examined me in the night and found no deceit. My mouth does not deviate from my heart. I have guarded myself from the paths of the violent...

-> Psalm 18 <-

To the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David the servant of the Lord, who spoke to the Lord the words of this song on the day that the Lord delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul. And he said: I will love You, O Lord, my strength. The Lord is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust; my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower.

---

<margin>Our steps</margin>
<margin>They surrounded me</margin>
<margin>Your hidden treasure</margin>

**Regarding the deeds of man.** Understand this according to what is hidden and revealed. Regarding the deeds of man and turning away from transgressions, this is the meaning of "I have kept the paths of the lawless." The term *paritz* <note>meaning 'lawless' or 'violent'</note> refers to a wicked person. It is like one who guards the path to the Tree of Life to prevent man from reaching it, just like a guard of an orchard. After guarding what is before him... <unclear>illegible</unclear> my steps shall not falter before my sword. **Support my steps.** In a place like this, it is like an exchange... **In Your paths.** That is to say, let Your paths cover my shortcomings. **I have called upon You.** Because I have kept [the way] and because I trusted in You, I trusted that You would answer me. This is the meaning of **Distinguish Your kindness.** The word *Hafleh* (distinguish) means to separate, as in "And the Lord shall sever (distinguish) on that day." It means to set apart Your kindness for those who take refuge from those who rise up against Your right hand, for all know that the "right hand" is for those who hold fast. **Keep me as the apple of the eye.** Just as the heart protects the eyes. In the shadow of Your wings... <note>The commentator explains that the addition of the letter 'Yod' in certain words serves as a diminutive, expressing the tenderness of God's protection of the "little one."</note> This is a grave matter, for the "daughter of the eye" (the pupil) is the most delicate part. **My deadly enemies surround me.** They surround me like a nest, intending to take my soul. **In their fat.** Their luxury has closed their mouths, therefore they spoke with pride. **They have now surrounded our steps.** They set their eyes on our path to spread nets on the ground to trap us. **His likeness is like a lion.** This refers specifically to Saul <note>David's primary antagonist</note>. Just as a lion is eager to tear, so my enemy's face is set against me. **Arise, O Lord.** In Your arising to trample them and overturn them. **From the wicked by Your sword.** Save me from the wicked who are Your sword <note>meaning God sometimes uses the wicked as a tool of punishment</note>. **From men by Your hand, O Lord.** Deliver my soul from those whose death is a "death of the world" (*hald*), whose existence is transient. **Their portion is in this life.** Their reward is only in this world, whereas the righteous look to the World to Come <term>Olam HaBa</term>. You fill their bellies in this world, and they are satisfied with children, but David says: **I, in righteousness, shall behold Your face.** The wicked have their "satisfaction" in this world, but I look forward to beholding Your face in the World to Come. **I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with Your likeness.** This refers to the resurrection of the dead. When I awaken from death, I will be satisfied with the vision of God, as it is said, "He beholds the likeness of the Lord" <note>Numbers 12:8</note>. This is the ultimate hope and faith.

# To the Chief Musician

**To the Chief Musician. A servant of the Lord, to David.** One who places all his strength and intent in the Blessed One is called a "servant of the Lord." In everything David did and everywhere he turned, his intent and trust were in the Blessed One. This song is particularly appropriate for the end of the days of the Messiah. **I will love You.** This expression of love refers to the soul's desire to draw close to the Creator. Some explain "my strength" (*hizki*) as: You were my strength when I was strong. **The Lord is my rock.** Like snow and a fortress that provides high refuge. The Lord is my rock and my fortress in which I lie down; it is as written, "The name of the Lord is a strong tower; the righteous run into it and are safe." **And my deliverer.** For a fortress and high tower save a man, and I have found refuge in Your name at all times. **My God, my strength.** The theme is repeated in different words to emphasize that God is a strong refuge. **In whom I will trust.** Therefore, I will run to Him and take refuge in Him.

...and the strength of my salvation against my enemies, He in whom I trusted. David said in praise: I pray before the Lord, and from my enemies I am saved. And the earth shook and trembled, and the foundations of the mountains moved and were shaken because His anger was strong against it. <sig>Samuel</sig>

**The shield and the horn of my salvation.** It is the way of the Scripture to double the terms of reinforcement in them. Like "my horn," etc. I have strength in all the sections. Because he began the row and wrote "strengthened" in the sections before his rest... And Jonathan <note>referring to Targum Jonathan, the Aramaic translation</note> translates "my high tower" as "the one who trusts in me." **My high tower**—for He is a rock to me, like a tower or silver one thinks of. And in the Midrash, because it is all for the end... his foundation... those who surround him in his holiness. And his strength... Shimei ben Gera... and the curse... and David... the son of Jehoiada... the choice of my men... my shield. **The horn of my salvation, my high tower**—I will call out to the Lord who is strong in His power. My high tower means he said to me, **I will call upon the Lord who is worthy to be praised**, the Holy One who is glorified in His praises. And he says:
**The cords of death surrounded me.** "Surrounded me" means they went around me. "Cords of death" are like the labor pains of a woman giving birth. As it says, "the pains of a woman in travail." And the waters... and "the cords of death surrounded me." In the chapter "Hezekiah was strengthened"... and he said this regarding the groups of enemies who were in them, close to death, as in the chapter of the war. And when the sword was strengthened against me. **And the floods of ungodliness <note>Belial</note> made me afraid.** These are like the broken harvests. And in Daniel it says regarding every one... or let "Belial" be the name of the wicked. And Jonathan translates in the Book of Samuel "groups of the wicked and a company of the guilty." And to explain "floods," because a flood comes from a stream... vessels of destruction... and in the Book of Samuel "torrents of the wicked." Like a surrounding of the Presence. **The snares of death confronted me.** They opened before me. And in the Midrash it speaks of four kings. "The cords of death surrounded me"—they went around and wrote against me... the cords of death preceded me. **He heard my voice from His temple**—from the palace of the King, from the Temple, the house of my prayer, and this Presence, the house of my vision. **In my distress I call.** When distress comes upon me. And this is the crown... who is the one who helps me and makes me known. **And the earth shook and trembled.** He heard my voice... my voice came to Him. **And my cry came before Him, even into His ears.** My prayer which is before Him, before the Throne of Glory, enters into His ears... and there was a holy war and it stood. And they explain from this verse until "He sent from above and took me"—some interpret this regarding the miracles that the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for Israel. **And there went up a smoke in His nostrils.** And so is the opinion of the translator. And the Midrash on "the earth shook and trembled" is about the earthquake at the Red Sea, and likewise "smoke went up in His nostrils." And the translation says "smoke went up in His nostrils" regarding the matter of Pharaoh. **He bowed the heavens and came down** at the giving of the Torah <note>the Sinai revelation</note>, and such is the opinion of the homiletic interpretation. And so the verses after it... in the days of Joshua. And these are to save me. A hint to the drowning at the Red Sea, "and He came down." And what He did at the Red Sea, He will do to him as in the miracles of Isaac... and the correct way according to the plain meaning of the verse is that all these wonders... riding on a cherub... and fire, etc., are to give a sign to the enemies. For the Holy One is a sign of anger to the earth and its people... fire and storm and lightning. **And there went down from Him.** And this is as said in the Scripture "He came down" in many places... cloud and thick darkness... and the brightness of the sun and stars. And he sent a storm of anger from the height and came down to cover them in the sea. And these... were ready and His hand was upon the wings of the wind. That is, the speed of the quickness, and so we found in another place in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory... between those that were according to the Book of Kings. And thus he says, "the earth shook and trembled" because of the wrath upon all the inhabitants... "smoke in His nostrils"... from the heat of His anger... fire will not be extinguished... **And fire out of His mouth devoured.** Fire that consumes the faces, a metaphor for vengeance. And others found in it... **coals were kindled by it.** As we explained. **And darkness under His feet.** He placed thick darkness and cloud under His feet... **And He rode upon a cherub.** As we explained. He saw the vision from the Holy One and He spoke... as one who rides... and in Samuel, "He was seen"... that is, He was visible and the matter is one. **He made darkness His secret place.** A hint to the clouds as we explained... or it means that He is hidden from those who would seek Him... **Darkness of waters.** And in Samuel, "gathering of waters." Our eyes see the clouds gathering... and it is one matter. For when the clouds gather, there is darkness and the drawing of water from the seas... **thick clouds of the skies.** Therefore to its inhabitants the clouds pass... hail and coals of fire. That is, the thickness of the clouds is ordered against the enemies, hail and coals of fire in the manner of "fire flashing in the midst of the hail." **And the Lord thundered in the heavens.** He made thunder in the waters against the enemies and gave His voice against them. And in Samuel "the Lord thundered and the Most High gave His voice"... they were terrified by it as from a storm... and he says again "hail and coals of fire." For with the voices from the decreed clouds, those come out which are hail and coals of fire. **And He sent out His arrows and scattered them.** He sent arrows and scattered the enemies, and many lightnings. **And He discomfited them.** He terrified the enemies with the lightnings... and "many" is from "they shot and were many." The meaning is He shot many, and it is a past tense verb... the lightnings are the hidden arrows. **Then the channels of waters were seen.** These are the depths that contain water. As in "to the channels and to the animals." Upon all channels. And these are the hidden foundations that were in them. And they were diminished from there upon the face of the sea... the channels were seen. **And the foundations of the world.** Which were covered in water. And this is by the rebuke of the Lord of the waters, or "from Your rebuke, O Lord." Like "He rebuked the Red Sea and it was dried." And likewise from the "blast of the breath of His nostrils."... fire... and this is by way of a metaphor for the downfall of the enemies in war... and the wonder... as another matter... who will be saved from the sea. And likewise the salvation of David in every downfall of his enemies in war, like the seven cleansings... and his enemies did not prevail. And all this he said "He sent from above, He took me, He drew me out of many waters." And all this David said and sang to the Lord for those who were in His mouth and His ways. **He delivered me from my enemy.** A singular term for the group, or it refers to many. **They confronted me in the day of my calamity, etc.** Also in the Book of Samuel "they confronted me in the day of my wandering." And it was in the day of my wandering. That is, on the day when I had trouble and everything was dangerous, and the enemies were preceding me in their knowledge... **And He brought me forth also into a large place.** He took me out from the troubles I was in and brought me into a broad place. **The Lord rewarded me according to my righteousness.** For He knew that my righteousness was with me and I was clean with my enemies... He recompensed me according to my righteousness... and He added more. **For I have kept the ways of the Lord.** There is a difference in all this... saying I have kept the ways and he mentions his merit. **And I have not wickedly departed from my God.** I was not like the wicked... or if I was like the wicked... for I kept the ways of the Lord and did not act wickedly... that I was righteous and pure... and not my hand and my merit upon me... as he says, "he did not put forth his hand against the Lord's anointed." For the matter of the king was not... for all His judgments.

# Psalms

<column-break/>

For all His judgments were before me, and I did not remove His statutes from me. I was wholehearted with Him, and I kept myself from my iniquity.
<margin>His eye</margin> Therefore the Lord has recompensed me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands before His eyes. With the merciful You show Yourself merciful; with the wholehearted man You show Yourself wholehearted. With the pure You show Yourself pure; and with the crooked You show Yourself subtle. For You save the humble people, but the haughty eyes You bring down. For You light my lamp; the Lord my God enlightens my darkness. For by You I run through a troop, and by my God I leap over a wall. As for God, His way is perfect; the word of the Lord is tried; He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him. For who is God except the Lord? And who is a rock besides our God? It is God who arms me with strength and makes my way perfect. He makes my feet like hinds' feet and sets me upon my high places. He teaches my hands for war, so that my arms can bend a bow of bronze. You have also given me the shield of Your salvation, and Your right hand has held me up,

For You armed me with strength for the battle; You subdued under me those who rose up against me. You also made my enemies turn their backs to me, and I destroyed those who hated me. They cried out, but there was none to save; even to the Lord, but He did not answer them.

Let the God of my salvation be exalted!

<column-break/>

Because all His judgments are revealed before me, and from His laws and His covenants I do not depart. And I was perfect in His fear, and I was guarded in my soul from sins. And the Lord repaid me according to my merit, like the purity of my hands before His Word <term>Memra; a term used in the Targum to describe God's manifest speech or presence</term>. With the pious, You act piously, and with the man who is perfect in his ways, You act with kindness. With the diligent Isaac, who was perfect in Your fear, You fulfilled Your will with him. With Jacob, who was pure in Your womb, You chose him from among the nations <note>This refers to the Midrashic idea that Jacob was chosen even before birth</note> and separated his seed from all blemish; but with Pharaoh and the wicked Egyptians who thought evil thoughts against Your people, You confounded them in their own thoughts. Because You are the one who will redeem the people of the House of Israel, who are lowly among the nations in exile; and by Your eyes, the powerful nations who enslave them shall be humbled. Because You will light the lamp of Israel which was extinguished in exile, for You are the Master of Judah; O Lord my God, enlighten my darkness, and lead me from the darkness into the light, and let me see Your comforts. Because by Your help I run against a troop, and by the Word of my God I shall pass over walls, and by the Word of my God I shall conquer strong fortresses. God, whose ways are established, the Torah of the Lord is choice; He is a shield to all who trust in His Word. For who is God who is able to act, or who is the master of all powers? All the nations and languages shall say, "There is no God but the Lord," for there is none besides You; and there is no strength or ruler who is strong except our God. The God who girds my waist with strength and prepares my way perfectly. Who makes my feet like the hinds, and upon the house of my strength He establishes me. He teaches my hands to perform battle, and He strengthens my arms like a bow of bronze. And You gave me strength and salvation, and Your right hand helps me, and by Your Word You supported me. I open my steps in my place, and my joints do not shake. I will pursue my enemies and overtake them, and I will not return until I have destroyed them. I will strike them and they will not be able to rise, and they shall fall beneath the soles of my feet. And You girded me with strength to perform battle; You shall humble the nations who stand to do me evil beneath me. And my enemies You broke before me, and those who hate me I will destroy. They sought help but there was no savior; they prayed before the Lord but He did not receive their prayer. And I ground them like the dust that the wind blows, and like the mud of the streets I will crush them. You shall deliver me from the divisions of the people; You shall set me as the head of the nations; a people I did not know shall serve me. At the hearing of the ear they shall obey me; the sons of foreign nations shall lie to me. The sons of foreign nations shall perish and be uprooted from their palaces. He lives,

->the Lord, and blessed is my Strength, and exalted is the God who redeemed me! The God who performs vengeance for me and subdues the nations that stand against me. Who delivers me from my enemies; and even from those who stand against me to do me evil, You shall strengthen me; from the man of violence and wickedness, You shall deliver me. ---

*For all His judgments:* They were always before me; I did not forget His statutes. *I did not remove from me:* Always. I forced my heart to follow the strength of the Lord and not from the mire of sin, as it is said. *I was wholehearted with Him:* With God I was sincere, and I did not second-guess His attributes, nor did I deny His powers. My life was like a burden upon me because the king and the hater <note>Likely referring to Saul</note> stood over me every day to kill me. And so, "You shall be wholehearted with the Lord your God" (Deuteronomy 18:13). *And I kept myself from my iniquity:* From the guilt concerning the priests <note>Refers to the tragedy at the city of Nob, where David felt responsible for the priests' deaths</note>. *The Lord recompensed me according to my righteousness:* Because I showed revulsion to anything that violated His honor, and He pardoned my deeds. *With the merciful You show Yourself merciful:* Since it is the way of the world that with a merciful person, You wash him in Your mercy and surround him even more than he requested. *With the wholehearted man:* With the "wholehearted waters," You complete Your kindness and more. *With the pure:* Just as a hand is held against its opposite, so it shall be. *With the crooked You show Yourself subtle:* You bring upon him twisting paths according to his own way. *Regarding haughty eyes:* You always bring down the brazen and the arrogant, and humble those higher than them, like Cain regarding honor. This is the meaning of "haughty eyes You bring down," for they are a stumbling block for the eyes, being the cause of pride and sins. As it is written, "lest you follow your own heart and your own eyes" (Numbers 15:39). *For You light my lamp:* When there was darkness and wrapping from all the previous generation. He lights my lamp in my darkness. *For by You I run through a troop:* With Your help I seized the troop of my debtors. The language of "perfect/wholehearted" is said regarding those in a covenant. *He teaches my hands for war:* I did not tremble in my might, but rather He teaches my hands for war. *A bow of bronze is bent by my arms:* He taught my hands so much that they could bend a bow of bronze until it broke in my arms. The Midrash <note>Midrash Tehillim</note> says that David would take a bronze bow and bend it. Another explanation: it was easier for him to pull a bronze bow than to bend his own arms. *You have given me the shield of Your salvation:* In every battle, the Holy One, Blessed be He, was a shield for me. *And Your gentleness:* This was because of Your humility; I did not rely on my own strength. You did this because I was not worthy, but out of Your kindness, You made me great. I was small in strength but had great help. *You have enlarged my steps:* Your steps did not falter or fail. *And my ankles have not slipped:* I was spared despite my debt. "Ankles" refers to the knee joints and tendons. *I pursued my enemies and overtook them:* Like a standing place for warriors, I did not allow them any standing, for I struck them all until they were like dust outside. *They cried out, but there was none to save:* They prayed, but not to the Lord, and He did not wait for them. *I beat them small as the dust before the wind:* This refers to the completeness of his pursuit. *I emptied them out like the dirt:* I emptied them of their strength. *Deliver me from the strivings of the people:* In the Book of Samuel it says "strivings of *my* people." You delivered me from the wars of civil strife and those who gathered against me from my own people, and also from the wise men. *You have made me the head of the nations:* From the strivings of nations and destruction, to be the head and the seal of the world's wrath. *A people I have not known shall serve me:* For on the day I did not know them, they came to serve David. *As soon as they hear, they obey me:* From his writings and the pleasantness of David's rebukes. *Foreigners shall submit:* They shall be humbled before me; all the nations shall be ashamed in the battle. "Submit" means their hearts failed because of him. *They shall come trembling out of their strongholds:* In the place where they melted in fear because of the sins of the world, they shall fall and hide in holes. *The Lord lives and blessed be my Rock:* Because in the place where He spared me against those who challenged His piety, they shall be stirred up by the fear of death.

## The Lord lives, and blessed be my rock; and let the God of my salvation be exalted: The God who gives vengeance to me, and subdues nations under me: He delivers me from my enemies; indeed, You lift me up above those who rise against me; You deliver me from the violent man: Therefore I will give thanks to You among the nations, O Lord, and I will sing praises to Your name: He gives great salvation to His king, and shows mercy to His anointed, to David and to his seed forever.

> The Lord is existing, and blessed is the Strong One <note>original: "takkifa," referring to God as a mighty Rock</note> from whose presence comes my strength and redemption; and exalted is the God of my redemption: The God who executes vengeance for me, and humbles the nations who stand to do me evil under me: He rescues me from my enemies; more than those who rise against me, You shall make me strong; from the group of violent and predatory people, You shall rescue me: Therefore I will thank You before the nations, O Lord, and to Your name I will offer praise: He multiplies the performance of redemption with His king, and performs kindness to His anointed, to David and to his seed forever.

---

**The Lord lives, and blessed be my rock:** This means: why do I have all this good and honor? Because the Lord lives, and He is my power and my strength; He is the one who helps, honors, and subdues my enemies. **The God who gives vengeance to me:** The Power that grants me vengeance. Because the enemies are many, and each one seeks vengeance from his own place, the text uses the plural form, **vengeances** <note>original: "nekamot"</note>. And he summarizes by saying: **And subdues nations under me:** The word for "subdues" <note>original: "vaydaber"</note> is like "leading" or "speaking over them." It has another meaning related to guidance or leadership. This is because God weakened the power and might of the kings of the earth so that the honor would belong to David. **He delivers me from my enemies; indeed, You lift me up above those who rise against me:** He relies here on the absolute Power that will triumph over all the nations that fight him. **From the violent man You deliver me:** A man who is characterized by robbery and violence. Through the honor of God they shall be exalted; this is to testify to the guidance of Your people, and for this reason he said: "I will love You, Your kindness." He relies on the specific individual case but concludes in the plural, as is the way of the Scriptures: **He gives great salvation to His king, and shows mercy to His anointed, to David and to his seed forever.**

<column-break/>

## For the leader, a psalm of David. 19 The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament tells of His handiwork: Day to day utters speech, and night to night reveals knowledge: There is no speech, and there are no words, where their voice is not heard: Their line has gone out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world; in them He has set a tent for the sun: Which is like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, and rejoices like a strong man to run a course: Its rising is from the end of the heaven, and its circuit to the ends of it; and there is nothing hidden from its heat: The law of the Lord is perfect, restoring the soul; the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.

> For praise; a song of David. Those who gaze at the heavens tell of the glory of the Lord, and the works of His hands are shown by those who proclaim in the air <note>original: "be-avira," referring to the atmosphere or firmament</note>: Day to day adds and utters a word, and night to night increases and shows knowledge: There is no speech of vanity, and there are no words of folly, whose voice is not heard: Their expanse <note>original: "matichutehon"</note> extends through all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world; for the sun He placed a dwelling, bestowing its radiance upon them: and it, in the morning as it goes out, is like a bridegroom coming out of his canopy, and in joy it is as ready as a giant to run on the path: From the ends of the heavens is its exit, and its strength is upon their ends; and there is no one who is hidden from its heat: The Law of the Lord is perfect, returning the soul; the testimony of the Lord is faithful, making the foolish wise.

---

# The Heavens
**Declare the glory of God, etc.:** This psalm is joined to the previous one. From the stars, their vast number, their precious arrangement, and the order within them, the glory of the Blessed God is visible. It is easy to understand that God is Blessed, for the heavens "speak" to human beings, saying to them: "Arise, see, and recognize your Creator!" For through them, you can intellectually grasp the power of His wisdom and His might. All the celestial bodies, the spheres of the zodiac, and all the wonders—all of them point to His glory. This is the meaning of **The heavens declare**. For through observing them, people will think and "count" <note>a play on the Hebrew word "mesaprim" which means both "telling" and "counting"</note> in their hearts and praise the Creator of heaven and earth. They teach and form the words of His glory, acting as a vessel that holds blessing for one who knows his Creator. The testimony the heavens tell is strong, without end or limit. The heavens "declare" because the celestial sphere and the wondrous bodies are the means through which His glory is beautified. The entire matter of the stars, the constellations, and the spheres—it all reflects the glory of God and points to His wondrous wisdom, which He prepared in this world for anyone who looks at them and relates them back to their Creator with a wise soul and a pure heart. **And the firmament tells of His handiwork:** This means that the wondrous acts which the Lord performed in the firmament reveal and make known His glory. He says "the firmament" <note>term: "Rakiya" — the visible expanse of the sky</note> to mean the heavens that are visible to every eye. The intention is that the wonders seen in the sky are like the speech of lips or the report of a herald who tells things with his mouth. **Day to day utters speech, etc.:** This explains what was written about the heavens declaring. One day is handed over to the next, and the following day tells the praise of God. This progression continues forever. That is to say, the miraculous order found in day and night points to the wise and fixed order that never changes, which is a great testimony to the wisdom of God. This is **utters speech**, meaning it adds wisdom every day for one who knows and understands the "speech" and the knowledge of the constellations. **And night to night reveals knowledge:** That is, through the knowledge of the nights, appearing through the moon and the stars, the knowledge of the Creator is felt. Any person of understanding will realize that this is a superior order, which is the very definition of wisdom. Every moment, it "reveals knowledge" to those who ask and to those with a wise heart to know His wonders. **He says: There is no speech and there are no words:** For even though they do not have an audible voice like the speech of humans, nevertheless their "great voice" reaches the end of the world, and all who see them understand it. This is why he says **Their line has gone out through all the earth:** Meaning the "line" <note>original: "kavam," referring to a measuring line or rule</note> and the order of celestial movement is seen in all the earth and in all places where humans dwell. They testify to His glory. **In them He has set a tent for the sun:** Meaning that within the heavens, He established a specific place for the great luminary, the sun, which is the great ruler in the firmament. It is the light that illuminates the day, and its light and heat reach every place. **Which is like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber:** Meaning the sun's daily emergence in joy and strength is like a bridegroom coming out of his wedding canopy to meet his wife in whom he rejoices. **Rejoices like a strong man to run a course:** Meaning that with great strength and speed, it completes its heavenly circuit without stopping or delaying, like a champion athlete running toward a goal. **Its rising is from the end of the heaven, and its circuit to the ends of it:** Meaning that the sun's movement encompasses the entire world from one end to the other, and every single hour is renewed by its movement. Therefore, this psalm is placed next to the Torah (the Law). Just as the sun travels through the whole world and its light and heat reach every creature, so too is the Law of God perfect, illuminating the eyes of all. **And there is nothing hidden from its heat:** Meaning nothing under the heavens is concealed from the sun's warmth; it penetrates even the most hidden places. So too, the Torah examines hearts and minds and penetrates to the innermost depths. **The Law of the Lord is perfect:** Why is the subject of the Law placed next to the subject of the heavens? Because one who looks at the heavens and sees the power of wisdom and the Creator's guidance of creation will feel a desire in his heart to know his Creator more. Through this, he will return to the Torah, which is the straight and "perfect" path to teach a person the correct ways of life. It is called "perfect" <note>term: "temimah" — whole or complete</note> because it is complete, bringing a person to the ultimate perfection and making up for the deficiencies of the soul. **The testimony of the Lord is sure:** The Torah is the true testimony of God in the world, and through its fulfillment, a person is assured reward and success in this world and the world to come. **Making wise the simple:** Even one who is not wise or learned, when he occupies himself with the Torah, he becomes wise in the ways of Divine wisdom. This is the meaning of "making wise the simple."

# Psalm 19 (Continued)

The precepts of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart; the commandment of the Lord is clear, enlightening the eyes. The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever; the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether. More to be desired are they than gold, even much fine gold; sweeter also than honey and the drippings of the honeycomb. Moreover, by them is Your servant warned; in keeping them there is great reward. Who can understand his errors? Cleanse me from secret faults. Keep back Your servant also from presumptuous sins <note>original: "zedim," referring to intentional or arrogant transgressions</note>; let them not have dominion over me; then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from great transgression. Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in Your sight, O Lord, my rock and my redeemer.

<column-break/>

The orders of the Lord are straight, making the heart glad; the commandment of the Lord is clarified, enlightening the eyes. The fear of the Lord is pure, established for eternity; the laws of the Lord are faithful, righteous as one. They are more desirable than gold and much refined gold, and sweeter than honey and the sweetness of the honeycomb. Indeed, Your servant was careful with them; in keeping them, how much greatness was made for Israel! Who knows unintentional sins? Purify me from hidden things. Indeed, from the arrogant, rescue Your servant, so they shall not rule over me; then I will be without blemish and I will be pure from great sin. May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart <note>The Aramaic text here uses a term for "thought" or "speech" of the eyes/mind</note> be for favor before You, O Lord, my strength and my redeemer.

### Commentary on the Excellence of the Law

Regarding the "precepts," their reasons are revealed and visible. But the "statutes" are like hidden things, requiring one to return and seek their inner meaning. The comparison is made to them because their reason is not revealed for every statute, yet it says of them that they are "desirable" and "sweet," and they are hidden from most people. 

The Law is called "perfect" <note>original: "temimah"</note> because it is complete; nothing is said in it that would render a person lacking in this world or the world to come. And the phrase "restoring the soul" is used because the wisdom of the Lord makes the simple wise. There is no defect in it, for its glory is revealed to the eyes of all who see it—the wise and those who doubt. It "makes wise the simple" because all the words of judgment are hidden wisdom, and there is no empty thing in it. It is the Law of truth, and all its matters point to the higher wisdom, reflecting the upper world and hinting at the "small world" <note>a common medieval term for the human being as a microcosm</note>. 

The author then discusses "fear of the Lord" which is "pure." This refers to the fear one feels in their soul, which is distinct from the fear of physical punishment. This fear is "pure" because it is without dross or ulterior motive. He says it "stands forever" because physical commandments might have a specific place or time, but the fear of God is eternal. 

Furthermore, the commentary explains that while the sun (mentioned earlier in the Psalm) can sometimes harm or scorch, the Torah only benefits. The "precepts of the Lord are right" because they contain no crookedness or perversion. The wise man rejoices in the intellect, and as it is said, "it shall be health to your navel and marrow to your bones." This is the joy of the soul. Therefore, he says "rejoicing the heart" and not "rejoicing the body," for a man rejoices in the Law with his intellect. 

Regarding "more to be desired than gold": the Law and the commandments are more precious than "much fine gold" <note>original: "paz," a term for refined or high-quality gold</note>. Some explain that gold is for this world, but wisdom is for both this world and the world to come. Gold can be stolen or lost, but wisdom is a possession that stays with the soul. 

Regarding "errors, who can understand?": The speaker asks to be cleansed from "secret faults"—those mistakes made without realization. "Keep back Your servant from presumptuous sins": this is a request for help against the "Evil Inclination" <note>the internal urge toward wrongdoing</note> so that intentional sins do not take root and become "great transgression" <note>original: "pesha rav"</note>. If one is habituated to intentional sins, it leads to rebellion. 

Finally, "let the words of my mouth... be acceptable": May my prayers and the meditations I have not even spoken aloud be pleasing to You, my Rock and my Redeemer—the one who strengthens me and rescues me from both accidental errors and intentional arrogance.

### Psalm 20 (Aramaic Targum)
For praise, a song of David: May the Lord accept your prayer in the day of distress; may the Name of the God of Jacob strengthen you. May He send your help from His sanctuary and support you from Zion. May He remember all your offerings, and may He always accept your burnt sacrifices with favor. # For the Leader
**A Psalm of David:** I have explained "for David" as meaning "concerning David" <note>This identifies the psalm as a prayer offered *on behalf* of the king by the people</note>, similar to "For the leader, for Jeduthun." This psalm was composed to be said on behalf of David when he went out to war, saying: **May the Lord answer you in the day of trouble.** This refers to the time of battle with the enemy. "May He answer you in your prayer" which you pray before Him. **Protect you:** <margin>From the word for height, like a tower; when a person is high up, they do not fear the enemy.</margin> **The Name of the God of Jacob:** He mentions the "God of Jacob" specifically because Jacob was a man who experienced many troubles, from Laban, from Esau, and the fear of the Canaanites. And so we say in the Midrash <note>Ancient rabbinic homiletical teachings</note>: Why Abraham, Isaac, and then Jacob? It is like a woman sitting on the birthstool; we say to her, "May He who answered your mother answer you." Since Jacob said, "The God who answered me in the day of my distress," the Psalmist says: May He who answered Jacob in his distress answer you. Another explanation: The owner of the beam must carry the heavy end; since Jacob took the burden of his children's future, God is called his God specifically. It is also possible that "Jacob" here refers to all of Israel, as they are often called by that name. **May He send your help from the sanctuary:** From the holy place, the Temple in Jerusalem, which is the house of prayer. For from there the Divine Glory dwells, and from there help is sent in war. **And from Zion:** Because the Ark was in Zion. **May He remember all your offerings:** In the ancient style, when the king went to war, they would offer sacrifices and burnt offerings all at once to gain favor. **Accept your burnt-sacrifice:** The word for "accept" here literally means "to turn to ashes," meaning may the fire consume it quickly as a sign of favor. **May He grant you according to your heart:** May He fulfill your hidden thoughts and desires. **And fulfill all your counsel:** In the way of war, as it is said, "with wise counsel you shall make war." David would say this through the singers before the people, and every person would pray this for the king. We do not say this to just any person, for a person might have evil in their heart, but we say it to the righteous king: may He fulfill all your requests. **We will sing for joy at your salvation:** When you return in peace from the war. **And in the name of our God we will raise our banners:** Like a soldier following his flag. **Now I know:** Each individual says: Now I know that the Lord has saved His anointed. When the king is victorious, it is clear God desired him. **With the mighty victories of His right hand:** Because even with a small army, David would strike down tens of thousands of his enemies; this could only happen through the strength of God's right hand. **Some trust in chariots:** The enemies trust in their physical equipment, but we trust in the Name. **They were broken and fell:** They fell *because* they trusted in their chariots. **But we have been strengthened and stood firm:** We stood up because we mentioned the Name of the Lord our God. **O Lord, grant victory:** This is the prayer of the people for the king.

# For the Leader
**A Psalm:** This psalm is also written about David, though some say it refers to the King Messiah. If it is about David, it means it was composed by David. If it is about the King Messiah, then David said it through the Holy Spirit <note>original: "Ruach HaKodesh"</note> regarding his descendant. **O Lord, in Your strength:** The king shall rejoice in the strength You gave him. **The desire of his soul:** You gave him what he wished for in his heart. **For You precede him with choice blessings:** You provide blessings before he even asks. **A crown of fine gold:** Confirming his kingdom with honor. **He asked for life... length of days:** This refers to the World to Come <note>original: "Olam HaBa," the afterlife or messianic era</note>. **Great is his glory:** His reputation grows among all nations because of God's help. **Splendor and majesty:** Like the aura of a king. **You set him for blessings:** As it was said to Abraham, "you shall be a blessing," so too the king becomes a source of blessing for others. **You gladden him with joy:** The greatest joy is being in the Divine Presence. **Your hand will reach all Your enemies:** Your power will catch up to those who hide. **Like a fiery furnace:** They will be consumed as if inside an oven. **They intended evil... but they shall not succeed:** They planned harm, but because they lacked the power against God's anointed, they failed.

The commentary by Radak explains the historical context of royal warfare and the theological significance of trusting in God's name rather than military might.</summary>

# For the Leader
Regarding the Hind of the Dawn. Some explain that "Ayelet" is the name of the morning star <note>Venus</note>. And so in the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory, it is like the morning star that shines. And some say that it refers to the
Sages of the Assembly of Israel who are between the exile and the end of the exile, and all of it is like a hind. And they go to "My God, why have You forsaken me?" And "Shachar" (Dawn) its meaning is beauty and radiance,
for they had beauty and radiance. Like the dawn which breaks forth like the morning. And now they are in darkness in this exile as if they are among the stars and the clouds. And they ask from the exile: "My God, my God, why
have You forsaken me?" And this is in the language of an individual regarding the Assembly of Israel as a whole, for he speaks as an individual speaking in exile for every single person. "My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?" The repetition is the way of those who are hurried and crying out. Like "Awake, awake!"
"Abraham, Abraham!" "Moses, Moses!" And he said "My God" as if mentioning the appointment of my strength and my light, the source of my life, and now why have You forsaken me, being far from my salvation? And why will You be far from my salvation as implied by the words of
my groaning? And my God, I am appointed by day, day by day and by night, and I—You do not answer, and I have no silence, and I am not quieted, and why have You forgotten? And You are Holy and Live. And You, there is no delay at the gates, there is power...

# Psalms

They divide my garments among them, and for my purple robe they cast lots. But You, O Lord, do not be far; my Strength, hasten to my aid. Rescue my soul from the sword; my only one <note>original: "yachidati" – a poetic term for the soul, often translated as "my lonely soul" or "my precious life"</note> from the paw of the dog. Save me from the mouth of the lion, and from the horns of the wild oxen, for You have accepted my prayer. I will tell of Your name to my brothers; in the midst of the congregation, I will praise You. You who fear the Lord, praise Him; all the seed of Jacob, give Him glory; and tremble before Him, all the seed of Israel. For He has not despised nor loathed the prayer of the poor, nor has He withdrawn His Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> from among them; and in the time that he prayed before Him, He accepted it. From You comes my praise in the great congregation; I will pay my vows before those who fear Him. The humble shall eat and be satisfied; those who seek the Lord shall praise Him; the spirit of prophecy shall live in your hearts for the gathering and forever. All the ends of the earth shall remember and return before the Lord, and all the families of the nations shall bow before You. For the kingdom belongs to the Lord, and He rules over the nations. All the fat ones of the earth have eaten and bowed down; all who go down to the dust shall kneel before Him, even he who cannot keep his soul alive. The seed of Abraham shall serve Him; they shall tell of the Lord's power to the next generation. They shall come and tell of His righteousness to a people yet to be born, that which He has done.

### 23

A praise of David. The Lord is my shepherd; on Him I have leaned, I shall not lack anything. In a place of grazing, in the fatness of the earth, He has settled me; He leads me by the waters of rest. He restores my soul with breath; He leads me in paths of righteousness for His name's sake. Even when I walk in exile, in the valley of the shadow of death, I will not fear evil, for Your Word <note>original: "Memra" – a Targumic term for the divine Word or manifestation of God</note> is my support; Your rod and Your staff—they shall comfort me. You have arranged a table before me, opposite all my oppressors; You have fattened my soul with oil, and the greatness of my head is multiplied with an overflowing cup. Surely goodness and kindness shall pursue me all the days of my life, and I shall dwell in the House of the Sanctuary of the Lord for the length of my days.

### 24

<column-break/>

They divide my garments among them and for my clothing they cast lots. But You, O Lord, be not far off; O my Strength, hasten to my aid. Deliver my soul from the sword, my only one from the power of the dog. Save me from the mouth of the lion; from the horns of the wild oxen You have answered me. I will tell of Your name to my brothers; in the midst of the congregation I will praise You. You who fear the Lord, praise Him; all the seed of Jacob, honor Him; and stand in awe of Him, all the seed of Israel. For He has not despised nor loathed the affliction of the poor, nor has He hidden His face from him; but when he cried to Him, He heard. From You comes my praise in the great congregation; I will pay my vows before those who fear Him. The humble shall eat and be satisfied; those who seek the Lord shall praise Him—may your hearts live forever! <margin>forever and returning</margin> All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the Lord, and all the families of the nations shall bow down before You. For the kingdom is the Lord's, and He rules over the nations. All the fat ones of the earth shall eat and bow down; all who go down to the dust shall kneel before Him, even he who cannot keep his soul alive. A seed shall serve Him; it shall be told of the Lord to the next generation. They shall come and tell of His righteousness to a people yet to be born, that He has done it.

### 23

A Psalm of David. The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.
In green pastures He makes me lie down; beside still waters He leads me. He restores my soul; He leads me in paths of righteousness for His name's sake. Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will not fear evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me. <margin>and in my building</margin> You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; You anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows. Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life, and I shall dwell in the house of the Lord forever.

### 24

---

**They divide my garments among them.** This means they take my money and divide my possessions among themselves, and they distance themselves from my clothing while casting lots upon them. **But You, O Lord, be not far off; O my Strength.** When destruction begins to hang over me, do not be distant, for You are my strength and my power, and I have trusted in none but You; therefore, hasten to my aid. **Deliver my soul from the sword.** This refers to the sword of exile which strikes the drop <note>perhaps a metaphor for the remaining soul or essence</note> in exile. The "dog," "beast," and "lion" are metaphors for the kings of the nations of the world, each called according to their level of ferocity. And "my only one" is my soul, which has merited to dwell with the Torah of my spirit and is similar to God, whereas the lower body is merely called "the body." **And save me from the mouth of the lion.** For the decree and the company of the Holy One is like a flower; from there my only one shall be taken. "You answered me" is like "You shall answer me." Our rabbis explained this as a whole: that many times You have saved me from the throat of the holy covenant, like the time of the Temple—a covenant of mercy. **I will tell of Your name to my brothers.** When You redeem me from trouble and I return to my kingdom, I will praise You in the congregation of the pious. **You who fear the Lord, praise Him.** And you, the pious of Israel, praise Him, and all the seed of Jacob, honor Him. This includes the children of Ishmael and Keturah, for they are all children of Abraham, etc. Or it refers to those who lack the honor of the Passover and the firstborns of the nations who fell into exile for our souls' sake. **You who fear the Lord, praise Him.** All who stand in the house of prayer. The "fearers of the Lord" refer to Israel, and this division is like "Fearers of the Lord, bless the Lord; House of Levi; House of Aaron; House of Israel." The reason is that each is praised according to their level and their closeness to God. This verse mentions the praise and all the glory. For the fearers of God arrive at praise through their awe. And he mentions the poor man because his mind is beautiful and he is obligated toward the high Redeemer. God has already heard you, O certain poor man—heaven forbid that the pious should see water <note>perhaps a reference to the waters of distress or a specific midrashic image</note>. Our rabbis said he will have a vision of the priests. **All the seed of Jacob.** This refers to the Levites. **All the seed of Israel.** Taken literally. **For He has not despised nor loathed.** For He sees their piety even in exile. Exile is not an abomination; do not look down on your bowed stature. **Miatkha Tehillati (From You is my praise).** This is a greater kindness; my mouth is straight to praise You in the great congregation. I will arrange my vows. **The humble shall eat and be satisfied.** This means that the nations used to be arrogant over them, but now the humble will live in exile. When they are redeemed, they will be satisfied with words and obligations and will delight in what they lacked in exile. "May your hearts live forever" refers to their spirit and the life of Jacob, the opposite of a dead heart. For the spirit is a good living thing in the heart. When a person is in distress, his heart weakens, as it says "my heart is hollow within me." But when the blessing comes, the heart is established and they live forever. **For the kingdom is the Lord's.** This verse shows that all wealth and power belong to God. The kingdom's perfection is for all nations. **And they shall remember.** All the ends of the earth will turn and bow before You. **All the fat ones of the earth shall eat.** This refers to the pious ones. The nations were thickened with wealth, but they will bow and thank Him for the good. The wicked who descend to the dust—those who died in their beastly nature—will not have their souls live. Wisdom sustains those who possess it, but the wicked go to their eternal home like beasts. Only kindness remains. In the end of days, they will bow before the King. This is a hint that their souls will be considered in the World to Come, unlike the humble who "live forever." Every knee shall bow on the day of death. But the "seed that serves Him" is the seed of Israel who pass through the covenant constantly. **It shall be told to the Lord for a generation.** It shall be written and told in books, and they will be called the people of God. **They shall come and tell of His righteousness.** Those who emerge from exile from all the ends of the earth will tell of His righteousness to the people yet to be born.

# Psalm
**Of David.** David said this psalm about himself as a prayer for future generations, or he said it about the days of darkness in exile. Therefore, it is placed next to the preceding psalm. **In green pastures He makes me lie down.** This speaks of the blessing of the spirit. It is written: "And David went and dwelt in the forest of Hereth." Why was it called Hereth? Because it was dry as clay (*cheres*), but the Holy One moistened it with the dew of the World to Come. **He restores.** This refers to the kingdom... for His name's sake. **Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death.** This refers to the wilderness. **I will not fear evil.** For Your presence is with me. **Your rod and Your staff.** The "rod" refers to suffering, and the "staff" refers to the Torah. **You prepare a table before me.** Opposite my enemies. **You anoint my head with oil.** This means that through suffering, one learns. **Surely goodness.** This falls in this world. **The house of the Lord.** This is the Temple. **In green pastures.** This is also interpreted as the gathering of the Levites by the waters of rest. The shepherd leads his flock to a good place, not a place of drought, but to a place of morning grazing and peaceful waters.

> **Of David. A song of praise. The earth and its fullness belong to the Lord; the world and its inhabitants. Because He founded it upon the seas and established it upon the rivers. <note>This section completes the commentary on Psalm 23:2-6</note>
...[The shepherd] knows where to let them rest in their folds. And in the afternoon, he brings them to rest by "still waters." This means waters that move slowly and calmly, so that the force of the water does not sweep the sheep away while they drink. Therefore, it says: **He leads me beside still waters.** **He restores:** He brings [the soul] back. Like a good shepherd who leads his flock through level ground and does not strike them, but leads them gently to "paths of righteousness." He does all this for His name's sake, so that the one who follows Him lacks nothing. **Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death:** I will not fear evil, for even in a place of danger where a person might fear for his life—the darkness of the grave <note>original: "sheol"</note>, a place of gloom—I am secure. He compares the grave to a deep valley. I say that my trust in God is such that I fear no harm. **For You are with me:** Your support is with me. **Your rod and Your staff:** They are my comfort. Just as a shepherd uses a staff to guide and a rod to protect, Your presence provides the sustenance and protection I need. **You prepare a table before me:** You provide my food in the sight of my enemies. **You anoint my head with oil:** Oil signifies joy and greatness. A person’s body remains healthy and well-provided for when God’s favor is upon them. **My cup overflows:** My portion is full and prosperous. All of this is because of the great goodness He has bestowed upon me. **Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me:** I thank You for the bounty in Your house. I will not be removed from Your hand, for the days of my life are spent in Your truth. **And I shall dwell in the house of the Lord for many days:** In the Sanctuary <note>original: "Beit HaMikdash"</note>, to serve You and wait for You. The word "dwell" <note>original: "v’shavti"</note> implies returning or remaining. This refers to the length of my days—the years of my life.

# Of David

**A Psalm.** This psalm was composed for the occasion of the Ark being brought into the Holy of Holies <note>The inner-most chamber of the Temple</note>. This occurred after David had offered sacrifices on Mount Moriah and designated the site for the Temple, as written in the Book of Chronicles. He begins by saying **The earth is the Lord’s and its fullness**, to teach that although this specific spot is the "Mountain of the Lord" and His holy place, one should not think God is limited to it. He is the master of the entire world and everything in it. He founded the world upon the "seas and rivers," referring to the geographical boundaries. Our sages teach that the Land [of Israel] is surrounded by seven seas and four rivers. These four rivers are the Jordan, the Yarmouk, the Keramyon, and the Pigah <note>These names represent the traditional borders of the Land in rabbinic geography</note>. The phrase **upon the seas** means "adjacent to the seas." It is as if the land was drawn out from the water, as the Torah says: "Let the waters be gathered... and let the dry land appear."

**Who may ascend the mountain...** Only those with "clean hands and a pure heart." The verse mentions three human faculties: deed (hands), thought (heart), and speech (not swearing falsely). To have "clean hands" means to be free of theft or violence. To "not take My name in vain" refers to the sanctity of the soul and the prohibition against false oaths. **He shall receive a blessing:** Just as one brings a gift (blessing) to a king, the person of integrity receives a "blessing" and "vindication" from God. **This is the generation of those who seek Him:** This refers to the people of David’s time, or the generation of Solomon who completed the Temple. The people are called "Jacob," referring to the entire seed of Israel.

**Lift up your heads, O gates:** This refers to the famous tradition that when Solomon tried to bring the Ark into the Temple, the gates were too narrow or the lintels too low. He called out for the gates to "lift their heads." According to the literal meaning, this is a poetic metaphor. Just as a great king is welcomed with grand entrances, the "King of Glory" (God’s presence) is invited into His permanent home. These are called **everlasting doors** because once the Ark entered this house, it would never again wander from place to place as it did in the desert, or in Philistine captivity, or in the houses of Abinadab and Obed-Edom. Now, it has reached its "eternal rest."

**Who is this King of glory?** The gates are depicted as asking this question. The answer is: **The Lord, strong and mighty.** In the second half of the psalm, the answer changes to **The Lord of Hosts.** This is because after the Ark is settled in the "House of Eternity," God is recognized not just as a warrior in battle, but as the Master of all the heavenly legions (Hosts). This reflects the peace of Solomon’s reign compared to the wars of David.

# Of David
<note>This commentary is by Rabbi Meir Arama, from his work "Urim Ve-Tummim." He explores the poetic structure and deep philosophical meaning of the Psalm.</note>

The parts of this Psalm are divided according to an alphabetical arrangement <note>Psalm 25 is an acrostic poem where each verse begins with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note>. This is like the "Atbash" system <note>term: Atbash; an ancient Hebrew substitution cipher where the first letter is swapped with the last, the second with the second-to-last, etc.</note>, and there are missing letters in this book's version as there are in others. There are some missing letters in the cycle of the verses, specifically two letters. It is not written "to his sons" in these books for more than fifty, but every verse is in its "house" <note>stanza</note> of the poem. It appears that the whole Psalm is thus arranged according to the Alphabet... and here there is no letter *Bet* at the start of a verse, but rather the letter *Aleph* appears twice. There are letters that are doubled or skipped, such as the *Pe* that follows the *Tsadi*. 

**My God, in You I have trusted.** I have trusted in You in my old age. Therefore, grant me life and do not let me be ashamed. For if You do not grant me my sustenance, I will have shame in my soul. The request is for the body as well, for those who trust in You should not be ashamed. **Indeed, let none who wait for You [be ashamed].** I have removed myself from my own shame through You... I am lonely, for I have no one but You, my Holy One. 

**Show me Your ways, O Lord; teach me Your paths.** This doubling of the matter in different words means: teach me from my youth until I am old. The meaning of "Guide me" is "Show me," as it is written elsewhere, "Make known to me the path I should walk." For the one speaking is caught in wars all his days... he seeks knowledge of the divine way in both general and specific terms. 

**For You are the God of my salvation.** My hopes have been from of old, until today. **For You I wait all day long:** like a constant cycle for a man.

**Remember Your mercies.** Remember for me now Your mercies and kindnesses which have always existed. Since I have waited and hoped until now, it is right for You to say them to me. Remember Your covenant with Your people and the merit of the forefathers.

**The sins of my youth and my transgressions do not remember.** These refer to different types of errors. The "sins of youth" are those done in ignorance, while "transgressions" <note>Hebrew: pesha'im</note> are rebellious acts done with knowledge. He prays that God remembers him with kindness and not with strict judgment. **For the sake of Your goodness, O Lord:** Not just for my sake, but because it is Your nature to be good.

**Good and upright.** Because He is good and upright, He teaches those who have strayed to return to the path. He teaches the humble His way, for humility is the prerequisite for receiving divine wisdom.

**The secret of the Lord is for those who fear Him.** The "secret" <note>Hebrew: sod</note> refers to the inner wisdom of the Torah and the mysteries of creation. Those who occupy themselves with wisdom will be able to understand His paths. **And His covenant to make them know it:** This refers to the covenant God made to give understanding to those who honor Him. This is the primary reward for a human being.

**My eyes are always toward the Lord.** For He is my hope and my refuge. **For He will bring my feet out of the net:** This refers to the "net" of sins or the "net" of enemies who seek to trap him. 

**Turn to me and be gracious to me.** As he said at the beginning of the Psalm: "let not my enemies triumph." He describes himself as "lonely and poor" because even though he might be a king, he feels solitary in his devotion to God, and his eyes are dependent only on Divine grace. 

**The troubles of my heart have enlarged.** The worries and pressures have grown so much that they occupy his heart, leaving him no room to focus on serving God. Therefore, he asks for release from these distresses so his heart may be free for worship.
