<margin>Do not</margin> **hide Your face from me.** Do not hide the various aspects of Your presence from me. <margin>turn</margin> **do not turn Your servant away in anger.** This is like the words "my portions" or "your breadth," expressing toil and dwelling. **You have been my help.** Until now, You have been my help in times of flight.
<margin>O God of my salvation</margin> Similar to "the booth of my festivals," so uphold me from the time of old age, providing the strength of the fortresses of kindness.
This means: You knew that my sustenance and my vineyard were fading, and after the sickness, the kneading and the crushing remain; yet the heart of the disciplined remains with the Lord's way.
<margin>from their search</margin> **because of my watchful enemies.** Turn them away from the few who are strong like a leafy tree. This is like the phrase "and his sickness was..." <note>referencing linguistic parallels in biblical Hebrew</note>.
The text mentions "like a soul," "like a desire," "like a sickness." If I had not believed in the goodness... the heart is full of praise for His honor, occupied all his days with the war of the wearying struggle. **For false witnesses have risen against me, breathing out violence.** They testify as if they are burdened with words of violence, but I have no portion except in the Lord. **Do not deliver me...** and the matter remains settled in Him. **If I had not believed to see the goodness.** This is because my eyes were sick with words of violence, and I almost perished from their words if I had not believed in You and did not lose hope.
My belief gives me hope in the Lord to live in His goodness in the World to Come <note>original: "Olam Ha-Ba"</note>. This is what is meant by **in the land of the living.** He calls the World to Come the "land of the living," and it is fitting to trust in it. According to the joy of the good of the World to Come, one should wait and look to the Heavens. When one's path is measured, one should find mercy, as if preserved to live in hope, even while in toil and preparation. Therefore, one must be precise in following the straight path and looking toward the "land of the living." For when one causes a person to sin, it is as if death is decreed upon them. The Sages <note>original: "Rabbis of blessed memory"</note> say: "Master of the Universe, I am certain that You reward the righteous in the future, but I do not know if I have a portion among them," for sin may cause one to lose that merit.
**Wait for the Lord.** Because "I believed" is written, I say that I have already prepared myself all day to wait for the Lord's help. **Be strong and let your heart take courage.** He will strengthen you in His ways, so your heart should not fear the words of enemies. **Yes, wait for the Lord.** This is stated a second time to emphasize that hope should be constant and never depart from the heart.

# Of David
**To You, O Lord, I call.** This psalm follows the theme of the previous one. It asks the Lord for a sign to quiet the busy affairs of this world, so that one might be free to occupy oneself with holy matters. Through this, David's servants will be preserved and enter the divine treasury. He says: **my Rock, do not be deaf to me.** Do not let my ears be closed to You, for I fear that if You are silent to me, I will be turned away with those who descend to the Pit—meaning the wicked who go down to Sheol <note>the underworld</note> when their souls perish with them.
The word "silent" <note>Heresh</note> is related to "thought" <note>Heshbon</note>. It is as if he is saying: do not act as if my value has diminished and do not fail to answer my prayer. **Hear the voice of my supplications... toward Your holy Sanctuary.** This refers to the Holy of Holies where the Ark was kept. For there I spread my hands in the service of God. This is similar to "lifting up holy hands." Even when the Lord is on high in the heavens, one directs their heart toward the Sanctuary. Or **Your holy Sanctuary** might be understood literally, as his heart and hands are directed toward that place. It is a metaphor for the opening of glory. This way, his prayer reaches the holy dwelling place. Or, "holy Sanctuary" could refer to the heavens themselves, as we have explained. **Do not drag me away.** Do not let me share the death of the wicked, as in "Do not sweep away my soul with sinners." The language of "dragging" implies how every man is eventually pulled toward death. **Who speak peace.** For most wicked people speak peace with their mouths while harboring evil in their hearts. **Give to them.** Since only You know the heart, repay them for their evil deeds. **Because they do not contemplate.** They occupy themselves with physical service and do not understand the wisdom of the Holy One. As the Sages said: "If they knew, they would return to Him." Wisdom involves contemplating the works of the Lord—understanding nature and the work of His hands in heaven and earth. This is the strength of the first principles. Our Sages said: "They do not look at the work of the Lord"—this refers to those who do not calculate the celestial cycles and constellations. **He will tear them down and not build them up.** This is a prayer that they should vanish from the world. He repeats "He will tear them down" to emphasize that their works and the work of their hands will be destroyed.
**Blessed be the Lord.** He speaks with certainty, giving thanks to God who heard his prayer. This occurred at the end of his days when he was saved from the hand of the Lord. During that generation, he was nearly killed by the giants until he was saved and did not go out to war again. **The Lord is my strength.** This is a way of praise and thanksgiving. **The Lord is my strength and my shield.** He is my strength who saved me from being struck down by the giant. **In Him my heart trusted.** I was helped by Him even when my physical strength was spent. **And I was helped.** As it is written, "God helped him." **Therefore my heart exults.** Even when rescued from death, he rejoices with song. Since he was saved from the wars of the world, he now has the leisure to occupy himself with holy matters. Since he is in the House of the Lord, he prays for Israel, that God should be their strength and their fortress. Therefore, he gives thanks. **The Lord is strength for them.** In times when they need to go out to war, the Lord will be their strength, granting them victory over their enemies. **He is the saving refuge of His anointed.** He refers to himself as the "anointed" whom God has saved. As it is said: "The anointed of the God of Jacob." The Lord will be his strength. This is written in the plural—"they will understand and see"—and also "the work of the Lord's hands." **Save Your people.** Save them from enemies and bless Your inheritance. **Tend them.** Like a shepherd. **And carry them forever.**

# A Psalm
**Of David. Ascribe to the Lord.** This is like "Give to the Lord glory." Give strength to God. This is repeated for emphasis. **Ascribe to the Lord the glory of His name.** Praise Him with words of honor and exaltation, for that is the secret of His glory, like "honoring the face of the elder." # Psalms

<column-break/>

<margin>purchaser</margin>
> The voice of the Lord is over the waters; the God of glory thunders; the Lord is over many waters. The voice of the Lord is in power; the voice of the Lord is in majesty. The voice of the Lord breaks the cedars; the Lord shatters the cedars of Lebanon. He makes them skip like a calf, Lebanon and Sirion <note>Mount Hermon</note> like a young wild ox. The voice of the Lord hews out flames of fire. The voice of the Lord shakes the wilderness; the Lord shakes the wilderness of Kadesh. The voice of the Lord makes the deer give birth and strips the forests bare; and in His Temple, everyone says, "Glory!" The Lord sat enthroned at the Flood; the Lord sits as King forever. The Lord will give strength to His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace.

---

### A Psalm, a song for the dedication of the House; of David.
> I will exalt You, O Lord, for You have lifted me up <note>original Hebrew: "dilitani," literally "drawn me up like water from a well"</note> and have not let my enemies rejoice over me. O Lord my God, I cried out to You, and You healed me. O Lord, You brought up my soul from the underworld <note>Sheol</note>; You kept me alive from descending into the Pit. Sing to the Lord, O His devout ones, and give thanks to His holy Name.

<column-break/>

> The voice of the Lord is heard over the waters upon the strength of the ocean; the honorable God thunders and bellows from the heavens. The voice of the Lord is heard in power; the voice of the Lord is heard in praise. The voice of the Lord breaks the cedars, and the Word <note>Aramaic: "Memra," a term used to describe God’s manifest action</note> of the Lord breaks the cedars of Lebanon. And He makes them skip like a calf: Lebanon and the mountain of the fruits of Lebanon like a young wild ox. The voice of the Lord saws through flames of fire. The voice of the Lord shatters the desert; the Word of the Lord shatters the desert of Rekem <note>Kadesh</note>. The voice of the Lord strengthens the hinds and reveals the thickets, and in His Sanctuary above, the priests of the Lord upon the throne of His splendor say "Glory" before Him. The Lord sat upon the throne of His kingdom in the generation of the Flood, and the Lord sat upon the throne of mercy and will seat His children upon their children forever and ever. The Lord gives the Torah <note>The Aramaic translator interprets "strength" as the Torah</note> to His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace.

---

<margin>the house of the teacher</margin>
> A praise-song for the dedication of the Holy House of David. I will praise You, O Lord, for You have raised me up and did not allow my enemies to rejoice over me. O Lord my God, I prayed before You and You healed me. O Lord, You brought up my soul from the underworld; You sustained me from descending into the depths of the pit. Sing before the Lord, His devout ones, and give thanks at the mention of His holiness.

---

**The Voice of the Lord.** Our Sages of blessed memory <term>Sages: Rabbinic authorities, often abbreviated as Chazal</term> interpreted this as referring to the day the Torah was given. They said that the "Great Voice" from the heavens first passed over the waters. On this, the verse says "over many waters," meaning the waters of the sea. And it says "The voice of the Lord is in power," meaning the power of the voice was over the water, and afterward "in majesty" over Israel. This was so that Israel would not die from the sheer force of that sound; it passed through the water first to temper its strength, leaving a "majestic" strength for Israel to be able to endure it. Even so, through its majesty and strength, they stood as if scorched by death. It says "The voice of the Lord breaks cedars," meaning the sound shattered the trees and made them skip like calves. Afterward, "The voice of the Lord hews out flames of fire," like the statement regarding the giving of the Tablets and the miraculous signs. It says "The voice of the Lord shakes the wilderness" because the mountains and the plains trembled. Even the small animals went into labor and gave birth from the terror of the sound. "And strips the forests bare," for the animals in the forests were left exposed. "And in His Temple, everyone says 'Glory'" refers to Mount Sinai, where the Tablets were considered a holy ascent. 

Some commentators <note>referring to Abraham Ibn Ezra</note> explain the psalm according to its <term>plain meaning: peshat</term> regarding the wonders of natural sounds on earth, such as thunder. The "voices" are the sounds of thunder and lightning. The reason for mentioning these sounds is that they arouse the falling of rain by the help of the God of gods. "The voice of the Lord is over the waters" refers to the rain, as the descending rain is formed from the vapors of the clouds. It mentions Lebanon and Sirion because these are major mountains in the land of Israel. The "shaking of the desert" refers to the Great Desert. "Making the deer give birth" is because the fear of the thunder causes them to go into labor prematurely. 

In my opinion, this psalm refers to the future days of the Messiah. The "strength" God gives His people is the restoration of Israel through the power of the deeds of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. 

# A Psalm, a song for the dedication of the House.
David composed this in anticipation of the dedication of the Temple <term>Beit HaMikdash</term>, even though he did not build it himself. He mentions "You have lifted me up" because God saved him from the hands of his enemies who sought to prevent his kingship. Alternatively, it was said to him by a prophet that his son Solomon would reign after him and build the House. David's life was full of wars, and a king who sheds blood cannot build a place of peace and forgiveness. Thus, David prepared the foundations. He says "You healed me" regarding the healing of the soul from the trials he endured. "You brought my soul up from Sheol" refers to being saved from the judgment of the afterlife. "Sing to the Lord, His devout ones"—it is fitting for all the righteous to sing because God's anger is but for a moment, but His favor is for a lifetime.

<margin>To the Chief Musician, a Psalm of David. In You, Lord</margin>
I have taken refuge; let me never be ashamed; deliver me in Your righteousness. Incline Your ear to me; deliver me speedily; be my strong rock, for a house of defense to save me. For You are my rock <margin>Lord</margin> and my fortress; therefore for Your name's sake lead me, and guide me. Pull me out of the net that they have laid secretly for me: for You are my strength. Into Your hand I commit my spirit: You have redeemed me, O Lord God of truth. I have hated them that regard lying vanities: but I trust in the Lord. I will be glad and rejoice in Your mercy: for You have considered my trouble; You have known my soul in adversities; And have not shut me up into the hand of the enemy: You have set my feet in a large room. Have mercy upon me, O Lord, for I am in trouble: mine eye is consumed with grief, yea, my soul and my belly. For my life is spent with grief, and my years with sighing: my strength fails because of mine iniquity, and my bones are consumed. I was a reproach among all mine enemies, but especially among my neighbors, and a fear to mine acquaintance: they that did see me without fled from me. <sig>Parable</sig>

---

"For His anger is but for a moment." This means that the mercy and the anger of the Holy One, Blessed be He, are such that His anger lasts only a tiny amount of time. But the favor of the Master brings life forever. Similarly, in the Psalms, there are many accounts of His attributes, all of which are for good except for one: "visiting the iniquity of the fathers." This is for ten generations, while the reward for the righteous is for thousands of generations. Therefore, he said "And I..." etc., because the measure of goodness is much greater and lasts longer than the measure of punishment. "In the evening, weeping may lodge." If one lodges in weeping in the evening, the morning brings a blessing. The parable <note>original: "mashal"</note> here is that the evening represents the time of suffering, and the morning represents the kindness of the Lord. Likewise, David said that he accepted the Lord's kindness. Because the goodness of the world's blessing was in his eyes but a moment, while the time of life was eternal. "You girded me with joy." Since my sickness and my strength were such that I thought I would not fall or be moved forever, because I thought the reward of evil would not have the power to turn me from the good path. "For You are my rock..." etc. My nature and my strength are to pray for this, for I recognized that Your attribute is unique to me. As long as it is Your will, You will be my help and sustain me in my life. "Lord, by Your favor." My mountain <note>meaning my strength or kingdom</note> You have established in Your strength, so that I did not fall when I relied on it. There was no fear that evil would turn me away, for I was in a strong place. But when "You hid Your face" from me for a moment, and You were not there to help my understanding, then I fell and became terrified within myself. Then, in my distress, I called out from before You and saw that the time was difficult and powerful. Because of this, the danger fell upon me and my neighbors and my friends. Therefore, David said "Have mercy on me, Lord," because I knew I had no cure without You.

"What profit is there in my blood?" This refers to the soul. For the blood is the soul, and the soul is life. Because of the danger to my soul, I said, "What profit is there in my life if I go down to the pit?" If there is no reward or dwelling after my death, it is better to live a life of fearing You in this world. For the dead do not praise God. As it is said: "The dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God." The dust cannot thank You, nor can it tell of Your truth. If there is no reward for the soul, it will not return to God, and there would be no hope after life or death. I have explained this in the book regarding "if you are disciplined," that you should not die the death of the soul <note>spiritual death</note>. Some explain this as the death of the body. "Hear, O Lord." I accepted my suffering and said, "Lord, have mercy on me." "You have turned my mourning." My sackcloth, in which I mourned for my soul, You turned into my dance, saying to me that the Lord has removed your sin and you shall not die. "You have opened my sackcloth." My mourning and my fasting for my sins, You have opened and removed. "And girded me with joy." You strengthened me. "To the end that my glory may sing to You." This refers to the soul. It is called "glory" because it is the honor of the person. "And not be silent." Mentioning the glory that You gave me, joy and life. Therefore, he says, "O Lord my God, I will give thanks to You forever," for I am alive because of this. And in the Midrash: Anyone who thinks to do a good deed, it is credited to them as if they did it. Know that this was the case with David: since he desired to build the Temple, it was written in his name, as it says, "A Psalm, a song for the dedication of the House; of David."

# To the Chief Musician
A Psalm of David. David composed this Psalm when he fled from Saul. "In You, Lord, I have taken refuge." Since I have taken refuge in You, I shall never be ashamed. "In Your righteousness." Not by my own merit. "Incline Your ear to me quickly." Because those who pursue me are surrounding me, and I have no strength left. "For a house of defense." A strong tower. "For You are my rock." You are my strength and my fortress. I ask this for Your Name's sake, not for my own sake. "Pull me out." Save me from the hands of those who ambush me. "Into Your hand I commit my spirit." They are lying in wait for my soul, so I deposit it in Your hand, knowing You will guard it. "You have redeemed." Using the past tense for the future <note>A common prophetic/poetic Hebrew style where a future certainty is described as already happened</note>. "O Lord God of truth." Because You are the God of truth, it is in Your power to redeem me, and to fulfill Your word that I would be king. "I have hated those who watch." I do not look to omens or superstitions. Even in my flight from Saul, I did not trust in diviners, but in the Lord alone. "I will be glad and rejoice in Your mercy." After You perform this kindness for me and rescue me, I will rejoice. "For You have seen my affliction." You saw the distress I was in when I fled from Saul and You did not turn Your eyes from me. "And have not shut me up into the hand of the enemy." This refers to Saul. Since I did not fall into his hand, it is as if You set my feet in a broad place. "Have mercy on me, Lord." Because of my constant wandering, my eyes are failing. "My soul and my belly." As if from hunger and pain, for he often suffered hunger during his flight. "My life is spent." David's life was consumed with moving from place to place. "My strength fails because of my iniquity." David says that because of his sins, this evil has come upon him. "I was a reproach among all my enemies." My acquaintances and neighbors treat me as a disgrace. They distance themselves from me, fearing the reproach of being associated with me. "A fear to my acquaintances." Those who loved me are now afraid to be near me. "They that did see me without fled from me." Like a person who sees a leper or someone excommunicated, they flee from me. "I am forgotten as a dead man." Anyone who knows me acts as if I don't exist, and my name is forgotten as if I were already dead. "I am like a broken vessel." I have been discarded, and no one thinks of me anymore.

# Psalms

For I have heard the slander of many; terror is all around me. When they took counsel together against me, they plotted to take my life. But as for me, I have trusted in You, O Lord; I said, "You are my God." My times are in Your hand; deliver me from the hand of my enemies and from those who pursue me. Make Your face shine upon Your servant; save me in Your lovingkindness. O Lord, let me not be ashamed, for I have called upon You; let the wicked be ashamed, and let them be silent in the grave <note>Hebrew: Sheol</note>. <margin>For those who take refuge</margin> Let the lying lips be put to silence, which speak insolent things proudly and contemptuously against the righteous. Oh, how great is Your goodness, which You have laid up for those who fear You, which You have prepared for those who trust in You in the presence of the sons of men! You shall hide them in the secret place of Your presence from the conspiracies of man; You shall keep them secretly in a pavilion from the strife of tongues. Blessed be the Lord, for He has shown me His marvelous lovingkindness in a besieged city. And I said in my haste, "I am cut off from before Your eyes"; nevertheless, <margin>restrain, do in the second, finished</margin> You heard the voice of my supplications when I cried out to You. Oh, love the Lord, all you His godly ones! For the Lord preserves the faithful and fully repays the proud doer. Be of good courage, and He shall strengthen your heart, all you who hope in the Lord.

### 32: A Maskil <note>A term for a contemplative or instructional poem</note> of David
Happy is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered. Happy is the man to whom the Lord does not impute iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile. <margin>to wash away / judge</margin> When I kept silent, my bones grew old through my groaning all the day long. For day and night Your hand was heavy upon me; my moisture was turned into the drought of summer. Selah. I acknowledged my sin to You, and my iniquity I have not hidden. I said, "I will confess my transgressions to the Lord," and You forgave the iniquity of my sin. Selah. For this cause everyone who is godly shall pray to You in a time when You may be found; surely in a flood of great waters they shall not reach him. You are my hiding place; You shall preserve me from trouble; You shall surround me with songs of deliverance. Selah. I will instruct you and teach you in the way you should go; I will guide you with My eye.

Because I heard the evil report that many nations spoke against me—fear from the dwellers around me—when they gathered together as one against me, they plotted to take my life. But I have trusted in Your Word, O Lord; I said, "You are my God." The times of my redemption are in Your hand; deliver me from the hand of my enemies and from my pursuers. Brighten the light of Your countenance upon Your servant; redeem me in Your goodness. O Lord, let me not be ashamed because I have called to You; let the wicked be ashamed, let them be silenced and descend to the grave. Let the lying lips be bound, which speak insults against the righteous with pride and contempt. How great is Your goodness that You have hidden for those who fear You! You have performed it for those who hope in You in the sight of the sons of men. You shall hide them in a secret place, by Your side, in the time of Your anger, from the gatherings of men; You shall hide them in a shelter from the strife of tongues. Blessed be the Lord, for He has distinguished His kindness to me in a fortified city. And I said in my haste, "I am cut off from before Your eyes"; but truly You accepted and heard the voice of my prayer when I supplicated before You. Love the Lord, all His righteous ones! The Lord guards the faithful and pays back the extra measure to those who act with pride. Be strong, and let your hearts be hidden <note>strengthened/fortified</note>, all you who hope for the Word of the Lord.

### 32: A good instruction spoken by David
Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgotten, and whose sins are covered. Happy is the man to whom the Lord does not count sins, provided there is no deceit in his spirit. Because I was silent from the words of the Torah, my bones wore out in my weeping all day long. For day and night Your blow was heavy upon me; my freshness was turned into the parching heat of summer forever. I make my debt known to You, and my iniquity I have not hidden; I said, "I will confess my rebellions before the Lord," and You forgave the iniquity of the sins of my heart forever. Because of this, every righteous person shall pray for the time when he may find mercy, so that at the time when many springs of water break forth, they shall not reach him to do him harm. You are my place of confinement from distress; You shall guard me; with songs of salvation You shall surround me forever. I will make you wise and teach you in this way that you shall go; I will counsel you for good, and My eye is upon you.
</column>

### Regarding David
**For I have heard.** His enemies were mentioning many things about him to Saul. He said, "lest he remember from all around." For there were those dwelling around him under the protection of his place who went out against him. **In their taking counsel.** This simply means they were consulting together against me and thinking to take my life. The heart of the "three" <note>referring to a grammatical or traditional grouping</note> is to my words and to merit, and he mentioned that it was not to take my life. **And I:** They missed their mark in trying to take my life and my soul, and I trusted in You. For I was happy with my portion. **Portion.** Meaning, You are the Master and Ruler over me. And I did not explain specifically "my times." **My times.** Fear and trembling, and they gathered to save and to avenge between me and those in them. To release or to strike from the hand of my enemy and my pursuer. **Make Your face shine upon Your servant.** This is like saying "to Your servant." And the light of the face is salvation and rescue through Your kindness. And even though I am not worthy, O Lord, **let me not be ashamed.** Even if the wicked come with their power, for they did not call upon You. **Let them be silent in the grave.** This is a term for being cut off. **To the grave.** To receive. Or explained as a sudden blow to their souls. **Let the lying lips be put to silence.** Those who argue against him—and what do they say about him? They mention that he is harmful, that he is a schemer and enriches himself through folly. **Against the righteous.** Against David himself, and all the righteous say this. **Insolent.** Words that are insolent and strong. **How great is Your goodness.** The wicked speak with pride and contempt, insolent words against the righteous. Therefore, He hides those who are crushed and beaten, those who are abandoned. What word and what language is hidden in the lips of the mouth? And if it is not hidden now, it will be in the World to Come. And besides this, You have acted and sought great wealth for them many times in this world. Be strong among the sons of man, for his merit is hidden. **You shall hide them.** A word of prayer, then a word of His glory. **In the secret of Your presence.** In the secret of Your will. For in His presence there is no sorrow. **From the conspiracies of man.** From the thoughts of men—their plots. Like "the hiding of the plans." And these descend to the depth, which is like "ruggedness" and "gathering." **You shall keep them secretly in a pavilion from the strife of tongues.** Like it says, "the slander of many." And the reward for the righteous is prepared. **Blessed be the Lord.** And this is a song and light. **Blessed be the Lord, for He has shown me His marvelous lovingkindness.** Because the matter was not according to my expectation or my need. He said this **in a besieged city.** Meaning, when David was in a besieged city. And "besieged" is related to "siege," as in "and you shall place a siege." And as for what he said, **in my haste.** Like when it says, "And David was in haste to get away from Saul," then he sat in his hiding place. **I am cut off from before Your eyes.** Like "I am cut off in my ruins." He said, "I thought I was lost from before Your eyes and You would no longer turn to me." **Nevertheless, You heard the voice of my supplications.** This was when he sat in his hiding. As it says, "And I will sing, for I was not silenced." He asked of the Lord that he should not be trapped. And it is clear that he will come with a opening, like "and they sanctified the soul." He said, "Behold, I tell you to be strong, to see what is with me." **For the Lord preserves the faithful.** Protecting me from all my enemies. And "faithful" is a description. **And fully repays the proud doer.** He preserves the faithful from the hand of those who speak with pride. As it says, "and the words of their lips shall catch them," and He pays them for their excess and their pride. **Be strong.** Be strong, all who hope in the Lord, for He will strengthen your hearts.

**A Maskil of David.** "Happy is he whose transgression is forgiven." We have already written concerning the "Maskil" and the fourth psalm, and here "Maskil" means to be happy from the words of instruction. He says: Happy is the one who bears this burden of his sin and covers his sin through complete repentance. And his punishment, which he sees in this world—for there is no righteous man who does not sin—will be made light through his repentance. Behold, happy is the one who is pure and clean for the World to Come. And truly, "covering" is also needed for the double nature of sin, as in "and to cover my shame." And the matter is repeated when he says: **Happy is the man to whom the Lord does not impute iniquity.** This is the "Chata'ah" <note>unintentional sin</note>. That is to say, He does not count it in his spirit any longer, for he has turned away from it. And this is what is said, **and in whose spirit there is no guile.** For his repentance is not bitter, as if to say, "I will sin and then return," or like one who is caught and then regrets. David said this about himself when he was in distress. And he says, "Happy is the one who escaped through his return." **When I kept silent.** This is from the levels of the righteous. David fell to the lowest level, which is "Pesha" <note>willful transgression</note>. But after that, he returned in complete repentance, and it was forgiven him. **Whose sin is covered.** Meaning he has many merits and righteousness, and this one small sin is covered and not seen among his righteous acts. It is like a small amount of straw in a large pile of wheat—the straw is covered and not seen at all. **The Lord does not impute iniquity to him.** This is when He does not count it at all. **And in whose spirit there is no guile.** And he says, because he was silent at first because of the pressure, for most righteous people in this level might sin and hide from the judgment, but the Lord does not impute it to them. **When I kept silent, my bones grew old.** The word "Ki" <note>Because/When</note> here means "as when." As in "When you bear children." He said, "when I was silent, I groaned and was wasted in my bones, and I consumed my strength until my heart failed." **For day and night.** Day and night Your hand was heavy upon my iniquities. He says: "Your hand was heavy upon me, meaning the weight of my punishment, that You would not forgive me." Like the heat of summer that dries out the moisture of the body. **I acknowledged my sin.** Even though You know my sins, I acknowledge them in the way of human speech. Therefore, I will confess my rebellions to You and not hide them. **I said.** This is what I thought. For this was my intention: to confess my transgression, and You forgave the guilt of my sin. **Selah.** This refers to a future place, and according to the words of prophecy. He spoke a double word: "iniquity of my sin." **For this cause.** Since they saw that my prayer was accepted and my sin was covered, every godly person shall pray to You so they do not fall into iniquity. **In a time when You may be found.** For a time when he will have a covering like mine. **Only in a flood of great waters.** He will not turn to the Lord except when he is in distress. He compares the troubles of the world to "great waters" that sweep everything away; to such a person, the troubles will not reach him, just as it says regarding the high place. **You are my hiding place.** For You are my secret place beneath my covering. **You shall surround me with songs of deliverance.** The songs and praises of the people who have escaped shall surround me, for You saved me. **I will instruct you.** He mentions that he who knows his rebuke will have many songs of praise. **I will guide you with My eye.** I will give you counsel from the attribute that I have gained through my own experience. For I have looked and walked in a difficult way, but I returned to the Lord with all my heart, and He accepted me in repentance; so you should do as well.

Do not be...

# Psalms

**Psalm 33**

Do not be like the horse or the mule that have no understanding; their mouth must be harnessed with a bit and bridle to be restrained, so that they do not come near you. Many are the blows for the wicked, but for the one who trusts in the Word of the Lord <note>Aramaic: *Memra*, a term used to describe God's manifest action or presence</note>, lovingkindness shall surround him. Rejoice in the Word of the Lord and be glad, O righteous ones; give praise, all you who are upright in heart!

->Praise, O righteous ones, in the Word of the Lord; for the upright, praise is beautiful.<-

Give thanks before the Lord with the lyre; with a lute of ten strings, give praise before Him. Sing before Him a new song; play skillfully with a shout of joy. For the Word of the Lord is upright, and all His works are done in faithfulness. He loves righteousness and justice; the earth is full of the goodness of the Lord. By the Word of the Lord the heavens were made, and by the breath of His mouth all their host. He gathers the waters of the sea together as if in a flask; He puts the depths into storehouses. Let all the inhabitants of the earth fear before the Lord; let all the dwellers of the world tremble because of Him. For He spoke, and it was; He commanded, and it stood fast. The Lord has frustrated the counsel of the nations; He has nullified the thoughts of the peoples. The counsel of the Lord stands forever; the thoughts of His heart from generation to generation.

->Fortunate are the people whose God is the Lord; the people whom He has chosen for His own inheritance.<-

From heaven the Lord looked down; He saw all the children of men. From the place of His dwelling, He gazed toward all the inhabitants of the earth. He who fashions their hearts together, who observes all their deeds.

**Do not be.** Do not be like the horse and the mule who lack understanding, and do not know or go unless they are guided <note>The commentator contrasts animal instinct with human reason</note>. And with a bit and bridle, their finery is used to restrain them, so they do not come near to you to support you. You should not lack understanding or wisdom, only to be rebuked by words that require no action to prevent evil. But as for the horse, do not be so, failing to understand or be wise. For your sakes, the wicked and powerful. He mentions the horse and the mule because they are like riders and they trample the property... and every place it happens, you said from the place a word exists, and all this is for the mouth to rest from being... and it is a vessel used for the mouth... and not what is sheltered... <unclear>illegible</unclear>. **Finery.** Like the preparation of an army. **Many are the sorrows of the wicked.** He who trusts shall have mercy, not like one who is in his sins and his possessions. There are those who are removed from them. But if he trusts in God, his shield will be his support and they will grant him mercy for his errors. And the foundation is that good and evil are from God!

**Rejoice in the Lord and be glad.** Whoever takes refuge in Him shall rejoice greatly... and they shall not be ashamed in the pit. **Sing for joy.** All whose hearts are upright.

## Praise
**O righteous ones in the Lord.** In the knowledge of all. And so it is a fitting praise. For you seek the words given to many to be right and to be strengthened in Him. We have not seen for Babylon a precious lip... <note>original: *Sfat Yakar*</note> in which there is grace to enlighten in the holy spirit. From the beginning, He inclined and gave knowledge and wisdom, the precise knowledge that is not just a voice... and he who awakens and rests for the sake of the One who acts in all. And it is possible that there are those who are poor... and every house of seeking... and its writing **Sing for Joy** this language is doubled three times. And it appears that He is the one who explains alone in the final comfort... and this is the investigation of the internal... He is the one who seals and the founders in their deeds in God. And in the shaking of his hand... and all the words of the Psalms are not for lower knowledge.

**Give thanks to the Lord with the lyre.** For with the lyre, the soul is awakened to joy and strong song. **With the ten-stringed lute sing to Him.** For the *Asor* <term>Ten-stringed instrument</term> and the lute... and so also the five melodies... and the *Asor* is a musical instrument that has ten strings, therefore it is called *Asor* <note>from the Hebrew word *Esser*, meaning ten</note>. **Sing to Him a new song.** Sing to Him a song that is renewed. **Play skillfully.** With the hand of the musicians to prepare for Him. **For upright.** The decrees of God and His judgments and everything is in faithfulness, with no deviation. Just as Moses our teacher said. This is the foundation... and there is a revelation from the Great God... and what He does in faithfulness is in this. And like the grace of this and the goodness of the soul... upon the evil like the good... and the Lord is the one who was before...

**He loves righteousness and justice.** He watches over His world, for without righteousness there is no justice. The *Chessed* <term>Lovingkindness/Grace</term> is what helps. The earth is full of the Lord's *Chessed* because God is the one who does justice and righteousness in the land. For these things please Me. **By the word of the Lord the heavens were made.** And the spirit placed in the soul in the spirits... as the people of the Lord... and this God is very good. And behold the heavens and all their host were made by His word... and they are the "Host" because they have life... **He gathers.** Like a heap <note>Hebrew: *Ned*</note>. And it means a container of great waters... for if not for this, there would be no dry land but only water. But when He gathered the sea... as it is written that the sea surrounds the earth and its understanding... and so it appears in the waters of the heavens that lean over all the earth... and it was by the permission of the Lord.

**Let all the earth fear.** Since it is so, it is fitting that all the earth fear the Lord, for He established the place of habitation. **The Lord frustrates the counsel of nations.** He said that He created the world and everything is in His hand, and no one has the power to change the building of what is established. For He created it and it stands, and no one can cancel His decrees... and this is the uniqueness of the Creator to act on His thoughts... even if all the nations were of one counsel and one wisdom, the Lord would frustrate their counsel. **Happy is the nation.** Because the water in these external things... the simple and hidden... He who sees into the hearts... as it is said, "And you shall know the Lord your God," for He is the one who grants you power to act. And he said that the servants of the Lord... and he said in our singing his greatness will pursue... This matter does not happen by chance, and so all the blessings and curses testify... it was known that it is from Him.

**From heaven He looks.** This is the knowledge... not for the sake of vanity or false words... **From the place of His habitation.** The good place He mentioned... for He knows all their deeds. **He who fashions.** Like "looking." For who can fashion the heart of man but God? He understands all their deeds... all of them are known and revealed to Him in their connections.

<header>Psalms</header>

The Lord is near to the brokenhearted, and he saves those crushed in spirit. Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but from them all, the Lord rescues him. He protects all his bones; not one of them is broken. Evil brings death to the wicked, and those who hate the righteous will be held guilty. The Lord redeems the soul of His servants, and all who take refuge in Him will not be held guilty.

## 35
## Of David

Contend, O Lord, with those who contend with me; fight against those who fight against me. Take hold of shield and buckler, and rise up in my help. Draw the spear and the javelin against my pursuers; say to my soul, "I am your salvation." Let those who seek my life be shamed and disgraced; let those who plot my ruin be turned back and confounded. Let them be like chaff before the wind, with the angel of the Lord driving them away. Let their way be dark and slippery, with the angel of the Lord pursuing them. For without cause they hid their net for me in a pit; without cause they dug a pit for my soul. Let destruction come upon him unawares, and let the net he hid entangle him; into that very destruction let him fall. Then my soul will rejoice in the Lord, exulting in His salvation. All my bones shall say, "Lord, who is like You? Rescuing the poor from one stronger than he, the poor and needy from one who robs him." Malicious witnesses <term>Hebrew: 'edei chamas' — witnesses of violence or false testimony</term> rise up; they ask me of things I do not know. They repay me evil for good, seeking the bereavement of my soul. But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth; I afflicted my soul with fasting, and my prayer shall return to my own bosom. I went about as though for a friend or a brother; like one mourning for a mother, I bowed down in gloom.

<column-break/>

The Lord is near to those with broken hearts, and those humble in spirit He will redeem. Many evils reach the righteous, and from them all the Lord delivers him. He guards all their limbs; not one of them is broken. The death of the wicked is evil, and the haters of the righteous will be found guilty. The Lord redeems the soul of His servants, and all who hope in His Word <note>Aramaic: 'Memreih' — the Word or Divine Presence, a common Targumic substitution for God’s direct action</note> shall not be found guilty.

**Of David.** Contend, O Lord, with those who contend with me; fight against the masters of my wars. Take hold of the buckler and the round shield, and stand up in my assistance. And draw the spear and the axe to meet those who pursue me; say to my soul, "I am your redemption." Let those who seek my soul be shamed and humiliated; let those who think of my harm be turned back and humbled. Let them be like chaff before the whirlwind, with the angel of the Lord driving them. Let their way be dark and slippery, with the angel of the Lord pursuing them. For for no reason they hid a pit of their trap; for no reason they dug for my soul. Let confusion come upon him that he does not know, and let the trap that he spread catch him; in turmoil let him fall into it. And my soul will rejoice in the Word of the Lord, exulting in His redemption. All the limbs shall rejoice, saying, "Lord, who is like You? Delivering the poor from one stronger than him, and the poor and darkened from the one who oppresses him." Witnesses of plunder stand up; they ask me of what I do not know. They pay me back evil instead of good, seeking to bring bereavement to my soul. And I, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth; I afflicted my soul with fasting, and my prayer returns to my bosom. Like a friend, like a brother, like a mourner who mourns for his mother, I went about bowed down. <gloss>And written</gloss>

---

**The Lord is near.** He is near to hear their cry and their prayer. **And He saves those crushed in spirit.** A repetition of the theme in different words. **Many are the afflictions.** For many times evil comes upon the righteous for his benefit, to show his righteousness in the righteousness of life, for his heart does not fear the coming of any of the mentioned evils. **And from them all the Lord rescues him.** And from every stumbling block in any of them, He brings a healing, and all the strength of the righteous is for his good even when they are entangled in evil. **He protects all his bones.** Because the bones are the supports of the body and its foundation. **Broken.** This is in the reflexive form <term>Hebrew: 'itpa'el'</term>. The text emphasizes "not one" to teach that while all his bones might suffer afflictions, a great healing will come to the broken among them for the sake of the life of the whole. It is not possible that they should be permanently separated by fracture or injury. **Evil brings death to the wicked.** The death of the wicked is caused by the evil of their deeds; "death" <term>Hebrew: 'temutat'</term> is derived from the word for dying. **The Lord redeems the soul of His servants.** Redemption of the soul comes to them from the recompense of judgment and from every evil and trouble. In the trust of the Lord’s holiness they shall trust, and all who take refuge in Him will not be held guilty, because they took refuge in the One whose action and power can save them.

## Of David
**Contend, O Lord, with those who contend with me.** This psalm was also said regarding his flight from Saul. <note>David frequently fled from King Saul, and many Psalms are traditionally attributed to these periods of distress.</note> **Contend** <term>Hebrew: 'Ribah'</term> comes from the same root as "my contenders" <term>Hebrew: 'merivai'</term>. **Fight against those who fight against me.** A repetition of the idea in different words. **My contenders.** The 'yod' is additional, similar to the word for weapons of war. **Take hold.** Meaning to strengthen with might and power. **Draw the spear and the javelin.** To empty the spear for battle. Some explain "Sogor" as a specific weapon used by kings. **I am your salvation.** Let my soul know this. **Let those who seek my life be shamed.** This refers to the shame of sudden disgrace. **Let them be turned back and confounded.** The verse teaches that they will retreat despite their wisdom. **Let them be like chaff.** Like the fine dust of straw that the wind drives away. **The angel of the Lord driving them.** This refers to divine assistance that stands against them. **Their way be dark and slippery.** This is a double evil, for they stumble in the dark. **Without cause they hid their net.** For David had done no violence, yet they set traps for him as one does for wild animals in the field with pits and nets. **Let destruction come upon him.** The word for destruction <term>Hebrew: 'shoah'</term> implies a sudden, chaotic ruin. **All my bones shall say.** The joy of the heart will rise and strengthen until it permeates the very bones. Some explain "pit" <term>Hebrew: 'shachat'</term> as related to death. **Lord, who is like You.** No one can match His power. **Rescuing the poor from one stronger than he.** This refers to God saving the weak from the mighty. The great Sage **Rabbi Bahya** and the great Rabbi **Moshe son of Maimon** <note>Maimonides (Rambam)</note> explained this concept—that the "bones" here represent the entire structure of the body which joins in the power of prayer and purity. **Malicious witnesses.** These are people who testify falsely to seize property or cause harm. **They repay me evil for good.** I did them good, and they repaid me with harm. **Bereavement of my soul.** This thing is like death to my soul, seeking to take my life through their false claims. **But as for me, when they were sick.** I showed them kindness even when they were my enemies; I wore sackcloth and fasted for their recovery. **My prayer shall return to my own bosom.** Meaning, the good I sought for them was sincere and heartfelt, even if they did not deserve it. **Like one mourning for a mother.** Because a person mourns for their mother more than for others. I went about in gloom <term>Hebrew: 'koder'</term>, which means his face was darkened with grief. <gloss>And written</gloss>

->### Psalms<-

In my distress they rejoiced and gathered together; the wicked who strike me with their words <note>This Aramaic translation (Targum) interprets the Hebrew "stricken ones" as those who attack with speech.</note> assembled against me, and those who are not wise who triumphed over me did not cease. They sharpen their words against me like lines of writing and fly about. They clap their hands at me in their weeping; O You, the Trustworthy One, You see! Restore my soul from their desolation, my soul from the young lions. I will thank You in the great assembly; among a mighty people I will praise You. Let not those who are my enemies for no reason rejoice over me, nor those who hate me without cause wink their eyes. For they do not speak peace; against the righteous of the earth and the quiet ones who are at rest in that world, they devise deceitful words. They opened their mouths wide against me and said, "Aha, aha! Our eyes have seen it." You have seen, O Lord; do not be silent! O Lord, do not be far from me. Bestir Yourself and awake for my justice, my God and my Master, for my cause. Judge me according to Your righteousness, O Lord my God, and let them not rejoice over me. Let them not say in their hearts, "Our soul is glad!" lest they say, "We have swallowed him up." Let them be ashamed and humbled together, those who rejoice at my harm; let them be clothed in shame and disgrace, those who magnify themselves against me. Let those who desire my vindication shout for joy and be glad; let them say continually, "Great is the glory of the Lord, who desires the peace of His servant." And my tongue shall meditate on Your righteousness, and all day long on Your praise.

The prophet said regarding the wicked man: in his wound within him, sin tells him that he will not find favor in his eyes <note>This is the Targum's interpretation of Psalm 36:1, suggesting that the drive to sin comes from an internal lack of fear of God.</note>. For it is smooth in his eyes to find iniquity, to hate instruction. The words of his mouth are wickedness and deceit; he has ceased to be wise and to do good. He plots wickedness upon his bed; he sets himself on a path that is not good; he does not reject evil. O Lord, Your kindness is in the heavens of heavens; Your faithfulness reaches to the skies.

---

### To the Chief Musician
**To the servant of the Lord.** Because he speaks of the wicked man's evil, these words are directed toward him. They deal with evil from its depths. Therefore, he says... for the voice of the cry of the wicked is far from... <note>The commentary here analyzes the psychology of the "servant of the Lord" (David) vs. the "wicked man."</note> **The utterance of transgression to the wicked.** Since it is said... that the transgression itself comes and speaks to the wicked man, telling him that there is no fear. Because... transgression is its name... **For it flatters him.** It smooths things over for him in his eyes and deceives him. And some say... that the evil he does is made to seem pleasant to him... **And in the midst of my heart there is no fear.** Because... his heart is a place for thoughts... to take instruction and to make his heart wise and to guard it. **He plots wickedness upon his bed.** Because the bed is a place for general thought... because the soul is settled in the body... and he says to it, "Good"... the world... the path is not good... and some explain that... there is no fear... in his bed... **Lord, in the heavens.** There is knowledge in the heavens... for in His light they will see light... and Your faithfulness... for faith is the life of the world... the righteous live forever. And the path of man... and Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains... life of the world... those who search for Him... and he said... it covers all His creatures. And furthermore, the life of the world... for those who are close to the life of the world... Therefore the water is more comforting than the salt... and every thought... because if the soul of a living being does not... the thought of the wicked man is lacking because...

<column-break/>

But at my stumbling they rejoiced and gathered; the stricken ones gathered against me, and I did not know; they tore and did not cease. With profane mockers for a cake <note>The Hebrew 'ma'og' is difficult; it likely refers to a circle of mockers or those who mock for a piece of bread.</note>, they gnashed their teeth at me. Lord, how long will You look on? Restore my soul from their destructions, my only one from the lions. I will give You thanks in a great congregation; I will praise You among a mighty people. Let not my enemies of falsehood rejoice over me; let not those who hate me without cause wink the eye. For they do not speak peace, but they devise deceitful words against the quiet ones of the land. They opened their mouth wide against me; they said, "Aha, aha, our eye has seen it!" You have seen, O Lord; do not be silent. O Lord, do not be far from me. Bestir Yourself and awake for my judgment, my God and my Lord, for my cause. Judge me according to Your righteousness, O Lord my God, and let them not rejoice over me. Let them not say in their hearts, "Aha, our soul!" Let them not say, "We have swallowed him up." Let those who rejoice at my harm be ashamed and confounded together; let those who magnify themselves against me be clothed with shame and dishonor. Let those who desire my vindication shout for joy and be glad, and let them say continually, "The Lord be magnified, who desires the peace of His servant." And my tongue shall meditate on Your righteousness, all the day on Your praise.

**To the Chief Musician, to the servant of the Lord, to David.**
Transgression speaks to the wicked in the midst of my heart: there is no fear of God before his eyes. For he flatters himself in his own eyes, until his iniquity is found and hated. The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit; he has ceased to be wise and to do good. He plots iniquity on his bed; he sets himself on a way that is not good; he does not abhor evil. O Lord, Your mercy is in the heavens; Your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.

---

<margin>gnashing</margin>
**But at my stumbling they rejoiced.** See how they compare to... they rejoiced and were glad and gathered against me... to tell about me and to plot one with another. **Stricken ones gathered against me and I did not know.** These are broken people. And so it says, "even the children of the base were driven out from the land." People who are low and broken from their sufferings. And "I did not know"—I did not know why they gathered against me... for I did them no harm. **They tore and did not cease.** "Tore" means the tearing of mocking, and they did not stop... like "and you tore your eyes with paint." Or they tore my flesh. And some explain that it refers to their evil thoughts... like a tailor who tears... **With profane mockers for a cake.** Bitterly mocking me... with words of mockery and foolishness... like "mockers for a cake" who are people of evil who delight in empty words. This is the meaning of "ma'og," which relates to "ugah" (cake/circle). Our Sages related this to... and these people join with mockers... like someone who makes a circle. And others say it refers to people who delight in the words of others while they themselves are idle... and like a "ma'og" (cake) on its embers. **They gnashed their teeth.** In their anger... to show their strength. **Lord, how long will You look on?** Until when will You see this with Your eyes... and the "maskilim" (wise ones) explain... **Restore my soul... my only one.** My soul is called "only one"... I will praise You in a great congregation... **Let them not rejoice over me.** Rejoice over my downfall... **Hate me without cause.** In their anger... those who are my enemies for no reason... **Wink the eye.** They wink their eye in mockery against me... it is the way of the wicked... or they signal with their feet... **For they do not speak peace.** Like "they do not speak for the sake of peace." **And against the quiet ones of the land.** All at once. Some explain "reg'ei" (quiet ones) as the poor who are broken... or those who dwell in hidden places... devising deceitful words. And it is correct that for their thoughts there is no... some explain "reg'ei eretz" as "moments of the land" (fleeing ones)... and it says... those who are at rest and quiet... and the explanation is... the humble and the afflicted... they plot deceitful words against me. **They opened their mouth wide against me.** In laughter and mockery... **They said, "Aha, aha, our eye has seen it!"** Meaning, our eyes have seen what we desired... "Aha" is an expression of joy... **You have seen, O Lord; do not be silent.** Do not be silent to the wicked... for You have seen the wickedness... awake for my judgment... for You are my God... **Judge me according to Your righteousness.** Take my judgment from them... for it is known to You... let them not rejoice further over me. **Let them not say in their heart... "we have swallowed him up."** Let them not say they have consumed me. **Let them be ashamed and confounded together.** Let those who gathered together to rejoice be ashamed together... **Let them shout for joy and be glad.** Those who desire my vindication. **The Lord be magnified, who desires the peace of His servant.** That is David, who asks for peace... **And my tongue shall meditate on Your righteousness.** They will speak of my peace... and I will always conduct myself in the way of the wise... as it says, "Let the Lord be magnified."

### Psalms

->**Aramaic Translation (Targum)**<-

Your righteousness is like the high mountains; Your judgments are deep as the great abyss; You save both human beings and beasts. How precious is Your kindness, O Lord! Human beings will find shelter in the shadow of Your <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>original: שכינתך (Shekhintekh); the Divine Presence manifested in the world</note> and they shall trust. They shall be saturated from the fatness of Your house, and from the stream of Your sweetness You give them to drink. For with You is the source of life, and in the light of Your eyes we see light. Extend Your goodness to those who know You, and Your righteousness to the upright in heart. Let not the foot of the arrogant come upon me, and let not the hand of the wicked cause us to wander. There the workers of falsehood have fallen; they are pushed down and shall not rise again.
**Of David:** Do not contend with the wicked to be like them, and do not be envious of the doers of injustice. For in their time, their labor is like straw; they shall be cut down like grass in haste, and like the green of the herb they shall wither. Trust in the <term>Memra</term> <note>original: מימרא (Memra); the Word of the Lord, used in Aramaic translations to avoid direct anthropomorphism of God</note> of the Lord and do good; dwell in the land and be strong in faith. Delight yourself in the Lord, and He will give you the requests of your heart. Reveal your ways to the Lord and hope in His Word, and He will act. And He will bring forth your righteousness like light, and your judgment like the noon sun. Be silent before the Lord and wait for Him; do not contend with one whose way prospers, with a man who carries out sinful advice. Refrain from anger and leave wrath; do not contend, only to do evil. ->Left<-

<column-break/>

->**Hebrew Source Text**<-

Your righteousness is like the mountains of God; Your judgments are a great deep; You save man and beast, O Lord.
How precious is Your kindness, O God! The children of men take refuge in the shadow of Your wings. They are saturated with the richness of Your house, and You give them drink from the river of Your delights. For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light do we see light.
<margin>Extend to those who know You</margin>
Extend Your kindness to those who know You, and Your righteousness to the upright in heart.
Let not the foot of pride come against me, and let not the hand of the wicked drive me away.
There the workers of iniquity have fallen; they are thrust down and cannot rise.
Of David: Do not fret because of evildoers, nor be envious of those who work unrighteousness.
<margin>They shall wither</margin>
For they shall soon be cut down like the grass, and wither as the green herb.
Trust in the Lord and do good; dwell in the land and feed on faithfulness.
Delight yourself in the Lord, and He will give you the desires of your heart.
Commit your way to the Lord; trust also in Him, and He shall bring it to pass.
<margin>And your judgment</margin>
And He shall bring forth your righteousness as the light, and your judgment as the noonday.
Rest in the Lord and wait patiently for Him; do not fret because of him who prospers in his way, because of the man who brings wicked devices to pass.
Cease from anger and forsake wrath; do not fret, it only leads to evildoing. ->Left<-

---

**Your righteousness is like the mountains of God.** The commentators differ: some say this refers to the high heavens from which God gives sustenance and provides for the inhabitants of the world. It means that the kindness of God is exceedingly great, reaching to the highest heights.
**How precious is Your kindness,** O God, and the children of men take refuge in the shadow of Your wings. They find mercy and lean upon Your kindness and compassion to shelter under Your wings, trusting in the shadow of Your grace; the preciousness of Your kindness is our very life.
**And it is even unto the heavens**, meaning from the earth up to the sky. For the kindness of the Lord is as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is His kindness toward those who fear Him.
**Your righteousness is like the mountains of God.** These are the high mountains; it is the linguistic custom to use "God" to describe something massive <note>as in "a great city to God"</note>. Just as the good water descends from the mountains to the valleys, so does the kindness of the Lord flow from the "mountain" of His righteousness. He says His kindness reaches the heavens and His righteousness is like the mountains, but "Your judgments are a great deep." This means that while He gives great righteousness to those who love Him, He deepens His judgment for those who are hated, reaching down to the great abyss. He humbles the wicked even as He exalts the righteous.
There is a teaching from Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri regarding "man and beast": God saves man because of his righteousness, but he saves the "beast" <note>referring here to the wicked who act without reason</note> because of His sheer mercy. Or, it refers to God providing for animals just as He provides for humans.
**Your kindness, O God.** This kindness is hidden for those who trust in Him in this world. But regarding the "World to Come," it says "they shall take refuge in the shadow." This kindness is more precious and honorable than anything in this world; it is the ultimate, enduring good. The word "How" <note>original: מה (Mah)</note> is used for emphasis, as in "How great is Your goodness which You have hidden for those who fear You!"
**They are saturated with the richness of Your house.** This refers entirely to the World to Come and the world of Wisdom. The "House of God" is the place of the soul's delight.
**For with You is the fountain of life.** This is the source from which the wise draw their understanding. Life in the World to Come is a life of constant flow, where we see "light within His light."
**Extend Your kindness.** As it is written, "I have extended My kindness to you." This refers to those who occupy themselves with wisdom in this world, that they may have a refuge from the affairs of the world and merit the "fruits" in the World to Come. "Those who know You" are the sages who exert themselves in the Torah and the wisdom of the Creator.
**Let not the foot of pride come upon me.** The psalmist prays that he should not be led into arrogance, which causes a person to stray from the depths of the heart.
**The hand of the wicked.** May they not have the power to move me from the path of the Holy Spirit.
**There they have fallen.** In the very place where they thought to rise in pride, they shall have a fall from which there is no rising. Unlike the righteous, of whom it is said "a righteous man falls seven times and rises," the wicked fall and cannot stand.
**Do not fret because of evildoers.** One should not be jealous of the success of the wicked, for it is temporary.
**Do not fret** <note>original: אל תתחר (Al tithar)</note> can also mean "do not join with them." For like grass they are quickly cut down. The "green herb" is something that looks lush but has no deep root; it withers in an instant.
**Trust in the Lord and do good.** Trust is the foundation. One should occupy himself with "faithfulness," which refers to the service of the heart. Dwell in the land and be nourished by faith.
**Delight yourself in the Lord.** If you make your primary delight the service of God, He will fulfill the desires of your heart, for your heart will desire only what is good.
**Commit your way to the Lord.** Cast your burdens upon Him and do not rely on other means, for He will act.
**He shall bring forth your righteousness as the light.** Your integrity will be visible to all, like the sun at noon, removing all doubt about your path.
**Rest in the Lord.** Be silent and wait until He answers you. Do not be envious of the man who prospers through "wicked devices," for his end is destruction.
**Cease from anger.** Do not let the success of the wicked bring you to rage, for anger is a negative trait that leads only to doing evil. Turn away from it and focus on the delight of God.

<summary>This page contains Psalm 36 and the beginning of Psalm 37, focusing on the contrast between God's infinite kindness and the fleeting success of the wicked. The commentary interprets the "mountains" and "deep" as metaphors for divine justice and explores the rewards of the World to Come.</summary>

### Psalms

<column-break/>

<margin>They shall inherit</margin>
For evildoers shall be cut off, but those who hope in the Lord—they shall inherit the land.
And in just a little while, the wicked will be no more; you will look closely at his place, and he will not be there.
But the humble shall inherit the land and delight themselves in an abundance of peace.
The wicked plots against the righteous and gnashes his teeth at him. The Lord laughs at him, for He sees that his day is coming.
The wicked have drawn the sword and bent their bow to bring down the poor and needy, to slaughter those whose way is upright.
<margin>Broken</margin>
Their sword shall enter their own heart, and their bows shall be broken.
Better is the little that the righteous man has than the abundance of many wicked people.
For the arms of the wicked shall be broken, but the Lord supports the righteous.
The Lord knows the days of the blameless, and their inheritance shall be forever.
They shall not be ashamed in a time of evil, and in the days of famine they shall be satisfied.
For the wicked shall perish, and the enemies of the Lord shall be like the glory of the pastures; they vanish—like smoke they vanish away.
The wicked borrows and does not repay, but the righteous is gracious and gives.
<margin>A man shall inherit</margin>
For those blessed by Him shall inherit the land, but those cursed by Him shall be cut off.
By the Lord the steps of a man are established, and He delights in his way.
Though he falls, he shall not be utterly cast down, for the Lord supports his hand.
<margin>From evil</margin>
I was young and now I am old, yet I have not seen a righteous man forsaken, nor his children begging for bread.
All day long he is gracious and lends, and his children are a blessing.
Turn away from evil and do good, and dwell forever.
For the Lord loves justice and will not forsake His pious ones; they are preserved forever, but the children of the wicked shall be cut off.

<column-break/>

For those who do evil shall be destroyed, but those who hope in the <term>Memra</term> <note>original: מימרא; the "Word" of God, a term used in Aramaic to avoid describing God in human terms</note> of the Lord—they shall inherit the land.
And in just a little while, there will be no wicked man; you will reflect upon his place, and he is gone.
And the humble shall inherit the land and take pleasure in the greatness of peace.
The wicked man thinks evil against the righteous and gnashes his teeth at him.
The Lord shall mock him, for He has seen that the day of his breaking has arrived.
The wicked have drawn the sword and stretched their bows to kill the poor and the lowly, to slaughter those who are upright in their path.
Their swords shall enter their own hearts, and their bows shall be broken. Better before the Lord is the small portion of a righteous man than the great wealth of many wicked people.
For the arms of the wicked shall be broken, and the <term>Memra</term> of the Lord supports the righteous.
The days of the perfect are known before the Lord, and their inheritance shall be forever.
They shall not be ashamed in an evil time, and in the days of famine they shall be satisfied.
For the wicked shall perish, and the enemies of the Lord shall be like the glory of the lambs <note>original: פלוסין; likely referring to the choice fat or the transient beauty of flowers in a field</note> which are consumed; they are finished and their end is to be consumed in the smoke of <term>Gehenna</term> <note>original: גיהנם; the place of spiritual punishment or purification</note>.
The wicked man borrows and does not pay, but the righteous man has mercy and gives.
For those blessed by His Word shall inherit the land, and those cursed by His Word shall be destroyed.
From before the Lord the steps of a man are prepared, and his path is desired. Though he falls into illness, he shall not die, for the Lord supports him with His hand.
I was a youth and have also grown old, and I have not seen a righteous man abandoned, nor his children seeking bread because of lack.
Because all day long he is compassionate and lends, his offspring are for a blessing.
Turn from evil and do good, and dwell in eternal life.
For the Lord loves justice and does not abandon His pious ones; they are guarded forever, but the children of the wicked shall be destroyed.

->**The Righteous**<-
<meta>Catchword: The Righteous (צדיקיא)</meta>

---

**For evildoers shall be cut off.** This means the complaints of the wicked will not be accepted because they will be cut off, and if you do not have strength now, stand firm after them. **They shall inherit the land.** Just as the matter of the wicked is judged according to their inheritance, those who hope in the Lord are the ones who truly inherit the land. **And in just a little while, the wicked will be no more.** Meaning, if you look closely at his place, you will see he is gone. It is certain that every person will eventually come to his designated place, and all will know it is from the Lord. <term>Nachmanides</term> <note>original: רמב"ן; Rabbi Moses ben Nachman, a 13th-century scholar</note> explained "And in just a little while, the wicked will be no more" as referring to the fact that the righteous are the true inheritors of the earth. **The wicked plots against the righteous.** Meaning, he thinks evil thoughts against him and seeks to kill him, as explained nearby. **And gnashes his teeth at him.** These are the evil actions; he thinks and plans to do harm to the righteous, and "gnashing" describes the sound of his suppressed rage. **The Lord laughs at him.** Meaning, the Holy One, Blessed be He, knows that his day of retribution is coming. **For He sees that his day is coming.** For when the day of payment is revealed, the wicked "open the sword." **The wicked have drawn the sword.** This means they bring their potential evil into action. Just as one draws a sword from its sheath to use it, they move their anger from thought to deed. Their "bow," representing their schemes, is "bent" so that the action does not fail. **Better is the little.** For what the righteous man achieves and succeeds with—the small amount that the Lord brings him in this world—is better and more praiseworthy than the abundance of the wicked. The wicked will not see peace, while the righteous man eats his small portion and lives a complete life. **The Lord knows the days of the blameless.** Meaning, the Lord recognizes the deeds of the righteous. This is a great source of faith for the righteous, as God testifies for them and supports their hand. Even if a righteous man worries that the wicked succeed with the little they have, **they shall not be ashamed** in a bad year or days of famine. **For the wicked shall perish... like the glory of the pastures.** The word "glory" here refers to temporary power which vanishes like smoke from a furnace, quickly dispersing. This is a metaphor for how their laughter and success suddenly vanish. **The wicked borrows and does not repay.** Because the Lord brings a sudden punishment upon them, and they find they have nothing with which to pay. **Though he falls, he shall not be utterly cast down.** If an accident occurs and the righteous man falls, he will not be totally rejected. He will live because of the reward and good that he is recognized for. This is like the concept of "grace" (<term>Chen</term>), which distinguishes the righteous from the wicked. When the wicked man falls, he is cut off with vengeance, but the righteous man is like a servant who falls but is shown mercy and raised up. **I have not seen a righteous man forsaken.** I have not seen him totally abandoned, nor his children begging for bread at doorways. Even if they face hardship, they are not reduced to hunger. **All day long he is gracious and lends.** This means throughout all his days, he gives according to his strength. Through this, his children become a blessing to the world. **Turn from evil and do good.** A person should distance themselves from the ways of the wicked, for the Lord rewards everyone according to their deeds. **For the Lord loves justice.** This is His kindness to all. The merit of the righteous protects their children. The righteous man is defined by his lack of arrogance and his dedication to justice. In general, "Turn from evil" includes all negative commandments ("thou shalt not"), and "do good" includes all positive commandments. One cannot simply avoid the path of evil without also performing good deeds. As it says: **the Lord loves justice.** One who acts with justice will not be forsaken by the Lord; he will not suffer lack and will not be ashamed. Unlike the wicked, who is cut off along with his children, the righteous man's lineage will endure.
