### Psalms

<column-break/>

<margin>They shall inherit</margin>
The righteous shall inherit the earth and dwell upon it forever. The mouth of the righteous meditates on wisdom, and his tongue speaks justice. The law of his God is in his heart; his steps shall not tremble. The wicked watches for the righteous and seeks to kill him. The Lord will not leave him in his hand, nor will He find him guilty when he is judged. Hope in the Word of the Lord and keep the way of strength, and He will exalt you to inherit the land; you shall see the destruction of the wicked. I have seen the wicked man powerful and strong like a rooted and leafy tree. But he passed from the world, and behold, he is not; I sought him, but he could not be found. Observe integrity and see uprightness, for the end of such a man is peace. But the rebellious shall be destroyed together; the end of the wicked is destruction. And the redemption of the righteous is from before the Lord; He is their strength in the time of distress. And the Lord shall help them and deliver them; He shall deliver them from the guilty and save them because they trusted in His Word.

->A song of praise for David, for remembrance:<-
The heavens shall shine upon Israel. O Lord, do not rebuke me in Your anger, and do not judge me in Your wrath. For Your arrows have descended upon me, and the stroke of Your hand has rested upon me. There is no healing in my body because of Your anger; there is no peace in my limbs because of my sin. For my sins have passed over my head; like a heavy burden, they are too heavy for me. My wounds have become foul and putrid because of my foolishness. I am bent and bowed down greatly; all day long I have walked in gloom. For my loins are filled with burning, and there is no healing in my body. I have grown faint and have been crushed greatly; I have groaned from the moaning of my heart. O Lord, all my desire is before You, and my sighing is not hidden from You. My heart palpitates, my strength has left me, and the light of my eyes—even they are no longer with me. My loved ones and my friends stand away from my plague, and my kinsmen stand far off.

<column-break/>

The righteous shall inherit the land and dwell forever upon it. The mouth of the righteous utters wisdom, and his tongue speaks justice. The law of his God is in his heart; his steps do not slip. The wicked watches for the righteous and seeks to put him to death. The Lord will not abandon him to his power or let him be condemned when he is brought to trial. Hope in the Lord and keep His way, and He will exalt you to inherit the land; you will look on when the wicked are cut off. I have seen a wicked, ruthless man, spreading himself like a leafy native tree. But he passed away, and behold, he was no more; though I sought him, he could not be found. Mark the blameless man and behold the upright, for there is a future for the man of peace. But transgressors shall be altogether destroyed; the future of the wicked shall be cut off. The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord; He is their stronghold in the time of trouble. The Lord helps them and delivers them; He delivers them from the wicked and saves them, because they take refuge in Him.

->A Psalm of David, for remembrance:<-
<margin>38</margin>
O Lord, rebuke me not in Your anger, nor discipline me in Your wrath! For Your arrows have sunk into me, and Your hand has come down on me. There is no soundness in my flesh because of Your indignation; there is no health in my bones because of my sin. For my iniquities have gone over my head; <margin>iniquities</margin> like a heavy burden, they are too heavy for me. My wounds stink and fester because of my foolishness. I am utterly bowed down and prostrate; all the day I go about mourning. For my sides are filled with burning, and there is no soundness <margin>bowed down</margin> in my flesh. I am feeble and utterly crushed; I groan because of the tumult of my heart. O Lord, all my longing is before You; my sighing is not hidden from You. My heart throbs; my strength fails me, and the light of my eyes— <margin>feeble</margin> even they have gone from me. My friends and companions stand aloof from my plague, and my nearest kin stand far off. <margin>and my kinsmen</margin>

---

**The righteous shall inherit the land.** As we have explained. **And dwell forever upon it.** This is repeated to emphasize that their existence and standing will be permanent. **The mouth of the righteous.** In addition to doing good, he speaks and directs others, for the primary benefit of all his wisdom is that he teaches others and guides them in the good path. **And his tongue speaks justice.** He teaches his wisdom regarding what is lawful and what is proper to do, so that honesty is directed toward one's fellow. **The law of his God.** Just as he teaches the way, so was it first in his heart; this is "the law of his God is in his heart." **His steps do not slip.** He does not falter or stray from the path of his feet. **The wicked watches.** The wicked person looks at the righteous man, seeking a pretext against him, watching his movements to find some matter to use as an accusation, according to the wicked man's own lack of integrity and his desire to see the righteous fall. **The Lord will not abandon him to his power.** No matter how much the wicked man schemes against the righteous, the Lord will not leave him in his hand. **Nor will He find him guilty when he is judged.** Even if the wicked man brings false charges, the Lord will not let him be condemned, and the wickedness of the accuser will be overturned. **Hope in the Lord.** Even when hearing rebuke, one should hope in Him and not turn away, for He will exalt you to inherit the land when the wicked are destroyed. The wicked have no permanence in the land. **I have seen the wicked.** In his own eyes, the wicked man is "ruthless," strong, and advancing. **Spreading himself like a leafy native tree.** Meaning he grows strong like a lush, healthy tree. **But he passed away, and behold, he was no more.** Despite his former beauty and strength, he vanished. I looked for him, but in a very short time, he had passed. **Though I sought him, he could not be found.** His memory was so completely gone that he could not be found. **Mark the blameless.** Observe the man of integrity and the upright, for their "end" <note>Hebrew: acharit, meaning future or final outcome</note> is peace. **But transgressors.** All sinners and wicked people are destroyed together. **The salvation.** Their salvation comes from the Lord, who is their stronghold in time of trouble. Therefore they trust in Him. **And the Lord helps them.** He helps them against the wicked and rescues them because they sought refuge in Him. This entire Psalm concludes by showing that the end of the wicked is evil, while the end of the righteous is good, leading to peace.

### Psalm
**Of David, for remembrance.** To tell that he intended to bring to mind one of his sins and his sufferings, as written in the fourth Psalm. Some explain "for remembrance" as a form of thanksgiving. In my opinion, David composed this Psalm to be used for prayer in times of distress, whether in private or in the synagogue, to inform everyone of the prayer he offered. **O Lord, rebuke me not in Your anger.** This is a request that even if discipline is necessary, it should not be done in "wrath" <note>Hebrew: chemah, implying a more intense, destructive fury</note>. **For Your arrows.** These refer to pains and illnesses. **Have sunk into me.** They have struck and entered deep within, like an arrow that enters the flesh. **And Your hand.** The weight of Your hand has come down upon me; the illness is described as the "hand" of God. **There is no soundness.** No wholeness or health. He says his body is consumed. **Soundness** <term>metom</term> refers to physical integrity. **There is no health in my bones.** Even in the bones, which are harder than flesh, there is no peace or health because of the "indignation" and "wrath" that have fallen upon me. **For my iniquities have gone over my head.** He compares his sins to a flood of water that has risen above his head, or a burden too heavy to carry. **My wounds stink.** From the infection and rot. These refer to the hidden blows that have now become visible as festering sores. **Because of my foolishness.** Because I did not keep the way of the Lord. **I am utterly bowed down.** From the magnitude of the pain, his posture is bent. **All the day I go about mourning.** This refers to the restlessness of his soul; he finds no repose. **For my loins are filled.** The "loins" <note>Hebrew: kesalim</note> are the areas near the kidneys and the base of the spine. He describes them as being filled with "burning" <term>nikleh</term>, meaning scorched or inflamed with disease. This adds to the description of his physical suffering. **I am feeble and utterly crushed.** I have lost all strength. **I groan because of the tumult of my heart.** I roar with pain, and my groaning comes from the internal pressure of my heart's distress. **O Lord, all my longing is before You.** My internal pain is not hidden from You. **My heart throbs.** My heart palpitates and is confused. **My strength fails me.** When the limbs are weakened, the strength fails. **The light of my eyes.** Even my intellectual vision and clarity have left me. **My friends and companions.** The Psalm notes that in his great suffering, his friends stayed away, being repulsed by his "plague" or fearing contagion. **My nearest kin stand far off.** He repeats the idea that those who should be close have distanced themselves.

->From upon me Your plague, from the camp of Your power, by Your hand I have been finished. With rebuke for sin You chastise a man, and You melt his desire like a moth; surely all flesh and the world are but vanity.<-
<meta>With rebuke</meta>

---

<margin>And they lay snares</margin>
**And they lay snares** • My lovers and my friends stand afar, and those who love [me] speak evil. The meaning of "they lay snares" (Hebrew: *vayanakeshu*) refers to his being struck. It is similar to the phrase "the snare and the stumbling block." The author explains that those who seek his life are mentioned without a connecting "and" to show the intensity of the situation. He felt as if he could not hear with his ears or open his mouth to respond. Even though he had the ability to speak, he chose silence as if he were truly mute, placing his hope entirely in the help of the Creator.

# TO THE LEADER
<margin>To the leader</margin>
**For Jeduthun, a Psalm of David:** This psalm was composed by David and arranged to be sung by Jeduthun the musician. Many commentators say the name is used literally. Perhaps, as the psalm recounts a story, it was given to him. Others say it refers to a specific musical instrument or a style of melody used for lamentation. The core of the psalm reflects the experience of one who hears those who speak against him but chooses to remain silent, directing his heart toward God instead.

<margin>I said</margin>
**I said, "I will guard my ways from sinning with my tongue":** I said in my heart when I thought of my distress, "I will guard my ways from sinning with my tongue." He meant that he would not complain against God's justice or speak harshly to his enemies. He describes his mouth as having a "muzzle," a strong metaphor for self-restraint while the wicked are present and prospering.

<margin>My heart was hot</margin>
**My heart was hot within me:** My heart was troubled and burning because I did not speak. When a person holds back their feelings, the internal pressure increases. He finally spoke, but not to his enemies; he spoke to God, asking for understanding about the shortness of life.

<margin>Make me know</margin>
**Lord, make me know my end:** He asks to understand how many days he has left. This is a request to understand the fragility of human existence. He compares his life to "handbreadths" (a very small measurement), emphasizing that in the grand scale of God's eternity, a human life is virtually nothing.

**Hear my prayer, O Lord, and give ear to my cry; do not be silent at my tears; for I am a stranger with You, a sojourner, as all my fathers were. Look away from me, that I may recover my strength, before I go and am no more.**

->**For the leader, a Psalm of David.**<-

**I waited patiently for the Lord; and He inclined to me, and heard my cry. He brought me up also out of a tumultuous pit, out of the miry clay; and He set my feet upon a rock, making my footsteps firm. And He has put a new song in my mouth, even praise to our God; many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the Lord. Happy is the man who makes the Lord his trust, and has not turned to the arrogant, nor to such as fall away to lies. Many things have You done, O Lord my God, even Your wonderful works, and Your thoughts toward us; there is none to be compared to You! If I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be numbered. Sacrifice and meal-offering You have no delight in; mine ears have You opened; burnt-offering and sin-offering have You not required. Then said I: "Lo, I am come; in the roll of the book it is written of me; I delight to do Your will, O my God; and Your law is in my inmost parts." I have preached righteousness in the great congregation; behold, I will not refrain my lips, O Lord, You know it. I have not hid Your righteousness within my heart; I have declared Your faithfulness and Your salvation; I have not concealed Your mercy and Your truth from the great assembly.**

**Accept my prayer, O Lord, and incline to my petition, and to my tears do not be silent, for I am a guest before You, a dweller like all my fathers. Cease from me and I shall rest before I go and am no more.**

->**For the conductor, by the hand of the Psalm of David.**<-

**Waiting, I waited for the Word <note>original: "Memra," a term used in Aramaic translations to refer to God’s manifest presence or speech</note> of the Lord; and He inclined to me and accepted my petition. And He brought me up from the pit of turmoil, from the sinking silt, and He established my feet upon a rock, making my steps firm. And He placed a new praise in my mouth, a hymn before our God; many shall see and fear, and they shall believe in the Word of the Lord. Blessed is the man who placed the Lord as his trust, and did not look toward the rebellious and those who speak lies. Many things have You done, O Lord my God, Your wonders and Your thoughts toward us; it is impossible to set them in order before You; I will tell and speak of them, they are too powerful to count. Sacrifice and offering You did not desire; ears You have opened for me; a fatling sacrifice for sin You did not ask. Then I said: "Behold, I have come; in the writing of the scroll it is written about me. To do Your will, my God, I have desired, and Your Torah is kept within my innards." I have brought news of merits in the great congregation; behold, my lips I will not withhold, O Lord, You know. Your merits I have not hidden within my heart; Your truth and Your redemption I have spoken; I have not concealed Your goodness and Your faithfulness in the great congregation.**

---
<columns>1</columns>

<margin>Hear</margin> **Hear my prayer.** See my acceptance and receive my prayer alongside my high standing; hear my acceptance. **For I am a stranger with You, a sojourner, as all my fathers were.** Similarly, David says in Chronicles <note>1 Chronicles 29:15</note>: "For we are strangers before You, and sojourners, as were all our fathers." The meaning is that a person in this world is like a stranger in a land that is not his; he stays for a time and needs the host to stand by him in his community. Likewise, the days are considered like a stranger in the land, for every day is on a journey away from it and will not return. It means to say: just as a pious person has pity on the stranger found in the city for all his needs, so too I trust in You, for You are pious <note>term: chasid — one who acts with loving-kindness</note> and our eyes are fixed on You in this world to strengthen our hands. According to our nature, as all our fathers, mercy and kindness are needed to strengthen the student of piety, to have pity on him... for in every generation a generation goes and a generation comes, and we are all like guests in this world by the will of the stranger in kindness and goodness. <margin>Look away</margin> **Look away from me.** This is to say: show Your face for peace and take Your eyes off my suffering for a little kindness during my fleeting days. It is like saying "loosen Your hand," for "look away from me" means "let Your anger turn away from me" so I may rest from turmoil and weakness before I go to do Your will. I recognized that the support of my hand was weakened by illness. Therefore, we wait to be finished with the loss and the healing before I go to the world <note>original: "cheled" — the transient world</note> according to the way of all the earth. For this world is the primary place of labor and action, while the World to Come is the primary place of standing. Our Sages, of blessed memory, said that the foundation of kindness is for human beings to perform deeds and acquire knowledge and wisdom in those allotted days in the world.

### For the leader
**I waited patiently for the Lord.** This entire psalm follows the theme of the end of the previous psalm; in it, he prays for redemption and against the wicked of the nations of the world who harm Israel. He calls them "arrogant" <note>Hebrew: "rahabim"</note>.

<margin>For the leader</margin> **I waited patiently for the Lord.** Just as I have waited for many days, He heard my cry. The double expression "waiting, I waited" <note>קוה קויתי</note> is like the command "Wait for the Lord; be strong and let your heart take courage" <note>Psalm 27:14</note>. It implies that God is close to Israel and the pious ones who trust in Him. **He brought me up also out of a tumultuous pit.** Meaning, from the distress of exile, which is compared to a pit of deep water, a "pit of noise" because of the clamor within it. Our Sages said that kingdoms are compared to roaring waters. Jonathan <note>referring to the Targum of Jonathan ben Uzziel</note> translated it as "a pit of turmoil," meaning the exile is like sinking sand. **Miry clay** refers to thick, wet mud. **And He set my feet upon a rock.** In contrast to the mud and clay, He strengthened my feet on a solid place. **Making my footsteps firm.** Meaning, I have now moved past the uneven tracks of the road, and He set my feet on a high and straight place where my standing is secure. This is the meaning of "the way of the Lord is a stronghold." The purpose of this kindness is to show that a person is obligated to thank God for every good thing, every miracle, and the acts of righteousness and mercy performed for him. **And He has put a new song in my mouth.** A great and new miracle will be renewed through which many shall see and fear the Lord. How good and pleasant it is to give a song of kindness to God. The miracle will be famous to all, and they will acknowledge Divine Providence and trust in Him always. **Happy is the man who makes the Lord his trust.** This is the greatest trust, which stands forever. **And has not turned to the arrogant.** Meaning, he has not turned his heart toward the "rahabim," who are idolaters. The pious man says: "Heaven forbid I should deny You and turn to the arrogant." These are the "seekers of lies," meaning those who deviate toward the path of falsehood, like sinners. **Many things have You done, O Lord my God.** Your kindnesses and goodness have increased toward us. When rest comes and the Lord is near, He shows us His miracles and wonders. Your thoughts toward us have no equal; the thoughts You have planned for us are many, and Your goodness is beyond our ability to recount or remember now. **Sacrifice and meal-offering You have no delight in.** At the time of the kindness of redemption, when the Temple stands, they will return to that service. But as Samuel said <note>1 Samuel 15:22</note>, "Does the Lord delight in burnt offerings as much as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice." **Mine ears have You opened.** You have opened my ears to Your voice to perform acts of kindness and commandments. You did not ask for burnt offerings and sin offerings, but rather for us to look toward Your Providence and piety. **Lo, I am come; in the roll of the book it is written of me.** This refers to the Scroll of the Torah. **I delight to do Your will... and Your law is in my inmost parts.** Your Torah and kindness are written upon my heart. I will fulfill everything written about me. "In my inmost parts" means in my very being; Your kindness and righteousness will always be in my heart. I have preached this righteousness to all nations. **I will not refrain my lips.** I will not withhold my lips from telling of Your will and Your righteousness. **I have not hid Your righteousness within my heart.** Just as I have committed myself before the Lord, I did not hide it out of fear, but rejoiced in Your mercy. I promised to tell of Your faithfulness and salvation. He repeats "in the great assembly" to emphasize that he taught these truths publicly, and that God’s goodness is established through those who trust in Him.

### For the leader, a Psalm of David. Happy 
is he who considers the poor; the Lord will deliver him in the day of evil. ### 42

### For the leader, a *Maskil* <note>A technical term for a contemplative or instructional poem</note> of the sons of Korah. 
As the deer pants for the water brooks, so my soul pants for You, O God.

---

**Your kindness:** Just as You have appointed Your kindness, so "Your kindness shall continually preserve me," like one speaking of his path. For Your kindness is always with me. "My iniquities have surrounded me": because they sinned. Just as they snatched what was around me, for they dreamed of me... [The commentator continues to analyze the grammatical roots of the words for "kindness," "mercy," and "iniquity" as they appear in the preceding verses.]

# For the leader
A Psalm of David. This psalm was also among the ancients, and some say that David composed it concerning his illness. **He who considers the poor.** This refers to the sick person. As in: "Why are you so haggard, O son of the king?" (2 Samuel 13:4). The "wise person" <note>maskil</note> is one who visits the sick and acts intelligently regarding the matters of the patient's illness and his voice in his suffering. **The Lord will deliver him in the day of evil.** Some explain: the day of the fever is the "evil" day. Others explain that the Lord will protect him, for the word "evil" here refers to a lingering sickness. It is possible to interpret these verses in this manner: that because they occupied themselves with the sick person... and his prayer is for the wise ones... David spoke these verses as words of support to comfort the sick. To tell him: "May God forgive your sins and strengthen your heart," for in the name of the Lord is his healing. **And he shall be blessed on the earth.** He shall be healed from the sickness and his life shall be blessed. **He will support him.** This refers to his resting place "on the bed of suffering." The Lord will support him on his bed, meaning He will give him strength to endure the pains of his illness. **You have overturned all his lying down in his illness.** This means You turn his bed of sickness into a place of rest, or that his illness is overturned into health. **I said: "Lord, be gracious to me."** David prays for healing, recognizing that physical suffering often stems from spiritual "sickness" or sin. **My enemies speak evil.** He returns to the words of the one speaking in his illness. The enemies hope the sick man will die so his name might perish. **And if he comes to see.** If an enemy comes to visit the sick person, he speaks falsely. His heart is not with the sufferer; instead, he gathers "iniquity," looking for signs of impending death so he can go out and spread rumors. **Whisper together.** When the evil visitor leaves, he joins others to whisper about the patient's condition. **A base thing is poured into him.** They say a "thing of Belial" (a curse or terminal illness) is poured into him like molten metal, so he will never rise again. **Even my close friend.** This is the height of betrayal: someone David trusted and fed has turned against him, "lifting his heel" to kick him while he is down. **But You, Lord... raise me up.** David asks to be raised from his sickbed so he can "repay them," perhaps by showing them that God has not abandoned him. **And as for me, in my integrity.** Because I have been wholehearted with You, You have supported me. **Blessed be the Lord.** This is the concluding blessing of the first of the five books of Psalms. **Amen and Amen.** A double confirmation of the blessing. "Amen" implies truth and permanence. 

The first book is completed.

# For the Chief Musician
<margin>800</margin>
**A Maskil of the sons of Korah.** The sons of Korah were inspired to return, pray, and strengthen themselves. It is said that they composed this psalm through the Holy Spirit and David recorded it in his book. Likewise, the psalm before it is a *Maskil* of the sons of Korah, like a prayer-script for Moses. It is for comfort and to say that those who were outside felt the matters of the heart most strongly in this psalm. Some say the meaning of "for the sons of Korah" is for them to repeat. But there is no sense to that interpretation. <margin>T</margin> **As the deer longs.** This is the general theme of the psalm, and it does not single out any one person but represents the pleasant song. And also for our Rabbis, this psalm was said by them regarding the lack of the Temple, which has been destroyed for a long time. Furthermore, one might ask why it was not attributed to the singer but attributed to Korah. Some say that a portion of the psalm was composed by Korah and written for the sons of Korah, the singers who were present in the Temple service. And because the sons of Korah were descendants of Korah, he attributed it to the "sons" in respect to their lineage. To say "to the sons of Korah" refers to their role. This psalm is said by some to be a hidden measure between the divisions. And some say that it is a longing for the time of this exile. It is the voice of the examiner. It speaks in the singular because it includes every individual within the exile and the harsh time of the blows of exile from afar, do not draw near to it. It is for his glory upon him. And so it is said: **As the deer.** This refers to a bitter place of parched water from which one hopes for relief. Furthermore, because they seek the forest and the deer and look for wine. The meaning here is according to the longing of the one who seeks the mountain from a distance. Some say that they go like hunters to lure them; the heart goes and they merit from within until the deep water and the voice of the prayer; while they were tired and merited from him. It is interpreted as a metaphor for the soul that seeks and longs for its source, and it awakens and they begin to rise towards the water. As the deer longs for the water brooks. One might ask why "longs" (*ta’arog*) is in the feminine form, when the deer mentioned is male. It is common for nouns to be used interchangeably between masculine and feminine, such as "ox and donkey." Or perhaps the longing is a feminine trait and it is used descriptively here. **So my soul longs.** For they shall gather many together, my soul and my community. It says "longs" because it lacks the script of awakening more than the source. **Longs.** Comfort and the cry of the heart's prayer. Like a garden bed (*arugah*) that yields its fruit in its season. And all the springs of water are like the godly ones. And there are many like it. **My soul thirsts.** As if to say, it longs and desires for the place. To experience the sweetness of the words of the living God more than the physical thirst. For a person can survive without food for a day, but without water, one feels the immediate lack of life. Just as the wisdom of water is sought, so too the soul seeks the living God. From the depths of the heart more than from the visual sight of the water. **God.** It says this regarding the living God, because he mentions the parched land and the danger of lack of water. **When shall I come and see.** Like those who would go on the pilgrimage to the House of the Sanctuary. **My tears have been my food.** My constant companion. It is always with me by day and night, like your food. It says to me every day as the nations mock me. There are those who interpret the beginning of the exile: **When they say to me all day long.** Throughout the long exile, my enemies will say to me, "Where is your God?" and "Where is your Savior?" They mock the one who serves Him, saying that he will not return from exile. **These I remember.** In the gathering of the holiday, as I hope to return. **For I passed through the throng.** Before the tangles of exile, I would go in the beautiful processions. And so they intend the gathering. And they would prepare. And so it was for me to be comforted, and my mouth said "for I passed through the throng." For I would say to myself: when will I return to see Your face? For You have ceased and did not turn Your face to Your chosen ones, and we were with the voice of song and thanks. It is the teacher of my hand, saying the company of the Lord is in the assembly. **A multitude keeping the festival.** All the multitude, the sound of the celebration. For in their writing they were the holy vessels on the holiday. It was a celebration from the many ways. And so a celebration of the heart and soul. **Why are you bowed down.** He returns to his soul after praising it by remembering its past, and the soul is now desolate and grieving. And he says again: **Why are you bowed down.** And the interpretation is: wait for my God. **The salvation of His presence.** By the salvation of His presence. As if to say, yet before these things my life was filled with hope and I waited for the salvation. The interpretation of "salvations of his face" is like the king who bestows honor. **My God, within me.** For all that is desolate. Therefore I remember You. Meaning, because these things are upon me and I am grieving, I remember You from the land of Jordan, from the mountains of the Sanctuary. And so he mentions the Jordan and its surrounding at the mountain of Hermon. And so **From the mountain of Mizar.** A small mountain near where he was. For Mount Hermon is from the Jordan and the heights, and Mizar is not its name. But it is a descriptor of the Jordan. And he remembers the divine command from the heights and the day he was on the mountain. **Deep calls to deep.** This hints at the troubles of the exile and the bitterness, like the waters that rise and rage. And so in many places in the Scripture. It says as the motion of the death of the day passes, and the life of the sea is now in exile passing over me. The depths of one deep call to another, as if the troubles call to one another to come. And also **At the sound of Your waterfalls.** Meaning, my soul opens to the sound of Your channels. Meaning, thus the breaks have come upon us as the water flows from the channel and returns the sound. And there is an interpretation that the clouds bring down the rain according to the drawing of the water. And he refers to the troubles. And so **All Your breakers and Your waves.** My breakers and my waves have passed over me. The troubles have passed over us. And also "Your breakers and Your waves" because You brought them upon us for our sins. **By day the Lord will command His lovingkindness.** It is interpreted that a person should not say that because the light of day departs, the person is left without his kindness. Even when one walks in the way and all who walk in the way are arranged and filled with the Blessed God. And it would be said for every individual: **A prayer to the God of my life.** Some interpret that the verse is a comfort for the one who is despondent. For he will yet merit His kindness in his days, and if he is despondent from the rule of the sea and the exiles compared to the night, his soul should not turn from the rest, for he will yet merit His kindness and He will save us. **And in the night His song is with me.** And while we are in the night of the exile, His song will be with me to the Blessed One for all the kindnesses He has done with our ancestors and what He does every day with us in exile. And furthermore, **A prayer to the God of my life.** As if to say, in my prayer to the God of my life, He will save us until the end of the exile and we will see His comfort and His kindness as our ancestors did. **I will say to God, my Rock.** From the depths of the Sanctuary, my Rock and my Fortress from the time of the enemy; why am I forgotten now in exile and going in darkness under the pressure of the enemy who sends me into exile? **Why have You forgotten me.** And the meaning is: You have left me and abandoned me and hidden from me. **As with a crushing.** Like a killing sword in my bones. While they say to my soul, where is your God? If Your God is for you, how are you in exile? And this reproach is in my heart like one who stabs him with a sword and destroys him. And this is in my bones because it is the strength of the body. From the spirit of the Lord is what will return my soul from its desolation. **Why are you bowed down.** He returns to comfort his soul after asking "why have You forgotten me." He says: why should I be despondent? Wait for the Lord, for yet etc. my God. And this psalm is regarding the few who will be there and it is interpreted by the mouth. As if to say, the mouth that saves my presence and my strength. My intentions are overall that He is my God. May His presence be before me and out of the depth of my heart I will build a house where my salvation will rest. **And my God.** And this shall be my God at the day of salvation and this will be for me yet another reason to praise.

# Judge Me
<margin>Psalm 43</margin>
**God, and plead my cause.** In this book, this psalm is the prayer of the children of the exile. **Judge me.** Take my vengeance and my judgment from my enemies. **And plead my cause.** For I have no one to argue my case. **Against an ungodly nation.** For the exile is under the authority of an ungodly nation, and I would say this even if I did not know the specific sin. **And from the deceitful and unjust man.** Because while in exile under the rule of all, if he is a man of kindness, he is not from the people who keep these laws, for all have gathered against me and they seek to destroy me. This is my prayer. **For You are the God of my strength.** In this he takes refuge. To say that God is my strength and my fortress and he strengthens me now in exile. **Why have You cast me off.** Why have You distanced me? The letter *resh* is weak, but the *lamed* is doubled <note>Grammatical note on the Hebrew word *me-’ol*</note> because of the length...

</margin>

**Awake!** This is like one who says: "Wake up for us and bring relief to our exile." It is like one who is in distress and cannot be silent. This is the plea that comes from the many hardships that have overtaken us, saying: "Do not abandon us forever." **Why do You hide Your face?** Like a person who turns his face away from seeing a sword. See our vision and our proof; see our affliction. Our strength has failed; the sword shall be in our hearts like a thorn. **For our soul is bowed down.** That is to say, we are brought low to the point of death, for our soul is bowed even to the dust. This means we are close to descending into the pit. **Our body cleaves to the earth.** For one who is exhausted leans on his hands, and if he slips, his face hits the ground; thus, he "cleaves to the earth." **Arise.** This is stressed on the first syllable. **Help us.** This is like saying "for our help." **For the sake of Your kindness.** Act graciously toward us among the nations that have escaped for Your name's sake; do it for the sake of Your kindness.

## For the Conductor
**On the Lilies.** This refers to a musical instrument. Some explain that this Psalm is about the King Messiah. The phrase "A Song of Loves" means a song that is beloved to all. **My heart is stirred.** My heart is improved. From the ways of our Rabbis (of blessed memory), they saw this Psalm as a prophecy. The "swift scribe" refers to one who moves quickly as soon as speech is heard. Therefore, this saying refers to the stirring of the heart because it speaks almost through the mouth, though you are in hiding. The heart is the source of words, just as a fountain is the source of water. The Psalmist is praised for the conversation of his speech, for the words flowed from his heart regarding the King Messiah—good words. **I address my verses to the King.** Meaning, I do not speak with my lips alone, but my actions are dedicated to the King. **My tongue is the pen of a swift scribe.** My tongue speaks of him with speed, like the pen of a scribe who writes with a focused heart. **You are more handsome.** This form of the word <note>Original Hebrew: *Yafyafita*</note> is a doubling used for emphasis, as in "very beautiful." He says that this king is much more beautiful than any other human being. When you speak, your words have grace, as if grace itself was poured upon your lips. **Therefore God has blessed you forever.** Because you find favor in the eyes of all, and this is a divine blessing. **Gird your sword.** There are swords used for protection, and he says: "Gird your sword and place it upon your thigh." **In your glory and your majesty.** This means your sword shall be your glory. **And in your majesty, prosper and ride.** This refers to the beginning of his kingdom and the battles he will fight. Our Rabbis (of blessed memory) interpreted this verse as referring to the words of Torah—the "war of Torah." However, the plain meaning remains the primary interpretation. Ride for the sake of truth and humility. **And let your right hand teach you.** Your right hand will show you fearful and wondrous things. **Your arrows are sharp.** They are ready, and your eyes shall not be closed. **In the heart of the King’s enemies.** They shall fall into the hearts of the enemies until all the nations beneath you fall. **Your throne, O God.** Some explain that your throne shall be established by God. Like the verse "and Solomon sat on the throne of the Lord" <note>1 Chronicles 29:23</note>. Because your scepter is a scepter of equity, therefore your throne shall be forever. **You loved righteousness.** Because the whole world is sustained by it. **The oil of gladness.** This means that God has chosen you and anointed you more than your companions, for you are the supreme king. **Myrrh and aloes and cassia.** These are types of spices. The verse says that all your garments have a good scent, as if they were made of these spices from the ivory palaces. **Out of ivory palaces.** This is a poetic way of saying your houses are filled with the scent of luxury. **Daughters of kings are among your favorites.** This means the noble women of your court will be the daughters of kings, for every king will desire to give his daughter to you. **At your right hand stands the queen.** The queen stands in the place of greatest honor, adorned in the gold of Ophir. This is a metaphor for the Assembly of Israel <note>Original: *Knesset Yisrael*</note>. **Hear, O daughter.** He addresses each of the daughters of kings who come to him, telling them to forget their former homes and father's house. **So shall the King desire your beauty.** For he is your Lord. **The daughter of Tyre.** This means the congregation of Tyre. They shall bring gifts. **All glorious is the King’s daughter within.** This means the king's daughter who stands inside is honored, and her clothing is woven with gold. **In embroidered work she shall be led.** She is brought to the king in beautiful garments. These verses are metaphors for the nations who will accept the faith of Israel and the rule of the Messiah.

My heart is stirred by a noble theme; I address my verses to the king; my tongue is the pen of a skillful writer.
You are the most handsome of the sons of men; grace has been poured upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.
Gird your sword on your side, O mighty warrior; clothe yourself with splendor and majesty.
In your majesty ride forth victoriously in the cause of truth, humility, and justice; let your right hand display awesome deeds.
Your sharp arrows pierce the hearts of the king’s enemies; the nations fall beneath your feet.
Your throne, O God, will last for ever and ever; a scepter of justice will be the scepter of your kingdom.
You love righteousness and hate wickedness; therefore God, your God, has set you above your companions by anointing you with the oil of joy.
All your robes are fragrant with myrrh and aloes and cassia; from palaces adorned with ivory the music of the strings makes you glad.
Daughters of kings are among your honored women; at your right hand stands the royal bride in gold of Ophir.
Listen, daughter, and pay attention: Forget your people and your father’s house.
Let the king be enthralled by your beauty; honor him, for he is your lord.
The city of Tyre will come with a gift; people of wealth will seek your favor.
All glorious is the princess within her chamber; her gown is interwoven with gold.
In embroidered garments she is led to the king; her virgin companions follow her and are brought to you.
Led in with joy and gladness, they enter the palace of the king.

My heart has brought forth a good word; I shall speak my works to the King; my tongue is like the pen of a swift scribe.
You are more beautiful, O King Messiah, than the children of men; the spirit of prophecy has been poured upon your lips, because of this the Lord has blessed you forever.
Gird your sword upon your thigh, O mighty one; your radiance and your splendor are great.
And your splendor is great! Prosper and ride upon the horse of the kingdom for the sake of truth, humility, and righteousness; and the Lord shall teach you to do awesome things with your right hand.
Your arrows are sharpened; the nations shall fall beneath you, even into the heart of the enemies of the King.
The throne of Your glory, O Lord, stands forever and ever; a righteous scepter is the scepter of Your kingdom.
You have loved righteousness and hated the guilty; therefore the Lord your God has anointed you with the oil of joy more than your companions.
Myrrh and aloes and cassia perfume all your garments; from the palaces of ivory they have gladdened you.
The daughters of kings come to meet your honor; the queen stands at your right hand, clothed in a crown of kingdom-gold, her garments adorned with gold of Ophir, sapphire, and pearls.
Listen, O Congregation of Israel, to the Torah of His mouth, and see your works are good; incline your ear to the words of the Torah and forget the evil deeds of the wicked of your people, and the house of idols where you served in the house of your fathers.
And the King shall desire your beauty, for He is your Master, and you shall prostrate yourself to Him.
And those who dwell in the fortress of Tyre shall bring an offering; the wealthy of the nations shall seek your face.
All the treasure of the daughters of kings who are gathered within is for the priests; their clothing is bedecked with much gold.
In embroidered garments they shall bring their offerings before the King of the world; and the rest of their companions who are scattered among the nations shall be brought in your joy to Jerusalem.
They shall be led with joy and dancing; they shall enter the palace of the King of the world.

I will perpetuate your memory through all generations; therefore the nations will praise you for ever and ever.

In place of your fathers shall be your righteous sons; you shall appoint them to be great leaders in all the land.
I will remember Your name in every generation; therefore the nations shall give thanks before You for ever and ever.

I will say of the buildings that the city of the Lord of Hosts, in the city of our God, is excellent and its buildings are strong... And to say further "in the city of our God," for it belongs to God and is protected from the miracles of the idolaters... and He will establish it forever. **We have meditated.** We thought in our hearts during the exile... for He is pious and of great kindness... He will desire us. And the Glory is within it in the Temple... This is the meaning of "we meditated"—they hoped and expected. As in "meditate until the sorrowful..." **As Your name, O God.** Just as Your name is in the mouth of the creatures who bless the future, so will it be today at the ends of the earth. For the seal of all... they will be praising and lauding Your name... **Let Mount Zion rejoice.** On the day of salvation, Mount Zion will rejoice, metaphorically. Like speaking of orphans... this refers to the stars of Mount Zion. **Let the daughters of Judah be glad.** The cities and villages surrounding Jerusalem. **Because of Your judgments.** Which brings death upon the stars <note>metaphor for powerful enemy nations</note> over Jerusalem. **Walk around Zion.** This speaks of the building of Zion and Jerusalem. Zion is the main part. It tells the nations to come around Zion... and count her towers, meaning to see her surroundings. **Set your hearts to her ramparts.** This is the small wall in front of the large surrounding wall. **Go through her palaces.** Meaning, see her heights... **So that you may tell it to a later generation.** Meaning the living generation, the final generation... the building and its palaces for the world to come. It was like a holy matter to have a resting place in our hearts... **For this is God.** Because He led him, and He is the great leader. **He will lead us even unto death.** Meaning until old age He will lead us with glory. And some say it means "eternally," from the concept of "world" <note>Olam</note>. And its meaning is like "hidden" <note>Almut</note>... as a heart considers it high. Like the "days of our youth," meaning as He led us previously with great joy... like "youthful beauty."

# To the Chief Musician
**A Psalm of the sons of Korah.** Concerning **This.** This Psalm is about the matter of this world and the world to come. Therefore it addresses "all you nations and all you inhabitants of the world"—anyone who desires the good path that brings life despite death. **Both low.** Those of low degree. **And high.** The great ones. Like Gideon... and the sons of the nations and the middle class, all should hear, for wisdom does not distinguish. **My mouth shall speak.** Wisdoms and understandings... my heart spoke... a language of teaching. To speak by way of parable and riddle. For this Psalm is a path of taking... and since the Psalms were played with a harp... **To open my riddle on the harp.** Meaning, why... as the musician... and so "to open with a harp."

->Why should I fear<-

Why should I fear in the days of evil, when the iniquity of my heels <note>original: "akevai"; often interpreted as one's final days or the sins of one's youth that "follow at the heels"</note> surrounds me? Those who trust in their wealth and boast in the abundance of their riches: A brother cannot redeem a man, nor give to God his ransom. For the redemption of their soul is precious, and it ceases forever: That he should live on eternally and not see the pit. For he sees that wise men die; together the fool and the boor perish, and they leave their wealth to others. Their inward thought is that their houses are forever, their dwellings to all generations; they call their lands by their own names. But man in honor does not abide; he is likened to the beasts that perish. This is their way, their folly; yet their followers approve their speech. Selah <note>A musical or liturgical pause for emphasis</note>. Like sheep they are set for Sheol <note>The biblical underworld or the grave</note>; death shall shepherd them; and the upright shall rule over them in the morning; and their form shall waste away in Sheol, far from its dwelling. But God will redeem my soul from the power of Sheol, for He will take me. Selah. Be not afraid when a man becomes rich, when the glory of his house increases. For when he dies, he shall carry nothing away; his glory shall not descend after him. Though while he lived he blessed his soul—and people will praise you when you do well for yourself—it shall come to the generation of his fathers; they shall never see light. Man that is in honor, and understands not, is likened to the beasts that perish.

<column-break/>

The path is faulty in the days when evil foundations surround my end, because of the distance of my transgressions; and it is a debt for those who trust in their property and boast in the greatness of their riches. His brother, who is found, will not truly redeem a man with his property, nor give to God his ransom: For the value of the redemption of their souls is precious, and their wickedness and redemption shall cease forever. But he shall live again for eternal life and not see the judgment of Gehenna <note>original: "Gehinnam"; the place of afterlife punishment or purification</note>. For the wise see the wicked who die together; fools and those who wander will perish and leave their possessions to the righteous. The children of their graves shall remain forever, and they shall not rise from their dwellings for all generations, because they were arrogant and built houses named for themselves upon the earth. But a wicked man in honor will not dwell with the righteous; he is compared to the beasts that are slaughtered. This, their way, causes folly for them; and in their end, they will recount their transgressions in the world to come. Like sheep they place the righteous toward death, and the righteous shall slay them; the path of the weary will pass away, and their bodies shall wear away in Gehenna because they stretched out their hands and destroyed the dwelling place of His Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"; the Divine Presence</note>. David said in the spirit of prophecy: Truly God will redeem my soul from the judgment of Gehenna, for He will teach me His way forever.

---

->G<-

Concerning Korah <note>The leader of a biblical rebellion, whose sons are attributed with writing these Psalms</note> and his followers, he prophesied and said: Do not fear when Korah, the man of strife, becomes wealthy, for the honor of his house shall increase. For in his death he shall not take everything; his honor shall not descend after him. Because his soul, which he taught during his life, shall bless you; and the righteous will praise you when you do good for your soul. You shall enter the generation of the righteous, until the generation of their fathers; but the wicked shall not see light for all eternity. A guilty man who is in honor and does not understand—and in the contemplation of his honor he is forgotten—is likened to the beasts and the slaughter that is prepared.
Praise.

---

**Why should I fear in the days of evil.** Now he begins with words of parable and riddle. Why, why should you fear and tremble? The "days of evil" refer to the days of this world, for they are days of evil for anyone who busies himself with it. And why should one fear the strength of discipline? And concerning the end of them, the "honor" of this world? For he is concerned about the debts of this world—"my heels surround me." That is to say, they surround me as I pursue the goodness of this world. "My heels" means at my end <note>The heel being the lowest/last part of the body represents the end of life or the final consequences of actions</note>. Just as the heel is the end of the whole body, the end of every matter is called the "heel." Those who live according to the "heel" of the world, everything is based on the corruption of nature and the reward that stands at the end of the deed. Because one who is immersed in the goodness of this world all the days of his life, it will be dead to him in the World to Come, which is after death. That is his "heel," the end of the deed. For this world is a world of loss and abandonment. "Iniquity surrounds me"—meaning, when my standing is finished, having pursued the goodness of this world all my days, the sin of this path will surround me.

**Those who trust in their wealth.** They are confident and boastful of their great riches, but it is not fitting for me to do so. For wealth does not help in the day of death; a man cannot redeem his brother from death, nor can they give to God a ransom for his life. **And the redemption of their soul is precious.** Meaning, it is a heavy price that cannot be paid. This matter is hidden from them forever. **That he should live on eternally.** Meaning for a long time. **For he sees that wise men die.** Even the wise, who are esteemed, die; they stand for a while and then are no more. And it says "together the fool and the boor perish." This refers to the spirit of this world and its memory. For when the wise die, their wisdom does not die with them, but the fools leave their "wealth"—their physical glory—to others. What will it benefit them? But the words of the wise are not lost.

**Their inward thought is that their houses are forever.** Some interpret "inward" <note>Hebrew: "kirbam"</note> as a reversal of "their graves" <note>Hebrew: "kivram"</note>. That is, the grave is their house forever. Others interpret it as "their thoughts," meaning in their minds they believe their houses will stand forever. They call lands by their names to be remembered, but this is a vanity. **But man in honor does not abide.** Even if a man is in honor and wealth, it will not stay with him forever. It will return to others after him. **He is likened to the beasts.** Just as the beast is destroyed and forgotten, so this man is destroyed and not remembered, as it is written: "the soul that sins shall be utterly cut off."

**This is their way.** This is the way of the wicked and their thoughts. **Yet their followers approve.** Their children follow their ways and their speech. Just as they tasted the sweetness of their thoughts at the beginning, so they will multiply in that same path. **Like sheep they are set for Sheol.** Just as sheep are led, so death leads them to the grave. **And the upright shall rule over them in the morning.** Meaning, now the wicked are on top and the righteous are on the bottom, but in the "morning"—the Day of Judgment—the upright will rule over the wicked. As it is written: "and you shall trample the wicked, for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet." The day of judgment is called "morning" because it brings light to the righteous.

**But God will redeem my soul.** Unlike the wicked who trust in their wealth, the psalmist trusts that God will redeem his soul from the hand of the grave. **Be not afraid when a man becomes rich.** Do not be envious or fearful when you see a wicked man prosper, for he takes nothing with him. **For when he dies he shall take nothing.** His glory will not descend after him. **Though while he lived he blessed his soul.** He only cared for his physical needs and his own comfort. But he will eventually come to the generation of his fathers, the wicked who preceded him, and they shall never see light. **Man that is in honor and understands not.** A man who has wealth but lacks the wisdom called "honor" is no better than a beast. His memory will perish and he will not be remembered.

# PSALM

**By Asaph, the Mighty One, God, the LORD.** This psalm concerns the Day of Judgment that will be in the future to come, as it is written in the prophecy of Joel <note>OCR "vzal" likely refers to "Yoel"</note>: *In those days and at that time, I will restore the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, and I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat and judge them there.* After the poetic portion comes the rebuke in the final section. And why are the names "Mighty One" <note>El</note>, "God" <note>Elohim</note>, and "the LORD" <note>YHVH</note> used? This repetition emphasizes God's total power and ability. Afterward, the psalm says, **He spoke and called the earth.** He spoke through His prophets to all the nations. The word "called" <note>va-yikra</note> is used here in the sense of a future event. This linguistic style is found in many places in Scripture. Similarly, "shines forth" <note>hofia</note> implies He *will* shine forth. He calls to those who dwell from the rising of the sun to its setting to come for judgment. The meaning of **He summons from above** is that He intends to rule over them with all His host, as written in the prophecy of Ezekiel <note>OCR "yizaza" likely refers to "Yechezkel"</note>: *I will bring you from the far north and bring you against the mountains of Israel.*

**From Zion, the perfection of beauty.** This is as the prophet Isaiah <note>OCR "izail" likely "Yeshayahu"</note> says: *From Zion shall go forth the Torah.* It is as if to say that Zion is the source of all that is great. **Our God comes.** This refers to the time when He will avenge the nations for what they did to us, for our humiliation and their contempt. **A fire devours before Him.** This refers to the destruction of the enemies. **And around Him it is very stormy.** That is to say, around His holy place where His judgment occurs. **It is very stormy.** This refers to the King, meaning all the inhabitants will be caught in a stormy wind. **He summons the heavens.** He calls upon the angels <note>original: "malakhim"</note> to take up the judgment of His people against the nations, as it is said: *And His angels shall go out with Him.* **And the earth.** This refers to the kings of the earth, for they themselves will see the judgment. It will be like a "terror of the Lord," as written in the prophecy of Ezekiel: *Every man's sword shall be against his brother.* And as it says in the prophecy of Zechariah: *A great panic from the LORD shall fall on them.* They will call to the heavens from above—this refers to the angels—and to the earth to judge His people—this refers to the nations. This means that on the Day of Judgment there will be a tumult among the nations, and they will be judged for their wisdom.

**Gather to Me My pious ones.** This is said to the nations of the world, that they should gather the exiles to Jerusalem, as written in the prophecy of Zechariah: *And they shall bring all your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the LORD.* And Isaiah says: *From beyond the rivers of Cush, my worshipers shall bring my offering.* He says this regarding the world: **Those who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice.** For at Mount Sinai, He made a covenant with them through the blood of the sacrifice. There is also a hint here to the covenant of circumcision <note>term: "Berit Milah"</note>, which is also like a sacrifice. **The heavens declare His righteousness.** Because the heavens and their hosts stand forever, unlike the earth where one generation goes and another comes. The heavens are witnesses to the time when Israel was in exile and the time when they are redeemed. The heavens will testify that God is a righteous judge and does not withhold the judgment of Israel from the nations.

**Hear, My people.** He turns from the judgment of the nations to address Israel regarding what they have done. He mentions the "Prophecy of the Names" <note>likely referring to God's attributes</note>. **Not for your sacrifices do I rebuke you.** He rebukes them regarding the matter of burnt offerings. It is like the word of the prophet Isaiah: *To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?* And Jeremiah said: *Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices and eat meat.* And the prophet Malachi said: *Oh, that there were one among you who would shut the doors.* All the prophets rebuked them for this. God says: I do not need your animals. **For every beast of the forest is Mine.** All that you think is under your authority is actually under Mine. **The moving creatures of the field.** This refers to all the wild animals of the desert. The "Ziz of the fields" <note>original: "Ziz Sadai"</note> is a legendary bird so large that when it spreads its wings, it hides the sun. It is called "Ziz" because it has many different flavors <note>a folk etymology based on the Hebrew "zeh" (this) and "zeh" (that)</note>. **If I were hungry, I would not tell you.** If I were like a human who hungers, I would not need your food, for the whole world is Mine. **Sacrifice to God a thank-offering.** If you want to merit the Torah, let your sacrifice be the subduing of your evil inclination. Fulfill your vows to the Most High. This means that God does not need the physical sacrifice, but rather the speech of your lips and the fulfillment of your heart's promise. **And call upon Me in the day of trouble.** This refers to the judgment. If you honor Me with your soul, I will deliver you. But as for the wicked, God says: *What right have you to recite My laws?* This refers to those who speak of the Torah but do evil deeds. They are like those who are close to God with their mouths but far in their hearts.

<summary>This page contains Psalm 50 in both its Aramaic Targum (paraphrase) and original Hebrew, followed by a medieval commentary. The text emphasizes that God desires sincere gratitude and moral conduct over the ritual slaughter of animals, framing the psalm as a vision of the future Day of Judgment.</summary>

They shall go and be bad... And previously it was explained "they feed" and not the mouth. What is written in the Torah proves this, saying "the Torah is for this." And it says "it was seen by your mouth," teaching that the Torah is like the statutes
from his mouth. And the head of knowledge and the curse to his father and his teachers. And it says "light/fire of the teacher," a harmful light to the place and a fence. And on this it says "it was strengthened and finished," and all who find it have found life. They distance
the Torah from others through their evil deeds which they perform, and they are turned away from occupying themselves with the study of Torah, hiding and shaming those who rebuke the children of men. For who is it that sends those words
if not the one who remains after us? And they are hasty in their deeds that reveal their shame. But their deeds that are hidden from most people are evil. Therefore it says: "If you saw
a thief, you were pleased with him." And they are ashamed of your God. Only their deeds are hidden. And "My covenant"—these are the commandments of the Torah, called a covenant. And "to the wicked this I saw." And "My covenant" which you took—
his Torah was nothing but from the lips and the tongue. "And you hate instruction"—these are the commandments between a man and his fellow. "My words"—these are the ten commandments. "If you saw... and you were pleased"—like "placing a face of favor,"
meaning you desired to be hand-in-hand with him. "Your mouth you sent into evil"—to mention evil against the children of men. And it says "you sent" in the way of a release, as if he does not restrain it from speaking evil. Also this
is from the abominations mentioned in the book, speaking evil of people in his house or from one person to another in a place. "You join deceit"—words of deceit you join, connecting your words with the words of another person who
speaks evil like you. "You sit against your brother"—"sitting" means a gathering set for a person to speak against another or his brother, and he has it in him. And so it said of the men of the city "your hand and so-and-so," speaking an evil word that cannot be given. For he
is prepared for inheritance and blasphemy. "These things you did"—and because I was silent—meaning I made myself as if I did not know, and I did not rebuke you—your heart became haughty through your evil deeds. "You imagined being like Me"—
sitting with brothers like you, as if the silence I kept was approval. Now I will rebuke you and set it before your eyes. Everything I was silent about, I was helping him <note>likely referring to the victim or the record of the sin</note>, and I knew everything. And although I delayed the punishment for you, now
it shall come at the time of speaking of the wicked, to make known who are the good and who are the wicked. As it is said in the book of Malachi: "Then you shall return and see the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between him who serves God and him who
serves Him not." And some in it give another explanation from the Sages, saying: the word "blessed" is a general blessing and an inheritance and a strengthening. These are the wicked, yours is upon them, but everything that you imagined and thought I would assist in,
I will rebuke you and set it before your eyes, for this is the honor of the blessings. "Understand this now"—the rebuke, and turn from your evil deeds, for you have forgotten the All-Powerful. "Lest I tear you to pieces and there be no deliverer"—
for I will not delay any longer until the day of judgment. And as it says in Malachi: "Lest I come and strike the earth with a curse." "A sacrifice of thanks"—whoever offers a sacrifice with Torah, meaning that the Torah
reproves his evil deeds, he is the one who honors Me and prepares a path for his salvation. "And he sets a way"—this refers to whoever he may be, whose way is set and ready to provide his path and his heart to his Creator, and he shall not turn before Him to sacrifice. "He will see
the salvation of God"—because the vision of salvation will be on the day of judgment, and this is the time of repentance, the time of the power of God's salvation, and it will be good all the days of the world. And it said "in the salvation of God" after
it said "it honors Me," as if it said "in My salvation." And similarly, "and to God" is said instead of "to Me." And in the Aramaic translation, "and sets a way" is written in the language of one who weighs his paths, meaning he measures his paths so they may be
in righteousness and in judgment before the children of men, to see the salvation of God.

Now and the judgment of my judgment. "Wash me"—explanation: multiply Your washings and wash me from my iniquity, and this will be a great washing like a multitude. Meaning, wash me greatly from my iniquity, for the soul is satiated with the reward.
"Cleanse me"—as the language of washing clothes. "For my transgression"—will be like my rebellious act. "My word"—I acknowledge that I have sinned and will not deny the sin, as one who says "I did not know." "Before me
constantly"—as if it were always placed and written before me because of this deed of mine. "Against You alone"—for my sin was in secret. And all the paths of the wicked. And I will not deny the sin. And although I called
them <note>likely the witnesses</note> regarding what passed, they did not know why I called them. And also in the secret way, no man knows to me why I ordered his death except You. For although I told Joab the matter of Uriah
in a secret letter that men speak of according to the passing of their commandments, this is why our Sages said: "It is written: 'He who covers his sins shall not prosper,' and it is written: 'Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.'" This applies to sins between a man
and himself that are not known. And the righteous Rav Saadia explained thus: "Against You alone I have sinned etc." He said: "I sinned to You alone," meaning to You alone I confess and say "I have sinned." "And the evil in Your eyes
I have done." And I saw that they explained it as our Sages said: "It is written: 'He who covers his sins shall not prosper,' and it is written: 'Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.'" This means for sins between a man
and his fellow, "he who covers his sins shall not prosper," but for sins between a man and the Place <note>God</note>, it is correct that he is one whose "sin is covered." And because I have found for them proof from the explanation of
sins. "So that You are justified in Your words"—meaning that You forgive my sin, just as You said to Cain "if you do well, there is lifting up." And You said to Moses when I made known my iniquities that You would forgive, for thus it is set and spread
and spoken. "So that You are blameless when You judge"—and it is not within the judgment that a man could say to You that You spoke a word and turned and changed its reward. And after he said that he sinned the sin of the commandment, that
I sinned. And this is "for to You alone I have sinned"—for if Uriah were alive, I would have sinned against him, but now that he is dead, I have sinned to You alone, more than against any man. For all my sin is surrendered
to You. and I have nothing to ask for forgiveness except from You, who warns against this and against other things like it. "Behold, in iniquity I was brought forth"—because the formation of the heart of man is as if in iniquity
it begins. And the drop, for in the language of sin it is said that the thing is evil in nature. And what is this? This is a hint to man not to be moved after his desire. And I have seen another explanation for this matter in order to be understood and to remove
from him the iniquity. He said that from Your way this is: the iniquity of my transgression in my creation. And it was the drop of seed and from it I was conceived by my mother, as a person who plants a bitter seed and it is ruined and the fruit is bitter by nature.

<column-break/>

"With the power of the Lord, Nathan the prophet came"—for he gave the rebuke and said "I have sinned to You." But all this prayer which Nathan placed to our master he said: "Have mercy on me, O God,
according to Your kindness." All according to my deeds. You have rebuked me with this rebuke, and this prayer I have prayed. Or its explanation is that in this verse there is a hint to the matter of Bathsheba and the matter of
Uriah. "As the greatness"—it is written "and he shall send and he shall hide" and this. Like "wash me from me, wash me from me." And in the secret of the washing that they laundry their clothes together now also
and all the things shall go after their results. And the person is conceived from a drop of seed in the language of the heavens. And the explanation is that in this there is a hint of instruction and prohibition so that a man shall not be moved in his heart to the way of sin from which
he was created, and it is not a great thing if they are strengthened, their desire will bring them to transgress this matter. But in the prophet and the blessing and every other person there is no anger and no others, a hint like this. Therefore I am more concerned if he shall err
and it is worthy that he place his hope in the way of the perfect ones, that they shall not be strengthened in their desire through evil. And this is the secret and the parable they inherit in his spirit so that he shall not write and shall not explain there is nothing in it and also an earthly sin
for this is his creation and to God it is not his desire. The word "conceive me" <note>original: "yehematni"</note>—"heat" of my mother. For when the heat of the female is joined with the male, the heat and the desire begin to grow within her. And so, "the sheep conceived." And it was warmed
in the sticks. And it said that the desire of the male is greater than the female, as it said: "When a woman has conceived seed first and gives birth to a male." And it is said as a parable. And this is in the explanation of Rabbi Levi after he said "in iniquity
I was formed." Even the most pious among the pious, it is impossible that he should not have one side of sin within him. David said before the Holy One: "Master of the universe, I am the one who was made from a drop that is all sin, and from it do not leave me but
to Your word alone." Multiply the washing of these things, for they are like a laborer hiding the deed. And this root is turned from between the father and this is turned from between the father, and You are the covering of every person, for
it is plundered. He said, "I and my father are in my iniquity," and this is what washed me. "Behold, Truth!"

->For praise, regarding a good understanding<-
By the hand of David: When Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, saying to him, "David has come to the house of Ahimelech."
Why do you boast in evil, O mighty man who sheds innocent blood? The kindness of God is all the day. Your tongue devises sins like a sharp razor, performing words of mockery.

---

**Behold, You desire truth in the inward parts.** This refers to the will and desire that overcame me. My heart did not rise within me and my kidneys did not tremble before You and Your commandments; instead, I allowed a dream-like state to remove my honor. For I know that my heart stands in its depths within the hidden things of Your strength and understanding. And now my heart is my tunnel <note>An idiom for secret introspection or searching</note>. And You have made wisdom known to the hearts of those wise men in the inner chamber. It is not through outward action but through the way of wisdom from my depths; wisdom clears its own deep path. **And in the hidden part You will make me know wisdom**—wisdom from the hidden paths in the way of truth. For in the heart and in the depths of the kidneys, it is fitting to search the depths of a matter and the wisdom of the heart. The "kidneys" are the seat of counsel, as in the phrase "Who put wisdom in the inward parts?" <note>Job 38:36</note>. **Purge me with hyssop and I shall be clean.** This is like the "clean heart" of my inner parts. For I know the scripture will clear him, as the scripture grants atonement. **And in the hidden part You will make me know wisdom**—to me it is revealed in my heart, and I have searched the depths of my heart, uncovering the sand that removes my sin. **And wash me.** A person becomes white upon his return, for our sins though red like scarlet shall be white like snow. **Make me hear joy and gladness.** When my iniquity is forgiven, there will be joy. When one is vindicated, gloom departs and his feet and his whole soul shall dance for the name of the Lord. He mentions **the bones** because it is the body itself that rejoices. After the forgiveness, I alone will recognize this joy in my heart. The memory of my sins will not depart from me, so that I may always fear my debt. These "broken bones" which were desolate from the ruin of my sin will receive joy after the pardon. **Hide Your face from my sins.** Have mercy on me, for You know I have sinned. **Do not cast me away.** That is, let my mind be steadfast forever to serve You and never to be separated from You. **And do not take Your Holy Spirit from me.** This is the spirit of holiness and prophecy given to him by God, that it should not depart because of sin. **A generous spirit.** A willing heart and an expansive spirit to receive Torah and wisdom. **I will teach transgressors.** The way to teach sinners the path of repentance and forgiveness. **Deliver me from bloodguilt.** From the blood of Uriah, or from the killing of the people of Nob, the city of priests, or generally from all bloodshed. **God of my salvation.** Because He saves everyone. In place of the forgiveness, he says **my tongue shall sing aloud of Your righteousness**, for it is the righteousness of God to forgive sinners when they return. **O Lord, open my lips.** Because of the magnitude of the distress, regret, and prayer, his lips were closed from telling the praise of the Holy One until the news came that he was forgiven. **For You do not desire sacrifice.** His debt is not of the type of sacrifices called "Zevach" <note>Peace offerings or animal slaughter</note>. Even if You desired it, I would give a burnt offering, but the main thing is the intention and repentance. **The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit.** This is the essence. **Do good in Your good pleasure.** During his reign, when he was despised in the eyes of the people—as Shimei son of Gera spoke—he prayed for the needs of Israel. In his days the House was sanctified, and the continual sacrifice was offered in the Temple built in the days of Solomon his son. Everything—the service, the incense, the lamps—is called a whole burnt offering to God. **Sacrifices of righteousness.** These are the sacrifices Israel offered when they were righteous in their Torah. **Then they shall offer bulls upon Your altar.** All offerings—meal offerings, libations, bulls, and rams—will be brought without hindrance, neither in war nor at any other time. And the kindness of the Lord is forever upon those who fear Him.

# To the Chief Musician
**When Doeg the Edomite came.** <unclear>Like the pits of the fallen</unclear>. Like a pious servant... <note>The commentary here becomes highly fragmented or uses obscure linguistic comparisons to the Book of Samuel</note>. **Why do you boast in evil, O mighty man? The goodness of God endures continually.** Does the kindness of the world not stand? Will the world's kindness be canceled because of the deed you did? The kindness of God is upon us every day and will be established in our minds. For the wicked descend... as it is written, "For the wicked boasts of his heart's desire." The kindness of God is His will and His judgment for thousands of pious ones. **Your tongue devises destruction.** He begins his speech to explain that the tongue is like a sword to sell the sickness of the warrior's debt. **Like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.** He calls the tongue a razor because it is sharp, like that which Jacob <unclear>used</unclear>; it is small but cuts much. You have deceived with a few evil words, and the iron rod of your words has brought destruction.

->Psalm 55<-

To the Chief Musician with stringed instruments, a *Maskil* of David. Give ear to my prayer, O God; and do not hide Yourself from my supplication. Attend to me, and hear me; I wander in my thoughts and moan.
