<margin>**You loved evil.**</margin> **You loved evil.** The "evil and good" mentioned here refers to the time David was fleeing. He was stirred to be wary of those who sought his harm. This refers to the hands of Hezekiah <note>The commentator here links the preservation or editing of these texts to the era of King Hezekiah</note>, for David was fleeing and did not know that he was being pursued in this way. This wicked man mentioned is Doeg, as is written explicitly in the commentary. Because of the reporting against him regarding his hiding place, it refers back to Hezekiah... <margin>**His strength**</margin> ... **Strength.** A refuge or a fortress for him. "You loved all devouring words"—words of incitement, for the words of the pious bring joy. "Deceitful tongue"—you loved every tongue of trickery, for lashon hara <note>evil speech/gossip</note> is hidden and distant, intending to destroy life. "He shall take you and pluck you"—this is an expression of breaking. He will cut them off from the dwelling and uproot them from the land of the living. <margin>**Does**</margin> ... **Does.** Remind yourself of him. This is "He will pluck you." It means uprooting from the land, as it is written "the roots of his feet." "The righteous shall see"—they shall return. It refers to the World to Come. <margin>**He will pluck you**</margin> ... **He will pluck you.** A matter of destruction and pulling down, as in "the Lord will pluck up the house of the proud." "He will shatter you"—He will open and break you. "And your root"—a matter of uprooting. "The righteous shall see"—they shall see the power of the destruction upon the wicked, and the righteous are compared to a green olive tree. They will say, "Behold the man who did not make the Word of the Lord his strength." David did not stretch out his hand against Saul, even though it seemed bad at the time, for he trusted in the kindness and strength of God. <margin>**All-**</margin> <margin>**In his wickedness**</margin> ... **In his wickedness.** In his wealth and his thoughts. This refers to the abundance he had, as explained in its place. "But I am like a green olive tree"—while the wicked are uprooted like dry wood, the righteous flourish in the house of God and live forever. Because all that happened to me will only make me flourish more. **In the house of God.** Because I was hidden, I prayed and trusted in the kindness of God. I will praise You forever because You have done this—referring to the salvation. "And I will wait"—I will always look to You.

<margin>**Abominable**</margin> <margin>**Assured**</margin> **The fool says in his heart.** We have already explained this Psalm above in the First Book <note>Refers to Psalm 14, which is nearly identical to Psalm 53</note>, and now it is repeated here with slightly different wording. Our sages explained that David repeated it to apply it to the destruction of the Temple and the exile. Just as David had enemies like Doeg and Ziphites who tried to prevent his kingship, so too the nations will try to prevent the kingship of the Messiah. "God has scattered the bones of those who encamped against you"—this refers to the armies that will surround Jerusalem in the end of days. They will be put to shame because God has rejected them. In the first version of this Psalm (Psalm 14), it mentions the "kindness" and "salvation," but here the language is harsher, referring to "bones" and "rejection." The meaning is the same, but the context is adapted for the historical suffering of Israel.

<margin>**When... came**</margin> <margin>**Ziphites**</margin> **When the Ziphites came.** This is a place in the territory of the tribe of Judah. "Save me by Your name"—David is calling out from his hiding place. "By Your strength judge me"—I trust in Your power to vindicate me from those who pursue me. David repeats his plea: "Hear my prayer" and "words of my mouth." "For strangers"—those who have become like strangers to me, seeking my life. "They have not set God before them"—they have no fear of Divine judgment. "Behold, God is my helper"—they thought to consume me, but the Lord supports my soul. "He shall reward evil to my enemies"—the evil they planned for me shall return upon their own heads. "In Your truth cut them off"—for Your word is truth that I should be king, therefore cut off those who oppose this. "I will freely sacrifice"—when You deliver me, I will bring a voluntary offering with a good heart. "For He has delivered me"—this refers back to how God saved him from previous troubles.

<margin>**Melody and You**</margin> **To the leader with stringed instruments.** David said this Psalm when he was fleeing from Jerusalem because of Absalom, and he was told that Ahithophel was among the conspirators. "Give ear... and do not hide"—a repetitive plea for urgent help. "Attend to me"—in my wandering and my moaning. This refers to the deep distress and the "stormy wind" of the rebellion.

From the voice of the enemy’s enmity, from before the oppression of the wicked; for they cast falsehood upon me and hate me in their anger. My heart trembles within me, and the terror of death has fallen upon me. Fear and trembling come upon me, and darkness has covered me. And I said: "Who will give me a wing like a dove? I would fly away and dwell [in peace]." Behold, I would go far away to wander; I would lodge in the wilderness forever. I would hasten my escape from the stormy wind, from the whirlwind. Destroy them, O Lord; divide their tongues, for I have seen violence and strife in the city. Day and night they go around it upon its walls, and iniquity and falsehood are in its midst. Tumult is in its midst, and falsehood and deceit do not depart from its streets. For it was not an enemy who insulted me—that I could bear; and it was not one who hated me who magnified himself against me—from him I could have hidden. But you, Ahitophel <note>The Targum identifies the "man of my rank" as Ahitophel, King David's advisor who joined Absalom’s rebellion.</note>, a man like me, my teacher and my instructor who taught me wisdom. We together would take sweet counsel; in the sanctuary of God, we would walk with the crowd. May the judgment of death find them, and let them descend alive into Gehenna <note>term: Gehenna (Hebrew: *Gehinnom*); the place of punishment or purification in the afterlife.</note> while they are still living, for evil is in their dwellings, in their bodies. As for me, I will pray before God, and the Word of the Lord <note>original: "Memra d'Yeya" - a common Targumic way to refer to God's manifest presence or action.</note> will save me. In the evening, and the morning, and at noon, I will pray and be troubled, and He heard my voice. He redeemed my soul in peace so that no one might approach me, for in many matters his Word was my support. God will hear and receive from them; He who sits [on the throne] from of old. *Selah*. For the wicked do not change their evil ways and do not fear before God. He has stretched out his hands against those who were at peace with him; he has profaned his covenant. Their words are smoother than butter, but war is in his heart; his words are softer than oil, yet they are drawn swords. ->Conclusion<- | <margin>As such, so give, give</margin> From the voice of the enemy, because of the oppression of the wicked; for they cast iniquity upon me, and in wrath, they hate me. I would fly away and be at rest." Lo, then would I wander far off, and remain in the wilderness. *Selah*. I would hasten my escape from the windy storm and tempest. For it was not an enemy that reproached me; then I could have borne it: neither was it he that hated me that did magnify himself against me; then I would have hid myself from him: But it was you, a man my equal, my guide, and my acquaintance. We took sweet counsel together, and walked unto the house of God in company. Let death seize upon them, and let them go down quick into hell: for wickedness is in their dwellings, and among them. As for me, I will call upon God; and the Lord shall save me. Evening, and morning, and at noon, will I pray, and cry aloud: and he shall hear my voice. He has delivered my soul in peace from the battle that was against me: for there were many with me. God shall hear, and afflict them, even he that abides of old. *Selah*. Because they have no changes, therefore they fear not God. He has put forth his hands against such as be at peace with him: he has broken his covenant. <margin>Openings/Swords</margin> The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.

<column-break/>

**Commentary**

**From the voice of the enemy:** My refuge, keep me from the way of evil and from mentioning it, and save him and strengthen him. Kindness is for those who take refuge in Him, and likewise for all of them. They shall save the stiff-necked and the proud heart... and the fear of our memory shall be with him. **Because they cast iniquity upon me:** And the explanation is that their voice brings me down and cools me... to awaken the heart to receive and rest.

**My heart is pained:** Pained with labor like a woman in childbirth. And he said from the remainder... like the king alone. **Fear and trembling and horror:** These are matters of fear concerning illnesses, deaths, and blows. **And covered me:** Like a garment covering a person to strengthen him in the place of a level ground.

**Oh that I had wings like a dove:** Why a dove? Because the dove, when it becomes tired in its flight, rests one wing and flies with the other, whereas other birds must stop entirely. David says: "If only I had wings like a dove to distance myself and dwell in the wilderness."

**I would hasten my escape:** To hasten to a place of escape. **From the windy storm:** This refers to the tempest of the enemy. **Destroy, O Lord, divide their tongues:** David prays that God would frustrate the counsel of Ahitophel and his companions, confusing their language so they cannot agree on their wicked plans. 

**Violence and strife in the city:** Day and night they go around the walls. The city is surrounded by violence and theft. **Wickedness and deceit:** Meaning that David's own people have turned to treachery. **It was not an enemy who reproached me:** This is the core of the pain. If it were a known enemy, David could have prepared. But it was a "man of my rank"—Ahitophel, who was David's chief advisor and friend.

**We took sweet counsel together:** You were the one I shared my secrets with! We walked to the House of God together in the crowd. **Let death seize upon them:** A prayer for a sudden end for the traitors, that they might descend into the depths while still alive, much like the rebellious Korah in the desert.

**Evening, morning, and noon:** These are the three times a person must pray to God. David says that in all these times he will cry out, and God will hear him. **He redeemed my soul in peace:** God delivered him from the battle. **For there were many with me:** Some interpret this as the angels who were with David, helping him against the many who were against him.

**His words were smoother than butter:** This describes the hypocrite. Ahitophel spoke words of peace and loyalty, but in his heart, he was preparing for war. His words seemed soft like oil, but they were actually **drawn swords** <note>original: "peticnot" - an unusual Hebrew word for drawn swords or openings of war.</note> meant to kill.

**Commentary**

**Finally:** David said, shaking himself and passing all the curses which are upon the one who "casts" etc., and he shall not turn from his path and shall not fail, for He will sustain you. **For He will never allow the righteous to stumble:** He will not leave him forever in stumbling. And the meaning of **your burden** (*yehavcha*) is "your load." This is based on the words of our Sages of blessed memory <note>reference to the Talmud, Tractate Rosh Hashanah 26b</note>: The Rabbis did not know the meaning of "Cast upon the Lord your *yehavcha*" until they heard an Arab merchant say to his fellow: "Take your *yehava* (load) and cast it upon my camel." And the meaning of **He will sustain you** is like the verse "the heavens and the highest heavens cannot sustain You." There it is explained as "He will not give you over." That is to say, cast yourself upon Him who will provide for you.

**But You, O God, will bring them down:** meaning to the pit. As it was said in the vision of the pit, "soul and body." And also "men of blood" refers to those who are worthy of being cut off. **They shall not live out half their days:** For they shall not live half the days that were written for them; they shall be shortened and their days will end, and You will advance my kingdom.

### For the Chief Musician

<margin>
56
</margin>
**On the silent dove of distant ones, a Michtam of David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath:** David called himself "a silent dove" when he was in Gath, when he was seized by the hand [of the Philistines]. And he said that at the time the Philistines thought to kill him, he changed his behavior in their eyes, as it is said that he acted insane. Therefore he called himself "a silent dove." A dove is a symbol for Israel. And it was "silent" because he could not speak according to his judgment and knowledge, but only as one who is insane. Then he called himself a silent dove because he was seized because of the fear he had of them. **When the Philistines seized him in Gath:** The explanation is that they seized him.

**Be gracious to me, O God, for man tramples me:** This "man" refers to Saul, who pursued me or beat me down. **All day long the warrior oppresses me:** This refers to the battle always surrounding him. **My enemies trample me:** My enemies who watch me from the hidden places of the world where I am hiding among them. And this is truly the reward of the Blessed God. And he says: "Have mercy, O God, for my heart is broken and my mother told me that I have no hope." And I called out from my hiding place to strengthen myself among them, to say to myself: "Be strong in the Lord."

**On the day I am afraid, I will trust in You:** And so "trust in the Lord with all your heart." **In God [I praise]:** The meaning is truly I trust in God. That is, I trust in God and I will praise His word. That is, what they said to me, those words of insanity I spoke, they thought they could use them against me. And he said: "I will praise my words which were like madness," and God helped me so they would be accepted in their eyes.

**All day long they twist my words:** Regarding my kingdom, they anger me more, and all their thoughts are for my harm. **They gather, they hide themselves:** They gather and see and hide at my heels, in the place where I go. **They hide:** Like being in a pit or a trap. **They watch:** In the sense of lurking, like "he waits in the hidden place." As they wait for me in a secret place, they watch my soul. **As they have waited for my soul:** They wait to catch me. **Because of their iniquity, cast them out:** In the place of my hiding, I cast myself upon God. Let there not be any hope for them, as they have done to my father and my relatives.

**You have counted my wanderings:** As You have counted them, so deal with them. **Put my tears in Your bottle:** A metaphor, as it is the way of a king to listen to those who cry. Therefore he says: "Collect my tears in Your bottle," meaning preserve them and do not forget them. **Are they not in Your book?** This is a language of strength and certainty. "Put my tears" corresponds to "in Your book," like a book of remembrance, for the matter is written in His memory always.

**Then my enemies will turn back:** When I call to You, I know this—that God is for me when my enemies turn back and are afraid of me, for I call to God and He answers me. **In God, [whose word I praise]:** In Him I trust and I will praise the word He said to me. As explained before, I will praise the word. He doubles the word "word"—once with the name of God (attribute of judgment) and once with the name of the Lord (attribute of mercy). Whether it be good or bad, I will praise the word. Thus it is found in the Midrash: "In God (judgment) I praise the word; in the Lord (mercy) I praise the word." David says: "Whether You judge me with the attribute of judgment, I praise You; whether You judge me with the attribute of mercy, I praise You."

**In God I trust; I will not fear what man can do to me:** Above it said "flesh," and here it says "man." If they come to harm me, I will not fear. **Your vows are upon me, O God:** I have taken vows to You to pay You thanksgivings when I am saved from my enemies. **For You have delivered my soul from death:** When You saved me and did not allow those who hate my soul to kill me. **Have You not kept my feet from stumbling:** A language of strength, as explained. "He kept my feet from stumbling so I should not be in the pit anymore." **That I may walk before God in the light of the living:** For when I was saved, I was as one who could walk in the ways of God. This refers to the World to Come, or the Land of Israel, which is called the "light of the living," which is the Garden of Eden.

**Do Not Destroy:** We have already written at the beginning of the book that it is not known whether this refers to the melody. And the question is why many psalms are written about David and Saul. It is possible that this refers to "Do not destroy" when David said to Abishai: "Do not destroy him," regarding Saul in the cave.

**Be gracious to me:** The repetition is for emphasis. **Refuge:** The root of the word is *hasaya*, in the weight of a verb. **Until the calamities pass:** Until the evil thing that Saul thinks to do to me passes.

### For the leader; do not destroy. A *Michtam* of David, regarding the distress of the time when he spoke of being destroyed by the hand of Saul.

Is it true that in silence you speak my righteousness? In the time of the dispute of the mighty ones, where righteousness is spoken, will you judge the sons of men with uprightness? Indeed, you wicked ones, what is in your heart? You work injustice on the earth; you prepare the violence of your hands. The wicked are estranged from the dwelling of the womb; they wander from the belly, speaking lies. They have venom <margin>and stopped up</margin> like the venom of a serpent, like a deaf cobra that stops up its ear, <margin>charmer</margin> which will not listen to the voice of the charmers, or the binder of spells, however wise he may be. O God, break their teeth in their mouths; break the fangs of the young lions, O Lord! Like a snail whose head is crushed, let them go; like an abortion that fell, let the wicked vanish from this world, having never seen the sun. Before the wicked become soft, they shall be like thorns; while they are still raw and ripe, in the whirlwind of destruction, He will sweep them away.

### For the Chief Musician; "Do Not Destroy" (*Al-Tashchet*). A *Michtam* of David.

Do you indeed speak righteousness in silence? Do you judge uprightly, O sons of men? No, in your heart you work wickedness; on earth you weigh out the violence of your hands. The wicked are estranged from the womb; they go astray from the belly, speaking lies. Their venom is like the venom of a serpent, like a deaf cobra that stops up its ear, so that it does not hear the voice of charmers, or the most skillful binder of spells. O God, break their teeth in their mouth; break out the fangs of the young lions, O Lord. Let them melt away like water that flows <margin>everything</margin> for them; let him aim his arrows, let them be as if they were cut off. Like a snail that melts as it goes, like a stillborn child of a woman, let them not see the sun. Before your pots can feel the thorns, whether green or burning, He will sweep them away with a whirlwind.

---

**I cry out to God:** To delay the heat of my pursuers to weaken them... this is the "fulfillment." That is to say, from me they are weakened, and You, O Lord, are over me. **I will awaken the dawn:** As a matter of kingship. **He will send from heaven:** He will forgive... and save me from the reproach of the one who swallows me. This refers to the injustice of those who disqualify this... for already my mouth knows the fortress of the king... **His kindness and His truth:** He stores up kindness for me and his spear is in kindness... my truth is like his... **Among lions:** Among the mighty. And the scribe says "in the place of horses"... and the meaning of "those who are aflame" is that they are set in the order of sorcery and a wicked debt against me... **Their tongue is a sharp sword:** This mentions the tongue of the slanderers and their biting in judgment... to cut with a small blow... **Be exalted above the heavens:** Let everything be exalted, for it is not unique... my glory shall be exalted... **They prepared a net:** Like a snare... **My soul is bowed down:** Bowed and brought low... in life and comfort... **They fell into its midst:** They will be consumed within it. It is the way of the language to speak in the past tense instead of the future in matters of prophecy. **My heart is steadfast:** My heart is prepared... always steadfast and trusting in You that You will save me... **Awake, my glory:** Prepared and additional... and the heart will praise... I will awake the dawn, meaning I will awaken the morning, for it was his custom to praise at every dawn.

---

### Do You Indeed
**Do you indeed speak righteousness:** *For the Chief Musician; do not destroy.* We have already said that David composed this psalm when fleeing from Saul in the cave. The meaning of the psalm is that by law he was pursuing Saul... for there were those who incited Saul to pursue him. **In silence:** Some explain this as "speechlessness." He says: when you gather to gather my judgment... you are silent like a mute. Do you indeed speak truth and judge uprightly? **Indeed in your heart:** Iniquities... for you work iniquity in your heart... even so much that the injustice is as if it were a finished deed... **The violence of your hands you weigh out:** You establish violence on the earth... through deceptive measures and weights. **The wicked are estranged from the womb:** They are alienated from the path of good... as if from their birth they were meant to do strange and evil deeds. **Their venom:** The wicked have a poison like the poison of a serpent... **Like a deaf cobra:** Because he compared them to a serpent, he mentions the cobra. The "deaf cobra" is one that stops its ear so as not to hear the charmer... for there is a known charm for snakes that prevents them from harming, but this small snake is not helped by a charm, as if it were deaf. **O God, break their teeth:** Since he spoke of charmers... he says that since they do not listen to the charmers, God should break the teeth of the wicked. **Break the fangs of the young lions:** Let them melt like water... let them go to their destruction. **Let him aim his arrows:** Every one of them, as he bends his bow to shoot his arrows, let the arrows be as if they were cut in pieces and of no use. **Like a snail:** Let them be like the snail that crawls and melts... it is a creature that is called *limitza* in the language of the Mishnah <note>original: "למיצא" - a slug or snail.</note>. **Like a stillborn child of a woman:** Just as a stillborn child does not see the sun... so too the wicked. **Before your pots:** Before they understand... while the thorns are still green, the whirlwind will sweep them away... a difficult verse regarding the speed of judgment.

"The righteous man shall rejoice when he sees" — he sees in everyone who was pitied by Meron... <note>This is a difficult grammatical note possibly referencing a specific rabbinic interpretation of "judgment" or a place name.</note> and he will learn. Every man will say to him that there is fruit for the righteous from good deeds, whose fruit is consumed in their land in our lifetime. And they will say that there is a God who judges in the earth because they used to think there was the "face of Passover," <note>original: penei pesach; likely a corruption or specific idiomatic reference in the commentary to fatalism or chance.</note> and judgment involves grace... and these will know them... because God reached them with their melody...
The text uses "judges" in the plural <note>original: shofetim</note> as a way of honor, as one says "holy people." Or, it means "God judges the angels," and some of them judge as the emissaries of God and according to His will.

### To the Chief Musician
->Upon the Lily of Testimony, a Michtam of David, to teach; when he fought with Aram-Naharaim and with Aram-Zobah, and Joab returned and smote twelve thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt.<-

"To the Chief Musician" — make it prevail, set me on high. "When he sent" — wander us in a place that is not... "a Michtam" — forever straight... "to do me evil and to drive away my night." "Deliver me" — the angels are the workers of iniquity and men of blood who were thinking to kill him. "For behold... the mighty gather against me" — strength and gathering against me, as in "and Moab feared." "Not for my transgression, nor for my sin" — they did it because of me, for they pursued for nothing without iniquity or sin, as they found no ruin or injustice in my hand. "Arouse" — a language of calling... "without vision or knowledge." "Without iniquity" — without my transgression or my sin against them, yet they run and prepare to catch me. "Awake to meet me" — help me. "And see and see." "And You, Lord God of Hosts, awake to visit the nations" — to pay them back and to judge. "And You, Lord God of Hosts..."

<margin>
In the Psalms. When he fought. Like "which he struck." And in the Midrash <note>Rabbinic homiletic interpretation</note>: His covering in the destruction of the Temple... lack of Rivers... the bread of the child of Psalms... eighteen written in the Tanakh <note>The Hebrew Bible</note>... and in the Valley of Salt... struck 12,000. And in the Book of Samuel it says 18,000, and in the Book of Chronicles it says 18,000. It appears that from the war of Edom there were three groups... and in two books it says 18,000. "And Joab returned and struck Edom." However, David struck 18,000, and Joab struck 12,000... for so it is written "he struck Aram Naharaim"... and the phrase "he struck" is used for both... and according to the ruling of the Sages... all of them were 12,000. And the men of war took... and Joab returned and struck... meaning he struck after Joab had broken them...
</margin>

**God, You have abandoned us.** Through Abner <note>King Saul's general</note> we were breached, and Edom took advantage when we were separated from the land... and our God abandoned us. We are all like a king whose land is breached... return to us in Your mercy.

**You have shaken the land.** You breached it like the opening of a wound. **Heal its fractures.** Because of the sins of the people, the land was broken. And now, heal the fractures caused by the enemy. For the land is collapsing under the weight of war.

**You have shown Your people hard things.** We have suffered and been humbled as if we were drunk on the wine of bewilderment. <note>This "wine" refers to a state of confusion and divine judgment</note>.

**You have given a banner to those who fear You.** Like a sign. Many say this refers to the miracles performed during the battles. **To be raised.** To be elevated above our enemies. **Because of the truth.** Because of the true promise God made to us.

**That Your beloved ones may be delivered.** Save with Your right hand. This refers to the tribe of Benjamin or the righteous ones who are called "beloved." Save them so they may be established in their prayers.

**God has spoken in His holiness.** He spoke through the Holy Spirit regarding the kingdom of Israel. **I will exult, I will divide Shechem.** He mentions these places which were under the control of the house of Saul... but now Gilead is mine and Manasseh is mine... meaning I shall rule over all of them. The meaning of "divide" and "measure" is that they will now be under my jurisdiction and authority.

**Gilead is mine.** One of the places of my scribes... and the kingdom belongs to Judah. That is to say, Judah is my lawgiver at all times... and Ephraim is the strength of my head to save me from the hand of my enemies.

**Moab is my washpot.** He uses the metaphor of a basin where one washes his feet to describe the subjugation of Moab. **Upon Edom I will cast my shoe.** As a sign of ownership and trampling. It is like a person who hands his shoe to a servant to carry. **Philistia, cry out.** This is a cry of brokenness and submission.

**Who will lead me to the fortified city?** He asks, who will bring me to the strongholds of the enemies? Who will lead me to Edom to subdue them?

**Is it not You, O God?** He returns to his prayer. Though You seemed to have abandoned us during the time of Saul, now go out with our armies. **Give us help from the adversary.** Help us in our distress, for the help of human beings is worthless. **Through God we shall do valor.** If God is with us, even a small group will do great deeds. **He will trample.** He will tread them down like one who treads in a winepress.

# For the Conductor
**On a stringed instrument (Negginat)** of David. Regarding the word *negginat*, it appears with a *patah* vowel under the letter *het*, similar to the word *negginat* in other contexts. It is interpreted as a musical reference. The scribe notes that this refers to a superior level of the verse. **When my heart is faint (be-atof)**: this refers to the abundance of prayer during times of trouble. Similarly, we find "A prayer for the poor man when he is faint (ya'atof) and pours out his speech before the Lord" <note>Psalm 102:1</note>. The commentary explains "lead me to a rock higher than I" as a request for Divine guidance to a place of safety that the psalmist cannot reach on his own.

**For You have been a refuge for me**: from the high places, You were a refuge to lead me. **I will dwell in Your tent forever**: Your kindness is the Holy Temple. Some interpret "forever" as a reference to the endurance of the soul. **For You have heard**: already in the past You have listened. The heritage given to those who fear God refers to the merit of the forefathers or the land of Israel.

**Add days to the days of the king**: regarding the King Messiah, or David himself praying that his days be added to the appointed time. **As many generations (dor va-dor)**: refers to the long-lasting impact of the dynasty. **May he sit enthroned before God**: all the days of his life he shall dwell before the Lord, occupying himself with the study of Torah and wisdom. **Appoint kindness and truth (man yinzeruhu)**: may these virtues merit him protection. **So I will sing praise**: to fulfill my vows daily. This chapter 61 is often associated with the holiday of Sukkot.

# For the Conductor
**On Jeduthun**, a psalm of David. David composed this psalm and gave it to Jeduthun, one of the chief musicians, to perform. It is named after him. Some suggest it refers to a specific musical instrument or a style of melody passed down to his descendants.

**Only toward God is my soul silent (dumiyah)**: the word *dumiyah* is an expression of silence and waiting, meaning the heart's intention is directed toward God alone. As in, "Be still (dom) before the Lord and wait patiently for Him." **Only He is my rock**: David emphasizes that his hope and salvation come from no other source. **Greatly (rabbah)**: "I shall not be *greatly* shaken"—though he may stumble slightly, he will not fall entirely.

**How long will you threaten (tehotetu) a man?**: Until when will you plot against a person? **You shall all be crushed (teratzhu)**: the commentary notes a grammatical variation here; it suggests the enemies will be destroyed by their own violence. They are compared to a "leaning wall" that is about to collapse. **To push him down (le-hadiach)**: they plot to remove the king from his greatness. **They delight in lies**: they speak kindly with their mouths while harboring curses in their hearts.

**Only for God wait in silence**: here the psalmist repeats the sentiment, reinforcing his trust. **My glory**: my honor and refuge are found in God’s praise. **Trust in Him at all times**: an exhortation to the people in exile to trust God regardless of the era. **Pour out your heart**: true prayer is the pouring out of the inner soul. **Sons of men are vanity**: common people and nobles alike are insignificant compared to God; in the "scales" of judgment, they have no weight. **Do not trust in oppression**: a warning not to seek wealth through illegal means or violence, for such wealth does not last. **Power belongs to God**: this is the ultimate lesson—though humans may seem powerful, true strength and the ability to reward or punish belong solely to the Creator.

# Psalms

And for You, my God, it is to perform kindness for the righteous, for You repay a man according to his deeds.
->**A song of praise by David, when he was in the wilderness of the children of the tribe of Judah:**<-
O God, my strength, You I seek early in the morning to find Your favor; my soul thirsts for You, my flesh yearns for You in a parched land, weary and fainting for a drop of water. Just so, in the place of the Sanctuary, I have seen You, to behold Your strength and Your glory. For Your kindness is better, which You will perform for the righteous in the world to come, than the life You give to the wicked in this world; therefore, my lips shall praise You. Thus I will bless You in this life, and in the name of Your Word <note>Aramaic: *Memra*, a term used in the Targum to represent God’s active presence or speech without implying a physical form</note> I will spread my hands in prayer for the world to come. My soul shall be satisfied as with fat and richness, and my mouth shall praise with lips of exaltation. If I remember You upon my bed, in the watches of the night I meditate upon Your Word. For You have been a help to me, and in the shadow of Your Divine Presence <note>Aramaic: *Shekhinah*</note> I will rejoice. My soul has cleaved to Your Torah; Your right hand has supported me. But those who seek to destroy my soul shall enter the depths of the earth. They shall be dragged by the power of the sword; they shall become the portion of foxes. And the King shall rejoice in the Word of God; everyone who swears by His Word shall praise, for the mouth of those who speak lies shall be stopped.

And to You, O Lord, belongs kindness, for You repay each man according to his work. **63**
->**A psalm of David when he was in the wilderness of Judah:**<-
O God, You are my God; early will I seek You; my soul thirsts for You, my flesh longs for You in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is. So I have looked for You in the sanctuary, to see Your power and Your glory. <margin>I have seen You</margin> Because Your lovingkindness is better than life, my lips shall praise You. Thus will I bless You while I live; I will lift up my hands in Your name. My soul shall be satisfied as with marrow and fatness, and my mouth shall praise You with joyful lips. When I remember You upon my bed, and meditate on You in the night watches. Because You have been my help, therefore in the shadow of Your wings will I rejoice. <margin>64</margin>
**For the conductor, a psalm of David:** <margin>Hear</margin> Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer; preserve my life from fear of the enemy. Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked, from the insurrection of the workers of iniquity. <margin>Portion</margin> Who whet their tongue like a sword, and bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words.

---

"And to You, O Lord, belongs kindness." Some explain that the Blessed Lord performs kindness with human beings according to their own customs, informing them that He repays sin for life according to one's actions. Others explain that His power is His will. Like the verse "for it is a stiff-necked people, yet pardon us," implying that even if they are unworthy, You perform kindness according to Your nature. Regarding the phrase "kindness according to the measure of justice," this speaks in the language of exile, to give us what we have lacked in exchange for the kindness You have done with us, supporting us according to our customs. For You will perform kindness for the living according to their ways; if their depths were established in this world so that folly would be removed, the dream would be whole in the world for all the good You have done.

And so, "kindness," for the power of the pious will prevail. This is the language of Judah, as interpreted by Rabbi Judah the Pious <note>likely referring to Judah He-Hasid, a 12th-century leader of the Chassidei Ashkenaz</note>, who established the depth of the matter: the essence of life and grace is found in His attributes, and the source of blessing is the depth of prayer. Therefore, I have stood in judgment because "it is better," for it is more precious than all else, all for the good they will receive. As it says, "for the judgment of Jacob was pitied." And so the matter is explained: "for he saw him," in his weariness he waited for the turning of our eyes. This stands before our eyes, turning toward our eyes. To You, O Lord, is kindness, for You will do kindness for the Levite according to his custom. In his custom, grace is his power, and the custom of the resting place is established for the living. Kindness within kindness, even if not for our service. And so to support us in the time of the house of destruction. One who is hindered by it dies; one who tastes of it dies. This is the secret of my violence, called "lack of kindness," if You do not pardon the sins of the community. Everything is compared to the plant that grows under the grace of the transition. Like the importance of the striking force of the grace of the great one, seen by the power of the matter, "to You, O Lord, is kindness."

And this is to be said: that grace will be established for the living according to the deeds of the hand. As we are supported, grace is the power of the dream according to its custom. There is a secret to the deeds of destruction, and not according to the life and the receiving from what is written upon the decree. Therefore, if the generation was not worthy of kindness, it would be crushed. But if one does kindness to do blows, the silence of the decree stands over the fullness of its depth. After the generation of kindness, it is written that between the Sanctuary and the power to do evil, there is nothing but what is written upon the decree in this entire Psalm.

->A psalm, a song for the dedication of the House <note>A traditional heading often associated with Psalm 30, perhaps cited here to connect the theme of sanctuary worship</note><-

# **Psalm**
**Of David, when he was in the wilderness.** This Torah is the life of the King for all. And the wilderness of Judah refers to the place where he went after his flight. Some say this refers to the time he was in the forest of Hereth <note>See 1 Samuel 22:5</note> where he sought a place of holiness. Our Sages of blessed memory <note>abbreviated as Hazal</note> said that "beholding" only refers to a vision of the Divine. And this is "O God, You are my God," and this is the fear of the pious before Him. Our Sages said this wilderness refers to being hungry and thirsty for the Word, for his soul yearned for it. This is why he says "my soul thirsts for You," for the pious of the world, as the Sages said: "quiet kindness." This psalm was composed because of his closeness to Him. And as is explained in the "Life of the Early Ones," his heart was wise and he sought to draw near to his God. He remembers that he is in a dry place with the spirit of life, a weary land without water.

"My soul thirsts for You." He has no friend in this place. The meaning is like "parched and faint," both terms meaning "thirsting for water." And "all the land is weary," an land mentioned as masculine because it refers to the people in it, or it is a "weary land." "Just so I have seen You in the sanctuary," meaning I yearn for Your presence in the holy place as I once did, to see Your strength which is the Ark, along with the Glory, for there the Glory dwells. "For Your kindness is better than life." For the goodness of Your kindness that You do with humans according to their custom is better than the life of the body. For the life of the soul which is eternal is better than the life of the person who lives today and is gone tomorrow. Therefore "my lips shall praise You." And this kindness is for those who know the good. Because he mentioned water for the throat, the soul is drawn from wisdom to the source, therefore he said "so."

"I will bless You in my life." Just as I have thought of You here, so in the days of my life I will bless You. "I will lift my hands in Your name." Meaning, in prayer to You. And let my hands not take anything else, like a child who reaches for its mother. "As with marrow and fatness." He will be satiated as if he had eaten rich meat. And so they will not be hungry or faint. He says "with joyful lips my mouth shall praise," for this shall be my salvation while I am hungry and thirsty, for the praise of the faithful is sweeter than anything else.

"If I remember You upon my bed." When he lies down on his bed, he meditates on God. This happens in the watches of the night. "For You have been a help to me." Just as You helped me before when I was fleeing from place to place, so You will help me now. I hide in the shadow of Your wings and sing for joy. This is like the verse "He will hide me in His shelter." "My soul follows close behind You." For Your right hand supports me so that I do not fall before my enemies who pursue me. "But those that seek my soul, to destroy it." Those who seek to kill me and take my life. "Shall go into the lower parts of the earth." Meaning the grave. "They shall fall by the sword." They shall be spilled out by the sword, and the foxes shall eat their carcasses. "But the king shall rejoice in God." David speaks of himself as the king. While his enemies fall, he and those who follow God will rejoice. "The mouth of them that speak lies shall be stopped." Referring to those who spoke slander against him to Saul.

Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked, from the insurrection of the workers of iniquity. Who whet their tongue like a sword, and bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words.

# Psalms

<margin>Suddenly</margin> [To] shoot from secret places at the innocent; suddenly they shoot at him and they do not fear.
<margin>66</margin> They encourage themselves in an evil matter; they talk of laying snares secretly; they say, "Who will see them?"
<margin>149</margin> They search out injustices; "We have accomplished," [they say], "a diligent search"; for the inward thought of every one of them, and the heart, is deep.

<margin>Psalm 65</margin> ->**Psalm 65**<-

For the Chief Musician. A Psalm and Song of David. Praise waits for You, O God, in Zion; and unto You shall the vow be performed. O You who hear prayer, unto You shall all flesh come. Iniquities prevail against me; as for our transgressions, You shall purge them away. Blessed is the man whom You choose, and cause to approach You, that he may dwell in Your courts; we shall be satisfied with the goodness of Your house, even of Your holy temple. By awesome things in righteousness will You answer us, O God of our salvation; who are the confidence of all the ends of the earth, and of them that are afar off upon the sea. Who by His strength sets fast the mountains; being girded with power.

<column-break/>

[To] throw in secret places at the blameless; suddenly they throw at him and do not fear. They strengthen themselves with an evil word; they tell of hiding snares; they say, "Who sees them?" They search for hidden sins; they finish the search for sins; and the holy support is within the flesh, and the sharpness of the heart is deep. But God threw an arrow at them suddenly, and they were wounded. And they will stumble over their own tongues; all who see them will be shaken. And all sons of men will fear and tell of the work of the Lord, and they have contemplated His deeds. The righteous will rejoice in the Word <note>Aramaic: *Memra*</note> of the Lord and trust in Him, and all the upright of heart will be praised.
For praise, a song of David: Before You, silence is considered praise, O God whose Divine Presence <note>Aramaic: *Shekhinah*</note> is in Zion; and to You the vow shall be paid. Receiver of prayer, unto You all sons of flesh shall come. Matters of sin have overpowered me; You will forgive our rebellions. Fortunate is he whom You choose and bring near to dwell in Your courts; the righteous will be satisfied with the goodness of Your house, in the glory of Your holy temple. Awesome things in righteousness You will accept our prayer, O God of our salvation, the hope of all the ends of the earth and the islands of the sea that are far from the dry land; who prepares mountains with His strength, girded with power in His might.

---

**To shoot the innocent.** He says this about himself, that he walked in integrity and did no evil to any of them. **Suddenly they shoot him and do not fear.** Arrows are shot at him suddenly. That is to say, like a marksman shooting an arrow at him suddenly.
**Selah.** They will turn away from him, yet my heart does not fall like a secret from the windows <note>The commentator appears to be using a metaphor for vulnerability or transparency</note>. **And they do not fear.** They shoot in secret and do not fear the God who sees them. **They strengthen an evil matter.** They spoke against me suddenly and strengthened themselves with strong arguments. **And in their writing to him.** Another time out of anger. **Snares.** Meaning to trap me with them. And those hidden things against me in their persistence; they thought in their hearts, "Who will see us?" for they did not believe that there is one who sees their strength and their signature, and they did not fear Him. And even though they were all afraid of the evil ways in public, like the generation of the Flood and the Greeks, and today they do so, some of them are afraid to speak evil of the generation in public. For they thought it better for that person to be like a castaway tomorrow, while the power is in his hand. **They search for injustices.** Like injustices in the street. And he says that these kings and those who tell evils have clothed themselves in deceit, and violence, and injustice, and they search and distance in their hearts injustices and deceits. **They finish a diligent search.** They prepared it, like "they finished it for them in the place of the worthy." **Like one who is refined from suffering.** An object of proof. Meaning every diligent search. **For the inward thought of a man and the heart is deep.** That is, everything a person can search and investigate in the heart, and every thought of thoughts, everything that can be carved out within a man—they all placed in their thoughts of salt and every hidden horse to deepen more than them in the features of the heart and all its thoughts. **And God shall shoot.** "Suddenly" uses the past tense in place of the future. And so "they were afraid" and "they told" in the tradition. All are past tense in place of the future. For God will shoot a sudden arrow, and their wounds will be sudden. **They will stumble over their own tongues.** Before and after. **And they shall make him stumble.** The people of the generation remembered the blows. And they became a ruin. Like "they sent an arrow and God..." beneath them, they live for ruin. **And they cast upon them.** Tomorrow they made themselves stumble upon themselves—meaning the evil words they spoke against me will return upon them. In the way of "he falls into the pit he made." And the "tongue" refers to speech, as in "my tongue speaks from my palate." **All who see them shall be shaken.** From the greatness of their blows and their fall, all who see them will be shaken and recognize and weep over the blows, so that they will be astonished and their sickness will begin. **And they shall fear.** Then all common people will fear because these events are the work of His hand, and they will fear the action of God and His deed. **They wisely consider.** They will understand and consider that God judges and strikes the children of men according to their deeds; for His power is with Him and His rebuke is to him, and they will fear Him. **The righteous shall be glad.** He said it about himself, as he said "the innocent." For the righteous will be in his judgment, and if they knew how to live. **And trust in Him.** He says he will trust in Him more because He delayed His vengeance on the secular ones. And some explain "and he was strong" in place of "because to him was a refuge." Like "wine and the lips of the simple." Meaning, now in my spirit I rejoiced and took refuge in the Lord, meaning that in Him alone was his refuge and his hope did not fail. And so "all the upright in heart shall glory" in Him, like "let him glory" in Him. And in the Midrash, this is applied to the scroll of Daniel. And they said "a generation in a holy generation" regarding the language of Daniel, "to the Lord and..." and he says "praise to be established in Zion etc." like those who were jealous of him and he was cast into the lions' den and the lions were let loose on his friends. This is "And God shot them with a sudden arrow etc. and they declared the work of God." This is what Darius the king wrote to all nations and they mentioned it... and the explanation of the whole psalm is correctly applied to Daniel.

# For the Chief Musician

This psalm is said regarding the return from exile. And the generations that will live at its beginning. Like "the foundations of the generation" and "the ancient ones." "A Psalm of David" and also "A Psalm of David" said regarding the victory of humans.
**To You silence is praise.** He said, "For You, praise is waiting," which will be said to You in Zion at the gathering of the exiles. **And unto You shall the vow be performed.** He says, "The exiles, the children of Daniel, who vowed that if they rose they would perform it for You there in the House of the Sanctuary." As it is written, "Return, O captive daughter of Zion." For it will not be opened. **O You who hear prayer.** And there You will be the Hearer of Prayer, for the time of revelation is when You receive my prayer. **And there, unto You all flesh shall come.** Meaning, all flesh shall come to prostrate before our God. My father explained "To You silence" as being like "there is no portion." That is, to You alone are power and praise. For there is more in You than can be praised by any person; as much as a man is praised for his strength or his goodness or his wisdom, those praises are complete in him only as long as he lives, but they do not remain when he dies. And some explain "silence" in the sense of quietness. An arrow unto You. Or when praise is silent, it is considered as Your service from the nations, so that the praise is not constant—and here it is as if it is opened and its power is it. And the reason for "in Zion" is because there was the residence of their stay in the mountain and in the heights of the heart and in the heights of the soul. And from there "unto You shall the vow be performed." Therefore, because Your praise will not be supported by us from the heights of the mountains, we rely on the praisers. And in the Midrash, it is interpreted regarding David. David said, "To You silence is praise," as if to say, "The silence of the day." All our voices are praise to You. And You are silent from my dwelling in Zion. From where? It is written in the First House. And then we were in the First House. Our hands told silence and... all this. And he said "O God" meaning "my voice etc." there the children of Daniel took refuge and one was silent. One was silent regarding their words. He turned to the One and glory was to Him. **Hearer of prayer.** The prayer of all flesh You hear, and even our prayer You will hear. **And unto You shall the vow be performed.** A king of flesh and blood cannot hear from this one or from that one, and he cannot prevent from all, but You hear the prayer of all flesh as one. And each and every one prays his own. Therefore it says "Hearer," if You hear us all. Also "when I cry out and shout, You hear the prayer." "To dwell in Zion for You to pass over the prayer." He said to them, the Holy One, blessed be He, "You are seeking these kingdoms and... they said before Him, 'We do not seek kingdoms or ways or the hidden things of the heart, but only the mercies for the iniquities that prevail against us; our transgressions, You shall purge them.'" **Matters of iniquities prevail against me.** Singular language. **Our transgressions, You shall purge them.** Plural language. For he speaks about the children of the exile in the plural. "Iniquities have prevailed over us, and our transgressions as well; You shall purge them." For if they led us with heaviness and violence, we come to You so that You may purge them, for You are the Forgiver, not another. Like "learned by the mouth of the one who removed the side." And the secret for the one you gave. **Blessed.** Blessed is he whom You bring near to dwell in Your courts, and not in the courts of a dog, but in the holy heights he shall dwell. **Blessed is he whom You choose and bring near.** Blessed is he who labors for the sake of the deed, who is chosen by it, and You bring him near to Yourself to raise him from the exiles, and this is "he shall dwell in Your courts." **We shall be satisfied.** He speaks of their will who will then be at the time of salvation, "we shall be satisfied with the goodness of Your house." Meaning, we shall be honored by its goodness there in a pure place, the holiness of Your temple. Meaning, the Sanctuary that I mentioned to you. And it is the Temple... sitting upon the glory. **By awesome things in righteousness will You answer us.** In Your greatness You will answer us with wonders and miracles that You will perform with us. For You are the God of our salvation. These actions are in the time of the wonders... being powerful, for He is the one who took up the holy vessels in the service. **The confidence of all the ends of the earth and the sea far off.** And You are the confidence of all the worlds that are scattered at the ends of the earth, even those far off from the dry land. Every language is compared to it. And the "sea" is mentioned as a place of rest, as we say "after his brother." And "far off" there is the end of the sea. And so "from the north and from the sea to..." because from the west and all. **Who sets fast the mountains by His strength.** These will be said in the times of the one who will be established in His greatness, who will say the praises of the verse until... and a friend of the psalm who stirs up who will bring from within them. Like "the one who established, who will move the nations from the crossing that was mentioned etc." and the company of the one who said also that there is the Divine Presence... like an arrow and the sights still escape. For "I will bring back... and I will bring back from the depths of the sea." Then he said, "You prepare the mountains" from the powerful nations that were handled in the greatness of the kingdom, and He will be able to bring them into their desire. One of the mountains, for the high nations are recognized by these for Your word... then he said in seeing to... like: **Girded with power.** And He is included in power, for then when his girding is mentioned, the language of "He prepared" to... for in power He is girded. And so from His powers: **Preparing**...

**Who stills the roaring of the seas.** This refers to Him quieting and calming the sound of the tumult of their waves. That is to say, He silences them. This is similar to the expression "when its waves rise, You still them." **And the tumult of the nations.** Just as He stills the roaring of the seas and their waves, so too He stills the noise of the nations and their recklessness. This leads to **and the dwellers of the ends [of the earth] fear.** One might ask: what is this fear that strikes the wicked? It is the fear they felt when they saw the wonders of the Creator. This is the meaning of **from Your signs.** Meaning, from the signs which You performed for them in Egypt and at the Sea. **The outgoings of morning and evening You make to sing.** This is said concerning Moses and Aaron, or the prophets, or the righteous who call out and praise the Holy One, Blessed be He, in the morning and the evening. **You have visited the earth and watered it.** You visited it for its benefit, as in the phrase "God will surely visit <note>original: "פקוד יפקוד"</note> you." **And watered it.** This is an expression of longing or overflowing, related to the idea of "on that day the mountains shall drip sweet wine." **You greatly enrich it.** This is an expression of multiplication; that is, You visited the earth so that it might be enriched with great wealth. **The stream of God is full of water.** This refers to the rain which is in the hand of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and it is like a stream that never ceases; it is "many waters" and is the "stream of God." **You prepare their grain.** That is to say, by means of the rain, You prepare their grain. **For so You have prepared it.** Meaning, to prepare the rain itself. **Watering its ridges.** The rows made by plowing are called "ridges." This is like the phrase "for the rain has passed and gone," referring to irrigation and saturation. <unclear>And settling</unclear> **its furrows.** This is an expression of resting and sinking; meaning, You watered and settled the furrows that are within the ridges. **You soften it with showers.** This is an expression of melting and softening; meaning, through the rain, the earth becomes soft and dissolved. This is what is written: **You bless its growth.** **You have crowned the year of Your goodness.** This refers to a year in which there is goodness and favor from before the Creator, Blessed be He. This is the matter of the rain that brings up plants and fruits for the trees and vines—it is the crown of the year. **And Your paths drip with fatness.** The paths and ways where the rain descends are "fat" and good; meaning, it grants oil and blessing to the land. **The pastures of the wilderness drip.** The fields and grazing lands in the desert will be lush and good. **And the hills gird themselves with joy.** This describes the rain bringing joy to everything, as in "the rivers shall clap their hands"; by means of the rain, there is singing in all things. **The meadows are clothed with flocks.** These are the valleys that will be "clothed" with sheep and cattle, referring to the good pasture that will be in them; this is the nature of the blessing. **And the valleys are covered with grain.** These are the valleys of the field that are wrapped in grain, referring to the abundant produce that will be in them. **They shout for joy, they even sing.** Everything will give thanks and praise to the Holy One, Blessed be He, for His goodness which He has bestowed upon them.

# **To the Chief Musician**
->A Song, a Psalm. Shout for joy to God, all the earth. This psalm is said regarding the gathering of the exiles and refers to the future redemption.<-
->Sing the glory of His name. That is, sing the glory of the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. Make His praise glorious. Meaning, all the praises that you sing to Him, perform them with honor and awe.<-

**Say to God, "How awesome are Your deeds."** That you should say before Him: how awesome are Your works. **Through the greatness of Your power, Your enemies shall cower before You.** Meaning, because of Your great strength and Your wondrous deeds, Your enemies will deny their past rebellion and say they never intended to fight You. This is an admission of the Creator's power. **All the earth shall bow down to You and sing to You.** That is, all the nations will acknowledge Your sovereignty, as it is written: "And they shall all call upon the name of the Lord." **Come and see the works of God.** Meaning, contemplate His wondrous actions. **He is awesome in His deeds toward the sons of men.** His actions and deeds regarding humanity are awe-inspiring. **He turned the sea into dry land.** This refers to the Red Sea, which was split for them. This is what was mentioned above: "How awesome are Your deeds." **Through the river they pass on foot.** This is the Jordan River, which they crossed on dry land through a great miracle. This implies that just as You did for them in Egypt and at the Red Sea, so You will do for them in the future. **There we rejoiced in Him.** In that future redemption and salvation, we shall rejoice in Him—that is, in God who is our Savior. **He rules by His power forever.** By His power, He rules over all the worlds; His strength and His kingdom rule over everything. **His eyes watch the nations.** Everything is revealed and seen before Him; nothing is hidden from Him. This is why it says "His eyes watch the nations"—to see their deeds and reward them accordingly. **Let the rebellious not exalt themselves. Selah.** These are the nations that rebel and stray; let them not be proud or lift their heads against God. **Bless our God, O peoples.** Everyone shall acknowledge and praise the Creator, Blessed be He, and all nations shall acknowledge His kingship and the praise of His glory.

# Psalms

<column>

**Hebrew Text**

Who has kept our soul in life, and did not allow our feet to slip. For You, O God, have tested us; You have refined us as silver is refined. You brought us into the net; You laid an oppressive burden on our loins. You caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water, but You brought us out to abundance. I will come into Your house with burnt offerings; I will pay You my vows, which my lips have uttered and my mouth has spoken when I was in distress. <margin>rams</margin> I will offer to You burnt offerings of fatlings, with the incense of rams; I will offer bulls with goats. Selah. Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will tell what He has done for my soul. I cried to Him with my mouth, and He was extolled under my tongue. If I had seen iniquity in my heart, the Lord would not hear. But God has surely heard; He has attended to the voice of my prayer. Blessed be God, who has not turned away my prayer, nor His mercy from me. 

<margin>harps</margin> For the leader; with stringed instruments. A Psalm, a song. May God be gracious to us and bless us, and cause His face to shine upon us. Selah. That Your way may be known on earth, Your salvation among all nations. Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You. Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for You judge the peoples with equity <margin>uprightness</margin> and lead the nations on earth. Selah. Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You. The earth has yielded its produce; may God, our God, bless us. May God bless us, and let all the ends of the earth fear Him. 

For the leader; of David. A Psalm, a song. Let God arise, let His enemies be scattered; let those who hate Him flee before Him. As smoke is driven away, so drive them away; as wax melts before the fire, <margin>and they shall go up</margin> so let the wicked perish before God. But let the righteous be glad; let them exult before God; yes, let them rejoice with gladness. Sing to God, sing praises to His name; extol Him who rides upon the clouds <margin>rejoice</margin> by His name Yah, and rejoice before Him. A father of the fatherless and a judge of the widows is God in His holy habitation.

**Aramaic Translation (Targum)**

Who placed our soul in the life of the world and did not deliver our feet to trembling. For You have tested us, O God; You refined us as the refiner of silver. You brought us into the net; You placed a chain around our loins. You caused a man to rule over our heads; we entered <note>original: "into the fire of Nimrod and into the water of Egypt"</note> into the fire of Nimrod and the water of Egypt, yet You brought us out into wide relief. I shall enter Your house with burnt offerings; I shall pay You my vows, which my lips opened and my mouth spoke in my distress. Fat burnt offerings I will offer before You, with the incense of the spice of rams; I will prepare oxen with goats forever. Come, hear, and I will tell all who fear before Him what He did for my soul. To Him I called with my mouth, and praise was under my tongue. If I had seen a lie in my heart, the Lord would not hear. In truth, God has heard; He has listened to the voice of my prayer. Blessed be God, who has not removed my prayer nor His goodness from me. 

For the leader, with stringed instruments, a praise and a song. God will have mercy on us and bless us; He will make the brilliance of His face shine with us forever. To make known Your path on earth, Your redemption among all the nations. The nations shall give thanks before You, O God; all the nations shall give thanks before You. The nations shall be glad and sing, for You judge the peoples with uprightness, and You shall lead the nations on earth forever. Selah. The nations shall give thanks before You, O God; all the nations shall give thanks before You. The earth gave its harvest; may the Lord our God bless us. May the Lord bless us, and may all the borders of the earth fear Him. 

For the leader, for David, a praise and a song. God shall arise and His enemies shall be scattered, and those who hate Him shall flee from before Him. Just as smoke is puffed away, they shall be shattered; just as wax melts before the fire, the wicked shall perish from before God. And the righteous shall be glad, they shall exult before the Lord and be glad with joy. Praise before God, praise the name of His glory; laud Him who sits upon His glorious throne in the heavens—Yah is His name—and exult before Him. The father of orphans and the judge of widows is God in the dwelling-place of His holy Presence. God who joins couples together in a single union, who brought out the House of Israel who were imprisoned in Egypt to a level place, publicly, with redemption and liberation and mediation to their tranquility; they dwell, crying out in their sins over their wicked deeds, in their sins, in a song, publicly.

---

**Commentary**

**Who has kept our soul in life.** This means He has preserved us in life during the long exile, not allowing our feet to slip into total ruin. **For You have tested us.** You have refined us like silver, which is purified of its dross through intense heat. **You brought us into the net.** This refers to the traps and hardships of our enemies. **An oppressive burden.** <term>mu’akah</term> (an oppressive burden) refers to the heavy load of taxes and decrees placed upon our loins, until we had no strength left to stand. **You caused men to ride over our heads.** This describes the nations that have dominated us. **We went through fire and through water.** This is a metaphor for the various types of destruction we faced—fire that consumes and water that drowns—yet in our exile, we were not entirely consumed. **But You brought us out to abundance.** <term>revayah</term> (abundance/overflow) refers to the Land of Israel, a land of saturation and plenty. 

**I will come.** The speaker represents the community of Israel returning from the exile. They will enter the Temple with offerings to fulfill the promises made during their time of suffering. **Which my lips have uttered.** This refers to the prayers and vows made in the heat of distress. **Burnt offerings of fatlings.** The choicest and best of the flock. **Incense of rams.** Specifically referring to the offerings made on the Day of Atonement. **Come and hear.** A call to all who fear God to listen to the testimony of His salvation. **extolled under my tongue.** Meaning that the prayer was already prepared and sincere in the heart even before it was spoken. **If I had seen iniquity in my heart.** If I had intended to continue in sin while praying, God would not have listened. But because the prayer was sincere and the heart was pure, He answered. **Blessed be God.** Who did not reject the plea of the humble.

<column-break/>

<margin>For the leader</margin> **For the leader.** This entire psalm is understood as a prayer for the gathering of the exiles to Jerusalem. **God.** May He be gracious to us and grant us the blessing of returning to our land. **Cause His face to shine.** May His Divine Presence (the *Shekhinah*) be revealed among us as it once was. **That Your way may be known.** When the world sees the redemption of Israel, all nations will recognize God’s sovereignty. **The earth has yielded its produce.** A sign of divine favor; when the people are in their land and in God's favor, the physical world responds with abundance.

<margin>For the leader</margin> **For the leader.** This psalm is traditionally linked to the downfall of Sennacherib <note>The Assyrian king whose army was miraculously destroyed while besieging Jerusalem in the 8th century BCE</note>. **Let God arise.** Echoing the words spoken when the Ark of the Covenant would travel in the desert. **As smoke is driven away.** A metaphor for the sudden disappearance of the enemy forces. **As wax melts.** The wicked cannot endure the heat of God’s justice. **Extol Him who rides upon the clouds.** <term>aravot</term> (clouds/plains) refers here to the highest of the seven heavens in ancient cosmology, where God’s throne is established. **A father of the fatherless.** Even though He is the King of the highest heavens, He cares for the most vulnerable on earth—the orphan and the widow—and ensures their justice from His holy dwelling.

<column-break/>

*"God settles the solitary in a home"* — Hezekiah spread life to living creatures, and they were not protected and did not multiply. *"Settles the solitary in a home"* — the commandment encompasses [the idea]: as it says, "He made houses for them." <note>A reference to Exodus 1:21, where God rewarded the midwives by building them "houses," i.e., dynasties.</note> For my people, Sinai — for us likewise. Another explanation: the meaning in my opinion and the emendation is: as it says, "And the Lord brought them out." And likewise after *"settling"* — close to the house, before the understanding of that aspect. And likewise the hidden foundation, the clarification of judgment from the palaces, and blessing them and spreading.

And the way: *"He brings out prisoners into prosperity."* Hezekiah spread donkeys like Salmaic <unclear>garments</unclear> over all the house of imprisonment — settling them. Like the seal of the firstborn, living in their domain — for merit and connection. Like from the softening of Isaiah upon them while they worked. And the sages of Judah also explained regarding all the community of Judah: *"into prosperity"* — and they spread out — and in their weeping, they are the patience. And in this place it can be understood — like measures of the rebellious in the portion of vigor and their creatures who dwell in a parched place. That is to say, all grace given in the power of a strong portion, with thorns — and the matter speaks of the dry and desolate land. *"But the rebellious dwell in a parched land."* The pious shall dwell forever — and everything is holy. For the power and the letter Koph <note>A Kabbalistic reference to the Hebrew letter כ and its numerical/spiritual significance.</note> are from the same root of fear. And according to the treasuries of the emendation, the grace of God in the act of war — also Hedyan: "Blessed is the Lord who journeys before." And what is mentioned through the power of kingship in your going — "the Lord went, and behold, before you."

For in the marching, the treasuries of lightning — the Lord shall send the angel before them. That is to say, in the power of the strong portion and in the power of grace — for He graced us in every portion and in every grace until the land. *"O God, when You went out before Your people"* — as in the wilderness of Sinai, and the journey of the pious and the goodness of the King of Glory. And our Sages, may their memory be blessed, explained this regarding Mount Moriah, and regarding the chariots, and all the other kings — they drove away, refused, and were confounded and bewildered. That is to say, as one who walks before them — life and peace; their wars are now of a natural kind.

*"When You marched through the wilderness"* — that desolate place. And so it is written: "And you journeyed from Horeb and went before your people through that great and terrible wilderness" toward the hill country of the Amorites. And to say grace was upon us by His kindness until Mount Moriah, etc. And to say that it belongs to it by the grace of God's word, etc.

*"The earth shook"* — like the end of Your dread, and they fled, etc. *"The heavens also dripped before God"* — by way of parable, from the wisdom resting upon the lightnings. And there are those who say they came drop by drop. And likewise, after the conclusion, etc., and wisdom outside — and there are those who base the foundation of judgment upon the clarity of creation upon the lightnings.

*"This Sinai"* — as in "From this Sinai, the chariot of the God of Israel." And there are interpreters who understand this verse as being directed toward the giving of the Torah. And this Sinai: for both "the earth shook" and "the heavens dripped" also occurred, with a touch of grace, on the day of the giving of the Torah.

*"A generous rain"* — because it was said that their souls departed when the Lord spoke the lightnings — from the opposite of this: *"You poured out, O God, a generous rain."* According to the lightnings, You poured drops, etc. — and may Hezekiah be strengthened. *"And You, You established it in its weariness"* — that is to say, strong and complete — for the lightnings in grace beneath it, etc. And what comes from the good stored up for the son — they shall dwell in Your goodness, etc. *"For the poor, O God"* — *"The Lord gave the word"* — the women who proclaimed it, they inclined, etc., and poured out a rain of blessing.

And the words of the poet are directed toward the foundation. And would that it were right.

*"The lips"* <note>Referring to "the sheepfolds" (שְׁפַתַּיִם), interpreted here as "lips."</note> — they are the diggers. And in *"spreading"* it — according to the ships upon them, the sacrifices. *"And her pinions with shimmering gold"* — water in the power of knowledge coming from the thought of gold. And gold is called *charutz* <note>original: "חָרוּץ" — meaning "incised" or "refined gold."</note>. And likewise: "and *charutz* like the mud of the streets." And the meaning of *charutz* is branches of goodness — and refined gold is green-yellow. <note>In medieval Hebrew color terminology, pure refined gold was described as having a greenish-yellow hue.</note> To say: the Torah in the lower place and the garment in grace. Likewise "all multitude of peoples" — he should have said "all peoples many." <note>These are grammatical observations about Hebrew word order, where the adjective follows the noun unusually.</note>

*"When the Almighty scattered kings in it"* — *"when He scattered"* is a poetic matter, as in "Judah spread out" — and as in "and when spreading garments." And the meaning of "in it" — in Jerusalem. *"It snowed on Zalmon"* — and this is the atonement of the stripping of the kingship; it snowed like the evening snow in the wilderness in grace, it snowed. An intransitive verb. And from the opening of the goodness — the robber shall sacrifice and the grace against the Lord — on Zalmon, in darkness, as in "in the shadow of death." <note>original: "בְּצַלְמוּת" — shadow of death, cognate with Zalmon.</note>

*"The mountain of God"* — even today praised to every mountain to return the sound — a mountain like the servant in that wilderness, and a place of Horeb, and the house of the Lord — a mountain of lilac, there was the mountain of entanglement, for the glory rested upon it.

*"The mountain of Bashan"* — it is praised in might, for Bashan is a place of fatness and richness and a place of pasture. Like an abyss, by way of parable, regarding the attachments and the possessions — the fruits of the observation. And to say: companions of the belly — its border.

To each and every mountain, mouths to it — the high gift, each and every one according to what was established. And likewise singular with plural.

*"Why do you look with envy?"* — as is precise in Spain <note>A reference to the Sephardic grammatical tradition, meaning the Spanish school of Hebrew grammarians.</note> and in [its] power. And similar to them. And to say further: the mountain of power for the many, like the essence of desire and time. And all of them are the obligation of good life, like the Temple Mount. Therefore He desired.

*"Why do you look with envy?"* Some interpret *"teratzedon"* <note>original: "תְּרַצְדוּן" — an unusual verb, interpreted variously as "to leap," "to envy," or "to spy."</note> as "you dance."
