# Psalms

<column-break/>

<margin>Depths</margin>
...and His people for His sake, Selah. Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears our burden; the God who is our salvation. <note>original: "selah"</note> To God the Lord belong the escapes from death. But God will crush the head of His enemies, the hairy scalp of him who walks in his guilt. The Lord said: “I will bring them back from Bashan; I will bring them back from the depths of the sea, so that you may bathe your feet in blood, and the tongues of your dogs may have their portion from your enemies.” They have seen Your processions, O God, the processions of my God, my King, in holiness. The singers went before, the musicians followed after, among the maidens playing timbrels.
<margin>Exalt</margin> In congregations, bless God, the Lord, from the fountain of Israel. There is Benjamin, the youngest, <margin>Zebulun</margin> ruling them; the princes of Judah in their throng; the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali. Your God has commanded your strength; <margin>Their pit</margin> strengthen, O God, that which You have done for us. From Your temple at Jerusalem, kings will bring gifts to You. <margin>They desire</margin> Rebuke the beast of the reeds, the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples, till everyone submits himself with pieces of silver; scatter the peoples who delight in war. Princes shall come out of Egypt; Cush <note>Cush refers to ancient Ethiopia/Nubia.</note> shall hasten to stretch out her hands to God.

<column-break/>

He supports us and adds to our deliverance, command upon command, and He is our savior and our support forever. The God who is strengthened and saves; and from before God the Lord, through the Torah, in joy, comes the beginning of death and the departure of the soul at our end. Truly, God will break the head of His enemies, He will break the scalp of the man who walks in his sins. The righteous are destined to be gathered from the house of Bashan; God said, "I will bring them back, I will bring back the righteous who were choked in the depths of the sea." Because they loved Your salvation, You saved Samson, and they were bathed in the blood of the Philistines; the tongue of the wild beasts shall be fattened by the fat of the enemies. The House of Israel saw the processions of Your Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> upon the sea; O God, they said, "The processions of God my King, the Eternal, are in holiness." The singers went first and recited the song after Moses and Aaron, who were playing music in the assembly in the midst of the righteous women who were with Miriam, playing timbrels. In the assembly, bless God; praise the Lord, you who were formed in the womb of the mother of Israel. There was Benjamin, the youngest of the tribes, who descended first into the sea to sing; the pious and chosen ones, Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, emerged, and the tribes were amazed. The stones and the leaders who built their daughters were the princes of Zebulun and the princes of Naphtali. God has commanded your strength; be strong, O God, for You have performed this for us in this Holy Temple. From Your Temple which You shall build in Jerusalem, where Your Divine Presence rests, kings shall bring You offerings. Rebuke the camp of the guilty who are like the wild beast of the reeds, the assembly of the mighty who trust in the calf-idol of the nations; her desire is for the business of spears, but by the knowledge of the Torah, which is pure as silver, He scatters the nations that do not desire the battle of the righteous. The sons of Egypt shall come as dignitaries to convert; the sons of Cush shall run to spread out their hands in prayer before God.

***

**And His people.** <note>Referring to v. 20</note> Our explanation of this word is similar to "He loads the donkey," meaning He provides for us daily. **And He did for him.** This refers to a surrounding or turning back. It is interpreted according to the context. Some say it means "He will snatch away" or "He will hide," while others say "He will load us and add to our days." Blessed be He. **The God of salvations.** He is the one who provides escapes and saves us; He has many ways to save us from the clutches of death through various deeds. It is like the one who finds a treasure in this sea, or the dust of a king. It refers to the kings of Bashan, or perhaps it intends that the final salvation will be for the living. As it is said regarding the heavens, they were like a warning for the inhabitants of the land. So too is the blow against the mockers and the spiders in the heavens. And there are many other such examples. **God will crush.** This refers to the judgment of God. For who can stand against His deeds? For in a single night, an angel struck a hundred and eighty-five thousand <note>A reference to the biblical account of the destruction of the Assyrian army outside Jerusalem.</note>. God prepared this judgment for a person who does not understand anything. **The hairy scalp.** The scalp is the part that divides the hair. Therefore it says "hairy scalp," for He will crush the head and the hair of the head which is long and wild. And God will cause white hairs to sprout upon the head for evil or for the "Hazar" plague <note>Likely a reference to a specific type of skin disease or plague.</note>. Just as it says "and on the crown of the head of the one distinguished among his brothers" in the blessing, and "evil on his scalp." **Who walks in his guilt.** One who is weary; he who wanders in his guilt and wickedness and does not repent. **The Lord said.** The Lord said He would return them from Bashan and raise them up, just as one is returned from the depths of the sea. This means He will not let those who drowned in the sea escape. This is what the king wrote, and it is entirely for the dead. The matter is significant regarding the "Galgal" <note>The cycle or the region of the Galilee.</note> because that was the beginning of the war of the King of Assyria against Israel. For the King of Assyria took all that land. And the end of his wars was this year at Jerusalem, where they all died. **So that you may bathe your foot in blood.** This is a term for crushing or treading, like "treading the winepress" or from the "multitude of garments." **The tongue of your dogs from the enemies.** The meaning of the verse is: so that your foot may be reddened with the blood of the kings of the enemies. That is to say, they will spread out like water, and the dogs will lick it, and the foot that walks upon it will be soaked in blood. Thus "your foot" and "your dog" are directed at Israel. It mentions blood like wine... with your foot from the blood of the Egyptians. Wine is like the blood of the grape. And all the kingdom... and the word "blood" is placed next to "tongue of your dogs." Many examples of this exist, like "He saw the end" or "He saw from upon the back." It says "blood of the tongue" because it is close to the licking of the dogs from the blood of the enemies. This is an additional clarification, for it already said "from the enemies." It uses the singular "from him" <note>Hebrew: minnehu</note> referring to the King of Assyria. This is correct, for he was the head who died in the plague. **They have seen Your processions.** Israel saw, when they saw the plague of the enemies, Your processions. These are the processions of God, the ways of the Divine Presence returning to Jerusalem. And these processions were like those of my King in the Sanctuary. As it is written: "And all Your strength was revealed in the camp of Assyria." **The singers went before.** The poets who were in Israel. As it says, "He went out to meet them with instruments and with the joy of the soul." Or, the singers and musicians among the maidens playing timbrels. The order of the procession was like that found in the story of Miriam the prophetess, who took the timbrel in her hand. **After the musicians.** This means "and after." Like "from the sun to the moon." **In congregations, bless.** In the gatherings of the people. **From the fountain of Israel.** Bless the Lord, all who come from the fountain of Israel, meaning the descendants of Jacob. **There is Benjamin.** There Benjamin and Judah were in the days of Hezekiah. Regarding these tribes, it is said that the other tribes were exiled in the days of Hoshea, but these remained. Thus "Benjamin the youngest" is mentioned. And the King of Assyria came to remember those of Hezekiah. And then it mentions the "princes of Zebulun and princes of Naphtali," for they remained in the land after the tribes were exiled, and they were a remnant in the land. Also in the days of Josiah it was so, as it says in Chronicles. The princes of Zebulun and Naphtali came to Jerusalem to offer. And the princes of Judah from all places were there, and Benjamin as well. And **their throng** <note>Hebrew: rigmatam</note> means their gathering. That is, they were all gathered in Jerusalem. And Benjamin is called "youngest" because he was the smallest tribe. The term "ruling them" <note>Hebrew: rodem</note> means he was in charge. That is to say, Benjamin was in charge of the building. And the people of the land were with him. And Benjamin and Judah came together. **Your God has commanded your strength.** This means power in a general way. Or, regarding Hezekiah, it says that this strength and boldness were given to you by God. Therefore, strengthen it and say, **"Strengthen, O God, that which You have done for us."** You have done these miracles for us. **From Your Temple.** Upon Jerusalem. Some explain this as being in the place of the House. Thus it says "the Sanctuary of God." That is, from Your Temple where the Glory dwells over Jerusalem, from the time it was saved from the enemy, the cities of Judah were strengthened. Therefore, kings will bring gifts to You. **Rebuke the beast of the reeds.** This refers to the group of the wicked. It is a metaphor for a king. The "beast of the reeds" refers to those who act like wild animals. **The herd of bulls.** They were like the calves of the peoples, until they were humbled. **Submitting himself with pieces of silver.** The meaning is that the silver was crushed. That is, those nations who were eager for war. **Scatter.** Like "spread out." The "beast" is like a "congregation." Like a herd of bulls that fight with their heads. **Submitting.** Like "trampling." **Calves of the peoples.** These are the kings and princes, compared to calves who follow the great bulls. **Princes shall come.** These are the nobles and the great ones. As we saw from our gift, for they brought a gift. And many interpret this regarding the war of Cush and Egypt against the Assyrian who besieged Jerusalem. And here in the text it says Israel went out and took spoil. **Princes shall come.** Regarding this it says in the book of Egypt, Cush, and Seba. And Assyria shall labor... in the book of Cush. And Egypt... they shall bow down to you and pray to you. For whoever took it to heart gathered people. And they shall be one with the land of Egypt, a beautiful and many-peopled witness. And all of them... they shall bring to the Lord. And so the herd of horses... and after this, he concludes the song.

# Psalms

<column-break/>

O God, when You went out in the pillar of cloud and in the pillar of fire before Your people, in their flight through the desert of Jeshimon <note>original: "Jeshimon"—a word for a desolate wasteland or wilderness</note> for eternity. The earth shook, and even the heavens dropped the dew of life before the Lord; this Sinai rose in smoke like a furnace before the presence of God, the God of Israel. You brought down a rain of generosity upon Your decree; <note>This refers to the "Dew of Resurrection" mentioned in Jewish legend.</note> their souls fled from within their bodies because they heard the Divine Word, but You raised them up with the hidden secrets of Your favor, O God, upon Your inheritance. And the assembly that had grown faint, You restored them. You brought back Your living creatures to dwell in it; in Your goodness, You prepared the angels to do good for the poor, O God. The Lord gave the words of the Torah to His people, but Moses and Aaron were the ones proclaiming the Word of God to the great host of Israel. Kings with their armies were uprooted from their palaces, and the wise were uprooted from their studies, while the assembly of Israel divided the ornaments of the sun. <note>An interpretive reference to Israel taking the spoils of their enemies.</note> If you sleep between the borders, the forge of Israel—which is like a dove covered by the clouds of glory—divides the house of Egypt, and the enemies who are pure as silver; their limbs are filled with gold. Then, the Almighty spread out the kings in that land, and a song shone forth like the snow descending upon Mount Zalmon.

<column-break/>

God settles the lonely in a home; He leads out prisoners into prosperity; but the rebellious dwell in a parched land. O God, when You went out before Your people, when You marched through the wilderness, Selah. The earth quaked, the heavens also dropped rain at the presence of God; even Sinai itself at the presence of God, the God of Israel. You, O God, sent a plentiful rain; You confirmed Your inheritance when it was weary. <margin>As its wings</margin> Your flock dwelt there; You, O God, provided from Your goodness for the poor. The Lord gave the word; the women who proclaim the news are a great army. Kings of armies flee, they flee! And she who waits at home divides the spoil. <margin>They flee</margin> Though you lie among the sheepfolds, you shall be like the wings of a dove covered with silver, and her feathers with shimmering gold. <margin>Sheepfolds</margin> <margin>And her pinions</margin> When the Almighty scattered kings in it, it was as white as snow in Zalmon. A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan; <margin>In scattering</margin> a mountain of many peaks is the mountain of Bashan. Why do you look askance, O many-peaked mountains, at the mountain which God has desired for His abode? Yes, the Lord will dwell there forever. The chariots of God are myriads, thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them as in Sinai, in the Holy Place. You have ascended on high, You have led captivity captive; You have received gifts among men, even from the rebellious, that the Lord God might dwell there. Blessed be the Lord day by day...

---

O God, by Your decree [their souls] fled, etc. Moses said: When Israel heard the first Commandment, their souls fled from them. <note>A common Midrashic theme: the Israelites died from the intensity of hearing God's voice and were resurrected.</note> And the secrets of favor You raised, O God, upon Your inheritance, etc. And the assembly of Israel that was weary, You restored it. Your flock You brought back into it, etc. Moses said: I thought that God would choose to dwell entirely on a grand mountain, but I saw that Sinai is a humble mountain, and the Lord accepted its nature, resting His Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> upon it. The Lord gives the words of the Torah to His people, but Moses and Aaron, etc. And the kings with their armies were uprooted, etc. And the assembly of Israel divided the ornaments of the sun. If you sleep between the borders, etc. The forge of Israel, which is like a dove covered in clouds of glory, divides the house of Egypt, their enemies who are like pure silver and their limbs are full of gold, then the Almighty spread the kings, etc. Blessed be the Lord day by day, who bears our burden.

---

**God settles the lonely in a home:** Those who were solitary, etc. **He leads out prisoners into prosperity <note>original: "kosharot"</note>:** "Prosperity" refers to the time of the month of Nisan, <note>The Hebrew month of the Exodus, coinciding with spring.</note> which is a "fitting" (kosher) time to go out. Moses said: When Israel heard the first Word, their soul fled from them, etc. And the secrets of the same, You raised, O God, upon Your inheritance. **And she who waits at home divides the spoil:** This means the women who stay in the home divide the booty with the men who go out to the army. **The wings of a dove covered with silver:** The Assembly of Israel is compared to a dove whose wings are coated in silver. **When the Almighty scattered kings in it, it was as white as snow in Zalmon:** Like snow falling on Mount Zalmon. **A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan:** A high mountain with many peaks. **Why do you look askance, O many-peaked mountains:** Why do you boast, you other mountains, over the lowly Mount Sinai? **The Lord will dwell there forever:** The Holy One, blessed be He, chose Sinai for the giving of the Torah. **The chariots of God are myriads, thousands upon thousands:** The chariots of angels, etc. **You have ascended on high, You have led captivity captive:** This refers to Moses, who ascended to the heavens to bring down the Torah.

# Psalms

<margin>
Depths
</margin>

God is a burden-bearer for us, the God of our salvation—Selah. The Almighty is to us a God of various salvations; to God, the Lord, belong the escapes from death. But God will crush the head of His enemies, the hairy crown of the one who walks in his guilt. The Lord said: "I will bring them back from Bashan <note>Bashan: a fertile, mountainous region known for its mighty bulls and oaks; here it symbolizes a place of hiding or a former battlefield.</note>; I will bring them back from the depths of the sea, so that your foot may be bathed in blood, and the tongue of your dogs may have its portion from the enemies." They have seen Your processions, O God—the processions of my God, my King, into the Sanctuary. The singers went before, the musicians followed after, among the maidens playing tambourines. At this time, He adds His commandments upon us—mighty commandments—He who is our redemption and our helper forever. The God who is our support and redemption, from before whom come the departures of sickness and death, and the exit of the soul into the afterlife. <note>The Aramaic "Sarsankia" refers to the departure or transition of the soul.</note> Truly, God will strike the head of His enemies, the hair of the man who walks in his sins. The righteous who died and were eaten by the beasts of the field—the Lord said: "I will bring them back from Bashan; I will bring back the righteous who were drowned in the depths of the sea." This is so that the punishment of the wicked may be struck, and you shall be soaked in the blood of the slain, the tongue of the wild beasts from their destruction, which shall be from the enemies who carried them away. The House of Israel saw the movements of Your Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"—the Divine Presence</note> upon the sea, O God; You commanded the movements of God, Your King, for all eternity in holiness. The singers came first, followed by the camps, and last were the musicians with drums, in the midst of the righteous women who, like Miriam, played tambourines. In groups, bless God the Lord,

---

You who passed through the sea, who are of the people of Israel. There is Benjamin, the smallest among the tribes, who from the beginning descended into the sea; for this reason, he received the kingship from the start. And in the end, those of the house of Judah descended, and the nations pelted them with stones; <note>This refers to a traditional Midrash where the tribes argued over who would jump into the Red Sea first; Benjamin jumped, while Judah's princes stood by.</note> they took the leadership after them, the heaps of the house of Judah, heap after heap. God has commanded your strength; be strong, O God, who dwells in the Sanctuary, for what You have done for us. From Your Temple, which receives the offerings above Jerusalem where Your Presence dwells—at their request, kings shall bring You offerings. Rebuke the camps of the guilty wicked who are like the reeds of a nest, the assembly of giants who trust in the calves of the nations. His delight is in the people who occupy themselves with the Torah, which is purer than silver; He scatters the nations who desire the benefit of war. Nobles like the colors of burning bronze <note>original: "Ostamchi"—a term for refined or precious metal</note> shall come from Egypt, those who were circumcised in the past; the property of the Ethiopians shall come to spread out their hands in prayer before God.

---

**He carries us:** Our Father-in-law <note>This is a play on the word "Hatanu" (our Father-in-law/our protector).</note>—He gathers us to Himself every day. It is like the word for "melting," or a path that is not closed off. And He doubles His blessings or His dwellings, and the prayer is offered before Your deeds. Or: our fruits He gathers, like our sustenance from wherever they are. Our God shall carry the burden of our salvation every single day. The Almighty is to us a God of salvation. Even to the Lord belong the "outlets of death." That is to say, He has many ways to bring someone out from the power of death, or to put the guilty to death and destroy them. As it is written: some die from snakes, or from the plague of the mice in the field. There are many such paths. **But God:** God is the one who will strike; He will be seen in His actions. For in a single night, at one moment, He struck the camps of a hundred and eighty-five thousand. God, with a single blow, strikes the head of His enemies with the sword and pestilence. **The hairy crown:** This refers to the hair of the head. It says "the hair of the crown" because your pride is your head. Or it means the hair that grows on the right and the left. The crown signifies the very top of the head, and this refers to the pride of the wicked. **Who walks in his guilt:** He who strengthens himself in his way, who walks in his sins and wickedness and does not turn back from them. **The Lord said:** The enemy that you fear, I will bring him back to his place, as it was with the king of Assyria who came from the depths of the sea. I will bring back the sinners; even from far away, from the king of Assyria and the kings of Persia. Mention is made of Bashan because it is in the path of the wilderness; Sennacherib brought his camp from there to conquer the whole land, and the end of his journey was at Jerusalem, and there they all died. **So that your foot may be bathed in blood:** You shall trample. It is like turning over, or from the sound of waves. **The tongue of your dogs from the enemies:** The meaning is that your dogs will lick the blood of the enemies. That is, the dead corpses will be eaten by the dogs, and the tongue of the dogs will be stained with blood. **They have seen Your processions:** Israel saw Your judgments upon these enemies. They realized that Your processions were leading before them to destroy their foes. These were the "processions of my God," the King of the universe, from His holy place. **The singers went before:** Those who sang in the camps. The musicians followed behind, and in the middle were the maidens with tambourines. Just as Miriam took the tambourine in her hand at the sea. **In assemblies, bless God:** This is a call to everyone in our community. **From the fountain of Israel:** All those who come from the source of Israel, like those who were in the womb of Jacob. **There is Benjamin, the youngest:** Benjamin and Judah were the princes of the tribes. Even though Benjamin was the smallest tribe, he led them into the sea first. The princes of Zebulun and Naphtali are mentioned because they came to Jerusalem to help, just as the princes of Judah and Benjamin did. **Ruling them:** Benjamin was like a leader among them. The men of the tribe were a great force. This refers to the blessing and the praise given by all the princes of the tribes when they bless God in the assemblies of the people. Our Sages also interpreted this verse as referring to Israel when they crossed the sea. **Your God has commanded your strength:** This is addressed to Israel generally, or to King Hezekiah. It means: be strong against your enemy. Thus, they all give thanks and say, "O God, You have done this for us." **From Your Temple:** Some interpret this as "because of Your Temple." Because of Your glory that dwells in Jerusalem, the enemy was struck. Therefore, kings will bring You gifts; they will recognize that this salvation came to Israel from Your glory. **Rebuke the wild beast of the reeds:** This is a rebuke of the nations. The "wild beast of the reeds" refers to a king who is like a beast hiding in the reeds. He rebukes the company of the mighty until they bring silver as tribute. **He scatters the nations:** Those who desire war. He scatters them like chaff. **Nobles shall come:** These are the messengers and ambassadors. As we find in the days of Hezekiah, they brought gifts from Egypt and Ethiopia to Jerusalem. In the future, even more nations will bring their hands in prayer to God. They will realize that there is no other God but the God of Israel.

Kingdoms of the earth, praise before the Lord; sing to the Lord forever! These matters turn to the traditions of the Sanhedrin <note>The supreme rabbinic court of ancient Israel</note> who go out from the camp of the tribes until they sustain me, like a vessel that is hidden over the soul. I have sunk into the exile like this, until it troubles me like a vessel hidden over the body. I have sunk in the exile and there is no standing; I have come into deep waters and the current has swept me away. They who hate me without cause are more than the hairs of my head; my lying enemies, who would destroy me, are mighty; then I restored what I did not steal. For for Your sake I have borne reproach; shame has covered my face. I have become a stranger to my brothers, and an alien to my mother's children. For zeal for Your house has consumed me, and the reproaches of those who reproach You have fallen on me. I wept in the fasting of my soul, and it became a reproach to me. I made sackcloth my clothing, and I became a proverb to them. They who sit in the gate talk about me, and I am the song of the drunkards. But as for me, let my prayer be to You, O Lord, at an acceptable time; O God, in the abundance of Your mercy, answer me in the truth of Your salvation. Let not the water-flood overwhelm me, nor the deep swallow me up, and let not the pit shut its mouth upon me. Answer me, O Lord, for Your mercy is good; turn to me according to the multitude of Your tender mercies. And hide not Your face from Your servant, for I am in trouble; answer me speedily.

# For the conductor, upon the "Lilies," of David: Save me,
O God, for the waters have come up to my soul. I sink in deep mire where there is no standing; I have come into deep waters, and the flood overflows me. I am weary with my crying, my throat is parched; my eyes fail <margin>Waiting/Hoping</margin> while I wait for my God. More than the hairs of my head are those who hate me without cause; mighty are those who would destroy me, being my enemies wrongfully; what I did not steal, I then restored. O God, You know my foolishness, and my sins are not hidden from You. Let not those who wait for You, O Lord God of Hosts, be ashamed through me; let not those who seek You be brought to dishonor through me, O God of Israel. Because for Your sake I have borne reproach; confusion has covered my face. <margin>Confusion</margin> I have become a stranger to my brothers and an alien to my mother's children. For zeal for Your house has consumed me, and the reproaches <margin>Stranger</margin> of those who reproach You have fallen on me. When I wept and chastened my soul with fasting, that was to my reproach. I made sackcloth also my garment, and I became a proverb to them. They who sit in the gate talk of me; and I was the song <margin>Drunkards</margin> of the drunkards. But as for me, my prayer is to You, O Lord, in an acceptable time; O God, in the multitude of Your mercy, answer me in the truth of Your salvation. Deliver me out of the mire, and let me not sink; let me be delivered from those who hate me, and out of the deep waters. Let not the water-flood overflow me, neither let the deep swallow me up, and let not the pit shut her mouth upon me. Answer me...

<column-break/>

<meta>catchword: Answer me</meta>

---

**Kingdoms of the earth.** This means when this kingdom reigns <unclear>ss</unclear>. **To Him who rides upon the highest heavens of old.** "Highest heavens" is like the heavens of heavens, and "of old" refers to the uppermost celestial sphere that encompasses everything, which is called *Arabot* <note>The seventh and highest heaven in Jewish cosmology</note>. And it says "of old" because the heavens have stood from the beginning. **Behold, He sends out His voice, a mighty voice.** He places all voices within His voice, which is the definition of a "mighty voice." **Ascribe strength.** Give strength to God; this voice is the meditation, for by His strength He gives power to all through their might and the strength of their hands. **His majesty is over Israel, and His strength is in the skies.** <unclear>v'z ych ch ych</unclear> The joy is like a shepherd's strength over our people, acting for the good of our strength. That is to say, just as His choice is expressed in the glory of strength, so His glory and majesty are over our strength and His rest is upon Israel. For their strength is in the skies, which are the mighty clouds. **From Your holy places.** Because it comes from the honored place and the throne of glory. **He dwells in Israel;** His glory is upon them and from His sanctuaries. It is written "Your sanctuaries" <note>original: "מקדשיך"</note> with a *yod* to indicate the plural, because the sanctuary below is aligned exactly with the sanctuary above, which is aligned with the Divine Glory. For this reason, the glory of the heavens called it the plurality of "Your sanctuaries," for the sanctuary includes the Levites, the Courtyard, the Temple, and the Inner Sanctum. **The God of Israel is He who gives strength and power to the people.** The use of the definite article <note>the "He" in "He who gives"</note> points to specific knowledge—namely, the "known people," which is Israel <unclear>pul chalom</unclear>. For this matter, it is fitting for everyone to learn: **Blessed be God!** Some explain that this whole Psalm refers to the future during the war of **Gog and Magog** <note>The apocalyptic battle mentioned in Ezekiel</note>, and I have written in my poverty what I have written about it.

# For the Conductor
**Upon the Lilies, of David.** This Psalm is said in the language of the **Exile** (*Galut*). It is spoken in the singular voice as a general rule, and in it, every individual in exile prays and weeps over their troubles. **Save me, O God, for the waters have come up to my soul.** Until the moment they are all choked; that is, close to death. He compares the exile to drowning in a deep mire. He compares the troubles to sudden waters that reach up to the neck to choke one to death. **I sink in deep mire.** Like being inside a pit. To say **where there is no standing** means the depths are so deep that there is no place to stand, for I have sunk in the mire. **I have come into deep waters, and the flood overflows me.** The "flood" (*shibbolet*) refers to the current or the gathering of waters. In deep waters, there are waves that gather, and the flood of the river has swept me away. All this is a hint to the exile and the strengthening of the blows. **I am weary with my crying, my throat is parched.** I am exhausted from screaming until my throat is parched. The word "parched" (*nachar*) is a verb meaning "burned" or "dried out." **My eyes fail while waiting for my God.** Because of the drowning, I lift my eyes upward in hope and waiting. He mentions "waiting for my God" until his eyes fail from looking upward. This is a metaphor for the length of the exile. **More than the hairs of my head are those who hate me without cause.** He says the number of those who hate the singer is greater than his hair. They hate me and accuse me of stealing. This refers to the many enemies in the exile. **Mighty are those who would destroy me.** My enemies are numerous and strong <unclear>ss ss</unclear>. **What I did not steal, I then restored.** Meaning, they accuse me of theft and I must restore what I did not take. **Let not those who wait for You be ashamed.** This is a prayer that the faithful should not be embarrassed by the delay of salvation. He mentions "God of Hosts" because He is the Judge of the heavenly powers. **I have become a stranger... an alien to my mother's children.** This refers to his own people or neighboring nations who treat him as an outsider because of his suffering. **For zeal for Your house has consumed me.** Because I suffer the reproach of the exile for Your sake. If I had wanted to leave Your faith and join theirs, I would have been as great as one of them. **I wept in the fasting of my soul.** I am constantly crying and fasting. **And it became a reproach to me.** My very devotion to You is used by them to mock me, saying: "Where is your God?" **I became a proverb.** My name is used as a standard for disgrace. **They who sit in the gate talk about me.** They mock me in their public gatherings. **But as for me, let my prayer be to You... at an acceptable time.** I pray that eventually, there will be a "time of favor" when my prayer is accepted and I am delivered from exile. **Answer me in the truth of Your salvation.** In the abundance of Your kindness, answer me. **Deliver me from the mire.** He repeats the request "let me not sink," whereas earlier he said "I have sunk." This is to ask that he not stay in the exile forever. **From those who hate me and out of the deep waters.** He mentions the enemies and the depths together. **Let not the water-flood overflow me.** Meaning, do not let me be buried in this exile. Let not the pit "shut its mouth," meaning let there be an exit from this state. **Answer me, O Lord...**

### Commentary Section

<margin>172</margin>
**Answer me, O Lord, for Your lovingkindness is good.** Your kindness is inherently good, and it should not be withheld from me. In the abundance of Your mercies, turn to me. **And do not hide.** This is like the previous phrase "turn to me." It follows the way of prayer: "Who is strong like You?" My prayer is turned away from me, and because I lack a friend, I need "answer me, answer me quickly." **Draw near to my soul.** Draw near my soul because Your mercy is as abundant as Your glory revealed.
**Redeem it.** Redemption for the soul. **Because of my enemies.** So they will not say that there is no help or salvation for me. **You know.** He mentions his reproach as a general category for all types of shame. **Before You.** For nothing is hidden from You. The meaning of "all my adversaries" is that You see them and their thoughts, which I cannot see. **Reproach.** And I am sick. The grammatical form is *v'anushah* <note>meaning "and I was desperate"</note>.
The heart is broken from the blow. This is like a man who is sick and seeks a place to rest. **I looked for sympathy, but there was none.** I hoped there would be someone to feel for me and lament my state, but there was none. This is the language of salvation, and I said "for comforters" as a plural form to show that even among many, none were found. **They gave me gall.** In my food. From the word *barut* <note>food or sustenance</note>. Or it refers to a bitter herb. They put bitterness in my food.
**They gave gall and vinegar in my food.** Or like one who is thirsty and they give him vinegar, which increases the thirst rather than quenching it. **Let their table.** Parallel to "in my food." **And their peace-offerings a trap.** What they intended for peace shall become a snare to them. **Let their eyes be darkened.** The eyes of the congregation should be darkened so they cannot see their path. And likewise, "pour out my wrath upon them." When they cannot see, their legs will stumble.
Or it refers to their loins and their strength. For the strength of a person's life is in the loins, which is the source of power. And likewise, "afterwards you will find his loins trembling from his pain." **Pour out Your indignation.** And it shall overtake them and finish them. **Let their encampment.** Their palaces. **For You.** For it was not because of their own righteousness that they did this evil. Rather, they saw that You had no desire for me, so they persecuted me.
**And they speak of the pain of those You have wounded.** This is like saying "they added to the pain." They tell each other about the wounds, saying to one another: "God has forsaken him, pursue and take him." They say these things to the wounded one to make him lose hope. **Add iniquity to their iniquity.** This means "measure for measure." Just as they added to my pain, add to their punishment. **And let them not come into Your righteousness.** This refers to the World to Come, as the next verse explains.
**Let them be blotted out from the book of life.** This verse is repeated in its theme; its meaning is that they should be blotted out from the count of the living in the World to Come. **But I am poor and pained.** And if I must die, let Your salvation set me on high. **I am poor.** In the exile. **Set me on high.** From the lowliness of my state. **I will praise the name of God with song.** When I am saved from the exile, I will offer a song and a sacrifice of thanksgiving. **And it shall please.** The prayer of praise will be better than the sacrifice of an ox or a bull.
Or he says that the prayer will be as if it were an ox. The text mentions "ox" (large) and "bull" (younger). **Horned and hooved.** This means the ox is fully grown and mature. The Midrash says that the ox Adam offered had horns that preceded its hooves, based on the word order "horned and hooved." They also said the ox had only one horn on its forehead. **The humble shall see.** The humble will see the salvation and rejoice, for they are the ones who look for salvation. They will recognize the greatness and say, "I have seen the low brought high."
And he said "seek God" because the mercy of God is upon the humble. **And let your heart revive.** This is like "my heart grew cold." Life and strength return to the heart, just as it says of Jacob, "the spirit of Jacob their father revived." **For the Lord hears.** For those in exile are the "needy" and "His prisoners." Even though they are prisoners of the nations, God considers them His own. The Levites would say "God hears the needy" while in exile. **Let heaven and earth praise Him.** Just as the sun and moon rejoice in the world.
As it says elsewhere, "Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice." He also mentions the sea and everything in it. **For God will save Zion.** When the nations are judged, Zion and the cities of Judah will be rebuilt. He mentions Judah because it is the primary kingdom. **And they shall dwell there.** To reside permanently. **And possess it.** From the root of inheritance. **And the seed of His servants.** They and their children will inherit it.
**For the leader... to bring to remembrance.** This psalm was recited when David was fleeing from Saul or Absalom. It is repeated here <note>Psalm 70 is almost identical to the end of Psalm 40</note> because it fits the theme of the surrounding psalms. **O God, to deliver me.** Hasten to rescue me. The repetition of the theme "hasten" and "deliver" is for emphasis.
**Let them be ashamed.** He repeats the theme in different words for emphasis. **Let them be turned back.** Let them retreat from their thoughts of pursuing me. When their thoughts fail, they will be ashamed. **Because of their shame.** Let them turn back because of the shame of their failed deeds. **Aha.** They used to say this when they saw me in distress. **Our right hand.** <note>Catchword for the next page</note>

->Quarter<- <note>Refers to a division of the book for study or liturgical reading</note>

**Let them rejoice and be glad.** This explains that those who seek You and love Your salvation will be sustained. **And let them say continually, "Let the Lord be magnified."** This means His greatness is constant for those who fear Him and increases through the many who seek refuge in Him. **But I am poor and needy.** David refers to himself this way because he was fleeing from the pursuit of his son Absalom.

**In You, O Lord, I have taken refuge.** At the beginning of this psalm, some commentators say it is connected to the psalm before it. David said this psalm when he was fleeing from his son Absalom. Furthermore, he says, **"Cast me not off in the time of old age."** This implies he was about seventy years old at the time. He says: Since I have taken refuge in You, I know I shall never be ashamed. **In Your righteousness.** Not because of my own merit, for David knew this trouble was a punishment for his previous sin <note>A reference to the matter of Bathsheba and the prophet Nathan's rebuke</note>, as it is written, "Behold, I will raise up evil against you out of your own house." **Be to me a rock of habitation.** Since he was exiled from his dwelling in Jerusalem by his son Absalom, he asks God to be his "rock of habitation" to protect him from his son. **You have given the command to save me.** Just as You have saved me many times in the past, so save me now. The sage Radak <note>Rabbi David Kimhi, a 13th-century grammarian and commentator</note> explains that this refers to the angels, as it is written: "For He shall give His angels charge over you, to keep you in all your ways." **My God, deliver me.** He calls Absalom "the wicked." **From the grasp of the unjust and ruthless man.** This refers to Ahithophel. "Ruthless" (chometz) is a metaphor for someone who is fermented or soured by sin. **For You are my hope.** I have known since my youth that You are my source of hope. **Upon You I have stayed myself from the womb.** Even in the womb, You prepared my sustenance. **You are He who took me.** Meaning, You are the one who brought me out from the womb. **My praise is continually of You.** Just as You are always watching over me to do me good. **I have been as a wonder to many.** Many people look at me in astonishment because they see how greatly I am punished, yet I still place my hope in You. Even though I am a "wonder" of suffering to the world, You are my strong refuge. The sage Radak explains "wonder" (mofet) as a sign; people were amazed that God would listen to him after his trials. **Let my mouth be filled with Your praise.** May my prayer be constant that You save me. **Cast me not off.** Now that I have reached old age and my strength is gone, do not abandon me. **For my enemies speak.** They speak about me, and those who "watch for my soul"—who were once my friends and guards—now take counsel together against me. Some say "watchers of my soul" refers to those lying in wait to do harm. **Saying, "God has forsaken him."** They believe that because his own son pursues him, God must have abandoned him. **Pursue and take him.** They encourage one another to capture him. **O God, be not far from me.** Just as they think You are far, show them You are near. **I will hope continually.** I will never stop hoping for Your salvation. **And will yet praise You more.** I will add to my songs of praise when You deliver me. **My mouth shall tell of Your righteousness.** Because Your salvations are constant, I cannot even count them; they are beyond "number" (seforot). **I will come with the mighty acts.** I do not come with my own strength, but with Yours. **O God, You have taught me from my youth.** This mentions that everything is from God. **And even unto old age and gray hairs.** Just as You did not abandon me until now, do not abandon me in my final years. **Until I have declared Your strength.** So that the next generation will know it was Your arm that saved me, not my own power. **Your righteousness also, O God, reaches unto high heaven.** Your greatness fills everything; who is like You? **You who have shown me many and sore troubles.** In the written text (Kethiv), this is plural ("shown us"), but it is read (Qere) in the singular ("shown me"). This suggests that while David speaks of himself, the text also refers to the collective experience of the Jewish people in exile. Just as David was pursued and then restored, so will Israel be brought back from the "depths of the earth" (the exile) to Jerusalem. **You will increase my greatness.** It will not be enough just to return me; You will make me even greater than before the trouble. **I will also praise You.** When You return us, I will praise You with the harp and lyre. This refers to the end of the exile, when God's truth will be recognized by all. **The Holy One of Israel.** For then His name will be sanctified through the redemption of Israel.

->Psalm 72<-
By the hand of Solomon, it was said in prophecy: O God, give the custom of Your judgment to the King Messiah, and Your righteousness to the son of King David. He shall judge Your people with righteousness and Your poor with the custom of justice. The inhabitants of the mountains shall carry peace for the house of Israel, and the hills through merit. He shall judge the poor of the people, he shall deliver the sons of the darkened ones, and shall weaken the crooked man. They shall fear You with the rising of the sun, and they shall be before You away from the moon, throughout the generations of generations. He shall come down like the favor of rain upon the grass that has been eaten by locusts, like the droplets of the late rain that drip upon the grass of the earth. In his days the righteous shall increase, and many shall be at peace until the moon-worshippers are finished. And he shall rule from the shore of the Great Sea to the shore of the Ocean, and from the Euphrates until the ends of the earth. Before him governors shall kneel, and his enemies shall lick the dust. The kings of the islands and provinces shall bring gifts, and the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer tribute. And all kings shall prostrate themselves to him, all nations shall be enslaved to him. For he shall deliver the impoverished who asks for help, and the poor for whom there is no helper. He shall spare the impoverished and the darkened, and the souls of the darkened he shall redeem.

From deceit and from plunder he shall redeem their souls, and their blood shall be precious before him. And he shall live, and he shall give to him from the gold of Sheba, and he shall pray on his behalf continually; all the day he shall bless him.

May it be. <note>This "May it be" (Yehi) acts as a concluding liturgical response.</note>

---

**My lips shall shout.** At the time that I sing to You, my lips and my soul shall rejoice as one. That is to say, his mouth and his heart are equal <note>This suggests total sincerity in prayer, where external speech matches internal intent.</note>. And so it says, "My heart and my flesh sing for joy to the living God." **Disgraced.** An expression of redemption or uncovering <note>The commentator is analyzing the root of the Hebrew word 'Hafar'.</note>... **My tongue also.** Since he mentioned the speech of the lips, he also mentioned the tongue, for external speech is attributed to the lips and the tongue. **For they are ashamed.** For they will be bent and will see and be disgraced.

# Of Solomon
**O God, give Your judgments.** David composed this psalm concerning his son Solomon when he made him king. And according to the fact that this entire psalm is a prophecy of David, so it shall be; for at the end of his days, he was writing with <term>Mammon</term> <note>Likely referring to wealth or royal resources</note> and no weak thing happened to him as is mentioned regarding him. And in this psalm are all his prayers and supplications, and the end of the book which is missing from here... for it is fitting to seal the book with the ways of Hallelujah. And because this supplication happened to him in a generation where a person would go out... And there are those who interpret this psalm regarding the **King Messiah**. And so "the righteous shall flourish like fruit." And the reason for the psalm being "for Solomon" is because it is hanging upon "righteousness and Your judgments," etc. Grant him knowledge and understanding to judge with justice and righteousness... **And Your righteousness.** Meaning, understanding. A king who is a son of a king will act as such, for the kingship was given to him and his father. And since in Your writing he shall rule, give him understanding... When they crowned Solomon on the throne of the Lord. And does it say to a man to sit on His throne? Rather, what is "on the throne of the Lord"? That he judged a judgment of truth without shame and without delay. As it is written regarding the King Messiah, so David prayed that He should give his son the wisdom to judge. **He shall judge Your people.** This matter returns to the leaders and the standing ones in blessing over the poor. **They shall bear.** There are those who say "they shall bear" is like a blessing upon the Kingdom of Israel, that they shall bear peace in [those] days... and so it was in the days of Solomon, and so it will be in the days of the King Messiah. And they shall be with Israel in righteousness... as it is written "if you follow My statutes... I will give your rains in their season." **He shall judge the poor of the people.** And behold, all seek peace and every person... find kingship for the world. As a person in his neighbor's vineyard, his neighbor says to him "what are you doing in my vineyard?" and they argue with one another. And since the provinces are kingdoms of goodness and peace in the world... as it says, "there was peace for Israel." And also regarding the Messiah... he will save from the oppressors... **Before the moon.** Forever. Meaning, they will continue to fear You as long as the sun and moon exist. This is a path of exaggeration <note>A rhetorical hyperbole often used in poetic prophecy.</note>. And some say this refers to the King Messiah, for in the days of the King Messiah the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the Lord. **He shall come down like rain upon the mown grass.** Like the grass that is cut. **Showers (Zarzif).** An expression of dripping or flowing. This king will come down upon the people for their rest and settlement like the rain that descends upon the cut grass to make it grow. And just as Solomon came in his time, for he was called Solomon (Shlomo) because there was peace (Shalom) in his days... and regarding the King Messiah, the days of Israel will be in great security and peace like no other. For Israel was like mown grass in exile, and in their peace they shall flourish and grow. **In his days shall the righteous flourish.** Meaning they will multiply. **Until the moon is no more.** Meaning as long as the moon exists. If this is about Solomon, it is an exaggeration. If it is about the King Messiah, it is literal. **From sea to sea.** Regarding Solomon, it is as was said of him that he ruled over all the side of the river. This refers to the Land of Israel... from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines. And it refers to the Land of Israel from the river onward... even unto the ends of the earth. And it says regarding Solomon that all the kings of the earth were afraid of him... and regarding the King Messiah, it is even truer, for his rule will be over the whole world. **Before him.** The "Tsiyim" <note>Desert dwellers or islanders</note>. Even those who are far away will kneel before him. **And his enemies.** They will want to be his supporters and will lick the dust from fear of him. **The kings of Tarshish.** Regarding Solomon, it is literal, for the kings of the earth brought him tribute. And regarding the King Messiah as well. **Eshkar.** Like a gift. They will bring it always. **All kings shall prostrate themselves.** This is clear, whether referring to Solomon or the Messiah. **For he shall deliver the needy.** Therefore all nations will prostrate to him and serve him, for they will see he is a righteous king who delivers the impoverished and the poor... **He shall spare.** He repeats the language to strengthen the matter... **From deceit and violence.** This refers to fraud and theft. **And their blood shall be precious in his sight.** The blood of the poor is precious to him, therefore he spares their souls and rescues them from the hand of the wicked so they do not spill their blood. **And may he live.** This is precious in the eyes of the Lord... **And may there be given to him.** Meaning may his name live. "And may he give to him of the gold of Sheba," meaning they will give him gold from their tribute... **And may prayer be made for him.** The poor will pray for the king always and bless him all day, meaning all his days.

May it be the end.

**May there be an abundance of grain.** In the days of this king <note>referring to the Messiah</note>, there will be a blessing in the world such that a man will sow a handful of grain on the tops of mountains and barren places by the sea, and by the power of the wind blowing through them, it will grow as tall as Lebanon. The literal meaning of "fruit" here refers to the yield of that handful of grain. **And they shall blossom from the city.** In the Talmud, the sages taught that blessing is not usually found in things that are easily counted. However, in both the city and the countryside, there will be such blessing that people will spring up from the city of Naveh like the grass of the earth. **May his name endure forever.** This refers to the king's name lasting eternally; he will be remembered for good because of his righteousness and greatness. **As long as the sun shines, his name shall increase.** The grammarians explain that the word <term>Yinnon<gloss>increase/endure</gloss></term> implies kingship and authority, while others say it implies continuity. Every usage of *Yinnon* suggests a name being firmly established, like a memorial. As long as the sun exists, his memory shall exist. **And they shall bless themselves by him.** Nations will bless themselves by mentioning him; all nations will praise him. They will say, "May we be blessed just like this king," similar to the blessing of Abraham: "By your offspring shall all the nations of the earth bless themselves." **Blessed be the Lord God of Israel.** This verse marks the conclusion of the second book. **Blessed be the Lord.** Just as we explained regarding Solomon's prayer. **The prayers of David are ended.** Since David directed his prayers toward his son Solomon, they are called the prayers of David his father. Or, the meaning is that all the prayers David prayed to God concerning the King Messiah are concluded. This is similar to the conclusion of the first book. Regarding the phrase "The prayers of David son of Jesse are ended": even though there are psalms attributed to Asaph, the sons of Korah, and Moses, David arranged them into the book. From here, the Sages deduced that every psalm with an attribution (like "A Psalm of David" or "To Asaph, a Psalm") was arranged by David into the heights of the Psalter. This particular psalm deals with the prosperity of the wicked in this world compared to the station of the righteous.

# Psalm 73
**Truly God is good to Israel, even to such as are of a clean heart.** This psalm is among the most profound in the Psalter, dealing with the misfortune of the righteous and the success of the wicked in this world. Asaph speaks to his own heart, asking why this is so. Similar themes are found in Job, Jeremiah, and the books of the prophets regarding the congregation of the righteous. Jeremiah said: "You are righteous, O Lord, when I complain to You; yet let me talk with You of Your judgments: Why does the way of the wicked prosper?" This verse begins with the goodness of God toward those with a "pure heart"—those who are sincere and do not act with deceit. Concerning this, David said: "Do good, O Lord, to those who are good and upright in their hearts." **But as for me, my feet were almost gone.** That is to say, my mind almost turned away from the path of God because I saw an upside-down world where the righteous suffer and the wicked prosper. He says "my feet were almost gone" like someone walking securely who is suddenly tripped by a burden. He uses the feminine form for "feet" <note>Hebrew: *natiyu*</note> and "steps" <note>Hebrew: *shupku*</note> because these body parts are grammatically feminine. **For I was envious of the mockers.** These are the fools who boast of their strength. They are the "fools" involved in worldly pleasures. He says the wicked were in such tranquility that they were like revelers, always in song and joy of heart. **When I saw the peace of the wicked.** For their tranquility in this world is what misled me to turn from the way of God, and I wonder at their great success. **For there are no pangs <note>hartzubot</note> at their death.** The older commentary explains that their death is not preceded by great suffering or agony. This comes from the term "shackles <note>hartzubot</note> of wickedness." Our rabbis interpreted the word as a compound of "free" <note>har</note> and "turned" <note>shav</note>, meaning they are not "turned" by fear or envy at their death because they do not die with a broken or sick heart. Instead, they remain healthy and enjoy the world until their last day. Instead of a difficult or strange death, they die in strength. **But their body is healthy.** Meaning their strength and standing are firm. Some explain *hartzubot* as a type of prophetic ailment, and *ulam* <note>body/strength</note> as a porch or hall of a house. **They are not in trouble as other men.** They do not suffer the toil and burdens that others endure throughout their lives; they do not feel the hardships of the world like the rest of their people. **Neither are they plagued like other folk.** They do not experience common human illnesses caused by sun, heat, or cold. No evil touches them. This is the opening of the psalm where Asaph begins to debate with his heart. **Therefore pride encompasses them as a chain.** Pride is to them like a necklace on the neck; they boast in their words and exalt themselves over other creatures. **Violence covers them as a garment.** Pride is like a cloak they wrap around their bodies, and all their words are violence. **Their eyes stand out with fatness.** Due to their great abundance and fat, their eyes bulge from their sockets, as their bodies are filled with grease. It is like a strong eye that is astonished by what it sees. This refers to their being wicked yet dwelling in pleasures higher than any heart's desire. Piety diminishes in their thoughts; their only intention is to gather wealth and worldly possessions. **They have more than heart could wish.** Often they gain even more than they imagined. One might expect to be wealthy and instead becomes exceedingly wealthy beyond his own thoughts. Because of this, they speak with a high tongue and all their thoughts are haughty. **They mock, and speak wickedly concerning oppression: they speak loftily.** They are powerful and great in their own words, despising everyone else. Their words are full of wickedness, and their tongues are strong. This was the beginning of the "slipping of the feet"—the feeling of distance from God. The word **mock** <note>yamiku</note> is related to "flesh decaying" <note>yimmaku</note>, suggesting that the words of the masters of death are empty. **They speak wickedly concerning oppression: they speak loftily.** They pursue their sins deeply and do not rely on the comforts of the Sages. **They set their mouth against the heavens.** Their pride has overwhelmed them; they speak against God as if their words were in heaven. **And their tongue walks through the earth.** They speak about everyone on earth, and no one stops them. They use their mouths to support their own opinions as they please. Therefore...

## 74
### A *Maskil* <note>term: "Maskil" - a musical or liturgical term, often interpreted as a "teaching" or "contemplative" poem</note> of Asaph. Why, O God, have You cast us off forever? Why does Your anger smoke against the sheep of Your pasture?

**Therefore His people return here.** "Return" is like "going back." Whenever their vision of wealth returns. The written form of "return" <note>original: "yashuv"</note> includes the letter *vav*. He says that the people who are weighed down in exile are oppressed by the multitude of the wicked, and they return with them to bitterness time after time. **Here** <note>original: "halom"</note> is like the phrase "do not draw near here." That is to say, they return in the exile of distress—Heaven forbid—to find themselves apparently destroyed by judgment. **And full waters are drained by them.** The intermediary is missing. It is like "a full cup of water." As in "they are fermented in the night." Against the nature of things. "To drain" is like "drinking." That is, a cup full of poisons will be drained by them, in the sense of drinking and striking. Some explain "here" as a root meaning "to strike," as in "the horse's hooves struck." That is, they are broken and struck by this matter. **And they say.** This is the claim that listeners argue all day to know what it is. **And they say.** They say, "How does God know the ways of human beings?" God forbid that He should know the ways of humans, for if He did, how could it be bad for those who follow His ways while He is good to those who deny Him and the wicked of the world? **And if there is knowledge in the Most High.** How could this be? **Behold, these are the wicked.** Behold, these are the wicked and all their wealth and honor is with them. **Surely in vain I have cleansed my heart.** My questions grew when I saw my own merit. I purified my heart and washed my hands in innocence. My heart is pure and my deeds are clean, yet I am in this poverty while the wicked are in goodness and success. **And I.** Good and bad are in the hands of the wicked. **All day.** Every day. **And every morning.** Constantly, every single morning. My rebuke and suffering are in their hands. **If I said.** This is what I said to tell of every generation in exile. **If I said I would speak thus.** This claim is as if the generation of Your children were guilty, then I would have betrayed You. This sentence is transposed; its meaning is: if I spoke like the generation of Your children, I would have betrayed You. Like "one who knows he should not tell the place of a grave." **And I thought.** My mind contemplated them, wondering why they are successful while I am broken. I thought to know what this was, but it was "toil" in my eyes, meaning in my heart. **Until I came.** I said in my heart to know this answer, and I was unable until I entered the thoughts of my heart and the knowledge of God. This refers to the sanctuaries of the priests and the heights, for there is the end of the grave and the permanent reward. For the good of this world is fleeting, but the World of Souls <note>term: "Olam ha-Neshamot" - the afterlife or the spiritual realm where souls exist after death</note> is where the good and the wicked are truly tested. This is what is meant by "I understood their end." **Surely You set them in slippery places.** After you taste the reason for their success in this world, it is like setting someone on a slippery path; it seems to him he is walking well, but in a tiny moment his feet will slip and he will fall into ruins. So too in this world, their success is only for a time, and like them, it will pass and vanish, and no good will remain for them in their end. This is why it says at the end "they are consumed by terrors." **How they are destroyed.** All who see them will wonder and say, "How did they become a desolation in a moment?" **Like a dream when one awakes.** Behold, they are like a dream, for upon waking, nothing remains of what was seen in the dream. As it says, "as when a hungry man dreams he is eating, but awakes with an empty soul." So the wicked now appear in their success, but they are gone in an instant. **In the city You shall despise their image.** It is clear that in this world they are tested through success, but the great blow comes in the World to Come. For the souls of the righteous will be in the "bundle of life," while the souls of the wicked will be punished within the body of the grave. As the scholar said regarding ruins. "In the city You shall despise their image" is similar to "despising." It means after the awakening in the "city of the dead," which refers to the wicked, their form will be despised. As the scripture says: "these to eternal life, and those to shame and eternal contempt."

---

### A Maskil of Asaph. Why, O God, have You cast us off forever? This psalm speaks of this current exile. It says: "Why, O God, have You cast us off forever," meaning the length of the exile is forever. **Your anger smokes.** For when a man is angry, heat and smoke seem to come from his nostrils. This is said about God as a metaphor.

Remember Your congregation which You acquired from of old, You redeemed the tribe of Your inheritance—this Mount Zion where You rested Your Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhintakh." In Jewish thought, this refers to the indwelling presence of God on earth.</note>.

**You divided the sea by Your strength; You broke the heads of the sea monsters upon the waters.**
**You crushed the heads of Leviathan; You gave him as food to the people, to the desert-dwellers.**

---

**Remember Your congregation which You purchased.** Just as You purchased them from Egypt, so merit them to be redeemed from this exile once more. The reason the word "purchased" is used is because they were slaves, and He took them from their masters and "bought" them for Himself. **The tribe of Your inheritance.** He mentions all the tribes together as one, for they were joined as one nation, and thus they are called the tribe <note>original: "shevet," which can mean tribe or staff.</note> called by His name. Or, to say Your inheritance is as if a measuring cord of inheritance from the house of bondage was torn for them all.
And so it says regarding the crossing of the sea: by the merit of the fathers, the sea was split and they became free men. Thus they are called "purchased" by the One who raised His hand. This refers to the mountain which we are connected to, until we arrive at Mount Zion where He dwelt.
**Lift up Your steps.** Some interpret "Your steps" <note>original: "pe'amecha"</note> as from the word for "feet." It is a plea for God to move and hasten to destroy the enemy. **To the perpetual ruins.** This is a noun form, like "perpetual desolations." This refers to the destruction of the Temple. He says: "Lift Your feet to see the ruins that the enemy caused in the Holy Place."
**Your foes roared.** Inside the Sanctuary where the people of Israel used to gather for the festivals. He says "roared" because they made a loud, tumultuous noise in the House of the Lord, like the noise of a festive crowd, but in this case, it was the sound of destruction.
**They set up their own signs for signs.** In the place where the signs of God’s presence used to be, they placed their own idols or military standards. As it says elsewhere: "I did not know their signs," but now their signs are everywhere.
**It was known as one bringing axes up into a thicket.** In the building of the Temple, it was a matter of pride to bring fine wood from the forest. But now, the enemy uses axes not to build, but to destroy.
**And now, its carvings together... with hatchet and hammers.** This is another verse, for the enemy smashed the beautiful work. When he finished destroying the house, he set it on fire.
**They set Your sanctuary on fire.** They sent fire into Your Sanctuary. And likewise, they sought to destroy the people's wealth and bodies. **They have profaned the dwelling place of Your name.**
**They said in their heart: "We will suppress them altogether."** They thought to destroy the name of Israel so they would no longer be a nation. **They burned all the meeting-places of God.**
**Our signs we do not see.** The miracles we used to see, or the signs of the prophets, are gone. There is no prophet to tell us how long this exile will last.
**Until when, O God.** This is a lament. There is no prophet to tell us the "end of days" <note>original: "ketz."</note> when the redemption will come. We are left only with our prayers to the One who works salvations.
**You divided the sea.** Like one who shatters a piece of wood. **You broke the heads of the sea monsters.** Referring to the Egyptians at the Red Sea.
**You crushed the heads of Leviathan.** This refers to Pharaoh, for he is the "great monster." Like it says: "the Leviathan, the twisting serpent." He gave him as food to the people, meaning the spoils of the Egyptians were given to the Israelites.
**You cleaved the fountain.** You split the rock for them to have water in the desert. **You dried up mighty rivers.** Referring to the Jordan river which dried up for them to cross.
**Yours is the day, Yours also is the night.** Since He mentioned the drying of the rivers and the splitting of the sea, which are changes in nature, he now mentions that God is the Master of the natural order itself. Just as He acted at the time of Creation, separating light from darkness, so He acts every day.
**You established the light and the sun.** The "light" <note>original: "ma'or"</note> refers to the moon and the stars, and the sun is mentioned separately. For the day and night are established by the sun and the moon.
**You have set all the borders of the earth.** So that the sea does not cross its boundary. **Summer and winter.** These are the cycles of the year. He mentions the boundaries of the land and the boundaries of time. Everything is in His hand. Just as He established the laws of nature, he can intervene to save His people. Our rabbis of blessed memory said: "There is no star or constellation that does not have an angel appointed over it," but God is over all.

**The Aramaic Translation (Targum)**

Luminous and fearsome are You, O God, praised from Your sanctuary that is upon the mountains of the kings. Those who dwell in the fortresses of plunder were destroyed. The synagogues were laid waste; the stout-hearted were made fools—those who sinned fell into a deep sleep and could not find their possessions in their dwellings. Not one of the men of war was able to take up their weapons in their hands. At Your rebuke, O God of Jacob, the riders and horsemen were cast down and uprooted.

You are fearsome, You and Your strength; and who can stand before You at the time of Your mighty anger? From the heavens You caused judgment to be heard; the land of the nations feared the land of Israel and then grew quiet. This happened when the righteous arose to establish judgment against the wicked, O God, to save all the humble of the earth forever.

In the mercy with which You crowned us, we will find favor; and the sinners will give thanks to You for the remainder of the wrath You have prepared. From the anger that becomes a fury, You will bring a future for the people. Make vows and fulfill them before the Lord your God; let all who dwell around Your sanctuary bring offerings to the House of the Sanctuary. He is fearsome; He shall cut off the spirit of the princes, He who is awesome to all the kings of the earth.

### **Commentary**

**Glorious are You.** Some explain that the scribe derived this from *nehor* <note>Aramaic for light</note>, meaning "Luminous," like "Ancient." It is an adjective in the form of "great" (*gadol*). **Meir HaLevi** <note>Meir Abulafia, a 13th-century Spanish rabbi</note> says it means "shining" and is pronounced with the palate. Others believe it comes from the root *chur* <note>meaning hole or white</note>, like a doubled verb... because in these dreams every living thing shall know the brightness in Israel and He shall fight their battles.

**More than the mountains of prey.** The mountains of prey refer to the kings who "prey" upon others. For the wrath of man shall acknowledge You; as if their very anger acknowledges Your power. **The remainder of wrath You shall gird on.** When You awaken Your stored-up anger, You shall gird it like a belt...

**For the leader on Jeduthun.** Jeduthun was one of the singers <note>see 1 Chronicles 25:1</note>. Some say the psalm was written for a specific musical instrument named after him. 

**My voice to God.** He says this twice for emphasis, meaning: "My voice is directed to no one else but You." 

**In the day of my trouble.** He sought God specifically because of the exile (*Galut*). **My hand was stayed in the night.** He uses "night" because at night a person is free from the business of the world and reflects on his heart and his troubles. **My soul refused to be comforted.** Even when I try to bring comfort to my heart, the thoughts of the exile prevent it.

**I remembered God and was troubled.** I mention Him constantly with my mouth and tremble. **My spirit is overwhelmed.** Like a person in a state of faintness because of the weight of their sorrow. **You hold my eyelids open.** <term>Shmorot</term> (eyelids/watches) are the coverings of the eyes. It is as if God is holding his eyes open so that he cannot sleep due to the intensity of his heart's pain.

**I considered the days of old.** While in exile, I contemplate the ancient days when God performed miracles. **The years of ancient times.** He repeats the idea in different words. He wonders if the length of the current exile means God has abandoned the people. 

**And I said: "This is my infirmity."** This is my prayer: the years of the right hand of the Most High. I will remember that the same "Right Hand" that brought us out of Egypt and Babylon will bring us out of this current exile as well.
