### 112
# Hallelujah!
Happy is the man who fears the Lord, who <term>delights greatly in His commandments</term> <note>meaning he performs them for their own sake, with joy, not out of compulsion</note>. Mighty in the land shall his offspring be; the generation of the upright shall be blessed. Wealth and riches are in his house, and his righteousness stands forever. A light shines in the darkness for the upright; he is gracious, merciful, and righteous. Good is the man who is gracious and lends; he will guide his affairs with justice. Surely he shall never be moved; the righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance. From an evil report he shall not fear; his heart is steadfast, trusting in the Lord. His heart is sustained, he shall not fear, until he sees [victory] over his foes. He scattered, he gave to the poor; his righteousness stands forever; his horn shall be exalted in honor. The wicked shall see and be vexed; he shall gnash his teeth and melt away; the desire of the wicked shall perish.

---

# Hallelujah

They said of him: "Happy is the man who fears the Lord, who delights greatly in His commandments."
This psalm is arranged according to the <term>Alphabet</term> <note>Acrostic: each phrase begins with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note>, with two letters per verse.
This psalm follows the order... <unclear>obscured text</unclear> ...in this world and... in the world to come.
Regarding <term>in His commandments he delights greatly</term>... he performs the commandment immediately as he desires it, for the sake of its honor... and not to become accustomed to it as a mere habit of the mouth... Therefore it says "greatly," for his desire to do the will of his Creator is intense and constant... even with his body and his money... as it is said of Abraham: "Now I know that you fear God."
<term>Mighty in the land shall his offspring be</term>: this refers to the merit of his children, like the kingdom of Jehoshaphat which did not turn away from... so his children shall be "mighty in the land," and they shall be seen and blessed...
<term>Wealth and riches in his house</term>: some explain this as referring to this world, and others to the World to Come... or that it remains for his children and his children's children...
<term>A light shines in the darkness for the upright</term>: for he is gracious and merciful in his ways. A man who is generous... when the time of the harvest comes...
<term>He will guide his affairs with justice</term>: all his words and desires are conducted by the attribute of justice and law, so that his passion and worldly desires do not overwhelm him entirely... he does not multiply... he sustains his words with judgment... with the proper weight and measure... and his pieties include <term>generosity, silence, and humility</term>...
<term>The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance</term>: even after his death, his memory is for a blessing... unlike the wicked whose name shall rot... for the righteous man's name will not be forgotten.
<term>His heart is steadfast</term>: he does not trust in his own strength or wealth, which are fleeting, but rather his heart is firm in its trust in the Lord... therefore he does not fear.
<term>He scattered, he gave to the poor</term>: he distributed his money to those in need, and this is considered a great merit... but the text does not say he scattered so much that he himself became poor, for that is not the way of the wise... rather he distributed according to his ability...
<term>His righteousness stands forever</term>: it stands for him and his children after him... or it refers to the reward for his righteousness in the World to Come.
<term>His horn shall be exalted in honor</term>: his strength and power.
<term>The wicked shall see and be vexed</term>: when the wicked person sees the honor of the righteous, he becomes angry out of jealousy... he would destroy him if he had the power...
<term>The desire of the wicked shall perish</term>: whatever the wicked plot to do to the righteous, the Holy One, blessed be He, will cause their plans to fail.

# Hallelujah

Praise, O servants of the Lord, praise the name of the Lord. May the name of the Lord be blessed from this time forth and forever. From the rising of the sun until its setting, the name of the Lord is praised. High above all nations is the Lord; His glory is above the heavens. Who is like the Lord our God, who dwells on high? Who humbles Himself to behold the things that are in heaven and on the earth? He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the dunghill. To seat him with princes, with the princes of His people. He makes the barren woman to keep house, a joyful mother of children. Hallelujah!

# Hallelujah

Praise, O servants of the Lord... It is appropriate to speak of His might... and the wonders He has done in the world... like those done for Israel... "Praise" is mentioned three times...
<term>Servants of the Lord</term>: these are the wise who fear Him... for all are obligated to honor Him... and each should praise Him according to his wisdom and his knowledge of His Name.
<term>From this time forth and forever</term>: "from this time" refers to the present, and "forever" refers to the future.
<term>From the rising of the sun until its setting</term>: all inhabitants of the world from East to West shall praise Him. For even the nations recognize that there are stars and constellations, but they all acknowledge that He is the High Authority.
<term>High above all nations</term>: even though nations may deny His providence, He is King over all, and those who are wise perceive His glory more than those below... even the heavens acknowledge His glory.
<term>Who is like the Lord our God</term>: because the nations think... who is like the Lord... He dwells on high above all the upper beings, yet He humbles Himself to see the lower beings... for all are small compared to Him... and He sees even that which is in the depths...
<term>He raises the poor from the dust</term>: He brings them out of their lowly state to the merit of the soul... from the dust and the dunghill... he brings them to sit with the noble... and specifically "the noble of His people," for they are higher than all other nations... and so it will be in the future.

## 115

Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to Your name give glory, for the sake of Your kindness and Your truth. Why should the nations say, "Where now is their God?" ***

**He settles.** And behold, as in the book of Judges: "He settles the barren woman of the house." This means He settles her with children of the house. Like the verse "and He made them houses." He settles individuals into a home. A barren woman was destined for death <note>Perhaps meaning her lineage would die out</note> as the end of the house. And for this it says, "in the mother of children," as she becomes a mother of children. And similarly: barren and mistress... from below, from below. And He settles the barren woman to live among the children, and she shall be alive with them and give the grace of her life to them for their strength. And for this, "Hallelujah"—which is to say, for all these high virtues that God <note>The text uses a scribal shorthand for God</note> performs, you are obligated to praise Him.

# When Israel
"went out from Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of foreign tongue." This refers to a people speaking a different language than the Hebrew language. That is to say, they were from a people who were strong in their power. As it is written regarding the exile: "a nation of fierce countenance whose language you will not understand." And it says "tremble" <note>Hebrew: *huli*</note> to mean fear and trembling. That is to say, they were preparing them while they were standing among them, and they were working them, and there was in them grace from their place that was designated for them... <note>The commentary here repeats several lines, likely a scribal or printing error in the source manuscript</note>

# Not
"to us, O Lord, not to us, but to Your name give glory for Your kindness." This part of the book is the beginning of the Psalm. To say: just as You repeated kindness with our ancestors and also with you... so You shall do with us in every generation. Therefore, forgive us in mercy; do not do it for our sake but for Your name. For even if we were not worthy, for us is the glory of Your name... and everything depends on the importance of the matter. "For Your kindness and for Your truth," like kindness and truth. <unclear>And it was for the sake of Your kindness and concerning their idols and there is no remainder among the servants and because it was for them and they will not speak...</unclear>

The youth <note>original: *talya* — interpretive translation of "stone"</note> whom the builders left behind has become among the builders as the chief cornerstone, to be appointed for king and ruler. | This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter into it. I will give thanks unto You, for You have answered me, and are become my salvation.
From before the Lord this was brought about, said the builders; it is marvelous before us, said the sons of Jesse. This is the day the Lord has made, said the builders; let us exult and rejoice in it, said the sons of Jesse. | <margin>Wonders</margin> The stone which the builders rejected is become the chief cornerstone. This is the Lord's doing; it is marvelous in our eyes.
We beseech You, Lord, save now, said the builders; we beseech You, Lord, prosper now, said the sons of Jesse. | This is the day which the Lord has made; we will rejoice and be glad in it. We beseech You, O Lord, save now! We beseech You, O Lord, make us prosper now!
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Word <note>original: *Memra* — the Divine Manifestation</note> of the Lord, said the builders; we bless you from the Sanctuary of the Lord, said the sons of God. | <margin>On festivals</margin> Blessed be he that comes in the name of the Lord; we bless you out of the house of the Lord.
God is the Lord, and He has given us light, said the tribes of the house of Israel; arrange the festival sacrifice with chains until you bring them to its blood at the horns of the altar, said Samuel the prophet. | The Lord is God, and He has given us light; order the festival procession with boughs, even unto the horns of the altar.
You are my God and I will thank You, said David. Praise before the Lord, O Israel, and give thanks before Him, for He is good, for His kindness is everlasting. | You are my God, and I will give thanks unto You; You are my God, I will exalt You. O give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endures forever.

<column-break/>

->**The voice of rejoicing and salvation.** This means that the right hand of the Lord performs power for the righteous at all times. The "voice of rejoicing" refers to the singing of Psalms. The joy is recognized through a loud voice. **The right hand of the Lord is exalted.** This strength returns to the world like the hand of heroes. It stands eternally to add strength and to empower, for power and wealth do not simply vanish. **I shall not die.** This is like one who fears for his status or life, but I shall live to tell of the miracles He performed for me. **The Lord has surely chastened me.** Meaning, I suffered the trials of the past when enemies approached to destroy me, but God did not deliver me to death. **Open to me the gates of righteousness.** This is a metaphor for words of prayer and thanks to the Creator. He asks the wise and knowing to help him give thanks. **This is the gate of the Lord.** Meaning the order of praise and thanksgiving belongs to God, therefore the righteous enter it to thank Him for all He has done. **The stone which the builders rejected.** This is a metaphor. Just as a shepherd or a stone can represent a leader, so too was David rejected. He came from a distant place, humble in his kingdom, and was ignored by the "builders"—the kings of the earth and the surrounding nations who did not consider him fit for the "building" of a kingdom. They thought to destroy him, but he became the **chief cornerstone**, the very foundation and corner upon which the house and its walls are strengthened. Thus, Israel will be the main part of the structure. **From the Lord.** The kings of the earth will wonder at this, but all of this—bringing a person from a low state to the height of kingship—was from the Lord, and it is a wonder in our eyes. **This is the day.** Everyone answers that this is the day of salvation for all, because God has acted. All Israel can trust in this salvation. **We beseech You, Lord.** Israel says: "Save us now," so that the nations do not mock us. **Blessed is he who comes.** The priests in the Temple say this to those coming to serve God. **The Lord is God.** Israel says He gave us light from the darkness of exile. **Order the festival sacrifice with boughs.** Bring the sacrifice bound with ropes to the altar. Some say this refers to the festival of Sukkot <note>the Feast of Tabernacles</note>. **You are my God.** Israel says: "You are my God who fought my battles and brought me out of exile with great honor." **O give thanks.** This is addressed to all the nations: "Give thanks to Him, for He is good to all." Some explain these verses as a dialogue between David, his brothers, and the prophet Samuel regarding David's surprising rise to the throne. David said, "I will give thanks," because he was the youngest and least expected to be king. His brothers said, "The stone which the builders rejected," and Samuel said, "This is the day the Lord has made."<-

### Psalm 119
->Happy are the upright in way, who walk in the law of the Lord.<-

# Happy (Ashrei)

**Happy are the upright in way, who walk in the law of the Lord.** This psalm was composed by David following the <term>alphabetical acrostic: where every eight verses begin with the same letter of the Hebrew alphabet</term>. In every single verse, there is a reference to the Torah using one of eight synonyms: **Law (Torah)**, **Way (Derekh)**, **Statutes (Huqqim)**, **Judgments (Mishpatim)**, **Testimonies (Edot)**, **Precepts (Piqqudim)**, **Utterance (Dibbur)**, or **Saying (Amirah)**. These words encompass the whole of the Torah. Now I will explain these terms: **Law (Torah)** refers to the gifts of instruction, like the Written Law. **Way (Derekh)** refers to the refinement of character—just as He is gracious, you should be gracious. **Statutes (Huqqim)** are commandments whose reasons are not revealed, like dietary laws. **Judgments (Mishpatim)** are the civil laws between people. **Testimonies (Edot)** are commandments that serve as reminders, like the Sabbath and Festivals. **Precepts (Piqqudim)** are charges deposited with us, like the duties of the heart. The author chose the number eight for this structure because while seven represents the physical world (the seven planets and seven days of creation), eight represents a level of wisdom and holiness that transcends the natural world. Wisdom is often associated with the number eight in ancient thought, representing the opening of the eyes and the hidden paths of understanding.

<summary>This page concludes Psalm 118 with a focus on the "rejected stone" metaphor for King David's rise and introduces Psalm 119, explaining its unique eight-fold alphabetical acrostic structure and the eight synonyms for Divine Law.</summary>

->**Shame**<- <note>This is a catchword referring to the first word of the next section.</note>

***

In our prayers and in our supplications and by our merits. For Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, wrote the Torah from the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>The Hebrew acronym *HKB"H* is a standard title for God</note>, concerning the renewal of the world and the work of creation; the matter of the Patriarchs; the generations; and the conducts of kindness and mercy. His piety is seen in the Prophets and the Kings, in the crossing of the Red Sea and the Jordan, the standing at Mount Sinai, and the sun and moon standing still for Joshua. He passed on the generalities written by the Prophets, and later, Ezra and his assembly returned and wrote everything in the Book of Psalms. The Holy One, Blessed be He, gave the Torah to Joshua, a man of wise heart, to understand the "plain meaning" <term>Peshat: the literal or direct meaning of the text</term> of the Torah; and he passed it to the Elders, and the Elders to the Prophets, and so on.

The significance of this book is that King David, peace be upon him, wrote the Book of Psalms, and in it were included eighteen great advantages and virtues for learning the plain meaning of the Torah. These verses are for our deeds, both the "face" <note>exoteric/obvious meaning</note> and the "secret" <note>esoteric/mystical meaning</note>, a full fortress. This book praises the Power that guides us... and anyone who wishes to learn to perfect the plain meaning of the Torah should arrange these verses at every hour. In every book, one finds the composition of King David, peace be upon him—this is the Psalms—arranged by the eight-fold verses of the Alphabet <note>Psalm 119 has 8 verses for every Hebrew letter</note>. In it, one finds the "rectification of the soul's seasons," as written in the Book of Psalms.

This refers to the kindness and piety of David. The Sages have derived from there the comforts of the way... for those who are strong in the wisdom of the Torah of the Lord, meaning those who study and meditate upon it. For it is the foundation of his path, and every man should review the Torah, as our Sages of blessed memory said: "May they be sweet." Some interpret "piety" as the way of the Torah of the Lord through thorough "dialectic" <term>Pilpul: a method of Talmudic study involving sharp analysis and debate</term> and the rectification of the Face and Secret of God. The "Way of the Torah" is the plain meaning and its conduct. One must explain the secret of the matter as the "Mercies of the Torah of the Lord," meaning that the learner should always be focused on the ten ways of "taste" <note>Ta'am: can mean 'reason,' 'flavor,' or 'musical cantillation'</note>, each one rectified according to the ways of the Psalms for those who study in the House of Midrash.

The Holy One, Blessed be He, is revealed to them before the eyes of all who learn in their company. One who speaks with a merciful heart, his actions will be simple and his secret will be known to every heart, and he has the power to merit the words of our Sages. Anyone who establishes all his deeds to be strong in the wisdom of his companions, in the rectification of the Face and Secret of God, and recites the piety of the Book of God—may His kindness be upon him with all his heart. His merit will bring him to understand the plain meaning of the Psalm, which is a sign for all the virtues of the plain Torah. There is pleasure in His kindness, and therein is the rectification.

Some explain the status of "revealing his work, righteousness, and humility" to be strong in the wisdom of his companions. For he will not fear the "scale of kindness," and reproach shall not surround him... meaning his plain meaning shall be upright and his wisdom pious... He should believe and his heart should be a fortress for His kindness. Even "if princes sit" <note>quoting verse 23</note>, he does not desire the favor of the world's great men. He has the power of a good heart... and in this is the rectification, for he is as happy as one who finds a great treasure. That is to say, his heart shall be happy and a full fortress, strengthening the prayer: "Let Your hand be ready to help me in the work of our hands."

This can be explained in this way because most of the world's deeds bear the innovation of the Psalms that King David commanded us: eight verses for each letter in the order of the Alphabet. King David intended for them to gain merit. This is the language of "rectification" in the practice of the Psalm according to this book: "The kindness of the Lord to all that is exalted." The teacher and the student should intend to pour out their speech and seek mercy before the Lord for every specific detail of the affairs of this world. This is well-trodden, as our Sages wished for a person to arrange his prayer. For there is a "subtle and accessible strength" in wisdom in our holy Torah, in the words of the Zohar, and in the wisdom of the scriptures. For so did Rabbeinu Bahya <note>Rabbi Bahya ben Asher, a 13th-century commentator</note> rule in the arrangement of his words: "In the kindness of prophecy, for the beloved who trusts in the Creator, His merit shall help him in the way of the Torah."

One who learns to merit the wisdom that King David sought in this book has power, ability, merit, and divine assistance. His heart shall be clear and pure, and his piety shall help him to shorten the way each day, and he shall flee from sin. If they tell you something like this is a "secret" in the conduct of the world—the kindness of the Lord is over the world and its fullness—the Leader desires this Psalm. Blessed be the Creator; may His kindness be upon us always... The teacher should keep these eight verses, and in every eight verses, he becomes strong in the wisdom of the Psalm that King David wrote to benefit the soul. For we have merit in the practice of the Psalm... one finds kindness and grace in this Psalm when the intention of the heart is pious.

The body and the weapons and the wicked tongue and many praises for seeing the afflictions of the heart and the company. Cursed is your movement, my soul. | **You rebuke the arrogant, the cursed ones, who stray from Your commandments.**

**Commentary:**
**You rebuke:** This uses a past tense form in place of a future tense. Its musical accent is at the end, indicating a sharp sound at the conclusion of the vowel. It suggests that the "cursed ones" will be destroyed, for they are the ones who stray from Your commandments. The Sages (of blessed memory) expounded that a curse is ready for the arrogant because they nullify the word of God. This indicates that they are part of the groups of "scoffers" <note>term: *leitzim* — those who treat spiritual matters with cynical derision</note>. My heart tells me this refers to those who wrap themselves in worldly vanities. This is what the Sages (of blessed memory) said about those who "stray": they will not merit to see the Divine Presence. They stray from the commandments and transgress them. 

**Remove from me:** Those scoffers who reproach me and mock me because I have dwelled upon Your laws. I ask: "Roll" <note>original: *gal* — also meaning 'reveal' or 'roll away'</note> this reproach away from me and remove the shame from them so that they might turn to me. 

**Kings also sat:** Princes and great men, kings and their helpers, sit together and speak against me in a disparaging way. Yet, I, Your servant, will meditate on the written word and the logic of Your laws. He uses the language of "speaking" to show that even while they speak with anger, I will respond with the logic of speech. 

**Also Your testimonies:** They are my delight and my counselors, reminding me of my Creator. 

**Clings:** My soul is in a state of lowliness and is afraid because the wise men have stumbled, and they were close to death, as if their soul "clung to the dust." He prepares himself to receive life from God, "Give me life according to Your word." 

**I told of my ways:** Like a man recounting and searching his paths. I have scrutinized my face, my eyes, my ways, and my words, which I was accustomed to revealing. I have surrendered them before You. As it is said, "And Ishmael spoke..." <note>A reference to a biblical character to explain the nuances of the word "spoke"</note>. You answered me many times when I asked of You; teach me Your statutes so that my intellect may understand them. 

**Drips:** They wrote that it "drips" from much sorrow. This is like the phrase "the heart of the people melted." My soul drips tears because of my suffering. 

**Sustain me according to Your word:** Support me in my kingdom through Your word which You spoke to me through Nathan the Prophet. 

**The way of falsehood:** Do not lead me in the paths of those who walk in vanity; keep them far from me and graciously grant me Your Torah. 

**The way of faith:** The opposite of the way of falsehood. I have chosen these and placed Your laws before me. When You broaden my heart, I will run, because it is as if the heart has more room to move without delay. 

**Teach me:** "And I will keep it to the end" (*equev*). This refers to the reward for following the path. Some explain *equev* as "the end," as in "the end of a matter." For example, "great reward" (*equev rav*). It refers to the consequence at the end of a life or an action. Therefore, I will always anticipate the "great reward" of the fruits of my labor. My teacher (of blessed memory) explained that "Teach me the way of Your statutes" means I will guard them. I interpreted *equev* as "end," for the heel (*aquev*) is at the end of the body. Because the heel is at the end, they called the end of a matter "equev." Reward is also called *equev* (as in "as a result of your listening") because the reward comes at the end of the deed. So the meaning is: I will keep it until the end of my days. 

**Give me understanding:** In the matter of Your word. I have already explained how my desire and my thoughts are to perform Your commandments. 

**Lead me:** Open my heart and my will so that I do not stray from the path of the commandment. 

**Incline my heart... and not to gain:** Let my heart not turn to laughter or the gathering of money that does not come through honorable means; let it be only upon Your testimonies. 

**Gain (*Betza*):** A strong desire for money. 

**From seeing vanity:** That I should not follow the desires of my eyes. 

**In Your way:** Which descends from holy thought. He says "give me life," for the one who recognizes the truth truly lives. 

**Which is for those who fear You:** Let my words be according to Your fear. 

**Remove my reproach:** For I said in a previous verse that I dread the shame. Even though You gave me Your word, he asks God to remove the sin so that he will not be remembered for it. 

**For Your judgments are good:** Do not judge a man according to the punishment he deserves, but rather bypass some of the punishment, for You are good and Your judgments are good. 

**Behold:** Even though I have erred, I long for Your precepts; therefore, in Your righteousness, give me life—meaning, lengthen my life so I may fulfill the commandments. 

**May Your kindness come to me, O Lord:** Which descends from holy thought. Let Your salvation and Your kindness come to me as You promised me. 

**And I will answer my reproacher:** Who says that God will not save me. I will answer him that I have trusted in Your word that You will save me. 

**And do not take... out of my mouth:** In my matters of truth. I ask this for I am like one standing at the feet of Your truth. If You do not do this, it is as if You have removed the truth from me. For by Your power I am guarded. 

**And I will keep:** The Torah will be constantly in my mouth and I will guard it forever and ever—meaning all the days of my life. Some say "forever" refers to this world and "ever" to the world to come. Or it means Your Torah stands forever, and I will fulfill it always. 

**And I will walk in a broad place:** For after You help me in the study of Torah, I will not be constrained but will walk in a "broad way," because Your precepts are always before me. 

**And I will speak of Your testimonies before kings:** When You help me reach the truth, I will speak of it even before kings and not be ashamed. For they will return to my heart the truth. When Israel occupies itself with Torah, kings will speak of it and I will not be ashamed to answer them. 

**And I will delight:** Like one who takes pleasure in them, for I loved them more than any other thing. 

**And I will lift my hands:** I will lift my hands and feet to perform the commandments and I will meditate on them.

Remember the word to Your servant, because You have given me hope. The Lord is my portion, I said, to keep Your word. I prayed before Your face with all my heart; be gracious to me according to Your Word. I considered my ways to be good, and I turned my feet to Your testimonies. I hastened and did not delay to keep Your commandments. A company of the wicked gathered against me; Your Torah I did not forget. At midnight I will arise to praise before You because of Your righteous judgments. I am a companion to all who fear You and to those who keep Your commandments. Your goodness, O Lord, fills the earth; teach me Your statutes. | **ח** (Het) The Lord is my portion; I have said that I would keep Your words. I entreated Your favor with my whole heart; be merciful to me according to Your promise. I thought on my ways, and turned my feet to Your testimonies. I hurried and did not delay to keep Your commandments. The cords of the wicked have entwined me, but I have not forgotten Your Torah. At midnight I will rise to give thanks to You because of Your righteous judgments. I am a companion of all those who fear You, and of those who keep Your precepts. The earth, O Lord, is full of Your mercy; teach me Your statutes.
Goodness You have done with Your servant, O Lord, as You have spoken. Teach me good taste and knowledge, for I have believed in Your commandments. Before I was afflicted, I was erring, but now I have kept Your Word. You are good and do good; teach me Your statutes. The arrogant have joined together a lie against me; I, with all my heart, will keep Your commandments. Their hearts have become dull like fat, like the hypocrites; as for me, Your Torah is my delight. It is good for me that I was afflicted, so that I might learn Your statutes. The Torah of Your mouth is better for me than thousands of gold and silver. | **ט** (Tet) You have dealt well with Your servant, O Lord, according to Your word. Teach me good judgment and knowledge, for I believe in Your commandments. Before I was afflicted I went astray, but now I keep Your word. You are good, and do good; teach me Your statutes. The proud have forged a lie against me, but I will keep Your precepts with my whole heart. Their heart is as fat as grease, but I delight in Your Torah. It is good for me that I have been afflicted, that I may learn Your statutes. The Torah of Your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver pieces.
Your hands made me and established me; give me understanding and I will learn Your commandments. Those who fear You will see me and rejoice, because I have waited for Your word. I know, O Lord, that Your judgments are truth, and in truth You have afflicted me. May Your kindness now be for my comfort, according to Your Word to Your servant. May Your mercies come upon me and I shall live, for Your Torah is my delight. Let the arrogant be ashamed, for they have wronged me with lies; but I will speak of Your commandments. May those who fear You and those who know Your testimonies return to my teaching. Let my heart be perfect in Your statutes, so that I may not be ashamed. | **י** (Yod) Your hands have made me and fashioned me; give me understanding, that I may learn Your commandments. Those who fear You will be glad when they see me, because I have hoped in Your word. I know, O Lord, that Your judgments are right, and that in faithfulness You have afflicted me. Let, I pray You, Your merciful kindness be for my comfort, according to Your word to Your servant. Let Your tender mercies come to me, that I may live; for Your Torah is my delight. Let the proud be ashamed, for they treated me perversely with falsehood; but I will meditate on Your precepts. Let those who fear You turn to me, and those who know Your testimonies. Let my heart be blameless in Your statutes, that I may not be ashamed.
My soul faints for Your salvation; I have waited for Your word. My eyes fail for Your Word, saying, "When will You comfort me?" | **כ** (Kaf) My soul faints for Your salvation, but I hope in Your word. My eyes fail for Your word, saying, "When will You comfort me?"

<column-break/>

**Zayin** - *Remember the word to Your servant*: specifically the promise You made to me. *You have given me hope*: You have caused me to wait. *My servant before [Me]*: You have forgiven me. I would have died from affliction if I had not kept Your promise which *revived me*. *The arrogant have mocked me*: those who acted willfully and intended to harm me because of my constant occupation with Your Torah. Despite this, *I have not turned away from Your Torah*. It is possible that this refers to the known interpretation of the verse *I remembered Your judgments of old*: remembering the judgment of the righteous ones of the past who endured many troubles but found comfort. For I know that the troubles coming upon me now are Your judgments, and afterward, goodness will come to me. *Shuddering*: a trembling seized me because of the wicked, lest I be trapped with them, or because of a storm and quaking. *Songs*: in the midst of the bitterness of my decrees, I remember and am encouraged; they become a pleasure in the *house of my pilgrimage*, for even there I had songs and stories of the sanctification of Your name in all the surrounding places. *I remembered Your name in the night*: out of the thought of Your Torah which went along and stirred my mind, always such a thought. *I remembered in the night*: You remembered me at the start, before the thought of Your speech went out; You forgave me at the beginning.

**Het** - *The Lord is my portion*: meaning, my inheritance. *I entreated Your favor*: with all my heart, be gracious to me according to Your word. *I entreated Your favor*: like one who turns the face of his friend toward a specific place, a thing that is endured; the order of service follows the order of the verses. I found a book of service according to this order and saw my mouth [acting] as a servant of Your will. *I entreated Your favor*: I arranged and agreed upon my ways, and *turned my feet to Your testimonies*. His piety directed his ways forever, so that wherever he went, his feet would lead him to the testimonies. My feet sought the goodness of Your testimonies, lest [evil] consume me. *I hurried and did not delay to keep Your commandments*: unlike the *cords of the wicked*. *Entwined me*: meaning, the ropes and sins of the wicked around me took from me, yet I did not forget. *At midnight I rise to sanctify*, etc.: remember this matter, like the "songs" mentioned before that returned to me in the house of my pilgrimage. *Midnight*: to wake from my direction and the dream I imagined. *I rise to give thanks*: this section is lacking the songs with which they thank You in the house. *Your righteous judgments*: a daily statute regarding the judgments of the "hairy ones" <note>This likely refers to "demons" or "goat-spirits" in medieval folklore, often associated with the wilderness or the night.</note>, the great ones of the heavens. *I am a companion to all*, etc.: I did not serve the wicked mentioned; rather, I am a companion to those who fear You and join them because of their piety.

**Tet** - *The Lord’s kindness*, etc.: I said that the "hairy ones" are always going and strengthening, so as not to leave the temperament in the moisture of the body and life. *Your kindness, O Lord, [fills the earth]*: *You have dealt well with Your servant*. The main point is that the two judgments of the decree will exchange shouts of joy for their creatures, and they will complain of fear and gloom. *You have dealt well*: the sum of good is labor. One who benefits from goodness because of his sin should not serve. The correct view was renewed through a "good trial," and he was blessed for repeating it constantly so as not to become pampered in his perfection. *Good taste and knowledge*: like distinguishing between one thread and another. *I believed*: before the depths of my life, I was sometimes an unwitting sinner due to the bitterness of the blows; after I was endangered in that pull, I learned from Your Torah and kept it. *You are good and do good*: You are good even when we are struck, and You do good with me by guiding my thoughts toward Your statutes. *Forged*: they joined a lie against me, to say his inside is not like his outside, but You know that with all my heart I remember Your precepts. *Dull*: their hearts are insensitive and foolish, but the understanding of Your Torah is the line by which I measured my life. *Dull as fat*: their hearts are thickened. *It is good for me that I was afflicted*: self-affliction and toil so that I might learn Your statutes for a good lot and pleasure. Others measure their own deeds to acquire wealth, but I was afflicted to serve, and my pleasure is to drink in the Torah, for *the Torah of Your mouth is better* than gold and silver.

**Yod** - *Your hands made me and fashioned me*: and prepared me for my Torah, for You sustained me in the flight of life to wait to acquire wisdom at the beginning of my standing. In the action of the intellect, through His good wisdom in an open heart, the king of the pious, and through the strength of his mind, he kept the precepts. Through the power of speech and the instruments prepared for it, he was able to receive grace and the cutting of speech with the tongue and lips. *Those who fear You*: they learn from me, they see and rejoice to see the children of wisdom in Babylon, and I found the commandments of our Torah and my interpretations of Your word and service. *I know, O Lord, that Your judgments are righteous*: and when the sickness turned my heart through what I had acquired, I knew that You afflicted me with a "dimissio" <note>original: "דימוס" - a legal term for release or pardon, here suggesting a purposeful or educational affliction.</note>. For the kindness of God is from the day of the Lord. *May Your mercies come to me*: and the mercies are theirs. *To comfort me*: from Your kindness You afflicted me, as You promised me. *May Your mercies come to me*: let Your mercies revive me, for I keep Your Torah and it is my delight. *Let the arrogant be ashamed, for they have wronged me with lies*: they were supporting me with statutes, and even though I was in the confusion of Your precepts, all my mouths were speaking and strongly remembering the pious. *May those who fear You return to me*: they will direct themselves, etc. Our rabbis of blessed memory interpreted this as the order of the spheres and the cycle of the night, and afterward they would be perfect in me. *Let my heart be perfect*: and at this time, let my heart be perfect and pious in Your statutes.

**Kaf** - *My soul faints*: for Your salvation, I have clung to the end. *My eyes fail*: from my great anticipation for Your help. Because the scriptures are open to the sons of freedom who stand on the path, they fainted for the help of kindness; their eyes were failing from much moaning. *Saying, "When will You comfort me?"*: from my affliction, forgive me.

<summary>This page covers Psalm 119 from the letters Zayin to Kaf, featuring the Aramaic Targum and a commentary that emphasizes the role of affliction in spiritual growth and the constant devotion of the psalmist despite mockery from the "arrogant." The commentary uniquely blends linguistic analysis with philosophical reflections on the creation of the human body as a vessel for Torah study.</summary>

<margin>
The opening of
</margin>

---

**I hate double-minded thoughts** <note>Hebrew: *Se'aphim*</note>. They explained this as a term for "thought," like those who possess evil thoughts. In my opinion, it refers to all things that are changeable <note>The commentator links the word to "branches" or "divisions," implying fragmented or wavering thoughts.</note>. The meaning is: I have considered all other thoughts to be vanity, but I have loved Your Torah and all my thoughts are upon it. **My hiding place**. My protection from those who are prepared to do me harm. **In Your word**. This is my security; I have placed my hope in it. <note>unclear text in original</note> For one who occupies himself with the Torah, harm cannot reach him. **Depart from me**. Do not disturb me; leave me to my thoughts on the commandments of my God. **Sustain me according to Your word**. According to what You have promised me. **That I may live**. Do not let me fall into the hands of evildoers. **And do not let me be ashamed of my hope**. The hope I placed in You for our salvation. And if it were so, it would be a matter of shame. **And I will look to Your statutes always**. To involve myself in them, to learn them, and to fulfill them. **You have rejected all** <note>Hebrew: *Salita*</note>. This is in the *segol* form. If it follows the context of "Your Torah" which I mentioned, then it means trampling or discarding. For their deceit is like dross which they trusted in, and that is the vanity of their idols <note>Original: *ta'uyot*, often used as a euphemism for idols</note> and their empty works. The word *Salita* means discarding and lifting up, as in "removing the dross." This is written in the future tense, but refers to the general way of the world: You trample all who stray from Your statutes. **For their deceit is falsehood**. It was a lie when they said they were good while they were actually evil. Their deceit was total, and it is written as a false thing. He mentions **dross** <note>Hebrew: *sigim*</note> because sometimes a person is refined of his impurities, which are the *sigim*. Like "I will refine your dross as with lye" <note>Isaiah 1:25</note>. These are those who deceive the world and are worse than the openly wicked, for a person can guard himself against the openly wicked, but against the hidden one, he is full of internal deceit. Therefore, You remove them from the world. When he says "all the wicked of the earth," it is like "all the inhabitants of the earth." **Therefore I love Your testimonies**, because they guide a person away from all evil, and they are good for a person both internally and externally. Therefore I have loved them and clung to them. **My flesh trembles**. For even the righteous should fear You, for my spirit is humbled before You. The wicked say, "He has no savior," but I shudder before You, so that the hair of my flesh stands up <note>Hebrew: *samar*, linked to a nail or bristling</note> and I am spread out according to my deeds before You. I am careful not to transgress Your commandments. **From Your judgments**. For I fear that You will punish me, for I know that You examine me for my hidden sins. This is "fear that removes sin." A person should have the fear of the Blessed One upon them so that they do not sin. As it says: "that His fear may be before you, that you do not sin" <note>Exodus 20:17</note>. The meaning of **samar** (trembles) is like "a nail <note>Hebrew: *masmer*</note> driven into a wall." For a person who trembles before You, his hair stands up like nails in his flesh. **I have done justice and righteousness**. Even though I tremble, do not leave me to my oppressors. Just as I have acted with justice, do not leave me in their hands. **Be surety** <note>Hebrew: *Arov*</note>. Like "it was sweet to the Lord," but here it is a transitive verb, meaning: do good and act as a guarantor for Your servant for good, so that the arrogant do not oppress me. In the same way, "deal with me according to Your kindness." **My eyes fail**. We have explained this matter as the eyes looking toward the heights. **For the word of Your righteousness**. Save me from the strangers so they do not oppress me. That is to say, I have not looked for human salvation, but only for Your salvation and for the word of Your righteousness which You promised me through the prophets. **Deal with Your servant according to Your mercy**. For many times You have done so for me; so too now, keep me alive so that others do not overpower me and I can occupy myself with Your statutes. And You, deal with me by making me wise in my understanding and teaching me Your statutes. **I am Your servant**. By using the letter *Aleph* <note>Referring to the word 'Ani' (I)</note>, he says: I have no desire but for Your service. If so, give me understanding away from the oppressors and the hidden ones, and give me understanding to know Your testimonies, for the essence of my service is my contemplation of them. **Time**. My teacher said: "Now is the time when they have made void Your Torah." Even though in this world You are patient with the wicked, a time will come when You will take vengeance upon them, and that is the "Great Day" as written in the book of Malachi. And the word "voided" refers to their abandonment. The wicked have voided Your Torah. Therefore, the time for the Lord to act is the time of their punishment. Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, interpreted this verse: "It is better to void one word of the Torah in order to act for the Lord." For example, Elijah at Mount Carmel, who sacrificed on a high place <note>Outside the Temple</note> at a time when high places were forbidden, in order to act there to stop the worshippers of Baal. They said: "The voiding of the Torah is its foundation" <note>A Talmudic principle that sometimes a law must be bypassed to save the religion</note>. And one can interpret "It is time to act for the Lord" in connection with what he said "I am Your servant, give me understanding." He says: You must help me with the knowledge of Your testimonies so that I may be strengthened in them. For the time is passing, and the time I am in is the time a person needs to strengthen himself to act for the Lord in Torah and commandments, for there are many who have voided Your Torah. Therefore, one needs to be very strong in the Torah so it is not forgotten entirely. **Therefore**. Because of this "voiding," every person of understanding acts. **Therefore**. Since I see that they have voided Your Torah and pursue vanity, and all their business and toil is to acquire wealth, I have set my desire to labor and occupy myself with Your commandments more than gold and fine gold which they toil to acquire. **Therefore I esteem all Your precepts concerning all things to be right**. He explains this as well. He says "all" twice, like "all the first fruits of all." It means all the precepts written in the Torah. They are written as a testimony for Israel to follow and to judge; I have established them all as right in the eyes of those who despise them and say they are not righteous judgments. But their thoughts and their ways are a **false way which I hate**. **Your testimonies are wonderful**. From the term "wonders," meaning they are hidden from you. That is to say, there are secrets in them. Therefore my soul keeps them and seeks them out. That is, it lifts its eyes to You to understand them. Or, it keeps them in time of trouble because it understands them and knows their benefit. For one who does not understand the commandments will not keep them properly. One might ask: Moses our teacher said, "For this commandment which I command you this day is not hidden from you" <note>Deuteronomy 30:11</note>. So how could David say "Your testimonies are wonderful/hidden"? The answer is: What Moses said was that the deed itself is not difficult or far from you, like a parable of a thing you cannot understand. For it is very close to you, in your mouth and in your heart to do it. As you speak it with your mouth, so you can understand it in your heart and do it. There is no parable in the commandment. And from here is an answer to those who say that the Torah is taken away from them. What David said about "wonderful/hidden" refers to the core of the commandments and their reasons, and how the intellect points to them, for there are many reasons for the commandments. **The opening of Your words**. The opening of Your words illuminates the eyes of those with a closed heart. For when a person begins to involve himself in them, light will come to him and he will become wise. He said this after saying "Your testimonies are wonderful" so that a person would not despair from contemplating them. One might say, since they are "wonderful," I cannot understand them and they are not for me; but one *should* contemplate them. The matters will open for you a path of understanding. For the opening of the words will shine for you, like a flowing spring. That is, it gives understanding to the simple. **I opened my mouth and panted**. In the way of the simple. That is to say, because I am thirsty for the commandments. He uses the language of "panting" <note>Hebrew: *she'ifah*</note> because of his great desire to understand; I opened my mouth and panted. The term *she'ifah* is the drawing in of breath to the mouth. Just as a thirsty person pants for water and opens his mouth to the spring before reaching it, so the soul pants for the light before the word arrives. The word **longed** <note>Hebrew: *ya'avti*</note> is unique in scripture, and its meaning is like "I desired."

The commentary provides deep linguistic analysis and discusses the famous rabbinic principle that sometimes the law is suspended to preserve the faith.</summary>

**Make Your face shine.** <note>original: "פניך האר"</note> According to the law. Just as it is said, "As is the custom for daughters, so shall he do for her" <note>Exodus 21:9</note>. **Streams of water.** This indicates a strong and steady flow. **See.** <note>original: "חמי"</note> This is like the interpretation and the written copy of the transcript <note>referring to Aramaic "Patshagen"</note> to add grace and pleasantness from You to me. **Streams of water.** We translate <note>into Aramaic</note> as "and they were upright" <note>original: "ותריצין"</note> through the plagues of Your people, and regarding a bridegroom... <unclear>illegible Aramaic gloss</unclear>. This refers to destiny; do not chatter about it, every cantor <note>original: "חזן"</note>. Like one who urges on, or the strengthening of your master's servant. **Sforno** <note>a reference to the commentator Obadiah Sforno</note> and his companion: all the pious of my people, a light service. **You commanded.** A division—why did You found them as a void? In the book its explanation is a space for the public. **Make Your face shine upon Your servant.** This is like "May the Lord make His face shine upon you" <note>Numbers 6:25</note>. He turned His face and all His mercy. As it is written, "In the light of the king's face is life" <note>Proverbs 16:15</note>. **And teach me.** Instruct me; this refers to the strong habit of **streams of water**. He was weeping over the sins he had committed and grew strong over them. The Psalm lacks for the poor, for the wicked are the insolent ones, and the strength is to return our eyes. **Righteous are You, Lord.** And Your judgments are also righteous and upright. Each one of Your judgments is "upright" <note>original: "ישר"</note> on its own. Its explanation is "in a straight path." **You have commanded.** Meaning the obligation of the community is great for all Your testimonies, for they are righteousness and faith indeed. **Consumed me.** Like one who cuts off life; my zeal... <unclear>complex grammatical note</unclear>. **I am small.** Small in my own eyes and despised in theirs because of the fear of Your statutes in Your Torah. **Yet I have not forgotten Your precepts.** As if they were forgotten... **Your righteousness.** The precept with the world is righteousness forever. **And Your Torah is truth.** For all its delights are one and exist forever... this is the establishment of the world and the writing of the Torah... **Distress and anguish.** In times of troubled thoughts, Your commandments are my delights. They strengthen their commandments through Your trust in them. **The righteousness of Your testimonies is everlasting.** Like Your righteous charge forever. Give me understanding that I may live in the World to Come <note>Hebrew: "Olam Ha-Ba"</note>. And he returns to teach now in the place of... **I called with all my heart, answer me O Lord.** A strong returning voice with all the heart, for I knew in my heart that Grace answers and saves. Therefore answer me... according to Your decrees. **I called to You.** Every explanation written in the verse "I called" is repeated to strengthen the promise. **I called to You.** While it was still night, I rose before any other person to take up Your words at night. **I hoped for Your word.** I hoped in Your promise. Its explanation: for Your word written in the Torah, for "He is near to all who call upon Him" <note>Psalm 145:18</note>. Therefore I hoped for Your word and turned. **I anticipated the night watches.** To interpret the time of transcription at night. As our Rabbis of blessed memory said, David rose before his eyes to wake at night before everyone else... and the voice of the night is for the purpose of reviving... this happened many times during the hours of interpretation for the many. **My voice.** **According to Your kindness.** Do with me as You have done for me many times. **According to Your judgments.** Like Your custom to those who love Your name. According to Your good customs given with Your statutes, so revive me. **They draw near.** They are close and attached to lewdness until they are far from Your Torah. For the pursuer is near. **Lord, and all Your path...** pursuers of lewdness. For if they were close to the Torah, they would not be pursuers of lewdness. **Lewdness.** <note>original: "זמה"</note> As in "for lewdness is with him." It is a matter of abomination and evil business. **Near.** You are far from them and from Your Torah, but You are near to all who call upon You. **And all Your commandments are truth.** And they are far from them because they did not know them and did not think they were truth. **Of old.** From the beginning of what I knew and gathered from Your testimonies, that You founded them forever. For they are the foundation and existence of the world. For at the beginning of the matter, when Man was born... his eyes were... to rise to the wisdom of the honorable commandments... **Deliver me.** Because I have not forgotten Your Torah. Despite all my affliction, I have not forgotten Your Torah. **Plead my cause.** Revive me for the sake of Your word. I seek life through Your teaching, let the world not be delayed. **Far.** Our Rabbis of blessed memory said the salvation is near to him who keeps the statutes, but for those who stray, salvation is far from them. **For they do not seek Your statutes.** And they have no merit by which they could be saved. **Your mercies.** According to my precepts, they were many... **According to Your judgments.** According to Your good customs as I explained above. **Many.** From Your testimonies. Despite all this, I have not turned away from Your testimonies. Even when they sought my harm, I did not turn. **I saw the treacherous and I contended.** From the matter of "strife" <note>original: "קטטה"</note> in the words of our Rabbis. I would contend with them more because they did not keep Your word than I would contend with them for doing evil to me. **See.** See how much I loved them... revive me. **The beginning of Your word.** From the beginning of the world and forever. All the days of this world, Your word and judgment are truth and established. So it was and so it shall be forever. **Righteous judgment.** Your judgments which are righteous. This is the beginning of what You opened... and similarly in our being over all Your righteous judgment... forever. This means that in the preparation of their beginning, You founded all Your righteous judgments forever. For they were made to lead to the knowledge of Your Unity.

---

**Commentary**

**Princes.** This refers to the Great Ones of the nations who persecuted me. Even so, my heart feared Your word more than I feared them. This means: I feared to transgress Your word more than I feared their persecution. Or, the meaning is: they persecuted me to force me to leave my Torah, as one might say, "Cross over this religion..." but at all times my heart feared Your word and I was afraid to violate the Torah. **I rejoice.** My heart rejoices in Your word <margin>And even over the trials!</margin> like one who finds great spoil.

**Seven times a day.** This is a common idiom for "many times." Just as it is said, "seven times a righteous man falls and rises," or "seven abominations in his heart." We have already explained this in the foundations of this Psalm. **For Your righteous judgments.** These are the laws of the Temple and the sacrifices, for which I praise You many times every day. **Great peace.** For the path of the upright is peace, and they will not stumble because they long for the Torah. Even if they face trials, they will not be brought to ruin.

**I have hoped for Your salvation.** This refers to the salvation of the soul. I have placed my hope in the Light of the World, and I have not let the evil inclination entice me. **My soul kept Your testimonies.** Because I loved them exceedingly. **For all my ways are before You.** Just as it says, "In all your ways, know Him." Our Sages, of blessed memory, said: all Your judgments and laws are established in Heaven and known on Earth, for they are the path I have chosen.

**According to Your word.** In the merit of my keeping the commandments, grant me understanding. **Let it come.** May my prayer enter before You. In this verse, he mentions "according to Your promise" <note>original: "imratecha"</note>. The Sages noted that this "promise" refers to the comfort of the testimonies. **Deliver me.** This is a prayer that the exile should end. **My lips shall utter.** This means the speech of praise. Just as a spring bubbles over with water, so my lips will bubble over with Your praise when You teach me Your statutes.

**My tongue shall answer.** This refers to teaching others and speaking of Your righteousness. **Let Your hand be.** I have chosen Your commandments, therefore let Your hand be my help. **I have longed for Your salvation.** Because I have waited for the redemption, let my soul live in this world and the next. **I have gone astray like a lost sheep.** I have wandered in the exile like a sheep whose shepherd has left it. Just as a shepherd seeks out a lost sheep, I ask: "Seek Your servant." Even though I am in exile, I have not forgotten Your commandments, so help me to live and do not forget me.

### A Song of Ascents
There are fifteen such "Ascent" songs. It is said they were recited on the fifteen steps in the Holy Temple that led from the Court of Israel to the Court of Women. Others say they refer to the ascents of the exiles returning from Babylon to the Land of Israel. **To the Lord in my distress.** The speaker uses the singular to represent the entire community in exile. **Deliver my soul.** From the nations who speak falsely against Israel. **What shall He give to you.** What benefit do you get from your deceit? **Sharp arrows of the mighty.** The deceitful tongue is compared to arrows and coals of broom, which keep their heat for a long time even after the fire seems out. So too, the damage of a deceitful tongue is lasting. **Woe is me, for I sojourned in Meshech.** Meshech and Kedar represent the lands of the exile, specifically the domains of Ishmael <note>Arabs</note> and the northern tribes. **I am for peace.** I seek peace, but my enemies only want war.

# Psalms

| **A song that was spoken concerning the ascents from the deep: I will lift my eyes to the mountains, to the [ancestral] heights: My help! My help is from before the Lord, who made the heavens and the earth.** He will not allow your foot to stumble; your Guardian does not sleep. Behold, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps. The Lord will guard you; the Lord will cast a shadow over you because of the *Mezuzah* <note>The Targum adds a specific reference to the Mezuzah, the parchment scroll placed on doorposts</note> that you fixed on the right side of your gate. By day, when the sun rules, the morning spirits <note>original: "Tzafrira"</note> and the *Lilu* spirits <note>original: "Luyey"; types of harmful spirits or demons in folklore</note> shall not strike you, nor the moon when it rules by night. The Word <note>original: "Memra"</note> of the Lord will guard you from all evil; He will guard your soul. For there the tribes went up, the tribes of the Lord, a testimony for Israel that His Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhintiah"</note> dwells among them when they give thanks to the Lord of Heaven. ---

**Song** of Ascents. This refers to the preparation made over the waves of the sea <note>This refers to a legend in the Talmud where King David sang these songs to stay the rising waters of the deep (Tehom) when digging the Temple foundations</note>. Our Sages of blessed memory <note>original: "chazal"</note> explain that these correspond to the fifteen steps in the Temple. Some explain that the verse is missing a letter *Lamed* [to/for], as if it said "For the Ascents." It also refers to the one who is destined to prepare "steps" for the pool in the time to come. **I lift my eyes to the mountains.** The Sages explain this as "I lift my eyes to the *parents*" <note>A pun on the Hebrew words *Heharim* (mountains) and *Hehorim* (parents/ancestors)</note>, meaning the Patriarchs, that they should seek mercy for me. It all relates to the same theme. **To the mountains** is like saying "upon the mountains." **My help.** If I lift my eyes to the mountains and ask "from where will my help come?", the answer is that the mountains themselves will not avail me. Rather, my help comes from the Lord. He will help me and surround me [protect me] from the nations, for all their power is nothingness before Him. **The Lord.** This means that any kindness one person does for another in this world is temporary, but the Lord is the Creator of heaven and the depths. **He will not let your foot be moved.** Even when we are in exile <note>original: "galut"</note> and struck by our enemies, the Wisdom of the Crown <note>A kabbalistic reference to the Sephirah of Keter</note> is open to us. He says that the Guardian of Israel does not sleep; He guards us at all times and rescues us from the power of those who oppress us. **The Lord is your guardian.** He stands at your right hand to protect you in all your paths. **By day.** Our cloud of glory will not be heavy <note>referring to the protective clouds in the desert</note>; the sun by day and the moon by night will not harm you. For the Lord of Heaven will protect you from the heat and the cold which cause sickness. **The Lord will guard you from all evil.** That humans or beasts of prey should not harm you. **He will guard your soul.** That diseases should not come upon you, which are often the result of sins. He will guard your soul from the "Second Death" in the future to come. **In your going and coming.** As it says, in your journeying from the land of your exile back to the Land of Israel in peace, He shall guard you from now until eternity.

**Song** of Ascents, of David. I was glad. This "Song of Ascents" mentions David as the author. The Sages say David composed this when he saw the people of Israel eager to go up to the Temple. It speaks of the time of the exile, longing for the days of the Second Temple. **I was glad.** Every person said to his fellow, "Let us go." **Our feet have been standing.** Because our feet stood at the gates of the crying exiles. **Jerusalem.** He says it is "like a city joined together," meaning the earthly Jerusalem is joined to the heavenly Jerusalem <note>The idea of *Yerushalayim shel ma'ala* (Heavenly Jerusalem) corresponding to the physical city</note>. Who has ever seen a city like this, so beautiful? **To which the tribes go up.** For there the tribes of God used to ascend. It was a testimony for Israel to give thanks to the Name of the Lord. When Jerusalem was "joined together," it served as a witness that the Divine Presence was there. No one ever said to his fellow, "The place is too crowded for me to stay in Jerusalem" <note>A famous quote from the Ethics of the Fathers (Pirkei Avot) about the miracles of the Temple</note>. Furthermore, the thrones of the House of David were there for judgment. **Pray.** This means one should ask for the peace of Jerusalem. This is the central hope of the exile, for as long as the city is in ruins, there is no peace. **May they be secure who love you.** Those who mourn over your destruction will eventually merit to see your joy. **Peace be within your walls.** May there be peace within your military forces and tranquility in your palaces—the buildings of the government within the city. **For the sake.** Every member of the exile says, "For the sake of my brothers, I will speak peace for you." **For the sake of the house.** Because of the House of our God, I will seek what is good for you.

**Song** of Ascents. To You I lift my eyes. This is spoken in the language of the people in exile, whose eyes are fixed upon the Lord to see when He will have mercy. **As the eyes of servants.** Just as a servant waits for the master's hand to provide or to release him from labor, so we wait for the Lord. We have been sated with the contempt of the nations. **Sated.** We have had enough of the knowledge of our troubles. **The scorn of those who are at ease.** This refers to the nations who live in tranquility while we suffer. They mock us and say we have no hope. **The proud.** This word is written as one word but read as two: "the proud ones of the pigeons" <note>A complex linguistic note on the word *Ga'ayionim*</note>. This refers to those who are arrogant. Some midrashic interpretations link this to the "waves of the sea" which rise up. We ask that our eyes be saved from the arrogance of the nations who think they have power over us.

**Song** of Ascents, of David. If it had not been the Lord. This is what Israel says in the exile: **If it had not been the Lord who was on our side when people rose against us.** When the enemies rose to destroy us. **Then.** This word *Azai* (then) is used here in a rhythmic sense. **They would have swallowed us alive.** Like a person who swallows something without chewing it, so they wanted to consume us entirely because of their burning anger. **Then the waters.** This refers to the nations, compared to flooding waters...

# Psalms
### 128

(Right column)
Our help is in the name of the Word <note>original: "Memra"; a term used in Aramaic translations to refer to God’s creative or communicative presence</note> of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.

**A song that was spoken concerning the ascents of the beloved righteous ones who hope in the Word of the Lord: Like Mount Zion, which shall not be moved, but sits forever and ever.** Jerusalem—mountains are all around her, and the Word of the Lord is all around His people, from now and forever. For the scepter of the wicked shall not rest upon the lot of the righteous, so that the righteous do not stretch out their hands in deceit. Do good, O Lord, to the good and to the upright in their hearts. But those who turn aside after their crookedness—the Lord will lead them to Gehenna <note>The Aramaic "Gehennam" is the place of punishment/purgatory</note>, their portion with the workers of lies. Peace be upon Israel!

**A song that was spoken concerning the ascents of Zion's return. When the Lord returned the captivity of Zion, we were like the sick who have been healed.** Then our mouths were filled with laughter and our tongues with praise. Then they said among the nations: "The Lord has done great things for these." The Lord has done great things for us; we were happy. Return, O Lord, our captivity like the land returns when springs of water break out in a drought. Those who sow in tears shall reap in praise. He who goes along weeping, carrying the vessel of seed—he shall surely come with praise, carrying his sheaves of grain.

**A song that was spoken concerning the ascents by Solomon, spoken in the spirit of prophecy.** If the house is not built from before the Word of the Lord, its builders labor in it in vain. If the city of Jerusalem is not guarded from before the Lord, the watchman wakes in vain. It is in vain for you who rise early to stand, to perform your labor, who delay and linger to sleep, who eat your bread—sons of sorrow <note>The Aramaic emphasizes that children can bring worry or pain if not raised well</note>. For He gives sleep to His beloved; behold, children from the seed of the Lord are an inheritance and a merit, and the reward is the fruit of the womb.

<column-break/>

Our help is in the name of the Lord, maker of heaven and earth.

### 125

**A Song of Ascents. Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved, but abides forever.** As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the Lord is round about His people, from this time forth and for evermore. For the scepter of wickedness shall not rest upon the lot of the righteous; lest the righteous put forth their hands unto iniquity. Do good, O Lord, unto those that are good, and to them that are upright in their hearts. But as for such as turn aside unto their crooked ways, the Lord shall lead them away with the workers of iniquity. Peace be upon Israel.

### 126

**A Song of Ascents. When the Lord turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like unto them that dream.** Then was our mouth filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing; then said they among the nations: "The Lord hath done great things for these." The Lord hath done great things for us; whereof we are glad. Turn our captivity, O Lord, as the streams in the South. They that sow in tears shall reap in joy. Though he goeth on his way weeping, bearing the measure of seed, he shall come home with joy, bearing his sheaves.

### 127

**A Song of Ascents; for Solomon. Except the Lord build the house, they labor in vain that build it; except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.** It is vain for you that rise up early, and sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows; for so He giveth unto His beloved sleep. Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord; and the fruit of the womb is a reward. As arrows in the hand of a mighty man, so are the children of youth. Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them; they shall not be put to shame, when they speak with their enemies in the gate.

---

**A song** of Ascents: Those who trust, etc. *Like Mount Zion.* From what you have read, the overall sense is "as a mountain," and the voice is a sign, and the mark is in the heart of the son. # Psalms

As arrows in the hand of a mighty man, so are the children of youth. It is good for the man who has filled his quiver with them; they shall not be ashamed when they speak with their enemies in the gate of the house of judgment.

### 128

A song spoken concerning the ascents from the deep <note>The Aramaic "masekin de-tehoma" interprets the "Song of Ascents" as rising from the primordial depths</note>: Blessed are all who fear the Lord, who walk in His ways. When you eat the labor of your hands, you are blessed in this world, and it shall be well with you in the world to come. Your wife shall be like a fruitful vine on the walls of your house; your children like olive plants surrounding your table. Behold, for thus shall the man be blessed who fears before the Lord. May the Lord bless you from Zion, and may you see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life. And may you see children born to your children; peace be upon Israel.

### 129

A song spoken concerning the ascents from the deep: "Many have afflicted me from my youth," let Israel now say. "Many have afflicted me from my youth, yet they have not prevailed against me." Upon my back, the wicked plowed like those who plow the Torah <note>The Targum here adds a religious layer to the metaphor of the plow</note>; they lengthened their furrows. The Lord is righteous; He has cut the ropes of the wicked. May all who hate Zion be ashamed and turned backward. Let them be like the grass on a roof, which withers before it is pulled up, through which the reaper does not fill his hand, nor the binder of sheaves his arm. And the passers-by do not say to them, "The blessing of the Lord be upon you," nor do they say, "We bless you in the name of the Lord."

### 128

**A Song of Ascents.** Happy is everyone who fears the Lord, who walks in His ways. When you eat the labor of your hands, you are happy, and it is well with you. Upon my back, plowers plowed; they made their furrows long." The Lord is righteous; He has cut the cords of the wicked. ### 130

---

**As arrows.** Because of the advantage of having a son in old age <note>The commentator discusses the timing of having children and their role as protectors</note>, and the king's son immediately succeeds him as his help. So are the children of youth. Therefore, the children born to a man in his youth are a great help to him, like arrows in the hand of a warrior. And behold, if he has good and mighty children in his youth, like the generation of the priests, they were warriors for the king and fought for his aid. All of them were wise and diligent... It is good for a man to pray for good and wise children for himself, as a good portion and inheritance given by God, may He be blessed.

**Fearing.** Because the end of a man is marked by his life and his legacy. Their merit is established when they speak in the gate before the wise... they will be able to speak in the gate before enemies and will not be shattered by them. And concerning the King Messiah, it is translated thus... regarding the Holy Temple and regarding Jerusalem. Behold, the existence of the Temple and the building of Jerusalem... because it was in the hands of the Greeks and the Ishmaelites <note>A reference to the historical control of Jerusalem by various empires</note>. And all the wise and royal ones will build it... for they were the builders who established the foundations. And David first founded Jerusalem... the Ishmaelites destroyed it... and all the days there was war between them until the coming of the Redeemer.

**A Song of Ascents.** Happy is everyone who fears the Lord. He mentions the ways of the precious Lord... anyone who walks in the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, will merit to see the good of Jerusalem. **Who walks in His ways.** He reflects on this now. Then he recounts the lower blessing: **The labor of your hands.** For the best good is that which comes from his own labor from the beginning, and he does not depend on others. If he works and tires himself in labor, he will be in a state of rest: **Happy and it is well with you.** People will say "Happy are you" in this world, and "it is well with you" in the world to come <note>This is a classic Rabbinic interpretation of the dual blessing "Happy" and "Well"</note>.

**Your wife.** This refers to everyone. It mentions the pleasures that dwell in this world... comparing her to a vine. Just as a man plants a vine in the inner parts of his house... so the woman should be modest in the inner parts of the house, not looking outside your house. This is the way of the modest queen. It says **In the inner chambers of your house**, meaning even her daughter should be modest and not leave the house to wander. For this is the way of a bad wife, as it is said of her: "She sits at the door of her house." Instead, she should always be in the inner chambers, seen only by her husband and her household. Like the branches of the vine that are fruitful and multiply.

Afterward, he compares the children: **Like olive plants.** The metaphor of olives is used because the oil of the olive is more exalted than other trees. The plants are good, like the children of one's youth. They are called "plants" from the beginning because they are not illegitimate <note>The commentator emphasizes the purity of the family line</note>. He mentions olives because the olive leaf is green all the days of the year; so too, they will be youths distinguished by good deeds. **Around your table.** They should be before you to be satisfied by the bread you eat, and always around your table, not scattered or devalued, nor eating or drinking except at your table.

**Behold, for thus.** By these traits and behaviors shall the man be blessed who fears the Lord. **May the Lord bless you from Zion.** From the place where His Presence dwells. **And see.** You shall merit to see the good of Jerusalem when Israel returns from exile. **All the days of your life.** You shall see it in goodness all your days, whether in exile or in the goodness of Jerusalem. **And see children to your children.** This refers to the ingathering of the exiles when the Redeemer comes quickly... and peace upon Israel.

**A Song of Ascents.** Greatly have they afflicted me from my youth. Israel speaks this. Comparing the exile to the days of a man's life... from the beginning of the exile they afflicted us greatly. Yet through all this, **they have not prevailed over me** to destroy me as they thought.

**Upon my back.** A metaphor for the abundance of suffering, labor, and shame... like one who plows a field. **They made their furrows long.** The "ma'anit" is the line the plowman makes. The longer the furrow, the greater the labor of the plowers. God is righteous; He will cut and destroy the cords of the wicked, meaning He will remove the yoke from our necks. **May they be ashamed.** When God removes the yoke, they will be ashamed and turn back from their evil thoughts against Zion. **Like the grass on the roofs.** Grass on a roof has no standing or permanence; the heat of the sun withers it. It is not like a seed of blessing... those who hate Israel are compared to this withered grass.
