# SONG
**Of Ascents: Out of the depths I have called You.** This hints at the exile, which is compared to deep waters, as in the matter of "the depths of the sea." **Lord, hear. Who can stand:** Even if we are as fragile as glass, Your mercy will stand for us according to our merit. **For with You.** The explanation is that despite my anger and all the sins, mercy comes from the Kingdom to us, for His kindness is to all who call upon Him. **Why?** People will eventually wait for You because You forgive sins; You open the way for us to return and be forgiven before You. This is to let us know that forgiveness is found within Your kindness, so that You may be feared. **I wait for the Lord.** My soul is strengthened in this world because I have hoped. **And in His word I hope.** Because I have trusted Him to deliver me from the exile. **My soul.** It waits in the night to be hoping for the morning. That is to say, like the morning watchmen who wait to pray. And he says "waiting for the morning" twice to show that from the earliest times they have been waiting and standing every morning to receive Him, or to emphasize the length of the exile. The wise Rabbi Abraham Ibn Ezra <note>original: "Ranc" referring to Ibn Ezra</note> explains the verse as: My soul is more eager for the Lord than those who watch for the morning are for the dawn. **Hope.** Be focused and constant. He tells Israel to hope because He will save you from your sins. **For with Him is mercy.** He is always with the humble and will deal kindly with you. **For with Him is abundant redemption.** Because He has already redeemed you many times from Egypt and from various troubles, so He will redeem you from this exile, for with Him are many ways to pay a ransom for you. **And He.** He will be the one to redeem you. **From all his iniquities.** He will forgive him for his sins. That is, He removes his sins and tests him for good, provided they wait with all their heart.

***

# SONG
**Of Ascents, of David. Lord, my heart is not haughty.** David said this about himself. This matter follows the "Song of Ascents" because even in the exile we are humbled. Therefore, he says, "My heart was not haughty" in secret, "nor were my eyes raised" in public. **I did not walk.** A verb referring to the soul's movement. **In great matters or things too wonderful for me.** In matters of seeking the hidden things that are too difficult for my intellect to grasp. **Surely I have stilled.** He speaks of a quiet spirit and says he silenced his soul for a moment and strengthened his mind. Like a weaned child with its mother, his soul is strengthened within him. **If I have not.** This is an oath. He says: "If I have not humbled and quieted my soul, let such-and-such happen to me." He means that he quieted his soul to be like a suckling baby who waits a little for its mother to nurse it. Just as the child is patient, so is my soul; I have strengthened it so as not to rely on "wonderful things" but to receive from the Lord. **Like a weaned child.** Just as the weaned child is patient, so my soul is patient within me. **Hope.** With these words, he comforts the soul in its hidden and public state. Let it hope in the Lord, and He will fulfill your desires from now and forever.

***

# SONG
**Of Ascents. Lord, remember for David all his afflictions.** David said this psalm when he built the altar on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite <note>A pivotal moment in the Bible (2 Samuel 24) where the site of the future Temple was identified.</note> by the word of Gad the Prophet. He offered burnt offerings and peace offerings and called to the Lord, and He answered him with fire on the altar. He said: "This is the House of God," and this was a joy for Israel. Until that time, the site of the Temple was not known. David sought and found the place of the building through a vision from the Lord. **Remember for David all his afflictions.** Because I did not merit to see the building in my lifetime, but remember the hardship I endured. **How he swore.** He used the language of an oath. **To the Mighty One of Jacob.** Why specifically the "Mighty One of Jacob"? Because Jacob was the first to seek the place of the Temple and called it "the Gate of Heaven." He said "this is none other than the House of God" <note>Genesis 28:17</note>. He saw the ladder in a dream and recognized the site's holiness. Our Sages say that David swore to the "Mighty One of Jacob" because Jacob was the foundation of the tribes. David swore: **I will not enter the tent of my house.** Just as he said: "I dwell in a house of cedar, but the Ark of God dwells within curtains" <note>2 Samuel 7:2</note>. He would not allow himself rest or luxury until a permanent house for the Lord was established. **If I give sleep to my eyes.** He pushed away his sleep to seek the location. His merit and knowledge led him to the site through a prophetic vision. **To my eyelids slumber.** He repeats the idea three times for emphasis.

His enemies I will clothe with shame, but upon himself his crown shall flourish."

->A Song of Ascents, of David: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity!<-
->It is like the precious oil upon the head, running down on the beard, the beard of Aaron, running down on the edge of his garments.<-

->A song that was spoken concerning the ascents from the depths <note>Aramaic: *massukei tehoma*</note>, by the hand of David: Behold, how good and how beautiful it is for brothers to dwell together in unity!<-
->Like the good oil that is poured upon the head, descending upon the beard—the beard of Aaron—which descends to the opening of his garments.<-

---

**Until I find a place for the Lord**: This refers to "the Place," blessed be He. **Dwellings for the Mighty One of Jacob**: What David learned for the Mighty One of Jacob in this place proves what I have explained—that the "place" is what he sought to discover. **Behold, we heard of it**: We heard of it through David, who was searching for the site of the Temple. **Behold, we found it in the fields of the forest**: This refers to the site in Ephratah. Some say this refers to the words of the prophets, who revealed that the chosen site was near Bethlehem-Ephratah. It was known that the Temple was to be built between the territories of Bethlehem and Jerusalem. The Midrash on Psalms explains that the foundation was established by Joshua. There is a tradition from the elders of our city that the chosen place would eventually be revealed. The "forest" refers to the site of the Temple which was once wooded or undeveloped. The Messiah and his wisdom are also hinted at here, for he is the one who will restore the "House of Glory." David mentions "dwellings" in the plural to signify the various chambers of the Sanctuary. **His footstool**: This refers to the place of the Divine Presence, the footstool of the Throne of Glory. **Arise, O Lord**: This is a prayer offered during the dedication of the Temple, as recorded in the Book of Chronicles. David says, "Arise to Your resting place," asking God to bring His Presence to dwell permanently in the Sanctuary.

# A Song
->**of Ascents, of David: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity**<-

**Behold, how good and how pleasant**: The commentator explains that this refers to all the people of Israel when they live as brothers. Once they dwell together in Jerusalem, it is good and pleasant, like the "good oil" that descends upon the beard of Aaron and his sons. The "goodness" is compared to the dew of Mount Zion. This psalm refers to the King Messiah and the High Priest. They are called "brothers" because they share the leadership of Israel. The King sits on the throne of judgment and sovereignty to command Israel in kindness and law, while the Priest teaches the Torah and offers the sacrifices. They are "together" in their greatness, neither one exalting himself over the other. **Like the oil**: Just as the High Priest was anointed by Moses, so too is the King. This is the "oil of anointing" <note>original: *shemen hamishcha*</note>. It signifies that the anointing of Aaron brought a spirit of peace and unity to Israel. The beard of Aaron is mentioned specifically because the anointing oil was poured on his head and flowed down his beard to his garments. This represents the flow of blessing from the head of leadership down to the rest of the people. **His garments**: The word used here (*middotav*) means his clothes.

---

<note>The following section is a medieval commentary, likely drawing from Rashi (Rabbi Shlomo Yitzhaki, 1040–1105) and Radak (Rabbi David Kimhi, 1160–1235), explaining the philosophical and literal meaning of the verses.</note>

**As the dew of Hermon.** Like dew that stays in a specific place. This means that even if the dew of Hermon is lacking, it is made up for by the dew that descends upon the mountains of Zion. The intention is to say that the dew of Hermon from the great mountains <unclear>fills the lack</unclear> of kindness. Just as one whose kindness is full, so a lack of trust will be rectified. He mentions "the mountains of Zion" because Rashi, of blessed memory, explained that Jerusalem has "mountains surrounding it." He mentions each verse to show the strength of the kindness... as it is written, "a cup of blessing," and mentions the kindness upon the grass... "as the dew of Hermon." Kindness is like dew upon these mountains, a security of kindness like the blessing of the Lord... for there, on the mountains of Zion, the Lord commanded the blessing, and this is kindness "forevermore." And "forevermore" is explained as "life," as it is written, "for he asked life of You," a permanent and eternal life.

## Song
**of Ascents. Behold, bless the Lord.** It is His custom to grant the grace of blessing as He wills; he also thought at the beginning that each person is rewarded according to their deeds. Therefore, he mentions "all the servants of the Lord," the pious ones and the workers who stand and serve in the nights, specifically in the House of the Lord to give thanks to His name. **Lift up your hands in holiness.** This means with holy cleanliness <note>Refers to the ritual washing of hands before prayer or service</note>. The meaning of "lift up your hands" is like taking hands from the pure waters of the Sanctuary... according to my opinion, it refers to the commandment of the hands in prayer, following the idea of "let us lift our hearts with our hands." As the Sages <term>hazal</term> said regarding the "Holy of Holies" (*Devir Kodesh*). When one reaches the Sanctuary, the kindness of the Lord strengthens the holiness. **May He bless you.** According to the commentators, this means the Priests will seal the blessing for Israel. It is possible to explain that the song returns to the grace of the Lord... "from Zion," for that is the place where the blessing rests for all Israel and all the earth. Then, **Maker of heaven and earth**, meaning He provides sustenance, and the blessing increases in the world, and a sound of joy connects the earth to provide its produce.

## Hallelujah
**Praise the name of the Lord.** Psalm 135. It begins with Hallelujah and divides into "Praise the name of the Lord" for the places of His kindness and "Praise, O servants of the Lord" for the places of His strength and His presence in the House of the Lord. He concludes the psalm with the House of the Lord—and the Priests. **In the courts of the house of our God.** For those standing in the courtyards... the kindness and praise given by those who praise God's essence... **Hallelujah! For the Lord is good.** It is proper to praise Him for He is good, and "sing to His name" because it is His will and kindness.

**For Jacob.** He mentions mercy before us over all nations... **For I know.** The psalm mentions His name, His caution, and the holiness of His kindness... "I know" from His wonders and His faithfulness that the kindness of our Lord is great... The kindness of the heavens is prepared... all kindness is according to judgment... we did not receive our merit based on our own worth but through the special kindness of the Great One. All the kindness of the Place <note>a common rabbinic name for God, *HaMakom*</note> and the conduct of the worlds is according to His voice and wisdom.

**Whatever the Lord pleases, He does.** All their guidance and boundaries are according to His will; nothing is lacking from them. He mentions the kindness of Moses and His deeds in the waters and the depths. He mentions the "seas" as the Great Sea and the "depths" as the deep waters. He adds more wonders on the earth, specifically regarding rain... as it is said that every drop is counted. Therefore he says: **He causes the vapors to ascend.** These are the clouds. They are explained as "ascending" because they rise from the earth and settle above, as it is written, "a mist ascended from the earth." It says "from the ends of the earth," meaning from the edge of the sea, for they rise from the water... He says that even from a small cloud the size of a palm, clouds rise. He mentions that at the time of rain, there is a great pressure of lightning with the rain. **He brings forth the wind from His treasuries.** Wind is created moment by moment, like something taken from a storehouse. Before it blows, we do not feel it; once it blows, we do. It is as if it was just prepared in the "house of blowing." The sage Rabbi Abraham ibn Ezra <note>RABG/Ibn Ezra, 1089–1167, a famous Spanish biblical commentator</note> wrote that the reason for mentioning this is to show that nothing is lacking in His power. Here he mentions the four elements...

From here he mentions the **plague of the firstborn** specifically, because through it they gained merit. **He sent signs and wonders.** This is a general term for the plagues. They were signs because all that the Lord pleases, He does; these plagues did not happen by chance... **In your midst, O Egypt.** The word "middle" is used like in "the midst of Jerusalem." **Upon Pharaoh and all his servants.** Even the highest leaders of Egypt could not escape God's will. Furthermore, He dealt with **many nations and slew mighty kings.** He mentions the kings specifically because they used their power to resist God's will. He mentions **Sihon and Og** specifically because they were the first to be defeated and were more powerful than the others, as it is written, "his height was like the height of cedars." Afterward, he mentions the kingdoms of Canaan in general. **And He gave.** He did kindness with Israel His people by giving them the land of all those kingdoms. **O Lord, Your name.** The verse repeats the idea of God's eternal name with Israel. **For the Lord will judge.** He intends to give kindness in the exile so that Israel will not be lost... He will judge His people against the nations... for they have already received their punishment and it is time for their comfort. **The idols of the nations.** These are the servants of the nations, who have no substance. They will be abandoned in their time of trouble, for they are but silver and gold... as explained in the previous psalm. **They have a mouth.** This means they do not speak; there is no breath in their mouths, only the vanity of the lips.

**Like them** • By way of prayer • Therefore, in the future to come, the idolaters and those who trust in them will be like them in their nothingness. **House of Israel** • Those who come from among the nations to seek refuge under the wings of the Presence <note>The Divine presence, or Shekhinah</note> • or those attributed to the seed of the Patriarchs. **(And so)** **House of Aaron** • These are the Priests who serve. Aside from the **House of Levi** • who sing before Him in His Temple. And among all of them, they shall conclude by "Blessing the Lord." They are the wise ones who isolate themselves in the House of the Lord to learn • God will pay the reward to everyone who acts with all their might to pray in the House of the Lord. **Blessed be the Lord from Zion** • For there His glory shall dwell in Jerusalem, a place of praise for all generations, and they shall bless Him and recount His deeds.

# **Give Thanks**
**To the Lord, for He is good; for His mercy is forever** • This psalm has twenty-six verses • and they all conclude with "for His mercy is forever." Our Sages of blessed memory said that this corresponds to the twenty-eight <note>likely a scribal error or variant for 26</note> generations from the beginning of the world until they received the Torah; God sustained them through His grace and kindness • for the world existed without the Torah solely through grace and kindness. Therefore, they start with the twelve established ones against the Assembly of Israel • and according to the plain meaning <note>Hebrew: *Peshat*</note>, all these are matters of renewal • and they have a logic in their division • and they concluded with twenty-six according to the matters explained in the psalm. 

After the beginning of the psalm, they are to the Lord for all who enter the world • and it is "to the Lord for He is good," for it is better to give thanks to the Lord because His mercy is forever and shall not depart • and likewise, it is part of the goodness and mercy that He is the "God of gods" and "Lord of lords" • this was done by the Lord alone • and they are to the "Lord of lords" • and they are the masters who have the rule of law over them. **To Him who does great wonders alone** • He is the "Lord of lords" • and He, blessed be His name, alone does wonders • **To Him who does great wonders alone** which are not done by the angels or the celestial spheres <term>Galgallim; refers to the medieval astronomical concept of concentric spheres carrying the planets</term> which revolve in the sphere of the world, and each one has a purpose like a part of the connection of the spheres and the constellations, which are parts of the world in the secret of the wonders of the creation of things from the power of the heavens with understanding. 

And the reason the Torah concluded with the stars is "with understanding, for His mercy is forever" • and why did it conclude with understanding? Because in the Works of Creation, God created the heavens and the earth upon the waters • and the reason is that all the wonders of the spheres are the Creator's • and they are to show the handiwork of the heavens. And it explains **To Him who spread the earth upon the waters** for His mercy is forever, for the dry land was separated from the midst of the waters • and the stars are to rule the rivers and streams. And so, it is one group from the power of the sun by day and the moon and stars by night—a wondrous matter. And it explains **the great lights** • because they are great in their dimensions and they shine, and it concludes here "for His mercy is forever" • because the light within them is received by the leaders, the princes, the spheres, and the stars from the Supernal Light. Thus, the mercy of the Creator is found in that He gave them power and illuminated them from His light • and this is His mercy forever. 

After mentioning the wonders of the Creator in the spheres • he mentioned His wonders among those who inhabit the world • and this is **who struck Egypt in their firstborn** • because all the plagues that Pharaoh was struck with in Egypt were not a mercy to the world • only a mercy to Israel to bring them out from there. And why did he conclude all of them with "for His mercy is forever"? Because in the Torah it is written "for His mercy is forever" • and he explained that because the firstborn were the essence and root of Egypt, and they were sinners before Him above all inhabitants of the world through violence • so judgment came upon them • and mercy came to all by striking them. And concerning this it is said, **And He brought Israel out from among them for His mercy is forever** • and the plague was a lofty wonder to the world • **with a strong hand and an outstretched arm for His mercy is forever** • because with this hand He broke the power of the supernal princes and the stars that lead through the power of the constellations, and this is a mercy to the world to make known the power of the Kingdom of the Lord over every existing thing. 

**And to Him who divided the Sea of Reeds into parts** • as it is written in the Midrash <note>Ancient rabbinic commentary</note> that it was torn into twelve parts • and this is a mercy to the world because through this it was known that He is the Ruler of sea and land, and there is no escape from His hand except to take refuge in the shadow of His wings. **And He overthrew Pharaoh and his army in the Sea of Reeds** • for by this the power of the wicked was removed. And with all these miracles, He led His people in the wilderness • and this is **To Him who led His people through the wilderness** • for the wilderness was a place of serpents, fiery snakes, scorpions, and thirst where there is no water, yet He encompassed them with mercy • for the Holy One, blessed be He, prepared all their needs in the wilderness. 

And therefore it is said, **To Him who struck great kings** • for the mercy was completed by striking great kings entirely, and that Israel were in their path in their portion through all the plagues • and that was a mercy to the world. **And He slew mighty kings** • for the mercy was fenced in for the sake of Israel because they would not allow them to pass through the land to cross their border • and there was mercy to the world so that they would know in every place that mercy is from of old. And what is written regarding **Sihon and Og, king of Bashan** • is because they were from the seed of Nimrod and were giants, because they were in all places, and the whole world boasted of them and feared them. And because they were the great preventers of Israel from coming to the Land, and the Lord gave their border to Israel as a heritage • thus far it is explained. 

And it can be explained that all these mercies are revealed to all who enter the world with great publicity • and if a man says in his heart, "perhaps there was no mercy for us," no and no! For by this, the mercy of the Holy One, blessed be He, is known in every generation • for He breaks the wall of the enemy and enemies and gives their land as a heritage • as it is written. And this is a greater mercy than that, for in every generation they stand against us to destroy us • and the Holy One, blessed be He, saves us from their hand • this is the great mercy for Israel. And he concluded **and He redeemed us from our oppressors for His mercy is forever** • within the existence that the Creator created. **And He gives bread to all flesh** • explicitly, for this is a mercy to every living thing. And the mercy fenced in the matter of Israel is written publicly • and they are all a mercy greater than this, for the mercy of the Lord is to every living thing, sustaining and providing, and He heard and gave bread. And it is the great mercy that He is able to bestow upon all the living • and this is the mercy explained in the verse. 

After all these things, he concluded with **Give thanks to the God of heaven** • and this is the general mercy. And the reason is that all this praise mentioned thus far are things and mercy visible in this world • but the mercy of the Lord forever applies to the souls of the pious • and this is the mercy that appears for eternity • and this is "mercy forever and ever." For the mercy of the body will not stand except for a little while • but the mercy of the soul is what stands forever. And therefore **Give thanks to the God of heaven** • for from there the mercy shall come forth to the soul which is from heaven and returns to heaven. And this is a mercy greater than that. Therefore he concluded with the prayer of "Give thanks to the Lord" • and this is a mercy greater than all. And he concluded with the prayer of "Give thanks to the Lord" • and this is the great mercy and that which is worthy of His mercy. **And He gives bread to all flesh** • because every living thing lives by the power of His mercy. Completion, the glory of the Lord. And this is a great mercy. "No eye has seen a God besides You" <note>Isaiah 64:4</note>. And he concluded with "Give thanks to the God of heaven." And this is the great mercy. And regarding this it is said to the Priests in the House of the Lord to give thanks and praise before the glory of His kingdom • for mercy is fenced in and gives repentance. And all these things are to increase your trust <note>Hebrew: *Bitachon*</note> • for every corner you turn to the Lord is above the constellations. Therefore he mentioned all these things to show trust in Him, blessed be His name. And furthermore, a great ledger exists and is established • to live forever until the future to come, his servant the Messiah and the bread of Israel • and according to all this world, they are the Resurrection of the Dead.

By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat, we also wept when we remembered Zion. Upon the willows in its midst we hung our harps. O daughter of Babylon, destined to be destroyed, happy is he who repays you the recompense you dealt to us. Happy is he who seizes and dashes your infants against the rock.

## The Inheritance of David, King of Israel
Our Rabbis of blessed memory explained that Hezekiah and his assembly arranged this <term>Siddur</term> <note>Meaning the arrangement of these specific psalms.</note> by the command of the King. This refers to what was given to Nebuchadnezzar to embolden his heart over the mixed multitude of Jews; Hezekiah and they called out and agreed with them that the "lowest parts" were for redemption... and what is the reward for this? Their reward is upon all these things. And were it not that Maimonides <note>original: הרמב"ם (Rambam)</note> mentioned this, and it is my hope... <unclear>and so it is decreed for every matter the power of the psalm of his kingdom as mentioned above. For he composed in this psalm "for His mercy endures forever" as a refrain for every kindness...</unclear>

**By** the rivers of Babylon, there we sat, we also wept when we remembered Zion. This psalm was spoken in the language of the exiled singers who were exiled in the Babylonian captivity. It recounts how by the rivers of Babylon they would mourn and weep, leaving their harps there [instead of] in Zion. **Upon the willows.** These are "willows of the brook," for willows grow on the banks of rivers. Their security and rest were by the riverbanks, yet the rivers stood between them and the exile, bitter and harsh. **For there our captors asked us.** "Words of song." It was as if they were mocking us, saying "Sing for us," intending to do evil and cause pain in our visible distress. When they saw us in our groups in the Babylonian exile from afar... and this is the kindness of David, peace be upon him...

**Of David** I give You thanks with all my heart. With all my heart, my will, and my entire being. And so we said regarding the tribes of Gad and Reuben and the Sages. Like the phrase **before the Elohim**, which is a well-known matter. Thanksgiving happens in the heart alone, while the "lip" and "melody" are with the mouth. **I bow down toward Your holy Temple.** Toward the House that contained the Ark. **For Your steadfast love and Your truth.** The "love" <term>Hesed</term> refers to the redemption from exile, and the "truth" <term>Emet</term> is the fulfillment of the matter of the monarchy as He promised him, even after many burdens and bitterness had passed over it. **For You have magnified Your word above all Your name.** Like a story; for the story of the Name is the power of His providence over you. And in every place, the power of the story... <note>Transcription of commentary is abbreviated due to density and script style.</note>

**And they shall sing.** They shall say a song and praise to the Lord and rejoice in His ways and His wondrous deeds. For in His hand is everything, to lower and to raise. And they shall always say that the glory of the Lord is great. And they shall say the words of the song. For in this way David speaks for himself, and likewise in all the Psalms. And so we find in the renewal of all the Scripture: "From him we were afraid, Heaven forbid," etc., for it was the law that in the way of David, in the way of war, he sent. For it is the rule for everyone, "Go, see the generation," from outside of him and by the strength of his powerful hand—Sihon the king of Sihon, to you alone. And he said, "Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who performed kindness outside the waters and the grace of the land, lacking from the Lord, to the generation, a Psalm," etc. All of this comes from the version <note>original: גירסא (girsa) - a traditional reading or study version.</note> of David our king, and under his hand, by his strong hand from the heavens and strong from the earth. "Your kindness," for it will be completed, for the Lord will reward him. "Spare and pity," etc., "and Your arm," etc., "and kindness and kindness," and "complete the deeds," etc. "From the darkness," for there is no word on the tongue. All these interpretations are similar to one another and show the kindness of the Lord and His wisdom and also His decree. Our priests have directed their words until they meet the kindness of the Lord. They prayed to see the wonders of the Lord and His fallen deeds; His hand shall scatter them. Merciful One, have mercy on us. The interpretation is: "He granted him height," and "from afar," the kindness of the heavens is spread out from the kindness of the waters, far from the earth, and his way is long and most of it is lacking from the Lord, and there His world is explained and famous, and He knows and informs. And by the power of "Your hand shall lead us and hold me," etc., and "afar off He performs kindness and grace," for it is the will of the Lord that "they sing in it," etc., and "the words of the song," etc. These are fitting from the heavens. Spare, Merciful One, have mercy, great is the glory of the Lord in war, strong, etc. And why is it said "the kindness of the Lord and all"? Because Your hand shall break his right hand. And it is written like the strength in the work of the hands suddenly "and You revive me." **Against the anger of my enemies.** On the verse: "If I walk in the midst of trouble You will revive me; You will stretch out Your hand in the midst of my enemies and Your right hand shall save me." **The Lord will perfect that which concerns me.** Like "You opened and it was solved." **Lord, Your kindness is forever; do not forsake the works of Your hands.** May the kindness of the Lord be with me forever, and do not leave the works of Your hands when You rest, etc., for is the work of Your hand the living work of Your people, etc. And You will fight against me and You desired those who do Your words, Your kindness.

You have seen this, etc., everything is before Him, etc., words of wisdom and ethics, everything is before Him, may He be blessed. And the explanation of His knowledge is that everything is seen and nothing is hidden. I have searched my heart all the days, etc. And all this is a broad and wonderful explanation, etc.

-> Gladly I said to the Lord: "You are my God; listen, O Lord, to the voice of my prayer." God the Lord, the strength of my deliverance, You have been a shield over my head in the day of conflict. <-

**I will praise You:** They interpreted the words *fearful* and *wonderful* as a verb referring to the Name of the Blessed One, for all His wonders are fearful in all His guidance of us and the preservation of our limbs from beginning to end. **And my soul knows very much:** The meaning of this word is attached to "wonderful are Your works"—that is to say, Your works are very wonderful, and my soul knows it. According to the plain meaning of the verses, it lacks the word "and wonders," and its explanation is: Your works are wonderful, and it is also missing "from it." You have placed within me a soul that is wiser and more intellectual than other living beings, and it knows Your wonderful works and praises You for them. The wonders and the generations of the heavens are revealed and hidden to the wise of the heavens, for every wise man is perfected in his wisdom, and all choice wisdom is to stand and reflect, and every womb is to understand their power, and within it, it will contain the wonders of the Rock and be his forever. It is not the purpose to recount in this composition the wisdom of anatomy and their utility, the mixing of the humors and their distress, and the way of their story. But what is hidden is supported by the secrets of the wise. **My frame was not hidden from You:** My essence was not hidden. The commentators associated this with the word "essence" (*atzmi*) meaning the intended form and shape, such as the perfection and body of the bone. He says: my body was not hidden from You when it was formed in secret in my mother's belly, as it says, "I was woven in the lowest parts of the earth." This is a metaphor for the place of concealment and hiddenness, called here "the depths of the earth." Similarly, it is said "in the belly of the earth." He means to say it is as if his bones were gathered from above. The explanation of "I was made" refers to actions like those done in the dark. From the words of the sages and "depths," you should interpret this concealment regarding the formation, like the treading of the master and the bottom of the vat and its height, like the treading of the master and the movements of the hand. For there was a dispute written here, and a person would say that the formation is like a sketch from the writing. And he said of it "I was woven" (*rukamti*), which refers to needlework in the language of the Hebrews and in the Talmud, and it is hidden below and written. And Rabbi Saadia Gaon explained that the body was like a garment before it had the light of action. And the secret from the beginning of my essence is living. He means to say everything exists before it is wise to create, and also in this composition, and so the rest of the book and its writer. It is written as if it were in a book and all shall be written, and the matter is cut off as written, and also from the beginning it was in the eyes of all my essence. My eyes to the heart, and it opens from the middle of the chest. **My unformed substance** (*Galmi*): This is the body that is folded before it has limbs, like a vessel which is a mass before the work of the craftsman. He said: these Your eyes saw, for through them You saw the limbs even before they were formed. **And in Your book they were all written:** These are the days that are fashioned, like a path written in a book. The explanation of "all of them" is all the limbs before they are known, which is similar to his word. **The days were fashioned:** For in many days the fashioning of the limbs is completed, for they are not created all at once. **When as yet there was none of them:** This means there was one among them, for if a person's knowledge is wise and he thinks, and not all as one. And its explanation is that there was not one among them that they did not know what day it would be. And the explanation for my soul is that it was written for God because it was in the word and brought into all the beginnings of its descent. And all were there in the power of the creation, and no animal was missing, and no one from the number of others, and so it was created and made after the manner of birth. **And to me how precious are Your thoughts, O God:** The word "precious" here means rarity or scarcity, as in "the word of the Lord was precious in those days." And the explanation of "Your thoughts" is Your intentions. **How vast is the sum of them:** He says my thoughts are numerous, as he said "I will count them." He means to say my thoughts are stronger than the strong and more numerous than the stars, as in "they were stronger than me." And "their heads" means their principles, as in "when you take the sum (*rosh*) of the children of Israel," meaning the principles of Your intentions in creation are many in all their details. **I will count them:** If I gather to count them, I would not be able, for they are more than the sand. **I awake and I am still with You:** Even if there is light or if I am asleep, in both I find my essence is with You. That is to say, in the thought of the soul's intelligence. This is the explanation of the commentators on the grammatical details. I am always precious, for my thought is in them until I am whole and there is no more left. He said "with You always." And Ibn Ezra said: he intended to swear that as long as I think in my heart to know my end, and I am wise as long as I am hurried to You, and I am good in my dwelling in wisdom, and I search in a second wisdom, and if you are the one thought of from me, therefore he said "I awake and I am still with You," for this is the way of all perfections. **If You would slay:** This is attached to "I awake and I am still with You," for these things are always in my thoughts, in Your stories and Your wonders and the goodness of Your works, which are explained as the matter of the wicked. And if You kill them, who disturb me—they are the speakers and the men of blood—he says to them "depart from me," and so on. And "if You would slay" refers to the men of blood, and such are my thoughts and all my business with You. **Who speak against You:** with the loss of the *aleph*, as in "they speak." And "mischief" (*limzimah*) means for thought, meaning they speak of You according to their thoughts, which is the wickedness of the eyes of the enemy. A day was created for mischief, as it says "his name is spoken," a matter of thinking. **Your enemies take Your name in vain:** These are Your enemies and Your opponents. In the explanation of "in vain" (*lashav*), the word "take" (*nasu*) means they lifted. For no one was missed. As in "they lifted," and even his house was lifted. And "Your enemies" (*arekha*) means Your opponents, as in "it became your enemy." He means to say Your name is in their mouths for nothing. And "Your enemies" is in place of "Your haters." **Do I not hate those who hate You:** The verse is doubled in meaning with different words. Our rabbis of blessed memory said this verse refers to heretics and unbelievers. And the word "those who rise up against You" is explained as those who rebel. **I contend:** A matter of a quarrel (*ktatah*), in the words of our rabbis. **Perfect hatred:** A great hatred so that I cannot hate them more. The matter is doubled for emphasis. **Search me:** Since the thought of the wicked is evil regarding the thought of God, he said: "Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me," for my heart is upright in Your paths. **My thoughts** (*sar'apai*): My reflections. Like "in the multitude of my thoughts within me." They are compared to branches on a tree (*sar'appim*), for thoughts in the heart are like branches on a tree. **And see if there be any wicked way in me:** A way of rebellion. **And lead me:** If You see any way of rebellion, lead me away from it immediately; this is the "way everlasting," as in "I too am going the way of all the earth," for he goes on the way to his eternal home.

## To the Chief Musician
**A Psalm of David:** This psalm was composed by David concerning the slanders and the informants who were slandering him to Saul. **Deliver me, O Lord:** One should not think these were evil things, and the verse is doubled for emphasis. **Who imagine:** They think evil thoughts in the heart and establish them as such. **Every day they stir up wars:** They gather, as in "they gather in their net." The word refers to gathering for the purpose of a trap. **They have sharpened:** Like a sharpened arrow. Their lips are bitter, for they are full of those who speak wickedly like a serpent that sharpens its tongue in its mouth. **Adder's poison:** The venom of a snake that casts out poison. The "adder" (*achshub*) is a type of snake that is very small and very bitter. **Guard me:** I said that when I am protected from the evil man and from the violent man, he is saved from them. **The proud have hidden:** He compares that person who was full of pride. **From the hands:** After recounting the slanders of the wicked, he prays to God that He should guard him from what they have planned for us. **They hidden a snare:** A snare and a stone they set in the king's hand. **By the wayside:** In a place where there were two paths, as it says "and he saw the place." **I said to the Lord:** When I feared that the words of the informants were being heard. In those places I said: You are my God. **Strength of my salvation:** Hear and gather to me the strength of my salvation so that my prayer does not fall. **You covered my head in the day of armor:** For the word's explanation is on my head, armor and helmet and all weapons of war. That is to say, You have placed a helmet of salvation on my head. **You covered:** Past tense in place of future, as is common.

**Translation:** When my spirit is weary within me, You know the path on which I walk; they have hidden a snare for me.

<margin>Let it not refuse</margin> Let it not withhold. Let it not be waved away from me. <margin>Anointing</margin> The holy oil of anointing that was my portion, He gave for my remembrance.
<margin>In his nets</margin> In his snares. <margin>Together until I pass</margin> The wicked shall all fall together, and I shall pass. <margin>Maskil</margin> According to the Midrash Aggada <note>A tradition of homiletic interpretation</note>, every psalm David uttered regarding a trouble that would come upon him and all Israel is called "Maskil."
<margin>When faints</margin> When my spirit was enveloped in me with pain and suffering.

<margin>Let the righteous smite me</margin> King David, peace be upon him, said: Let the righteous man strike me with his kindness and rebuke me, and this will be better for me than "oil of the head"—which is the oil with which they used to anoint kings and high priests. Let that oil not be withheld from my head, for my desire is that the righteous one should strike me with kindness and rebuke me, rather than have the wicked man anoint me with his oil. <margin>For my prayer is yet against their evil</margin> Meaning, even if they strike me and discipline me, there are still many evils—the evils of the wicked—and my prayer is to be saved from them. Thus our Sages of blessed memory <note>Hebrew: *RaZaL*</note> said that David used to pray regarding Doeg and Ahithophel <note>Traitors to David</note> that they should have no portion in the World to Come. <margin>Their judges were thrown down by the sides of the rock</margin> Regarding the kings and the great men of the generation, King David said: The judges of the wicked who were pursuing him were cast down by the hand of the rock and killed—these were Saul and Abner and their faction. <margin>And they heard my words for they are sweet</margin> The children of Israel, when Saul was killed, heard the words of David, who lamented with a great lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son; they knew my words were "sweet," for I did not rejoice in the death of Saul my enemy, and so they made me king over them.

<margin>As when one plows and cleaves the earth, etc.</margin> He means that the righteous who are put to death by the wicked are scattered like these clods of dust dug up from the earth; and just as the earth heals and returns to its former state, so these who die for the Sanctification of the Name <note>Martyrdom</note> will rise in the Resurrection. <margin>For toward You, O God, are my eyes, etc.</margin> The prayer of David, peace be upon him, who said to the Holy One, Blessed be He: My eyes hang upon You, therefore do not leave my soul "naked"—meaning, do not let it be stripped and weak, but let it be strengthened in faith and trust. <margin>Keep me from the hands of the snare, etc.</margin> His prayer further to be saved from the snares and traps of the wicked. <margin>Let the wicked fall into their own nets, etc.</margin> Meaning, let all the wicked fall into a single net together, and I shall pass in peace. <margin>Nets</margin> <note>Hebrew: *mikmorav*</note> is a tool for catching fish, meaning his snares.

## Maskil
Of David when he was in the cave; a prayer. There were times when David was in the cave and Saul came in while David was hiding in the inner parts, as it is written (1 Samuel 24:3): "And Saul went in to cover his feet <note>A biblical euphemism for using the bathroom</note>, and David and his men were sitting in the innermost parts of the cave." <margin>With my voice to the Lord I cry, with my voice to the Lord, etc.</margin> He repeats it twice to remember the outcry. <margin>I pour out my complaint before Him</margin> Speech of the heart is called "complaint" <note>Hebrew: *sichah*</note>. <margin>My trouble before Him I tell</margin> Speech of the mouth is called "telling" <note>Hebrew: *hagadah*</note>. <margin>When my spirit faints within me</margin> Like something covered; anything covered is called "faint" <note>Hebrew: *atuf*</note>. His heart was anxious and sighing, and he had no fear except of the Holy One, Blessed be He, alone, as it is written (ibid. verse 5): "David's heart smote him." Therefore he said, "For You know my path," saying: You know the strength of the heart, and that my intention was not to kill Saul. <margin>In the way wherein I walk, etc.</margin> Its meaning is that in the very path David wished to go, Doeg and the Ziphites were going and slandering him to King Saul.

Grant not, O Lord, the desires of the wicked; do not further his evil device, lest they exalt themselves. Selah.
The head of those that surround me, let the mischief of their own lips cover them.

Let burning coals fall upon them; let them be cast into the fire, into deep pits, that they rise not up again.

**Translation:** Do not grant, O Lord, the lusts of the wicked man; do not provide his request and his hidden plan forever. Let the head of those who surround me be covered by the weariness of their own lips. Let coals of fire be moved upon them; He shall cast them into the Gehenna of flaming fire so that they do not rise to the life of the world to come. A murmuring man shall not be established in the land; a man of violent evil—the angel of death shall hunt him and push him into Gehenna. I know that the Lord will perform the judgment of the poor, the judgment of the lowly. But the righteous shall give thanks to Your name; the upright shall sit before You.

### 141

Lord, I cry unto You, make haste unto me; give ear unto my voice when I cry unto You.
Let my prayer be set forth before You as incense; and the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice.
Set a guard, O Lord, over my mouth; keep watch over the door of my lips.
Incline not my heart to any evil thing, to practice wicked works with men that work iniquity; and let me not eat of their dainties.
**Translation:** Lord, I have called You, hasten to me; listen to my voice at the time I call to You. Let my prayer be established like the spice of incense before You, the lifting of my hands like the evening meal-offering. Place, O Lord, a guard for my mouth; watch over the door of my lips. Do not incline my heart to an evil matter, to linger in wickedness with men who practice falsehood, and I shall not be supported by their pleasant customs.

---

<margin>Desires of the wicked</margin> His coveted things. <margin>Do not further his device</margin> Do not give him his desire, lest they grow haughty and say, "My power and the might of my hand have gotten me this wealth." <margin>Head of those surrounding me</margin> It opens with the previous psalm: those who encompass me and surround me. <margin>Mischief of their lips</margin> That which they spoke evil against me shall cover them. <margin>Coals</margin> Burning embers. <margin>In deep pits</margin> A deep pit. <margin>Incline not my heart to evil</margin> So that they do not say of their evil deeds that they are good. Why is the language of "plots" <note>Hebrew: *alilot*</note> written? To indicate false words; this is "plotting in wickedness." <margin>Let me not eat of their dainties</margin> Meaning, I will not be their companion at their feasts.

<margin>Grant not, O Lord, etc.</margin> King David, peace be upon him, said to the Holy One, Blessed be He: Do not give the wicked man his desires. <margin>Desires</margin> A term of coveting and will. <margin>Do not further his device</margin> David said: Do not give him his desire, so he does not say he achieved everything through his own wisdom. Therefore, do not grant his device "lest they exalt themselves"—meaning, if they obtain their desire and their thought, their hearts will be exalted against the Divine Presence, saying, "Our power and the might of our hands have gotten us this wealth." <margin>Head of those surrounding me, etc.</margin> He who is the head of all who surround me—those rebels who spoke evil of me, namely Doeg and Ahithophel and their faction, who gathered for war against me and wanted to destroy me—let the mischief of their own lips cover them and kill them. <margin>Let them fall upon them, etc.</margin> His prayer further against those wicked ones, that coals of fire should fall on them and they be cast into Gehenna, from which there is no rising. <margin>A man of tongue, etc.</margin> This is Doeg, who used to tell slander; he shall not be established in the land—meaning, he will fall from his greatness and his land. <margin>A man of violent evil shall be hunted, etc.</margin> The angel appointed over the wicked will hunt the wicked man and push him from one trap to another, and so from trap to trap until he reaches Gehenna, from which he has no recovery. <margin>I know that the Lord will maintain the cause of the poor, etc.</margin> Meaning, I know in truth that the Holy One, Blessed be He, will execute the judgment of the poor and the justice of the needy. <margin>Surely the righteous shall give thanks to Your name, etc.</margin> Meaning, when the Holy One, Blessed be He, executes judgment upon the wicked, then the righteous will thank and praise the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. <margin>The upright shall dwell in Your presence</margin> Meaning, at that time when judgment is done and the upright are saved, they will always be clinging to You.

## Psalm
141: Lord, I cry unto You, etc. Behold, King David, peace be upon him, in this prayer asked of the Holy One, Blessed be He, that He hear his prayer like the smell of incense and like the evening sacrifice. <margin>Set a guard, O Lord, over my mouth</margin> David asked of the Holy One, Blessed be He, to place a guard over his mouth so that he would not speak things that are unseemly; likewise, "keep watch over the door of my lips"—the meaning is doubled with different words. <margin>Incline not my heart, etc.</margin> Meaning, do not let my heart incline after the wickedness of the wicked. <margin>To practice wicked works</margin> So they do not say of their wickedness that they are good deeds and not sins. <margin>With men that work iniquity</margin> these are the wicked who do evil. <margin>And let me not eat of their dainties</margin> Lest they count me as a partner with them in their evil-doing or as a partner in their money and wealth. <margin>Dainties</margin> <note>Hebrew: *man'amim*</note> is a term for delicacies, and he means: Let them not draw my heart to their food and drink.

**Look to the right and see.** "Look" is the root of the verb and an imperative form. It is said as if to say: Look to the right and observe that there is no helper for me and no one who recognizes me. Therefore he said, **refuge has failed me**, because the power of the enemy surrounds me on every side and I do not know where to flee, and **no one cares for my soul** to save me from the hand of my enemy. The meaning of **refuge has failed me** is that the paths of escape have been cut off from me.

# Psalm
**O Lord, hear.** David composed this psalm when he fled from his son Absalom. He said, "Behold, now I have touched the trouble of my soul," for when David was in flight from Saul, it was similar to what happened when he fled from Saul <note>The text likely means to contrast the two flights</note>. But now, in the flight from his son Absalom, he was in greater distress and thought in his heart whether he would succeed or not. Therefore he said: **O Lord, hear my prayer. Give ear to my supplications.** That is to say, "Now in the distress of my soul I call upon You." **Answer me in Your righteousness.** And "Your righteousness" refers to the charity <note>The Hebrew word *Tzedakah* can mean both righteousness and charity</note> found in God. **And do not enter into judgment with Your servant.** Meaning, do not deal with me according to the strict judgment written in the Torah based on my deeds. For in terms of the reward You grant a man according to his mouth, **no one living is righteous before You.** And it is written in the commentary of Rashi, of blessed memory, that by Your charity You have allowed man to live in this world. The verse is explained thus because the heavenly Attribute of Justice is not like the attribute of flesh and blood, for no man can withstand it. And it is written in the Midrash <note>Traditional homiletic interpretation</note>: David said, "Do not stand with me in the Attribute of Justice; even with the righteous, You do not conclude the judgment." **For the enemy has pursued.** This refers to his son Absalom who pursues his father. **Crushed my life to the ground.** For I thought in my heart that He would not restore me to my kingdom. **Made me dwell in darkness.** According to the Midrashic interpretation, this refers to the incident where he clung to Bathsheba. **Like those who have long been dead.** For he was afraid lest he perish in this world and the world to come. **Therefore my spirit is overwhelmed.** For my spirit has reached its end within me. **My heart is desolate.** And according to the Midrash, this was at the moment he remembered the incident of Bathsheba and his heart was afraid. **I remember the days of old.** I brought to my heart the kings who reigned before, or I remembered the deeds of the Patriarchs. **I meditate on all Your works.** In the interpretation: things done by Your word. **I muse on the work of Your hands.** The miracles and wonders You performed with my ancestors. **I spread out my hands to You.** Like one thirsty for water. **Answer me quickly.** For my spirit fails from the multitude of my troubles. **Do not hide Your face.** For if You hide Your face, I shall die. **And my death would be like those who go down into the pit.** For in life I would die without Your help. **Cause me to hear Your lovingkindness in the morning.** That is, quickly, as I have called out at dawn. **Cause me to know the way in which I should walk.** The straight path in which I should go. **For I lift up my soul to You.** To the measure of Your prayer. **Your spirit is good. Lead me.** Meaning, in the straight path, for I do not know what to do. **For Your name's sake, O Lord, revive me.** For the sake of the glory of Your name, that You may revive me from the hand of the enemy so that all creatures may know Your might and Your piety. **And in Your mercy.** So that whoever recognizes Your mercy will believe in You.

# Of David
**Blessed be the Lord.** David composed this psalm after he first became king; after the victory of the war with the Philistines and during the war of the Philistines and the wars of their kings. **Blessed be the Lord my Rock.** Its meaning is "my strength," for He is the one who gives me power and **teaches my hands for battle.** He repeats the matter with different words: **The battle, the war.** And the meaning is: "Strengthen my Rock, who teaches my hands for the battle of war." This is what the verse says in Psalms: *He teaches my hands for war, and my arms can bend a bow of bronze.* **My mercy and my fortress.** The text brings an explanation of the verse. And why does it say **my mercy**? Because the power of the shield is mercy, and it is an added explanation. Its meaning: in Your hand is the aspect of mercy, and this is the strength and refuge for kings whose face is toward the King; and many are like it. **Who subdues my people under me.** In the translation of Jonathan <note>The Targum of Jonathan ben Uzziel</note>: "And subdues nations under me." **My people** (*Ami*) is like **peoples** (*Amim*), and the letter *Yod* is a suffix for himself with a slight explanation, not as a possessive. **Lord, what is man, that You take knowledge of him?** The "Chariot" <note>Referring to the Merkavah or Divine Throne</note> which is from the void and from the place of its life below. **Lord, what is man, that You take knowledge of him?** "Knowledge" is a language of honor, signifying the importance of his status above all beings in the lower worlds. **Or the son of man, that You are mindful of him?** For the meaning of "knowledge" in this place and in this writing refers to reasoning and agreement, and this is for the distinguished, whether through intellect or prophecy, similar to *And the Egyptians shall know.* He said this "knowledge" because what importance does man have that You should praise him? Behold, he is like a breath—like the breath of the mouth that exits the mouth. For anything that has no substance according to its appearance is called "breath" (*hevel*), like the breath exiting the mouth. As per our explanation elsewhere in the verse. And so is its explanation in the Midrash: "Like every worker who is like a bird passing in a shadow and is worthless in its passing." **His days are like a passing shadow.** And so he said; and there are those who explain **his days are like the shadow of a bird** that descends and flies. May He be blessed to finish the wicked quickly. This is a prayer for an individual against the kings of the enemies who seek to fight with him. **On the mountains.** All the kings who are strong as mountains shall seek the thunders of their darkness; when He is revealed to them, they shall seek the denial of their people from them, like the ascent of smoke from the wilderness of the Glory among them. And many want "smoke among them," and the hint of "them" is similar. The firstborn of the wicked, may He be blessed, his flow of the Lord in His glory shall shake and thunder.

**Blessed be the Creator.** In every action, one should use haste and vigor to strengthen the matter. Similarly, regarding the matter of "crying," it is as written: "all my friends are like a harp." <note>The commentator is drawing linguistic parallels between various biblical roots</note>... and the Romans... and likewise "thickly laden."
And the "lightnings" and "arrows" mentioned here are the bitter punishments from the Place <note>term: "The Place" (HaMakom) is a common rabbinic title for God, emphasizing His omnipresence</note>. **Rescue me.** From many waters, which are the powerful nations. And "deliver me from the hand of foreigners," for their depth comes from the King of Assyria or from the men of the West. "Foreigners," and my mouth is like the one that hums, as the bird hums from its waters. For from the sea comes his certain death. **Whose mouth speaks vanity.** Those of the Roman exile who reveal themselves through their blessings, but their hearts are full of deceit and war; words that they harbor within. And so "their right hand," meaning violence and theft are in them, though he said "peace, peace" whenever you approach your work. **Who gives salvation.** To the nations, for the kings need their salvation. **Who delivers.** Rescuing in His eyes like the word "deliver me." **From the evil sword.** From the sword of the enemy. Some explain "evil sword" as a reference to the sword of the Angel of Death, which separates the soul from the body. **Rescue me.** Save us, for the hardship is like death.
**That our sons.** For all our sons are on the right path and grow larger than the sons of the strangers. For our sons grew in the Torah and its fruits are like the cedars and their branches are in the heights. And their abundance is written in the Torah in the blessings: "Blessed be the fruit of your womb" and "the fruit of your land." And he compared the sons to "plants," like the plants that grow by many waters and in the fatness of the oil; so our sons grow in the wisdom of the Torah and in the wisdom of the world, making them a place of good names. **And our daughters.** They are modest in their corners, and "carved" refers to the beauty of their features. Like the "corners of the Palace," which are the corners of the Temple, constructed with great art... so the daughters are beautiful and modest, built like the structure of a Palace. **Our garners are full.** Meaning that in every corner of the house, there is a kind of abundance. And from the greatness of the harvest of the land and the wine, they are blessed. **Providing.** They produce, as in the phrase "he shall obtain favor from the Lord." They are fast and diligent... and this describes the wealth of the house. **Our sheep.** They increase for the sake of the lambs. **Bringing forth thousands and ten thousands.** Giving birth to thousands and myriads, for they are fat and productive. **Our oxen.** Our leaders. And so "a chief of a thousand," "the chief of the house." **Laden.** Some say it comes from "burdens," implying they are strong to carry their heavy labor in the fields and in the flight of the clouds. And so it shall be. **No breach and no going out.** No breach of the fence and no going out from the fold to the wilderness. For the fence was breached, as in "Why have You broken down her fences?" **No cry.** No voice of weeping going out because of the enemies and their wisdom. **No cry.** It is not said "a cry in our neighborhoods" as we dwell in our streets. And they say "Happy is the people." And not for the kings, for every kind of man recognizes that if he were to rule, he would have this wisdom to tell of it. This is why it says "Happy is the people" twice. And because of what he had from the Name, he said this praise. According to some, his words are turned so that there is no city in this psalm that represents the fifty years. And what he said to the generation "Blessed be the Lord my Rock," who teaches my hands for war, the King of the fifty. And so "He who gives," for the generation of the passing. For the King who brings the generation will be his name, as it says "the generation of the passing is coming." If they are not the prophets of the end, everything is over and all is void.

**A Praise**
**Of David: I will extol You, my God.** This begins the group of five psalms until the end of the book that are all praises to the Holy One, blessed be He. Therefore, it is placed here at the beginning of the end of the book as a "Praise of David" initially. And this psalm, its first verse begins with "Praise" and its last verse ends with "Praise," saying: "And my mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord" at the beginning and the end. And everything is an offering of praise. And he says "Praise" and "Praise" for the Holy One, blessed be He, is blessed as the source of all creations... therefore he mentions here the multitude of languages and tongues that praise Him. And this psalm is the main praise of the Holy One, blessed be He. Therefore, it is ordered alphabetically <note>Psalm 145 is an alphabetical acrostic</note>. But the letter *Nun* is not mentioned in it. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, interpreted why it was not written: because it contains the fall of the enemies of Israel, as it is written "Fallen (*Nafelah*), she shall no more rise, the virgin of Israel." And the focus of this psalm is to speak of the praises of the Creator and the glory of His creation. Therefore, the Sages said: "Whoever says the 'Praise of David' three times every day is assured of being a son of the World to Come." And they did not say it should be said with the mouth alone, but with the mouth and the heart and the concentration. And he said "I will extol You, my God, the King" — I will extol You in my poverty and in my gathering, for You are the King in truth. And all the kings and rulers of the past and future are under Your kingdom. And how do they rule over them? "I will extol You, my God." For He is the God over all flesh and their divine portion. **Forever and ever.** From You, who lives forever and ever. Or its meaning: let me bless You forever and ever, which is all the days of my life. Or its meaning: I will extol You in this world and I will bless Your name in the world that is coming and beyond. And after the praise "I will extol You" and "I will bless Your name," he continues to inform that His name is He and He is His name. And this name is hidden and not called, for "His greatness is unsearchable." And the person cannot encompass it with much praise, for it is near to him, and they "shall praise Your name forever and ever." Every day he says "and I will bless" from the depth of my blessings. And the content of this verse "Blessed be the Lord day by day," and also this verse is near to "Great is the Lord." And if I say I will make Him great and praise Him, He is great and highly praised above all praises, until "His greatness is unsearchable." And a person cannot encompass it with much words, for there is no end. Rather, each person praises according to his ability. **Generation to generation.** Therefore, it is not possible for my life alone to suffice to praise Him; I cannot reach the heavens in all my days... but day to day utters speech according to the measure of their existence in the generation that goes and the generation that comes. And this generation tells of Your works... and Your mighty acts... because the praises of the generation are based on what they saw in their days and the mighty acts they saw in their times. **Splendor.** Like "He is clothed in splendor"... the splendor of the glory of Your majesty. Its meaning is the beauty of the glory of Your majesty. In it is the power and the wondrous acts of the glory, as it says "and His glory is in the heavens." **And the words of Your wondrous works.** Your deeds, hear them and taste them. And they are also for every time that they occur... and they shall tell it to the many. **And the might.** As they said in the section... so they shall say of the might of Your kingdom. And it is written "Your greatnesses" with a *Yod*... I will tell. For the goodness that is in the praise is for Him alone. And these qualities mentioned in this psalm — greatness, might, deeds, majesty, glory, kingdom — are indeed organized... but on the day of the unification, do not look at them as separate things... but because they are the names of the qualities, they are distinct from one another. **The memory of Your great goodness.** Great is His memory and praise, as if to say "and upon Your goodness." **They shall utter.** Speech, as in "the utterance of my lips." **And shall sing of Your righteousness.** And they shall say it with a loud voice, not like the children of men. **Gracious and merciful.** These words are mercy and righteousness... they shall utter and they shall sing, for He is gracious to the needy and gives them a blessing. And merciful to the poor and has compassion on them and saves them from the damages of the world. **Slow to anger.** Delaying His anger for the wicked and not bringing it upon them immediately. **And great in kindness.** Bringing abundance to those who need it. Since His kindness is great, he says it for all people... more than what they deserve to receive. **The Lord is good to all.** Even to the animals and the beasts and the birds and the reptiles He is good and merciful. And so it is appropriate for a man to follow His ways, to be merciful to the living creatures... and so it is proven from our Holy Rabbi [Judah the Prince], who was punished because he did not show mercy to a calf. And so we find that His mercies are upon all His works.

**To make known.** And it is written that the place of His power and His teachings is for the sons of man, so it is many-fold to make known to the sons of man. For they prayed and did not recognize His mighty acts and the glory of His kingdom.

**Your kingdom.** And life is in the kingdom of the Lord, and for the elevated, there is no interruption; he is alive in life and alive in his death. For every human kingdom there is an end, but His kingdom is a kingdom for all worlds, for all times. And even in His works, the world of death is included.

**The eyes of all look to You.** And so it said, all of them look to You. For every creature, the included life is abundant and sustained by His thought. Just as a person works and has food for himself, so do all their eyes hang and wait for You.

For every species and kind has a known time in which it relies on its food. And he used the language "look" <note>original: "yeshaberu"</note>. The wheels are full of kindness for the time of the day, for they look according to their nature, both the land animals and those. And His love makes it known that this is part of the rectification, for it is the sustenance and the preparation.

**You open.** He sent his blessing and gave bread to each according to their will in His mercy and His merit.

**Desire.** God provides according to one's preparation. For in glory and honor He gave to everything that eats. And even though He only helps the living, yet all those who are destined to pass are included. And so, the sending and existence and the arrangement of the table include even the lacking animals. And so among the bent-over ones, the souls that go after others and every living path. For with mercy and the response to the frantic, He gave them the strength of acceptance in life. And all who break through are like death, but the world of thoughts is sweetened in the depth where the joy of the song is found; sometimes He will sing the qualities of humility in the cleaning of myself. And it says that for everyone who remembers, he will die to himself or by the hand of that which breaks him, for they are in the power of their selves. For we truly say that when the cat preys on the mouse, or the hawk on the bird, and the like, it is a punishment and prey from the hand of the Blessed Name. And He strengthened the heart of the kings, according to the words of our Rabbis, or Rabbi Yohanan: when he saw a sea-donkey <note>Likely a reference to a shark or large sea creature</note>, he said "How manifold are Your works, O Lord." And you are similar to it and it is a full reward, and it enters into all types of holy living beings. And we see that there is luck and a star to say which types of living beings are under certain laws. For from His speech, may He be blessed, every living thing was formed. And it is said "His mercy is upon all His works." And it said, His soul is for the donkey. And there is no reward for a domestic animal like the donkey and the dog, for he said to them, may their memory be for a blessing: "How manifold are Your works, O Lord," they teach us in His truth for their creation. And the explanation according to its "taste" <note>Rabbinic term for underlying reason</note> is that there is a root there. And he said regarding all our prayers that He gives them to the Blessed Name, and in Him is their sustenance. This teaches us that He accepts the prayer of every creature in its creation. And there is a time for his perfection to be written.

**For He is good to all.** And His mercy is upon all His works.

**Our glory.** In them is the breath of life, not merely to give to them and let them live, but their joy is in everything.

**The Lord is near to all who call Him.** Precision is required: to those who "call." And it is already precise: "to those who call Him in truth" — meaning their mouth and heart are equal.

**He will fulfill the desire of those who fear Him.** For those who fear Him will call Him in truth, and He will do His will according to what they pray from Him, and He will hear their cry and save them from the trouble that comes into the world, or a sign of an omen for the humble group.

"And let all flesh bless His holy name" — meaning all human beings who are created, and not the other animals that pass away. And so, because there are living beings there, he spoke there.

**"The Lord opens the eyes of the blind."** This means He heals those who suffer from eye ailments. After this, it mentions those who are "sick of heart," showing that His kindness never fails, unlike a human who might strike his neighbor out of jealousy. **"The Lord opens the eyes of the blind"** also means the Creator desires to support and raise up the lowly and bring back many of the poor among them. As it is written below, He gathers the "outcasts" <note>the poor/exiles</note> in the Diaspora. This will happen during the rebuilding of Jerusalem, and the building and the return are linked to the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

**9. "The Lord protects."** The Lord protects the strangers according to their needs... and what was said in the previous Psalm is to strengthen the Prophet who speaks to the nation to comfort them, so they may see the consolation of Jerusalem quickly. The following verse says there shall be peace for you and the joy shall not be hidden from you. For the children of Jerusalem, there will be peace and joy in heaven and on earth. The term "Hallelujah" <note>Praise Yah</note> refers to the reward and success the Prophet found in his prophecy.

## Hallelujah

**"For it is good to sing to our God, for it is pleasant, and praise is fitting."** This entire section until the "end of the world" establishes His kingdom for us. These rulers of the kingdom shall be good and pleasant. Your praise shall be "fitting," meaning: fitting and strong as a serpent <note>possibly a metaphorical reference to enduring strength</note>, like "The Lord's Jerusalem." When the Lord builds Jerusalem, He will gather the outcasts of Israel. This refers to seeking out the building for the "bringer of news" to the heart.

**"He counts."** Behold, the sages of astronomy <note>original: "hachmei hatkhuna"</note> all agree that the number of the stars is one thousand and twenty-two <note>This is a reference to the 1,022 stars cataloged in Ptolemy's Almagest, a standard figure in medieval science</note>, besides those that are of the nature of a mass of stars. But God's counting is by the way of the Torah, which is beyond our great ones. Though you may be wise regarding the heavens, the sages did not know the smallest stars... which look down upon the earth and dwell there by His kindness. Even the stars that are seen, they are like a menorah <note>lampstand</note>. The number of stars is great and distant, each one more expanded and far than the next. But the Holy One, Blessed be He, knows the count of the stars because He created them. **"To all of them He calls names."** This is explained as calling them by names of honor, for He created them all as a host. Each one has a name fitting for the purpose for which it was created. For every star has power and dominion over something below; as the Sages said: "There is no blade of grass below that does not have a constellation above that strikes it and tells it: 'Grow!'"

**"Great is our Lord."** For a king of flesh and blood who has to lead many provinces becomes weary leading them all at once. Even if they were arranged perfectly, he would become weary. But for our God, who created this lowly world, He knows and foresees what will be in every generation, for His understanding is "without number." He counts the stars and the quantity of all things. Therefore, one must explain it thus: His understanding is not like human calculation. **"He encourages."** Though He is great and abundant in power, He still looks upon the clouds and the lowly and the poor, supporting them and humbling the wicked who are jealous.

**"Sing."** He speaks to Israel: sing according to My name... it shall be a song of thanksgiving. Our God is ready to receive your praise with great honor. **"Great is our Lord and abundant in power."** The story of His might is always found in the Scripture. Because as we have seen, His mysteries are without search and His successes without number. He then says: **"Sing to the Lord,"** and again uses this language. Who can understand His might? He shows Israel His great outstretched hand. **"Who covers the heavens with clouds."** He mentions that the clouds precede the rain, which is a wonder in our eyes but simple for Him. As Moses said, He is the source of all and brings forth His word. He provides for the grass which does not hope for man <note>i.e., it grows by divine decree, not human effort</note>. Therefore it says: **"Who covers the heavens with clouds."**

**"He gives to the beast its food."** For the beast does not have the intelligence to prepare its own food, yet He brings it its sustenance. **"To the young ravens."** It is the nature of ravens that when their young are born, they abandon them because they are white <note>a common medieval belief that ravens don't recognize their white hatchlings until their black feathers grow</note>, and they do not bring them bread. The Holy One prepares gnats for them and sustains them until they grow, for they have no power of their own. So too He does for Israel who are abandoned in exile. If one has merit in God, his salvation is not through the strength of the horse or human power. Therefore: **"Not in the strength of the horse does He delight."** This does not mean there is no use for horses, but that God does not desire the one who *trusts* in the strength of the horse. As the Prophet says: "The rider of the horse shall not save his life." Rather, He desires those who fear Him and hope for His kindness, not those who trust in their own strength.

**"Praise."** For He desires according to your trust in Him. He speaks to Jerusalem: "I will strengthen the bars of your gates." This means your peace will be so great it is as if the bars are impenetrable. **"He has blessed your children within you."** There will be peace within the walls and joy in Jerusalem. **"He makes your borders peace."** This refers to the "fat of the wheat" <note>the highest quality</note>. He will satisfy you with the best. His word runs quickly like a running servant who does his master's will.

### 148
Hallelujah! Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise Him in the heights. Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His hosts. Praise Him, sun and moon; praise Him, all you stars of light. Who gives snow white like wool; He scatters frost like ashes. He throws His ice like crumbs; before His cold, who can stand?
