->Thus far Your mercies have helped us. Mountains and all hills, trees that produce fruit and all cedars. Beasts and all cattle, creeping things and the bird that flies with its wing.<-

**Who gives snow like wool.** The snow is as white as white wool. In secret, it shall be a memory before His Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> because it is written: "You shall wash me and I shall be whiter than snow." And the author compares the frost to the wool, though it is less white than snow, and from the mouth of the horse <note>likely an OCR error for "the heavens"</note> it is sown in white on the earth. **He scatters frost like ashes.** He compares the frost to ashes because it is less white, falling like fine powder on the walls. He mentions the cold alongside the ice because it is stronger and more harmful. He explains "like crumbs" <note>original: "ke-fitim"</note> to mean small pieces of ice. **Before His cold who can stand?** This implies that the ice is from Him and can be harmful, and who can endure the strike of it according to their strength? In His mercy, He guards every living thing and provides a shelter from the heavy rains. And the frost is a fear <unclear>frost like ashes He scatters</unclear> and the ice is plain like a strong white substance, more harmful than the others. Therefore, he mentions his cold with the ice. He mentions these ways as a kindness for the inhabitants of the world. Some explain "Who gives snow" to mean that He gives it in whiteness. And he says the ice is like "crumbs" to describe the many small pieces of ice, asking "who can stand" before such cold? For the cold is strong, as if it seals the hand of man from performing work.

**He sends His word.** This verse teaches that He sends a word from the source of life to melt the snow, frost, and ice. He says "He makes His wind blow and the waters flow," for He melts them with the blowing of the warm south wind.

**He tells.** He makes His words, laws, and judgments known to us for our honor and for the Torah, for the word is strong. As it is written regarding the "great foot" <note>likely a reference to the Revelation at Sinai</note>. **He has not done so.** As it is written: "Has a people ever heard the voice of God..." **And judgments they have not known.** The judgments He wrote for Israel were not known to the other nations.

# Hallelujah
**Praise the Lord from the heavens.** Praise the Lord in the high places. This refers to the "Separate World" <note>a medieval philosophical term for the realm of angels/intellects</note> which is elevated above all. He says **in all the heights**, meaning everything prepared in the heavens. **Praise Him all His angels.** These angels are the celestial spheres, though some are physical and some are not. **Praise Him all His hosts.** These are the luminous bodies and the stars within the spheres. **Praise Him.** He mentions first the praises of the stars of light, for they provide more light than the spheres because they are closer to us.

**Praise Him, you heavens of heavens.** Some sages say there is a world of souls above us. And some explain "the waters above the heavens" as the clouds. And some say the "heavens of heavens" are the spheres one inside the other. The philosophers <note>original: "philosophos"</note> agree with this, saying that between us and the sphere of the moon there is nature. He says that these waters will eventually return to be water and fall to the earth by their nature.

**Let them praise the name of the Lord.** Not just the upper beings, but all the world, for He commanded and they were created. **And He established them forever.** He placed a law upon them that they should exist forever and their strength should not be diminished.

**Praise the Lord from the earth.** He calls to all the inhabitants of the earth to praise the Lord. He mentions **sea monsters and all depths**, referring to the creatures in the lowest points. He mentions **fire and hail**, for their creation is from the earth. The scientists <note>original: "hachmei ha-tolodot"</note> prove this with clear evidence. Rabbi Eliezer says everything in the earth was created from the earth. Rabbi Yose says everything in the water and the earth was created from the earth. **Fire.** This is the burning fire that consumes. **Hail.** Known. **Stormy wind fulfilling His word.** It moves by His command and not by chance. **The mountains.** He mentions the mountains because they are the cause of the rising of the mist and the hail. Then he mentions the fruit trees and the cedars. **Beasts.** He mentions the wild animals and all cattle, and the small creeping things, and the winged birds.

**Kings of the earth.** After mentioning the living things, the text mentions the living speech that oversees the sounds of the lower world. Likewise, when the remembrance is from afar, such as in the glory of war, his voice encompasses all sides. These last verses are before the ultimate goodness. He mentions these verses within the general scope of glory, status, and life. He says that they shall all praise His name, for His name alone is exalted before all. And He mentions "all nations," for all who possess grace and the foolish of Israel shall live unto Him. **Young men and also, etc.** And He mentions "also children," because they are destined to involve themselves in their establishment and in the house of peace itself. He says this once for all of these: **Old men with youths.** The elders shall teach the way to praise the Lord. He mentions "young men" to create a desire for their strength. Therefore, he speaks first of the strong ones and afterwards of the strangers and the languages. **They shall praise the name of the Lord.** All these mentioned who are in the lower world shall praise the name of the Lord. That is to say, instead of their own names, they themselves shall praise and be praised with many blessings, and they shall renew to Him that His name alone is exalted. According to what we investigated above, the kings are in a place of strength for whoever's mouth it was, for He is exalted over the high ones and the mouth of the wise is among them. But the life he granted them is like the grace of the "bed," for the life revealed to them shall establish their people. Therefore, the kings of earth and heaven shall not be forgotten, hinting that the kings of the earth and all nations shall live by their spirit. For He expanded below for those near the grace of hearts, and in some places His offering is called "for His people." He uses the expression "He lifted a horn" because it is an ornament for them and their strength. For "life" is like the meaning of "on that day" when Israel was small and poor, all the comforters descended upon them, but now the kings and all nations shall praise God. There shall be for them the grace of hearts of all His pious ones. And "pious" refers to the children of Israel, a people near and a gathering of the whole. Hallelujah!

### Hallelujah
**Sing to the Lord a new song, His praise in the assembly of the pious.** This is directed toward Israel, who is for the God of the kindness of the Lord. That is, it calls for the strengthening of the Lord's kindness through measures and the written comforts. These conclude the Psalms immediately following the wonders, little by little. **His praise in the assembly of the pious.** The language "assembly of the pious" means the praise was in the community of the devoted. **Israel shall rejoice in his Maker.** Written in the third person. And so "life" stands ready, for "when you lie down, they shall watch you." **And the children of Zion shall exult in their King.** This means behold, the chains of death <note>referring to historical exile or suffering</note> have been removed. His strength is for the whole, more than any tree, for he wrote "give milk, not cut." <unclear>Ancient abbreviations</unclear> from every nation, for in salvation you have seen them. **The pious shall exult.** The pious are strengthened and... from standing to greatness. **They shall sing upon their beds.** They shall sing to God the Lord on their future established places. **Their beds.** Like their dwellings and their unique lives. <unclear>sentence fragment</unclear> therefore they shall praise. Their strength is explained "upon their beds" as those who rise up in their solitude at night. **High praises of God.** When they go to war against a stubborn people, they shall pray to God the Blessed, and His exaltations are in their mouths and a weapon in their spirit. He will give them strength over the levelling of their enemies. Prayer is like a sword in their hand. Thus "two-edged sword" is like two mouths of a sword moving with the force of the army. And afterwards with your strength, for first the voice shall come to be magnified and a song and a high speech. He says this of the rider, for those who are amazed shall place a horn in his throat. **To perform vengeance.** To wipe them out entirely to be wise, and if they turn their backs on them. **Rebukes.** Rebukes with their kings... and if they do not see to stop fighting them. Therefore they shall perform vengeance on them and the sword etc. and all the reasons for fighting nations and peoples. **To bind.** Their kings shall be bound and the honorable ones shall be alive and their hamstrings in fetters and... iron to punish them. **To perform upon them the judgment written, it is a glory.** The judgment against the nations. This is written in his youth for his pious ones, the weapon of my sword... and the dance of the pious to receive the glory, and behold to make them move in their merit. **It is a glory.** Its vision is death, but it was a glory for all His pious ones. And all the sounds of the voices: Hallelujah!

### Hallelujah
**Praise God in His sanctuary; praise Him in the firmament of His power.** This psalm concludes and seals the prayer of all grace in the world... Hallelujah hints at the ten attributes of praise <note>the ten types of song in the Psalms</note> through which his praise is established. He says praise is "praise God in the holy." And "holy" is His temple. And he further says, "praise Him in the firmament of His power." This refers to the highest celestial sphere, and it includes the whole world because He is the support of all. Therefore he says "strength" and "power" as the power of God. **Praise Him.** He says this to Israel to praise in their glory, more than any other people. **Praise Him according to His exceeding greatness.** He shall be magnified and sanctified among the nations for His greatness. **Praise Him with the blast of the shofar.** This includes the times of the Jubilee. **Praise Him with strings and flutes.** These are musical instruments... like many strings or a flute. He says "with strings" meaning many instruments. **Praise Him with clanging cymbals.** With cymbals that make a great sound. So he says of the multitudes of days and their beginning to make heard. **With cheering cymbals.** Those that make the sound of the *teruah* <note>the broken, sobbing blast of the shofar</note>. **Every soul shall praise the Lord, Hallelujah.** And over all the flutes, the voice of the soul shall praise. It shall be blessed in its place, praising the Blessed One and His holiness, according to the power of its wisdom while it is still in the body. And he says this regarding the wise: Hallelujah!

->### Commentary on the Book of Proverbs called 'Kav VeNaki'<-
<note>The title 'Kav VeNaki' literally means "A small measure and clean." It is a Talmudic idiom used to describe a work that is concise but of high quality and accuracy.</note>

**The Author says:** My eyes have seen the words of this book and its excellence. In its understanding and beauty, from its head to its feet, the strength of the crown of all types of ethical instruction is revealed to all flesh. It spreads every desirable thing to every man who lacks it and loves it. It is a tower of strength for his kingdom, founded in wisdom and understanding, a perfect wall around the Torah and wisdom. In the choicest of high wisdoms and thoughts, no prayer's atonement can equal it, and every precious thing is found within it. It reveals hidden silver and its treasures. Let the reader who lacks the examination of the intellect be opened, for it is a key to openings in every sealed secret. Because of this, the vision of the intellect preceded me to contemplate it and gain insight. 

Arguments and proofs have been established for me, which day by day remove the confusion from one's eyes and soul, to learn and to teach from year to year the pleasant words, and to stand and teach in public. It is established now at the beginning of the summer, during the days of the counting of the Omer <note>The 49-day period between Passover and Shavuot, traditionally a time for studying ethical tracts like Ethics of the Fathers</note>, for then everyone is awakened to rouse the physical matter, and the intellectual soul longs to sit under its rod and live, and to engrave its days. Reading this book in the heat of the day is no less than passing through them and becoming like the stars when our Torah was given. 

Therefore, my heart stirred me to bring it up in my hands, along with the printers who turned their shoulders to the task. Included here is the commentary of the Ralbag <note>Rabbi Levi ben Gershom, a famous 14th-century philosopher and astronomer</note> of blessed memory, whose words are pleasant like wine, preceding all in status and grace. Also included is the master of interpretation and the face of the Torah, the sage Rabbi Abraham ibn Ezra; and the masters of grammar and commentators of the Scripture, the sage Rabbi Joseph ibn Yahya, son of Enoch, may they be blessed; and the sage who is the master of utility, in whose words all wisdoms are included, and the sage, the great prince who was supreme in the land, Rabbi Immanuel <note>Immanuel of Rome, a 13th-century poet and commentator</note>, the champion of knowledge in his compositions; and the one who enlightens the eyes of the community through this book in understanding and salt, the sage Rabbi Menachem HaMeiri <note>A famous 13th-century Provencal scholar known for his clear, encyclopedic commentaries</note>, his words are like a great tapestry. 

The master of the age in wisdom and mouth to speak in our generation, whose fame is before us like water in a fountain, the sage Rabbi Joseph Hayyun. There is no doubt that from their clean words, the proper intention and hidden strengths are decided. Sometimes, according to his level, the wise man follows their arrangement, sometimes because the length of their words was not blessed with brevity, and sometimes because the words of the book might seem contradictory to one of little knowledge. Therefore, I saw fit to place the hand of their supreme words—sapphire and diamond—and also the sage Rabbi Joseph Hayyun, a prince of our sages who enlightened the book. I have gathered from the hidden treasures and from the silver of the commentaries those which bring sapphire and gold. A comprehensive and clarified commentary of their words is offered to this excellent book, which in its printed form will not be equaled. For this reason, I have called its name *Kav VeNaki*, for as a *kav* <note>a small unit of measurement</note> of my mouth, I have gathered from the best of their commentaries of blessed memory. May my help come from the Lord.

Behold a book which is a book of my instructions
And let it flow like a reward according to the intention of my deeds
Behold the intellect, behold the desire and the joy
And from his mouth they will flow with confidence and joy
To all living things who desire to seek
His perfection stands as a teacher and his bride.

<column-break/>

In me is healing for the heart, doubled and redoubled
To every person of intellect, behold his kindnesses and his passing
And let the hidden things drop from the openings of the insides
And the words of understanding shall fly most swiftly
Only the best of the chosen details shall be selected
Like a fine veil, it is a *Kav VeNaki*.

<column-break/>

Whose mouth is like my cup of sweetness?
And its companions to the one who clings and knocks
The obscurities of the hearts, the secret of the verses
Upon the established throne of praise and desire
We have gathered that which is lacking, few but pure.

## The Proverbs of Solomon

**Proverbs of Solomon:** Below, Solomon composed three books: Song of Songs in our youth, Proverbs in our maturity, and Ecclesiastes in our old age. He used a different style of language in each of these sections. In Song of Songs, he did not mention his name except briefly for the children of his word. In Proverbs, he joined "King of Israel," for his instruction in his maturity was over all the kingdoms. In Ecclesiastes, he said "King in Jerusalem," for in his old age, his rule was not over all the kingdoms as it was in the beginning. This book exists because most of its words are like a sea, encompassing everything, like the good portion above the Torah and the preparation for it.

**To know wisdom and instruction:** "Wisdom" is a hint at the entire subject matter, and "instruction" refers to the practical application of the matter. From the mass of hidden treasures, he informs the creatures of the eye and the virtue. 

**To perceive the words of understanding:** This means to understand the "water" <note>a metaphor for Torah/wisdom</note> in the Torah that is hidden and beloved, to select the inner meaning from the grace, so that the new student does not stray in understanding this. 

**To receive the instruction:** "Instruction" is here connected to "wisdom" (*Haskel*). It hints that this book is integrated to learn from it the instruction of the intellect. 

**Justice, and judgment, and equity:** This refers to the action of good traits. To "receive" indicates haste in the action. "Grace" points to learning and taking from the physical matter that benefits its master. 

**To know wisdom and instruction:** This indicates learning by oneself: the first from the mouths of scribes, and the second from the mouths of books. So too, it points to the acquisition of good traits for oneself. 

**Judgment:** This indicates the step of truth toward another. 

**Equity:** This refers to the highest level of knowledge and grace for the traits, indicating a decision in laws. 

**To give craftiness to the simple:** A "simpleton" (*Peti*) is one who is easily seduced because of his lightness, without a sign. "Craftiness" is the sense for the logic of thought and the purity of analysis in matters that are confusing. When the wise prepare it for the simple, after starting with this study, they will become wise. So too, this book gives the "shrewd" knowledge to learn from the chapters. 

**Discretion:** This is the matter of the strength of perception from understanding.

<column-break/>

**A wise man will hear:** A wise man is a master of instruction who has learned from the mouth of his teacher and reviews what he has learned. 

**And will increase:** A wise man adds to his knowledge by understanding one thing from another, increasing upon what he has heard. These words of the book are not only for the simple and the youth; they also prepare the wise. Even though they may be advanced in wisdom and understanding, they will increase upon the acquisition they already have. He returns and "increases learning" (*Lekach*); "learning" refers to the acquisition of wisdom. 

**And a man of understanding... wise counsels:** This refers to the power of "maneuvers" or strategies to grasp the paths of thought within this book. 

**To understand a proverb:** Through the study of this book, one will prepare the inner meaning. 

**And a figure:** This is the material that indicates the goodness of expression. 

**The words of the wise:** Meaning the structures within the foundation of wisdom. 

**And their riddles:** One will understand the riddles. A "proverb" (*Mashal*) is in the category of "water within a proverb." A "figure" (*Melitzah*) is the path of connection to understand riddles. As our rabbis said regarding what is said of "two camps" (*Machanayim*). The matter is divided into three: where the sage goes and improves from the strength of high things, where the sitting below is, and that is learning the counsel in writing. The "riddles" refer to things that are closed and hidden, which one cannot bring out easily without the application of the proverb. For this, the sweetness is given.

**The fear of the Lord.** In the discipline of one's character, this is the foundation and the root of knowledge and all wisdom and instruction. If the Creator grants them grace and favor in the eyes of the creatures, through wisdom one will become wiser than all the wise men of the world and will inherit the trait of humility <note>The OCR text "חמס" (violence) is likely a typo for "ענוה" (humility) or "חכמה" (wisdom) given the context of "the choice part of knowledge"</note>, which is the choice part of knowledge. **Hear, my son, discipline.** This is a living instruction for the children, telling them to distance themselves from bad behavior, to listen and be reproved by the secrets of discipline and its laws. It is the wisdom that adds discipline, learning, and education for the child. **For they are a wreath of grace.** The strengthening power received by those who perform acts of kindness from this. The simple meaning of "wreath" <note>Hebrew: *livyah*</note> is a connection or an addition, like a cloak of thread and discipline upon the skull of the recipient, and a necklace for the throat. Grace is kindness, favor, and beauty. It is intended for us to find favor in the eyes of all who see us. Through it, the acceptance of the elders and the wise of the generation is suspended; they are the "treasure of the necklace" for grace, kindness, and beauty.

**My masters** and rabbis linked wisdom to the "dead" <note>possibly referring to the study of Torah after death or the "deadly" nature of sin</note>, beginning with the matter of hardship and the destruction found among those who are enticed to evil habits. **Secondly,** which is to say, the lesser ones. This book of wisdom and discipline, despite its severity regarding the various "deaths" mentioned in the scripture—why was it made so difficult? Because he who covers his sins shall not prosper, and the sin of the many is for the house... According to custom, the repair of wisdom depends on the strength of the custom established in the kingdom.

**In the Midrash:** Why did Proverbs begin with the letter *Bet* <note>The Hebrew letter ב</note> just as the Midrash on Genesis <note>Bereshit</note> does? They permitted the intermediate days of the festival in relation to the wisdom of the portion... The "place outside" <note>where wisdom cries</note> refers to the Attribute of Justice <note>Middat HaDin</note>, while "in the broad places" refers to the Attribute of Mercy <note>Middat HaRachamim</note>. "At the head of the noisy streets" refers to the attribute of mercy and rest, and the desire for honor... The heart, the dog, the pig, and the gluttony are all hints to the foundation of the place of judgment that covers sin... when you change the wickedness that destroys kindness and discipline, following the knowledge of the instructors of the Lord.

**Jesus** <note>This likely refers to a grammatical or Midrashic point rather than the historical figure, or perhaps a typo for "Yeshua" (salvation)</note> and the essence of everything, since it finishes and purifies all wisdom and the simple meaning regarding the evil will of the greedy. **Thirdly**, in the Midrash, like the law of one who dismisses his illness... mentioning the announcement of the judgment in the broad square... everything written returns with severity, in measure and in weight... and the boldness to twist the announcements of the judgment... the merit of the judgment. **Fourthly**, like knowledge and thought. Until when will the youth be called? Until twenty, as it is written... **Fifthly**, in the Midrash, my kings and my wise men shall rejoice over the simple ones who expire in my rebuke, to warn the honorable ones... the language of the Sages... my rebuke... and the Torah of wisdom. They are lenient with the simple and the foolish... the trait of humility. The masters of ethics taught that wisdom without discipline is like sand in a vessel that will erode and be hated.

**Keep, my son.** Meaning, according to the simplicity and importance and the discipline of my wise men for the sake of merit... the teaching of your mother... to choose between paths. It is said in the Midrash that one is obligated... the advice of the "wreath" upon the many steps. Therefore, it said "the wisdoms of the Torah" for the palate in the language of speech... the importance of the words of the wise... merit to hear the words... the life of the people. And for the one who understands, they shall not be withheld from our wisdom... grace will increase discipline for the understanding... a garment in the good way. Therefore, he repeated: "the discipline of your father and do not stray from your father." **For they are a wreath of grace.** Kindness is upon him. **And necklaces.** <term>Like a sanctuary</term> of a young goat. A "necklace" for your throat, which is the throat, and upon it they hang necklaces of silver rings, using the plural masculine and feminine forms to suggest that the discipline of the scribe should be a binding, not just a beauty on the head, but a kindness in the moral desires founded upon the... and all the beauty in the throat is of the male...

**My son, if they entice you.** He begins to give their answer, the wicked who use smooth speech to lure you; do not be willing <note>original: "al tovey"</note>. As the Midrash says: do not desire their path... do not walk... in a place of sin. **If they say.** Everywhere it says "if," it implies something that may or may not happen. **Let us lie in wait for blood.** To lust for the blood of the innocent. **Let us lurk.** To hide ourselves. **For the innocent without cause.** You, who are simple, let us go... and this is spoken in the language of those who lie in wait... and this will be for them a grace and a prayer... **Let us swallow them like the Grave.** We will swallow the possessions like the Grave swallows the living... the Grave receives the damage... **And whole.** They are not like... but they are in their simplicity in the heavens... **Cast your lot among us.** If you want to share, immediately it will be by lot... one purse shall be for all of us. **My son, do not go.** Warning that he should not go in the way of the wicked... keep your foot from their path... **For their feet run to evil.** He intends to do evil to himself and hastens to shed blood... **For in vain is the net scattered.** He brings a parable to those who run to their own trap... like the birds who see the seeds on the net... they do not pay attention to the net and descend to eat and are caught... **And they [lie in wait] for their blood.** They return to the owners of the net... their own lives. This returns to the birds of the parable... those who possess money and the foolishness of their blood... **So are the paths of everyone who is greedy for gain.** Anyone who is hurried to rob the money of others... it takes away the life of its possessors... **Wisdoms.** Inner wisdom in thinness and tranquility... as it says "the lips of wisdoms"... **Secondly,** the wisdom that protects the simple... **Wisdoms cry aloud in the street.** The language of singing... to bring... and to understand. One of the wisdoms will be established in the designated places... **At the head of the noisy streets.** The openings of the gates... the seat of the elders inside the city... **How long, O simple ones.** All those who desire wisdom, she says: how long will these things be? ... **And scoffers.** And the fools who are devoid of knowledge. **Turn to my rebuke.** Each of the wisdoms says to these...

# Proverbs

<margin>7</margin> "Turn to my reproof; behold, I will pour out my spirit to you, I will make known my words to you. Because I called and you refused, I stretched out my hand and no one listened. And you neglected all my counsel, and my reproof you did <margin>8 <br/> [variant] <br/> [variant]</margin> not desire. I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear comes. When your fear comes like a storm <margin>9</margin> and your calamity arrives like a whirlwind, when trouble and distress come upon you. Then they will call me, <margin>10</margin> but I will not answer; they will seek me early, but they will not find me. Because they hated knowledge and the fear of <margin>20 <br/> For <br/> 30 <br/> 40</margin> the Lord they did not choose. They did not desire my counsel; they despised all my reproof. And they shall eat of the fruit of their way, and from their own counsels they shall be satiated. For the turning away of the simple shall kill them, and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them. But whoever listens to me shall dwell safely, and shall be quiet from the fear of evil."

<margin>2 <br/> 1</margin> "My son, if you take my words and hide my commandments with you, to make your ear attentive to wisdom, incline your heart to understanding. For if you call for discernment, and to understanding <margin>2</margin> you lift up your voice. If you seek her as silver, and search for her as for hidden treasures. Then you will understand <margin>3 <br/> 4 <br/> 5</margin> the fear of the Lord and find the knowledge of God. For the Lord gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding. He stores up sound wisdom for the upright; He is a shield for those who walk in integrity. To guard the paths <margin>6 <br/> 7 <br/> stores <br/> [variant] <br/> 8</margin> of justice, and He keeps the way of His pious ones. Then you will understand righteousness and justice and equity—every good path. When wisdom enters your heart and knowledge is pleasant to your soul, discretion <margin>9 <br/> 10 <br/> 11 <br/> 12</margin> shall watch over you, understanding shall guard you, to deliver you from the way of the evil man, from the man who speaks perversities."

<column-break/>

<note>This column contains the Targum, an ancient Aramaic translation and paraphrase of the biblical text.</note>

"Turn to my reproof; behold, I will pour out my spirit to you and make known my words. Because I called and you did not believe, I raised my hands and there was none who listened. And you cast away all my counsel and my reproof you did not desire. I also will rejoice in your brokenness and I will laugh when trouble comes upon you. When your confusion comes in a rush, and your brokenness comes like a whirlwind, when trouble and distress come upon you. Then they will call me and I will not answer; they will arise early and they will not find me. Because they hated knowledge and the fear of the Lord they did not desire. They did not want my counsel and they rejected all my reproof. And they shall eat from the fruit of their ways and from their own counsel they shall be satiated. Because the perversity of the simple shall leave them, and the tranquility of the foolish shall destroy them. And he who listens to me shall dwell in hope, and be quiet from the fear of evil."

"My son, if you receive my words and my commandments you hide in your treasures. And your ear listens to wisdom and you turn your heart to understanding. And if you call to discernment and to understanding you give your voice. If you seek it like silver and like hidden treasures you search for it. Then you will understand the fear of the Lord, and the knowledge from before God you will find. Because the Lord gives wisdom, from His mouth knowledge and understanding. And He places hope for the upright and is a shield to those who walk in integrity. To guard the paths of judgment and the paths of the righteous He will guard. Then you will understand righteousness and judgment and uprightness and all good paths. For wisdom will enter your heart and knowledge to your soul will be sweet. Thought will guard over you and understanding will watch you. That you may be saved from the evil path and from the man who speaks subversions."

***

**Behold, I will pour out my spirit to you.** <note>original: "Hineh abia lakhem rukhi"</note> This means: it is not just a small measure of wisdom that I give you, but rather I express and pour out upon you the abundance of my wisdom. Because it is a "word of wisdom," it contains the various parts of intellectual insight.

**Because I called.** <note>original: "Yaan karati"</note> Meaning, wisdom personifies itself as one crying out to those who love her to merit her, telling them the words of their own testimony: "My heart is for you." You should have considered my voice as a constant, and not just a fleeting thing; my goal was to make you successful in wisdom, and certainly to make your companions successful in all precious possessions and physical goods. All this is the grace of my beloved in my voice.

**And you refused.** <note>original: "Va-temanu"</note> This is like saying, "Why would you take this path?" It implies the anger of the power of the matter and the entry of negation. It is as if you turned your back and your face away from me, saying "We do not desire the goodness of your knowledge." You did not want to listen or to incline your ear to the word of my reproof.

**I also [will laugh] at your calamity.** <note>original: "Gam ani be-idkhem"</note> This implies that you will see a great increase of force in the voice of calamity. Whatever life you thought you had will become a day of wrath and obligation. When your fear comes, it will arrive like a burden upon the one receiving it, according to its measure. On the day of the scattering of your fear, it will be according to its smallness <note>meaning: the destruction is total</note>, entering into the border of the forces of destruction.

**When your fear comes like a storm.** <note>original: "Be-vo ke-shoah padhkhem"</note> This is a vision of the entry of fear, suggesting that your fear and the pressure of its arrival will be so overwhelming and marked that there will be no ability to defend oneself.

**And your calamity arrives like a whirlwind.** <note>original: "Ve-idkhem ke-sufah ye-eteh"</note> Just as a great and well-known storm is regular and descends to strike, so your fear will come according to the dread you felt. Now he suggests that your fear is a vision of lack and ruin, a total darkness of the way.

**Note:** The more one is distant from the Master, the more one despises wisdom; yet wisdom remains secure in the heart despite the conflict.

**And your calamity...** even in the greatness of external wisdoms, as when one leaves the coolness of truth. For this vision is for one who is warm <note>impassioned for wrong things</note>. This is because the desire of the Lord is the core, and trust in the ultimate goal is what matters.

**B' (2): Mathematics and Knowledge.** It is known that natural wisdom can lead to destruction if it is separated from the wisdom of God. Every responder to their own thoughts and voice who relies on their own void will find that all their joy and knowledge was for violence.

**Verse 7:** One of the wisdoms is to see and to write one's absolute thoughts in the living wisdoms, and specifically in this: "The Lord opened..." The acquisition is from Him. According to their wisdom, they are drawn in, for "He knows my people will call and find me."

**They shall eat alone.** They will be left to their own devices.

**And they shall seek me...** <note>original: "ye-shaharunani"</note> The letters Chet and Samekh <unclear>referring to manuscript variants</unclear>. This means all the wise will take from the two <note>perhaps referring to the two types of wisdom</note>; more will be given to the one who opens the power of knowledge.

**And the fear of the Lord they did not choose.** Because they chose the house and the dwelling of the less important things, rather than the encompassing research of the hands of knowledge.

**They did not desire.** <note>original: "Lo abu"</note> He increases the proposal of the dream of his own knowledge in external wisdoms.

**And they chose all.** <unclear>They set their souls against every word of my reproof.</unclear>

**And they shall eat.** Wisdom is what provides the absolute possessions and the "fruit of their way."

**And they shall be satiated from their way.** They will be full of their own sorrow.

**For the turning away.** <note>original: "Ki meshuvat"</note> Meaning the lack and the voice of the evil way which brings us to those possessions. The death was caused by their simple-mindedness and poverty of spirit.

**And whoever listens.** To the exalted freedom. He will be safe from the pursuit of the "spoils" of life. He will have the ability to overcome, and he will be quiet from the bad desires that come upon him. Because of the peace he has, he will not fear an evil report, for his heart is secure in the Lord.

**Note:** The word "widening" <note>Hebrew: "merhavat"</note> suggests the pleasantness and trust that comes from taking up wisdom. This is because when he recognizes the evil of his ways, he turns to trust in wisdom, even with the depth of his previous coldness.

**Son, if...** <note>original: "Beni im"</note> That is, the student should remember the words of the excellent wise men and receive them as wisdom. He should incline his ear and receive this wisdom, hiding it in his heart. It should be like a path for his writing and a vision, becoming like wine to his gait. You should call out with great desires for those who seek it.

**If you call for discernment.** Like one who chooses a spouse, you should find understanding to be the main thing. It should be the "brightness" of your life.

**2:2-3.** He means that even in the gathering of wisdom there is great toil. You will not be able to achieve it unless He helps you in achieving understanding. Therefore, you must receive it with the same desire for benefit as one has for silver.

**If you desire...** if you do not consider your time as wasted! Just as your eyes are busy with possessions, like those who seek silver, so you should investigate it with total precision and research, even more than those who search for hidden treasures of gold and precious stones. Then you will understand, for he says: "I advise your heart in truth." From wisdom comes a great portion, and you will turn from it to the knowledge of the "Holy Ones," which is the knowledge of wisdom.

**For the Lord.** He says: this thing will not be hidden from you. It is not impossible for you if you pour out your heart before His wisdom. In your thoughts, you will find Him, for He is the one who gives wisdom constantly. The lack is only on the side of the receiver.

**He stores up for the upright.** He wants to help those who need the words of wisdom. He provides "thought" <note>original: "zimmah"</note> to explain the words of wisdom to those who walk in integrity before God.

**Sound wisdom.** <note>original: "Tushiyah"</note> This is a name for something that provides healing and strength. He will guard the paths of justice until it becomes a "shield" for them.

**To guard the paths.** Meaning, He protects the paths so they do not stumble. This "sound wisdom" and "attainment" are always with them because they cleaved to Him.

**Then you will understand.** That is, if you seek wisdom in the proper way, you will understand justice. This is the foundation of all. You will understand "equity" <note>original: "mesharim"</note>, which is the proper and balanced way of speaking. You will be among those who are "perfect in the way."

**Discretion.** <note>original: "Mezimmah"</note> Then wisdom will always be present, protecting you from the ways of death and folly. Wisdom will guard you so you do not seek the "strange woman." You will remember the paths of the lovers.

**To deliver you.** Wisdom will go before you as an inheritance, saving you from the way of the evil man who could harm you, and from the man who speaks perversities—meaning one who speaks things that are the opposite of uprightness and truth.

<summary>This page covers Wisdom’s stern warning to those who reject her and the subsequent promise that diligent seekers of understanding will be Divinely protected and granted moral clarity. The commentary emphasizes that wisdom is a gift from God that requires human effort, comparable to searching for hidden treasure.</summary>

# Proverbs
### Chapter 3

<meta>catchword: For</meta>

**Hebrew Source Text** | **Aramaic Translation (Targum)**
:--- | :---
[10] Your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will burst with new wine. | <margin>Books of the Living</margin> <margin>From the mouth of Phinehas</margin> [10] And your treasures will be filled with satiety, and from your wine-presses new wine shall drip.
[11] My son, do not despise the discipline of the Lord, and do not loathe His rebuke. | [11] My son, do not reject the instruction of God, and do not loathe His reproof.
[12] For whom the Lord loves He reproves, even as a father the son in whom he delights. | [12] For because God loves him, He shall rebuke him, just as a father who loves his son.

<margin>Hand</margin> [27] Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in the power of your hand to do it. | [27] Do not withhold good from those who deserve it, when there is power in your hand to act.
[28] Do not say to your neighbor, "Go, and come again, and tomorrow I will give," when you have it with you. | [28] Do not say to your friend, "Go and return, and tomorrow I will give," when it is with you.
[29] Do not devise evil against your neighbor, while he dwells securely by you. | [29] Do not think evil against your friend while he dwells trustingly beside you.

### Commentary

**Your barns shall be filled.** This means your wisdom <note>The commentator interprets material "barns" and "wine" as metaphors for the storage of intellectual and spiritual knowledge.</note>. And thus it will be <unclear>imrati</unclear> like "and He will visit tomorrow." The meaning of **your vats** is that they will increase in wine. Even if it were from the language of "spreading out" or "breaking through," the meaning is that the wine within your vats will break the fence because of its abundance, for the vat cannot contain it. If the word <unclear>imratu</unclear> comes from the concept of spreading out, as in "at the breaches of their vats," it refers to the overflow of the walls.

**The discipline of the Lord.** So that there shall be no lack of <unclear>hatch hachlamim</unclear> in this world, do not despise your discipline, and do not think of your rebukes as thorns. For God's assembly is with you; it is a discipline of rebuke to turn you from an evil path. One should not worry about the sufferings that come upon you, for they are intended to ensure your faithfulness.

**As a father the son.** He shall merit like <unclear>Moab</unclear> who finds grace <note>The text here is difficult to decipher, but it seems to compare God's rebuke to a father who disciplines a son not to push him away, but to bring him closer to the good path.</note>. The discipline of the one who reproves teaches one how to act with strength, even for the "deaf elder" who must contend with his weakened strength.

**The man who finds wisdom.** The intent is that the homiletic discipline <term>Derash</term><note>Interpretive or homiletic teaching.</note> grants a person wisdom. Likewise, "a man who brings forth understanding" merits that the <term>Demos</term><note>original: "Ha-Dimos". Likely from the Greek 'demos,' here used to mean a public or common intellectual standing.</note> will be with us, understanding one thing from another.

**For its gain is better.** That is to say, its "commerce" is better than the commerce of silver, and its "produce" is better than fine gold. Wisdom is more precious than **pearls**. These are the gems hidden in the innermost chambers so they are not stolen. When it says **all your desires cannot compare to her**, it means there is no object or ornament of value that equals the acquisition of wisdom.

**Length of days is in her right hand.** This refers to one who occupies himself with the <term>Torah</term> for its own sake <note>original: "Lishmah". Doing a holy act for the sake of the act itself, rather than for a reward.</note>; he shall merit length of days in the world of souls. This path is called "prepared" because the constant spiritual service is of such high degree... nevertheless, he also has a reward in this world from established goods: **riches and honor**.

**Her ways are ways of pleasantness.** These paths are pleasant to the soul and they are <unclear>betak lesomus</unclear>. They are secure from the reach of evil. The Torah teaches him a "good face" <note>An expression for a friendly, welcoming, and enlightened disposition.</note>.

**The Lord by wisdom founded the earth.** Because he warned about the holy and awesome <unclear>paras</unclear>, and the Torah which is supported by the pillars of the world, he mentions that the Creator, by His will, used Wisdom to establish the first foundations. This refutes those who deny the divine order. Just as there is no wonder in one who improves his wisdom, so too for the one who establishes the "theoretical ways" <note>Likely referring to the laws of nature or divine logic.</note>.

**By His knowledge.** Now he warns about the occupation with discipline. By His knowledge the **depths were broken up**, referring to the gathering of the waters into one place so the dry land could appear. We cannot truly know the "splitting of the depths" with our own minds, but we see the result in nature. Likewise, he established the **skies** as the place where the **dew** is born, to moisten the earth in the summer heat so the land does not perish.

**My son, let them not depart.** He means: do not let these moral principles turn from before your eyes, for they are the roots of the complete Torah. **And they shall be life for your soul**, meaning these conducts are like life-giving food for the soul, just as good food sustains the body.

**Then you will walk safely.** When you accept the discipline of the Torah, you will be secure. **Your foot will not stumble**, not in this world nor in the World to Come. When you are "gathered to your people," you will not fear death; it will be like a **sweet sleep**. The death of the righteous is called "sleep."

**Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due.** He speaks to the wealthy man, that he should not keep everything for himself but leave some for the poor. He also speaks to the wise man, that he should not withhold the Torah—which is called "good"—from its "owners," who are the worthy students. **When it is in the power of your hand**: as long as you have the ability. If you delay your neighbor by saying "come back tomorrow," it is a sin. Do not withhold the wisdom that has been prepared for a man at the time he is ready to receive it.

**Do not devise evil.** It is a great betrayal to think of doing evil to a companion who trusts in your friendship. This refers to a "hidden thought" of treachery.

The commentary explains these verses both as literal moral instructions and as allegories for the soul's intellectual perfection.</summary>

<meta>This page transitions from the end of Chapter 3 into the heart of Chapter 4 of the Book of Proverbs. While the previous page focused on the cosmic and personal value of Wisdom (Chokhmah) as a "Tree of Life," this page shifts toward practical moral warnings. It contrasts the "path of the righteous," which grows brighter like the sun, with the "way of the wicked," which is shrouded in stumbling darkness. The commentary provided is a classic Rabbinic analysis, likely by the 14th-century philosopher Ralbag (Gersonides), focusing on the psychological discipline required to maintain a virtuous life.</meta>

# Proverbs
### Chapter 4

**Aramaic Translation (Targum)** | **Hebrew Source Text**
:--- | :---
[14] Do not enter the path of the guilty and do not walk in the way of the wicked. | <margin>14</margin> **Do not enter the path of the wicked, and do not walk in the way of evil men.**
[15] Keep far from it and do not enter it; turn away from it and pass by. | <margin>15</margin> **Avoid it, do not pass by it; turn away from it and pass on.**
[16] For they do not sleep unless they do evil, and their sleep is driven away until they cause someone to stumble. | <margin>16</margin> **For they cannot sleep unless they have done wrong; they are robbed of sleep unless they make someone stumble.**
[17] For they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence. | <margin>17</margin> **For they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.**
[18] But the path of the righteous is like the light that dawns, going on and brightening until the day is established <note>original: "mitkan yoma"—referring to high noon</note>. | <margin>18</margin> **But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, which shines brighter and brighter until full day.**
[19] The way of the guilty is like darkness; they do not know what they stumble over. | <margin>19</margin> **The way of the wicked is like deep darkness; they do not know what makes them stumble.**
[20] My son, pay attention to my words; incline your ear to my sayings. | <margin>20</margin> **My son, be attentive to my words; incline your ear to my sayings.**
[21] Let them not depart from your eyes; keep them in the midst of your heart. | <margin>21</margin> **Let them not escape from your sight; keep them within your heart.**
[22] For they are life to those who find them and healing to all their flesh. | <margin>22</margin> **For they are life to those who find them, and healing to all their flesh.**
[23] Above all guarding, guard your heart, for from it flow the outgoings of life. | <margin>23</margin> **Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life.**
[24] Put away from you crookedness of mouth and keep devious lips far from you. | <margin>24</margin> **Put away from you crooked speech, and put devious talk far from you.**
[25] Let your eyes look directly forward, and let your gaze be straight before you. | <margin>25</margin> **Let your eyes look directly forward, and your gaze be straight before you.**
[26] Level the track of your feet, and all your paths will be established. | <margin>26</margin> **Ponder the path of your feet; then all your ways will be sure.**
[27] Do not turn to the right or to the left; remove your foot from evil. | <margin>27</margin> **Do not swerve to the right or to the left; turn your foot away from evil.**

<column-break/>

### Commentary

**Do not enter with the wicked** — This means do not join them. • Do not join them in their specific "path" <note>Hebrew: "orach," often meaning a local or personal habit</note> • and do not join them in their general "way" <note>Hebrew: "derech," a major road or lifestyle</note>. • This is warned because perhaps your heart will be stirred by seeing them and you will begin to resemble them. • **And do not walk in the way of evil men** — Do not even step onto their path. This is similar to the expression "walk in the way of understanding."

**Avoid it** — Leave it alone and pull your hand back from it. • Like the phrase "let his hair go loose" <note>original: "para," implying neglect or lack of control</note> or "you have neglected all my counsel."

**Turn away from it and pass on** — Abandon the way of the wicked and distance yourself from them to the furthest extreme.

**For they cannot sleep unless they have done wrong** — Because it is their nature to do harm. • If they do not commit evil, they feel as though their sleep has been stolen from them. • Perhaps they even harm their own companions and cause them to stumble.

**For they eat the bread of wickedness** — Their very sustenance comes to them through robbery and violence.

**But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn** — The way of the righteous is illuminating. • It continues to shine until "the day is established," meaning until the end of the day's increase, which is high noon when the light is greatest.

**The way of the wicked is like deep darkness** — The wicked walk in gloom. • Because they are in the dark, they cannot see the very things that cause their downfall. • For this reason, it says, **they do not know what makes them stumble.**

**My son, be attentive to my words** — Here the teacher begins to warn specifically about the words of the Torah and moral discipline <note>term: "Mussar" — ethical instruction</note>. • He says: My son, listen closely to my words, and incline your ear to hear my sayings.

**Let them not escape from your sight** — Do not allow the words of the Torah to be removed from your vision; they should always be before your eyes. • And "keep them within your heart" so that your heart is always prepared to receive them.

**For they are life to those who find them** — The words of the Torah provide life to those who discover them, and "healing to all their flesh," because the Torah is a remedy for both the body and the soul.

**Keep your heart with all vigilance** — Even more than you guard your other affairs, guard your heart against evil thoughts.

**For from it flow the springs of life** — Because proper thought is the primary cause of a good life.

**Put away from you crooked speech** — Do not speak twisted or evil things. • Keep "devious lips" far from you.

**Let your eyes look directly forward** — Do not look to the sides <note>implying distraction or looking for temptation</note>, but let your eyes look straight ahead.

**And your gaze be straight before you** — Let the focus of your eyes follow a straight path.

**Ponder the path of your feet** — Always weigh and measure your actions and your ways. • Then all your ways will be established and correct.

**Do not swerve to the right or to the left** — Do not deviate from the straight path to either side. • Turn your foot away from the path of evil.

<summary>This page contrasts the progressive enlightenment of a righteous life with the self-destructive darkness of the wicked. It emphasizes "guarding the heart" as the central discipline of moral life, arguing that our internal thoughts are the ultimate source of our external actions and well-being.</summary>

# Proverbs
### Chapters 4 and 5

**Aramaic Translation (Targum)** | **Hebrew Source Text**
:--- | :---
The food of the wicked and the wine of robbers they drink. And the path of the righteous is like the brilliance of light that shines as it goes, and its light increases until the full establishment of the day <note>original: "dikkan yoma"—referring to the sun reaching its zenith</note>. And the path of the wicked is like thick darkness; they do not know what they stumble over. My son, listen to my words and incline your ear to my sayings. Do not let them depart from your eyes; guard them in the midst of your heart. For they are life to those who find them and healing to all their flesh. With all vigilance, guard your heart, for from it are the outlets of life. Put away from you the crookedness of the mouth and keep the deviousness of the lips far from you. Let your eyes look straight ahead and your eyelids be directed before you. Move your feet away from evil paths and all your ways shall be established. Do not swerve to the right or the left; turn your foot away from evil. My son, listen to my wisdom; incline your ear to my understanding. To guard your thoughts, and may your lips guard knowledge. For the lips of a stranger <note>original: "nukhreita"—the "strange" or "foreign" woman</note> drip with honey, and her palate is smoother than oil. But her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a sword with two edges. Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold of the grave <note>original: "Sheol"</note>. Lest you ponder the path of life, her ways wander and she does not know it. And now, sons, listen to me and do not swerve from the words of my mouth. Keep your way far from her and do not approach the door of her house. Lest you give your glory to others and your years to the cruel. Lest strangers be satisfied with your strength and your labors go to the house of another. And you groan at your end, when your flesh and your body are consumed. | <margin>17</margin> **For they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.** <margin>18</margin> **But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, which shines brighter and brighter until full day.** <margin>19</margin> **The way of the wicked is like deep darkness; they do not know what makes them stumble.** <margin>20</margin> **My son, pay attention to my words; incline your ear to my sayings.** <margin>21</margin> **Do not let them out of your sight; keep them within your heart.** <margin>22</margin> **For they are life to those who find them and health to a man’s whole body.** <margin>23</margin> **Guard your heart with all vigilance, for from it are the sources of life.** <margin>24</margin> **Put away crooked speech from you, and put devious talk far from you.** <margin>25</margin> **Let your eyes look straight ahead; fix your gaze directly before you.** <margin>26</margin> **Pave the path for your feet, and all your ways will be established.** <margin>27</margin> **Do not swerve to the right or the left; keep your foot from evil.** <margin>5:1</margin> **My son, pay attention to my wisdom; incline your ear to my understanding,** <margin>2</margin> **to preserve discretion, and that your lips may guard knowledge.** <margin>3</margin> **For the lips of a forbidden woman <note>original: "zarah"—a "strange" or "outsider" woman</note> drip honey, and her speech is smoother than oil.** <margin>4</margin> **But in the end she is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a double-edged sword.** <margin>5</margin> **Her feet go down to death; her steps lead straight to the grave <note>original: "Sheol"</note>.** <margin>6</margin> **She does not ponder the path of life; her ways wander, and she does not know it.** <margin>7</margin> **And now, O sons, listen to me, and do not depart from the words of my mouth.** <margin>8</margin> **Keep your way far from her, and do not go near the door of her house,** <margin>9</margin> **lest you give your honor to others and your years to the merciless,** <margin>10</margin> **lest strangers feast on your strength and your labors go to the house of a foreigner,** <margin>11</margin> **and at the end of your life you groan, when your flesh and body are consumed.**

<column-break/>

**For they have eaten the bread of wickedness:** This expands upon the wickedness of the "wicked sages" and the cause of their evil sins. It is strong because they have already consumed the "fat of wickedness"—their wisdom has turned to bitterness, full of twisted laws and engagement in strife and conflict. Thus, they join with the wicked and are armed with the "wine of violence," which causes the exhaustion of the soul. **But the path of the righteous:** That is to say, the way of the righteous is like the dawning light in the morning; it begins to shine and continues to grow until the "establishment of the day," meaning high noon. This is a metaphor for the light of the Torah according to the tradition, which grows from small beginnings until it reaches the end of the purpose of wisdom. **The way of the wicked is like darkness:** He wishes to inform us that the way of lust and desire is like walking in deep darkness. In contrast to the expanding light of wisdom, their strength fades until they "know not what they stumble over," and their life force is cut off. This is a warning to those who hold onto the foundations of wisdom to distance themselves from the slippery slopes of the rebellious, where there are great deceptions and pitfalls.

**My son, pay attention to my words:** Because the foolishness of the wicked is prepared to speak against true opinions, and their false "wisdom" is rooted in a rebellious heart, the sage warns to keep his thoughts fixed on what is written "outside" <note>referring to manifest wisdom</note> through discipline and Torah. **Do not let them out of your sight:** Meaning, do not let these intellectual concepts and branches of contemplation be hidden from you. Let them stand always before your eyes and guard them in the midst of your heart. **For they are life to those who find them:** These virtuous words are life and healing, as opposed to the sickness and exhaustion that come from following the ways of the wicked.

**Guard your heart with all vigilance:** Every person must strongly guard their desires and the will of the heart, for "from it are the sources of life." This means that from the purity of the heart flow life and grace. Just as the heart is the most essential organ physically, so too must it be guarded spiritually from all things. The "guarding" refers to not allowing foreign thoughts to enter or for one to be delayed by the empty words of the foolish. **Put away from you crooked speech:** That is, do not let your mouth speak "crookedly"—let all your words be words of truth. Likewise, "devious lips" <note>original: "lezut sefatayim"</note> should be far from you.

**Let your eyes look straight ahead:** Your vision and your contemplation should always look toward the "True Path." Do not swerve to the right or the left, for the paths of the forbidden woman lead to destruction. **Pave the path for your feet:** Meaning, act with balance and weigh your actions. All your ways should be prepared and directed toward the ultimate purpose. **Do not swerve to the right or the left:** This is a parable for moderate action—turning away from the "left," which represents the material and the dangerous, and staying on the path that produces good.

**My son, pay attention to my wisdom:** He warns again about the dangers of the "forbidden woman" of desire and urges the student to draw near to the wisdom that gives life. **To guard your thoughts:** This refers to the noble thoughts that deserve to be guarded, so that they might lead a person to the light and keep them from the darkness of the wicked. **For the lips of a forbidden woman drip honey:** This is a metaphor for how "foreign" ideas or material desires seem sweet and pleasant to the listener at first—like honey or oil—but their "end" is bitter as wormwood. This "end" is the destruction of the soul. The forbidden woman represents those destructive philosophies that mislead the soul. **Her feet go down to death:** She leads those who follow her to the grave <note>Sheol</note>. The sages warned that one should not pursue these foreign wisdoms, for they do not lead to life but to the wandering and loss of the soul's essence.

**And now, O sons, listen to me:** The teacher repeats the warning to stay away from the "door of her house," meaning one should not even come close to the beginnings of such destructive desires or false opinions. **Lest you give your honor to others:** If one follows these paths, their dignity and the years of their life will be handed over to "cruel" forces—meaning the physical desires that consume the body and leave the soul empty. **And you groan at your end:** This describes the regret at the end of life when one's physical strength ("flesh and body") is gone, and one realizes they have wasted their years on "strangers" and "foreigners" <note>allegories for non-intellectual, material pursuits</note> instead of building a lasting spiritual legacy.

And you shall say, "How I hated discipline, and my heart rejected rebuke! I did not listen to the voice of my instructors, nor did I incline my ear to my teachers. Let them be for you alone, and not for strangers with you. Let your source be blessed, and rejoice with the wife of your youth. A lovely hind and a graceful doe; let her breasts satisfy you at all times, be intoxicated always with her love. And why should you be led astray, my son, by a stranger, and embrace the bosom of an alien woman? For a man’s ways are before the eyes of the Lord, and He weighs all his paths. <margin>He shall die in his [sin]</margin> His iniquities shall entrap the wicked, and he shall be held by the cords of his sin. He shall die for lack of [discipline]...
<column-break/>

**"And you say: 'How...'"** Every palate <note>taste/inclination</note> finds the words of discipline bitter before the action is done. Likewise, **"and rebuke"** <note>original: "tochechat"</note>—you should be ones who rebuke me after the evil deeds are done. "Rebuke" generally follows the path of "You shall surely rebuke your fellow" <note>Leviticus 19:17</note>. These are the ones who lead the person's heart, and this is the meaning of **"my teachers."** It is called this because they teach <note>mori</note> or guide <note>kori</note> or are the ones who show the way <note>hanari</note> like a priest before the sin. Similarly, for **"to my instructors,"** I turned away from my sins through those who taught me the ways of understanding or who helped me. And I saw how many fell into the snare because of my "teachers," for they were the ones who led them, and they are to die for not listening to their words. Likewise, all reproof and discipline of faith is a shield against sin.

**"I was almost in all evil."** This refers to the shame of the smallness of "almost"—that I committed every evil in the world. Rather, it is in a hidden and living way. He stumbled in his many desires. In all sins, light and severe. And it is explained further: "when will it be?" And that is what is meant by **"in the midst of the assembly and the congregation."** Or it may mean that "almost all the punishments in the world came upon me because of my sins and transgressions." And the meaning of "almost I was found in all evil and punishment" is that the words of the believer imply that the wicked are few and only their punishment is found among them.

**Note 1.** This woman <note>the "strange woman" of Proverbs 5</note> is compared to a foreign city. And for the person being rebuked, the explanation is about the "flowing" and "springs," which are metaphors. One of the interpretations is: she is compared to the sweetness of the water that a person stretches out for according to his laws and desires, but after he drinks, this thing turns into gall. 

**2.** He brings it to their desire and artfulness, and all their desires for other strangers who are children of foreignness from it. These integrities are dependent on desire. If you do not let a holy man who is among them speak to them, for everything is a secret and strength and such. The "cistern" <note>bor</note> is for the saturation of the whole man, whether it is his own eye or a settled well that talks about artfulness. And it is much to hint that he is all-capable and has choice. And he said, "and your work," to hint at the arranged family between the material desires with the intellect, and the wisdom that shines from the life of the material thoughts that distance one into other evils.

**3.** We speak of the sinner in repentance at the time of old age, when he is caught in the net and in the embrace of his brothers as a complete and living exile. Repentance is difficult and it is a desire, and God forbid, he is found in the midst of the waters in the bitterness of the heart. When the soul of understanding is delayed from its desire without power in peace. They have already said that a person's path goes down to the ways of its repair, and the rebuke said there is no helper. He explains "in your well" as a way of explaining that "your well" is your wife, your modesty, and you shall see and rejoice in your end, the joy of the righteous is in the end.

**"Drink water from your cistern."** This is a statement of distancing from sin. Let your path be to drink water from the cistern, and that is to cling only to your wife and not to strangers. For the waters are compared to intimacy, as the water in his lap. And the return to the "cistern" will clarify the path. Then those waters that you drink will be like flowing waters from your well of living waters. Because from your separation with your wife in holiness and in the future, and in piety and in the arrangement of the waters and in the desires, it is as if you drink from the life of wisdom, which is a precious well and a source. And this comes down to the waters that are done.

**"Let your springs be dispersed."** Do not let those waters decrease, but let them increase and turn into springs of life, and so "streams of water in the streets." This is a parable for children who will descend from him, who will be many in the streets and markets. And these children will be for you alone, for I will say they were born from your hand in purity.

**"Let your source be blessed."** A hint to the seed of the wise that brings forth and bears blessing, so that he will not be barren. **"And rejoice"**—like "and be glad." Or it may be like "and see the light in the lap," that your life should be blessed. And do not see <note>desire</note>, meaning, after foreign women. Therefore, rejoice with the wife of your youth. Or it may be the increase of your life... <note>The commentator explains that "wife of youth" can also allegorically represent the initial wisdom or Torah one studies in their youth.</note>

And because the sin will go to many tastes, it calls it "love" and "grace." Because all sweetness is soft, it is from this woman in the place of wisdom to remember this. And the "grace" rises according to its hints so that the students will be established and brought near. He said that the love is shifted to be in the life of the children, they will satisfy you at all times, like a holy thing. Until, because of this love, it will give a scent in the purity as is said for those who engage in its love and drink with it. "Intoxicated" <note>original: "tishgeh"—meaning both 'to err' and 'to be intoxicated'</note> means in holiness. And it increases from the movement of the dead and the joy like a sprout.

<margin>And still Chapter 5 and 4</margin>

**Note 1.** In this effort of the King <note>Solomon</note> to say the paths of truth from it, he calls it "always," from the fear of standing before Him. And so the calculating soul in its path, I saw an eye that is in the love of the command of water and water as in the light of water.

<margin>4th Note</margin>

**2.** The settled "cistern of water" and the "springs" and the "well of water" that are within, being between the lower beauties that are fixed from man to man until knowledge. He saw the waters that were desired in bitterness. And this is the principle of the law and the details of the faith. And if I were to investigate them as he said in "what is hidden from you, do not search." And there are sermons about me, and they are the sages in their assemblies, adding to them in the reasons of the Torah and the wings of the Torah, and we praise him who prevents it.

<margin>And 20 Chapter of Tirosh</margin>

And so he hinted that the calculating soul, if it prevents engagement in thoughts, will enter from it and the material will prevail over them. And as long as you strive, my son, for the needs... and the God of the waters of your teaching, they are like the waters that surround the rock of the declaration, the order of wisdom is ready. This is the time of being seated, her love was spoken. And to hint "drink water from your cistern," from the place of the sages, he said these are the pleasant ones for the souls and they are called so.

<margin>And "tishgeh" <note>err/intoxicated</note></margin>

**3.** We lean on the study of our Creator. At the time of this study, which prevents understanding one thing from another, it adds to your springs, and it is the streams from the midst of your well, like the waters that surround every day. This is the time of the one who establishes a Yeshiva <note>academy</note> for many students; the Torah of my Creator, every person is a master of the hall. Hear and turn and contemplate, and let these drink from your springs, etc. And every first student goes in this, that the verse comes to say that many have been killed by her, and if not for the study of the chosen one...

**4.** In the Midrash they said: "Let your springs be dispersed abroad" — if you have a generation that is worthy of it, let the words of Torah be dispersed abroad. And if not, "let them be for you alone." This is to say, at a time when they are not worthy, and the deed is bitter, his deposits are hidden in his heart. As it is said: "It is time to act for the Lord, they have made void Your Torah" <note>Psalm 119:126</note>. I say: they made void Your Torah, it is time to act for the Lord.

**5.** From the calculating wisdom, it is called the "source of life" that stands outside the light in the end. And that which is known in the intellects is "blessed." And you have seen one from the world and a saying that is said and spoken and clarified. And in the engagement of the Divine Torah, if it is "intoxication," this is it and all the artisans of the world.

And "why should you be led astray, my son, with a stranger?" He said... the one who embraces and stands... and see under it my son in the joy of the Torah of your brother... which is in it for you, and you embrace the bosom of the alien woman, for even its visions are forbidden to you.

**"For the ways of man are before the eyes of the Lord."** The intention is that after you have to be far from the act of what is in its calculation according to the natural and habitual evil from the outside, the dream is attached in his special account and not with a stranger or an alien woman. Indeed, more and more you have to be far from it because of the Divine punishment, for "the ways of man are before the eyes of the Lord" and his actions are revealed to Him.

**"And He weighs all his paths."** All his things are light, acting in the cycles of uprightness. **"His iniquities shall entrap the wicked."** For there is a judgment from above, and he needs to prepare, and his punishment is to see the thing from above. And if it is needed so that they do not return, his iniquities will trap him and bring him in, as it is said: "his feet go down to death." And as he said: **"and by the cords of his sin he shall be held."** These are the cords of sin that will place him and guard him in a place from which he cannot flee, like many of the previous ones who fled from his house of guard.

**"He shall die."** Either he will be prepared from himself for the root of repentance. And he said **"for lack of discipline,"** in the honor that he did not hear the discipline of his father who brought him near to the Torah and wisdom.

**"And in the greatness of his folly he shall go astray."** For when he says he was the one who was twisted in his life, he sinned and went astray in the secret of the hidden thoughts of his account, thus he is found as a wanderer and straying and his head is multiplied. And this is what it says "without discipline," which is to say he dies with the stings of the teacher that opened him, for he is also a man of suffering and rebellion and a death that is bitter for the wicked.

**Note 1.** We said of the mixture of the strange waters, and so the severe evils and their silence are misleading things, and they have no existence except for an hour. And therefore they said, "and why should you be led astray, my son, in the visions of my daughters."

**2.** We said "he shall go astray" <note>yishgeh</note> like a wanderer in all the land. And here the King and the King's son come to say according to what is inside.

**3.** We said that the height and the expansion of the waters are the ones that satisfy. And they are the students, and it is found that this is to fall from the law, and let it be blessed, for the action then is the man and in the thought of uprightness.

**4.** We said from the arrangement of discipline in the good thoughts, if they understand, and he has no covenant with people, and if he did not turn from the life of his brother, it is fitting for him in the end of his actions to investigate and turn, except in my end. And these shall not be poor for you by themselves, but all the days of life and the light of the Torah and the light in life.

<summary>This page concludes the warnings against the "strange woman" (folly) in Proverbs 5, interpreting the text as an allegory for intellectual purity and the importance of remaining faithful to the "wife of one's youth," which represents early, true wisdom. The commentary emphasizes that divine justice observes all human paths and that those who reject discipline are ultimately trapped by their own sins.</summary>
