<meta>This page continues the text of the Book of Proverbs, moving from the warnings against adultery in Chapter 5 to the dangers of financial liability (surety) and the vice of laziness in Chapter 6. The layout presents the Hebrew source alongside its Aramaic translation (Targum), followed by a dense rabbinic commentary that bridges the literal and allegorical meanings.</meta>

<page-num>ו</page-num>
<header>Proverbs</header>

**Hebrew Source Text** | **Aramaic Translation (Targum)**
:--- | :---
My son, if you have become surety for your neighbor, if you have shaken hands in pledge for a stranger; | My son, if you have become a guarantor for your friend, and have placed your hand [in pledge] for a stranger;
You are snared by the words of your mouth, you are caught by the words of your mouth. | You have been ensnared by the speech of your mouth, you have been seized by the speech of your mouth.
Do this now, my son, and deliver yourself, for you have come into the hand of your neighbor; go, humble yourself, and plead with your neighbor. | Do this, my son, and be saved, because you have fallen into the hand of your friend; go, be crushed and urge your friend.
Give no sleep to your eyes, nor slumber to your eyelids. | Give no sleep to your eyes, nor slumber to your eyelids.
Deliver yourself as a gazelle from the hand [of the hunter], and as a bird from the hand of the fowler. | Be saved like a gazelle from the hunter, and like a bird from the trap.
Go to the ant, O sluggard; consider her ways and be wise; | Go to the ant, O sluggard; see its ways and become wise;
Which, having no chief, overseer, or ruler, | Which has no leader, nor guide, nor ruler,
Provides her bread in the summer, and gathers her food in the harvest. | Yet prepares bread in the summer, and gathers food in the harvest.
How long will you lie there, O sluggard? When will you arise from your sleep? | Until when, O sluggard, will you lie down? When will you rise from your sleep?
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest; | A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to lie down;
So shall your poverty come as a traveler, and your want as an armed man. | And distress shall come like a traveler, and your lack like a man of arms.
A worthless person, a man of iniquity, walks with a perverse mouth; | A rebellious man, a sinful man, walks with the crookedness of his mouth;
He winks with his eyes, he speaks with his feet, he teaches with his fingers; | He casts [looks] with his eyes, and signals with his feet, and instructs with his fingers;
Perverseness is in his heart, he devises evil continually; he sows discord. | And perversion is in his heart, and he plows evil at all times, and he sends forth strife.

<column-break/>

**My son, if you have become surety for your neighbor** — After the text elaborated on the matters of food and drink <note>Referring to the metaphors of "cisterns" and "springs" in Chapter 5</note>, it removes the veil from the "stranger" who causes harm. The meaning here is the cessation of that action. The moralist proves that one's assets can be used for evil, just as he taught: "Lest strangers be filled with your strength." He says: "He harmed me in the matter of your assets." It is as if to strengthen the agreement and satisfy it until it was already bound and strengthened, until you were "bound to your neighbor." <margin>1</margin> **You were snared**: You passed from one matter to another. The obligation of these things brings ruin. The cause of this is that he is your "neighbor," for you are now troubled because of his weariness. You became a surety by the strengthening of the hand <term>hand-clasping (Kaf): a formal gesture used in the ancient world to finalize a legal contract or debt</term>. It was right to strengthen the opener and explain it to him.

This connection brings a commentary <note>The text here contains several OCR errors ("כנא"ה", "פיר"), likely abbreviations for "it is a fine explanation" or "the commentary of..."</note>. Regarding the "snare of his mouth," why would one ride into the lack of a hand? It is not good for the youth of his children. The "neighbor" is an exaggeration, for it will be destroyed for him, for by this hand you obligate yourself to his debt. In the end, it will be reversed. He wraps himself as if he did not win it for him. The correct view is that it is a service to a living friend. And as it is written: "He gave room and kindled the mouth," he will inherit to crumble quickly. From the language of "crumbling," he brings bread and reward to your neighbor. But if they lived for the concealment of money, "his mouth" and "the word of your mouth" mean you have somewhat bound yourself and were released to strengthen the legal obligation of a person.

**You are snared by the words of your mouth** — May his memory be a blessing <note>Hebrew: Z"L, indicating a quote from a deceased sage</note>. This entire section on "surety" sits upon the thought of the one who becomes obligated. If he had possessions in the world sealed for him, he remains in the heart in the proximity of money. For you are general in the illness of obligation and you cannot turn yourself away from this debt when you are bound, for the release is already his.

**Do this now, my son, and humble yourself** — This is from the root of "trampling" <note>Hebrew: Hitrapes</note>. We find "vision" and "sight." The meaning of "vision" is the strength of the thick rope of cessation. Humble yourself before the lender to say: "It was your will," and approach further with soft words. And what is written "your neighbor," he shall give room to be saved. He shall return to the neighbor with the veil. One who walks in soft ways, his debt shall be forgiven. <margin>2</margin> It is also possible to interpret this from the perspective of the action of the savior and the formation of the family. From violence, it shall be broken upon the perversions for the preservation of the body. He should not give himself slumber or sleep. The intention is that he should habituate himself with all his strength to be exempt from his obligation of surety.

**Deliver yourself as a gazelle from the hand** — That is to say: Open your eyes and run to lack and be saved quickly. Just as the bird is hidden from the hand of the fowler. It is possible that "the fowler" <note>Hebrew: Yakush</note> is at the end of the verse. 

<margin>6</margin> **Go to the ant, O sluggard** — See the grace in the prepared things. Chase after the beginnings and the foldings, like this for the measure of the night. This is wisdom from the verse: "They taught their mouth." One who looks at the prepared wisdoms — "and be wise." One who lacks the ultimate goal.

<margin>7</margin> In the **Midrash** <note>Interpretive homilies</note>: This refers to one who prepares for the ant. No Torah was given to it, yet it does not weaken to draw near. It goes without an overseer or ruler. It gathers in the harvest to prepare for the world. Even without being forced by the Torah, how much more so should you, who lack wisdom, prepare for the house of the future.

<margin>8</margin> **Provides in the summer** — According to the oaths that were said: "My son, support the few," and transgressed the Torah. Therefore, you have the wisdom of the humble.

<margin>9-10</margin> **The correction rolls before a person** — How long will you lie, sluggard? Even if you do not wake, he starts to inform you of the necessity. When will you hope for your end? Sleep is only for the necessity of the body's creation. **A little folding of the hands to lie down** — Like one who indulges in the preparation of his place. As they said: "Folding hands" is for those who learn. The matter is the existence of rest.

**So shall your poverty come as a traveler** — These words indicate speed and diligence. Poverty will not have a place to lodge, but will come like a "traveler" and will not rest. It is compared to a shield-man who comes with a sword. For your lack will be greater than your shield.

<margin>12</margin> **A worthless person** <note>Hebrew: Adam Beli-ya'al - literally "a man without ascent" or "without a yoke"</note> — A person should distance himself from laziness, for it prevents him from reaching the Torah. One who removes the yoke from himself. A "worthless person" is composed of "without" and "yoke." One who is not willing to accept the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven. His mouth is evil toward creatures. He walks with a perverse mouth.

**He winks with his eyes** — This is his work, like one who stretches his mockery. His perversion is in his speech. 

**He speaks with his feet** — He hints to his friends with his feet. 

**He teaches with his fingers** — He teaches with his fingers to speak with his woman. All these things are to teach the hand of destruction.

**Perverseness is in his heart** — He is a source for stealing souls and things. **He devises evil continually** — Even in his place of rest, he thinks of evil against his fellow.

<summary>This page warns against the dangers of becoming financially liable for others (surety) and uses the ant as a model for industriousness to avoid poverty. It concludes by describing the deceptive physical gestures of a "worthless person" who sows discord.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the text of Proverbs 6, transitioning from the description of the "wicked man" who sows discord to the famous list of the seven things God detests. It then moves into a parental exhortation to keep the commandments as a safeguard against the "forbidden woman," using the metaphors of light and fire.</meta>

# Proverbs

**Aramaic Translation (Targum)** | **Hebrew Source Text**
:--- | :---
...constantly sowing strife. Because of this, his destruction shall come suddenly; in an instant he shall be broken, and there shall be no healing for him. | ...continually sowing discord. Therefore his calamity shall come suddenly; in a moment he shall be broken without remedy.
There are six things that God hates, and the seventh His soul detests: | These six things the Lord hates, yes, seven are an abomination to Him:
Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood; | A proud look, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood,
A heart that devises sinful thoughts, and feet that are swift to run to evil; | A heart that devises wicked plans, feet that are swift in running to evil,
A false witness who speaks lies, and one who sows strife among brothers. | A false witness who speaks lies, and one who sows discord among brethren.
Keep, my son, the commandment of your father, and do not forsake the law <note>original: *nimusa*, likely referring to the Greek *nomos* used in Aramaic for law/custom</note> of your mother. | My son, keep your father’s command, and do not forsake the law <note>original: *torah*</note> of your mother.
Bind them upon your heart continually; tie them around your neck. | Bind them continually upon your heart; tie them around your neck.
When you walk, she <note>The wisdom/commandment</note> shall lead you; when you lie down, she shall watch over you; and when you awake, she shall be your guide. | When you roam, they will lead you; when you sleep, they will keep you; and when you awake, they will speak with you.
For the commandment is a lamp, and the law is light, and the way of life is reproof and discipline; | For the commandment is a lamp, and the law a light; reproofs of instruction are the way of life,
To keep you from the evil woman, and from the smooth tongue of the foreign woman. | To keep you from the evil woman, from the flattering tongue of a seductress.
Do not lust after her beauty in your heart, nor let her capture you with her eyelids. | Do not lust after her beauty in your heart, nor let her take you with her eyelids.
For by means of a harlot, a man is brought to a piece of bread, and an adulteress hunts for a precious soul. | For by means of a harlot a man is reduced to a crust of bread; and an adulteress will prey upon his precious life.
Can a man place fire in his bosom and his clothes not be burned? | Can a man take fire to his bosom, and his clothes not be burned?
Or can a man walk upon hot coals and his feet not be scorched? | Can one walk on hot coals, and his feet not be seared?
So is he who goes in to his neighbor’s wife; anyone who touches her will not be held innocent. | So is he who goes in to his neighbor’s wife; whoever touches her shall not be innocent.
People do not despise a thief if he steals to satisfy his soul because he is hungry; | People do not despise a thief if he steals to satisfy himself when he is starving.
But if he is found, he must pay... | Yet when he is found, he must repay...

<column-break/>

<margin>In foolishness</margin>
<margin>From the backsliding</margin>

**Sowing discord** — This refers to one who causes quarrels and fights between brothers. <note>original: *mariya*</note>. If he is forgiven, he might still burn like a ladder <note>meaning a rising flame</note> in their midst. **Therefore his calamity shall come suddenly** — Destruction comes upon him instantly and clearly, in quick succession without prior warning. Because he sought a "calamity of the nose" <note>an idiom for anger or sudden trouble</note> for the sake of strife and badness for other creatures, calamity will come to him suddenly. For the nature of those who cause harm is that their own harm is brought back upon them by the Sages and by their own evil deeds.

**These six... and seven are an abomination to His soul** — This refers to those with a physical-material nature. **These six**: Since this matter involves the nature of all transgressions, the author mentions commandments to counter the evil. Just as one who lacks moisture <note>humility/spirit</note> is scorched above, he was lacking comfort before God. After the "six things," the commandments begin so that he might repent from his corrupt thoughts. **And seven**: This means the seventh item, which is "sowing discord," is the one the soul of God truly detests. Is it not written for his children that an abomination is called by seven names?

**Haughty eyes** — The text stops here to explain that these six are common. One should not join with the sower of discord, for he will be an abomination to His soul—meaning the Will of the Blessed One. The shame would be hidden or removed because they return to the "Deeds of Jacob," referencing the level of "his fellow" mentioned above.

**A lying tongue** — One who speaks falsehoods. **Hands that shed innocent blood** — This does not only mean literal murder, but also one who shames his fellow in public, or one who denies the orphan their rights, or one who steals—all these are like "shedding blood" in the eyes of the world. Even one who is stingy <note>original: *kanah*</note> is like a murderer.

**A heart that devises wicked plans** — This is the root of evil. One of the Sages said that the heart is the source of all intentions, whether for the Law or for corruption. A bad heart allows the corrupt and sweet-to-the-evil to take hold. **The signs of these are**: haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed blood... Rabbi Hanina says that anyone who possesses these is kept away from the path of wisdom, for it is impossible to stand in this place of wisdom while following such ways.

**Feet that are swift to run to evil** — This refers to those who move between brothers to cause strife, and the Sages explain this with a blessing, for the opposite is the "quality of goodness" which brings peace.

**Keep, my son, your father’s commandment** — I have explained the passing lusts that drive one away from wisdom. Now we begin with the Torah and the degrees of the Sages' wisdom. One who does not follow these paths will be consumed. Guard the commandments of your "father" and do not forsake the instruction of your "mother." Some say these are actual parents, but others say "father" refers to God and "mother" to the Assembly of Israel or the Torah itself.

**Bind them upon your heart continually** — So that they never depart from his heart. Like a necklace, **tie them around your throat** — The Sages hinted that the heart should write the concepts and the tongue should repeat them, such as in the recitation of the *Shema* and prayer.

**When you walk, she shall lead you** — Even when you are preoccupied, wisdom will guide you until you walk in glory. When you lie down, she will guard you. When you wake, she will speak with you—meaning her language and grammar will become fluent in your mouth, more so than if you merely spent time talking with other wise people.

**For the commandment is a lamp** — This provides the reason why those who pursue wisdom are guided. A commandment is like a candle that lights the way in the darkness of this world, and the Torah is the light of the sun. The "reproofs of instruction" are the way to life—meaning they provide a physical and spiritual advantage in the world.

**To keep you from the evil woman** — All these warnings are to separate one from evil. Some explain "evil woman" as a bad character trait, while others see it as a warning against the physical "foreign woman" (adultery). The Halakhic sages <note>legal scholars</note> suggest this refers to the "smooth tongue" of heresy which draws one away from the path.

**Do not lust after her beauty** — The Torah will help you so that you do not desire her beauty in your heart, nor be captured by her eyelids. Even if she appears beautiful, her wisdom is empty.

**For by means of a harlot** — "By means of" means "because of." One who follows a harlot will eventually be reduced to begging for a "loaf of bread." He will lose his wealth. **An adulteress hunts for a precious soul** — This means she doesn't just take his money, but she destroys his life in the World to Come.

**Can a man take fire...** — Just as it is the nature of fire to burn, so it is the nature of adultery to destroy. One cannot touch fire without being burned. **So is he who goes in to his neighbor’s wife** — He will not go unpunished. His soul will be damaged by the very nature of the sin.

**People do not despise a thief** — This is a comparison. A thief who steals because he is hungry might be pitied or understood, but his crime is still a crime. How much more so the adulterer, who "steals" a wife not out of hunger, but out of corrupt desire. The thief **must repay sevenfold** — he pays with money. But the adulterer pays with his very soul.

<column-break/> | O you simple, understand wisdom: and, you fools, be of an understanding heart.

***

### Commentary Section

**Let us go** — Let us hear and be satiated with great love, and let us rejoice in our spirits... <note>The commentator interprets "love" here as a metaphor for intellectual or spiritual pursuit, though in the literal sense, it is the temptress speaking.</note> **Until the morning** — This refers to the hidden light of the wise. **The man is not at home** — You need not fear the "Master of the House" <note>The Intellect or the Creator</note>, for He is far away. **A bag of money** — This suggests that the "husband" has taken his resources and will not return until a fixed, distant time. **The full moon** <note>original: *keseh*</note> — This refers to a set festival or a time of gathering.

**She caused him to yield** — She drew him in with the "smoothness of her lips." This means she opened a path to turn him away from the good way. The "smoothness" refers to the seductive nature of physical desires which distract the person from the straight path through various transgressions.

**He goes... after her** — Any simpleton who cannot distinguish between good and evil follows the transgression without considering the evil prepared for him. He is like an ox going to the slaughter, or like a fool in leg-irons <note>original: *akhos*, likely a reference to a bangle or chain</note>. The simple do not understand that these paths lead away from the wisdom of the sages.

**Until a dart strikes** — This describes how the movement of desire captures him. He is compared to a bird rushing into a trap, not realizing that all these pleasures are actually the "medicine of death."

**And now, children** — The author now addresses the students, warning them against these evils. After mentioning the ruin that follows sin, he tells them to listen to his mouth and choose the words of wisdom. **Let not your heart turn** — Do not let your mind pursue the ways of the "strange woman" <note>Physicality/Folly</note>. The Sages have warned that one should keep a great distance from her.

**For many are the slain** — The desire for physical pleasure has caused many to fall. Even "mighty ones" — those strong in spirit — have been overcome by it. **Her house is the way to the grave <note>Sheol</note>** — Know that the paths leading to her house lead directly to destruction.

**Chapter 8** — The author now mentions Wisdom's call. While Folly hides in the dark corners, Wisdom is public. **She stands on the heights** — Wisdom is found in prominent places, meaning it is accessible to all who seek it. **Beside the gates** — In the place of judgment and the city center.

**To you, O men, I call** — The commentator <insert>R. Mordechai</insert> notes four classes of people Wisdom addresses:
1. **Men** <note>original: *ishim*</note> — The unique individuals, the elite who seek true knowledge and good deeds.
2. **Sons of man** <note>original: *bnei adam*</note> — Those engaged in the rational world, who work but are also capable of spiritual growth.
3. **Simple ones** <note>original: *peta'im*</note> — Those who are currently empty of wisdom but possess good traits; they are told to "understand cunning" (resourcefulness).
4. **Fools** <note>original: *kesilim*</note> — Those who currently follow folly; they are urged to "understand in their hearts" and turn away from their foolishness.

**Aramaic Translation (Targum)** | **Hebrew Source Text**

The Lord created me <note>The Aramaic *barani* specifically uses the word for "creation," whereas the Hebrew *qanani* is more ambiguous, often meaning "acquired" or "possessed."</note> at the beginning of His creation, and before His works from the beginning. | <margin> 6 <br/> 7 <br/> 8 <br/> In His decree </margin> The Lord possessed me at the beginning of His way, before His works of old.
From before the world I was established, from the start, before the earth existed. | I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, from the earliest times of the earth.
When there were no depths I was born, and when there were no springs of the fountains of water. | When there were no depths, I was brought forth; when there were no fountains abounding with water.
And before the mountains were sunk, and before the hills, I was conceived. | Before the mountains were settled, before the hills was I brought forth.
Until He had not yet made the earth and the rivers, and the beginning of the dust of the world. | While as yet He had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the beginning of the dust of the world.
When He established the heavens, I was there; and when He drew a circle upon the face of the deep. | When He prepared the heavens, I was there; when He set a circle upon the face of the deep.
And when He made firm the clouds of the heights, and when He strengthened the fountains of the deep. | When He established the skies above; when the fountains of the deep showed their might.
And when He set for the sea its boundary, so that the waters should not pass over His command, and in the establishing of the foundations of the earth. | When He gave to the sea His decree, that the waters should not transgress His commandment; when He appointed the foundations of the earth.
And I was beside Him, faithful; and I was His delight day by day, and I rejoiced before Him at all times. | Then I was beside Him, as a nursling <note>Hebrew: *amon*. This can mean a master craftsman, a ward, or someone faithful/hidden.</note>; and I was daily His delight, playing before Him at all times.
I was rejoicing in the world of His earth, and my delights were with the children of men. | Playing in His habitable world, and my delights were with the sons of men.
And now, children, listen to me; and happy are they who keep my ways. | Now therefore, O children, listen to me; for happy are they that keep my ways.
Hear instruction and be wise, and do not refuse. | Hear instruction, and be wise, and refuse it not.
Happy is the man who listens to me, to watch at my thresholds every single day, and to guard the posts of my gates. | Happy is the man that hears me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.
Because he who finds me finds life, and he shall bring forth favor from before God. | For whoever finds me finds life, and obtains favor from the Lord.
But he who sins against me harms his own soul; and all who hate me love death. | But he that misses me wrongs his own soul; all they that hate me love death.
Wisdom has built her house. | Wisdom has built her house.

<column-break/>

---

**“The Lord possessed me at the beginning of His way”** • After concluding the description of the excellence of Wisdom in terms of its essence and the actions that follow from it, the author wanted to make known its fixed nature from the perspective of the Creator who sends it forth and its priority over all existing things. Specifically, Solomon makes this known in two ways: by dividing the law of Wisdom and its essences, giving it four aspects of priority: priority of time, priority of excellence, priority of nature, and priority of cause. 

From within this, he makes known the path, dividing it into three general parts: the path of the celestial world <note>The world of the spheres or orbits</note>, the path of the world of stars and skies, and the path of the world of the angels. He makes known that in all these thoughts, Wisdom was the primary thought for them all, and she is the eternal Queen over every vessel used by God to create His world. 

Regarding the priority of the world’s spheres, he says: *“Before the mountains were settled, and before the hills, I was brought forth.”* He teaches that the law of Wisdom was prepared even for the lower regions. Regarding the creation of the world of nature, centered in the heavens: *“When He prepared the heavens, I was there.”* This refers to the actions of this world and its preservation from destruction. Regarding the separate intellects <note>Angels or pure spirits</note>: *“When He established the skies above,”* referring to the angelic world.

And he bequeaths and says: **“The Lord possessed me,”** meaning He created me <note>The commentator here reconciles the Hebrew "possessed" with the Aramaic "created."</note> at the start of the emergence of the "Way" and the excellence of the Merciful One's thought. I was a memory... **“From then” (Ma-az):** This implies that in every generation and time, even before time itself existed—since time is a consequence of motion, and before the creation of the heavens and earth, there was no time—Wisdom preceded even the concept of temporal order.

**“I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning”** • He wants to inform us that Wisdom has an enduring excellence, being higher in degree than all these things. Before the movement of the heavens and the earth, she was there in excellence... **“From the earliest times of the earth”:** I already existed in power and time even more than the foundations of the centers of the world's activity. 

**“When there were no depths”** • He wishes to show that Wisdom precedes nature. She is the essence that includes the four elements. Regarding the element of Water, he says *“when there were no depths,”* and regarding the *“fountains abounding with water,”* meaning the heavenly waters meant to water the earth. **“Before the mountains were settled”** refers to the development of the dry land. 

**“When He prepared the heavens, I was there”** • He wants to show that Wisdom has a fixed existence within the very centers and structures of the heavens. They were made through Wisdom... **“When He set a circle,”** referring to the weight of the world and its proportions. **“When He established the skies,”** referring to the measurement of the space between the heavens and the world of the angels. 

**“When He gave to the sea His decree”** • After mentioning that in the thoughts of Wisdom, the heavens were spread out, she answers that in her thought also stands the preservation of all creatures after their creation. Without this, matter would not have attained its purpose. This is the meaning of *“the waters should not transgress His commandment,”* referring to the boundaries of matter. By the merit of the Lord, Wisdom dwells there as a stronghold... 

**“Then I was beside Him, as a nursling [Amon]”** • Here he hides a deep metaphor. Before all generations existed, Wisdom was with Him. Just as a craftsman holds a plan in his hand to build and create, so Wisdom was with Him, may He be blessed, as the conceptual blueprint for all created things... **“And I was daily His delight”** • My true delight was being held before Him... rejoicing in the attainment of His essence. This "playing" or "rejoicing" refers to intellectual contemplation. 

**“Now therefore, O children, listen to me”** • Having established all these foundations, he says: receive from me the ways of my Wisdom and you will be happy, for this is the ultimate perfection sought by man. **“Hear instruction and be wise”** • He speaks of the character traits known as "Instruction" (Musar) and "Contemplation." Therefore, it is proper to receive these from me... **“Happy is the man”** who adds to his excellence... **“to watch at my doors”** and cling to them. **“For whoever finds me finds life”** — not just physical life, but spiritual life. **“And obtains favor from the Lord”** — he becomes beloved before the Creator. **“But he who sins against me harms his own soul”** — the sinner pursues vanity and distances himself from the holy source. The purpose of this section is to speak loftily of the excellence of Wisdom, which precedes all created things.

**Aramaic Translation (Targum)** | **Hebrew Source Text**
:--- | :---
Blessings of life are upon the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked hides the possessions of the robber. <note>original: "nechasei chatofa" - the Aramaic translates "violence" as "the gains of a thief."</note> | Blessings are for the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked covers violence.
The memory of the righteous is for a blessing, but the name of the wicked shall be cut off. <note>original: "yitganned" - meaning to be cast out or faded.</note> | The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked shall rot.
The wise in heart will receive commandments, but he whose lips are foolish will be entangled. | The wise of heart will take commandments, but a babbling fool <note>Literally: "a fool of lips."</note> will fall.
He who walks in simplicity walks in support, but he who perverts his ways will be held guilty. | He who walks in integrity walks securely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.
He who winks with his eyes gives pain, and he who is perverse in his lips will be entangled. | He who winks the eye causes grief, but a babbling fool will fall.
A fountain of life is the mouth of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked hides the possessions of the robber. | A fountain of life is the mouth of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked covers violence.
Hatred stirs up strife, but over all sins, love covers with mercy. | Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all transgressions.
On the lips of the discerning, wisdom is found, and a rod <note>term: rod (shevet) - used here as a metaphor for discipline or consequence.</note> is for him who lacks understanding. | On the lips of the discerning, wisdom is found, but a rod is for the back of him who lacks heart.
The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of a fool is a near destruction. | Wise men store up knowledge, but the mouth of the foolish is near ruin.
The property of the rich is his strong city; the end of the poor is their need. | The rich man's wealth is his strong city; the ruin of the poor is their poverty.
The deeds of the righteous lead to eternal life; the deeds of the wicked lead to sin. | The labor of the righteous leads to life; the increase of the wicked to sin.
<column-break/>
The path of life is keeping discipline, and he who leaves behind rebuke is led astray. | <margin>Keep</margin> The path to life is he who heeds instruction, but he who forsakes reproof goes astray.
The master of enmity has lying lips, and he who brings out an evil report is a fool. | He who hides hatred has lying lips, and he who utters slander is a fool.
In a multitude of words, sin does not cease, but he who restrains his lips is discerning. | <margin>And restrains</margin> In the multitude of words, transgression is not lacking, but he who restrains his lips is wise.
Choice silver is the tongue of the righteous; the heart of the wicked is of little value. | Choice silver is the tongue of the righteous; the heart of the wicked is worth little.
The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for lack of understanding. | The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for want of heart.
The blessing of God makes one rich, and He adds no sorrow with it. | The blessing of the Lord makes rich, and He adds no toil with it.
As a fool laughs while doing a deed <note>referring to a wicked scheme</note>, so is wisdom to a man of understanding. | As sport to a fool is the doing of wickedness, so is wisdom to a man of understanding.
The fear of the wicked shall come upon him, and the desire of the righteous shall be given to him. | What the wicked fears shall come upon him, but the desire of the righteous shall be granted.
As the whirlwind passes, so the wicked is gone, but the righteous is the foundation of the world. | When the whirlwind passes, the wicked is no more, but the righteous is an everlasting foundation.
As vinegar to the teeth and as smoke to the eyes, so is the lazy messenger to those who send him. | As vinegar to the teeth and as smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to those who send him.

---

**Blessings for the head of the righteous.** Everyone blesses the righteous because of his good actions. The text attributes the blessings to his **head** because the head contains the intellectual faculties <note>The commentator is referencing the medieval belief that the various powers of the soul—memory, imagination, and reason—reside in specific chambers of the brain.</note> which distinguish him from the lowly and the wicked. 

**And the mouth of the wicked covers violence.** Any word they utter that causes harm is considered "violence" weighed in their mouths; even if they try to speak a blessing, their inherent violence reveals itself. **The memory of the righteous is a blessing.** His memory is cherished day by day, for people remember him for good and for blessing during his life and after his death. **But the name of the wicked shall rot.** Meaning their memory will be immediately obliterated, and no trace of them will remain; even if they are remembered, it will not be pleasant to the soul. 

**The wise of heart will take commandments.** He will accept the decrees of the law and rejoice in them. A person who is truly "wise of heart" accepts the commandments whether they come from a friend or from God, whether he can do them with ease or whether they require great effort of body and strength. He feels a duty to perform them because his heart recognizes the inherent value of the "mint of wisdom." <note>term: mint of wisdom (matbe'a ha-chochmah) - a metaphor for the established standard or "currency" of intellectual and moral truth.</note>

**But a babbling fool.** This refers to one who does not perform the duties incumbent upon him nor the actions required by the laws of wisdom. This fool harms others with his speech and advises them to turn away from righteousness toward sin. The fruit of his mouth is a terror that strengthens evil positions. **He who winks the eye.** He directs his gaze toward evil ends, yet he brings anxiety and trembling upon himself because he will be punished for it. 

**A fountain of life is the mouth of the righteous.** Just as a spring has water that benefits everyone, so too the words of the righteous man's mouth provide life to the world through the words of Torah and the commandments. **But the mouth of the wicked.** His speech is harmful; it covers his violent intent like a garment. 

**Hatred stirs up strife.** Hatred causes a person to dig and search into the heart of his neighbor to find faults and sins. **But love covers all transgressions.** Conversely, love causes the pious to ignore the faults of their fellows, so that a small dispute does not escalate into a great quarrel. 

**On the lips of the discerning.** Because he speaks with understanding and with the purity of his refined thoughts, others accept his words. **A rod is for the back of him who lacks heart.** Wisdom is for the discerning, but the "rod" of discipline is for the one who refuses to learn. The wise man stores up his thoughts and only lets wisdom leave his mouth when it is useful. The fool, however, speaks of ruin and destruction; his words are always close to causing a disaster. 

**The wealth of the rich.** This passage compares the rich and the poor, and the virtues of wealth versus the trials of poverty. **The labor of the righteous leads to life.** This means that the actions of the righteous man result in merit and life, whereas the "harvest" of the wicked results only in sin and punishment. The righteous man acts to give life and happiness to himself and to others, benefiting discerning souls. The wicked man's "increase" is the destruction of his own soul.

**In the multitude of words.** It is often the case that much speaking leads to sin and harm. The holy Sages of old <note>original: "Chazal" - an acronym for the Rabbinic Sages of the Mishnah and Talmud.</note> taught that he who restrains his lips is wise. **Choice silver is the tongue of the righteous.** His words are like silver that has been refined and purified. **The heart of the wicked is worth little.** It has no value because it lacks good thoughts. 

**The blessing of the Lord makes rich.** Success does not come from hard labor alone, but from the blessing that rests upon a person's work. **As sport to a fool.** A fool finds pleasure in doing "wickedness" <note>original: "zimmah" - often referring to calculated or lewd evil.</note>, just as a wise man finds pleasure in wisdom. The fool laughs at the very moment he is doing wrong, but wisdom corrects the wise man's path. 

**As vinegar to the teeth.** This is a parable. Just as vinegar sets the teeth on edge and smoke causes the eyes to tear, so a lazy messenger causes frustration and pain to those who sent him. He delays his mission, and his laziness causes damage and loss to the business of his master.

<meta>catchword: as the way <note>Hebrew: "ka-orchah"</note></meta>

### Commentary

**The fear of the Lord adds [days]**: This refers to the reward for commandments which counters the shortening of life. The author explains that "the fear of the Lord adds days" beyond what is naturally decreed for a person based on their physical constitution. Conversely, the sins of the wicked shorten their lives because their habits and lack of guidance weaken the body’s natural strength.

**The hope of the righteous**: When the righteous wait for what the Holy One, blessed be He, has promised them, their very waiting is filled with joy. But the hope of the wicked is a lost cause; it will not stand because it is built on vanity.

**The way of the Lord is a stronghold**: This "way" refers to the path of integrity. For the upright, following God's path acts as a natural shield, protecting them from the pitfalls of life. However, for those who work iniquity, this same "way" becomes a source of terror and destruction. Their own actions act as a stumbling block.

**The righteous shall never be moved**: This is a promise of stability. A person who acts with virtue builds a "covenant" with reality that keeps them grounded. Even if they face temporary setbacks, they will not be "moved" in an eternal sense. The wicked, however, are like chaff; they have no deep roots in the "land" of existence and will eventually be cast out.

**The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom**: Just as a tree naturally produces fruit, the mouth of the righteous person naturally "buds" or produces wisdom. Their internal character is a source of understanding. The "perverse tongue," however, is like a diseased branch that must be cut off from the world to prevent the spread of its poison.

**A false balance**: This section moves into social ethics. Honest weights in trade are not just a legal requirement but "His delight" <note>original: "retzono"</note>. This suggests that God's will is manifest in the fairness of human interactions. Deception in business is an "abomination" because it destroys the social fabric.

**When pride comes**: The commentator notes that pride and shame are inextricably linked. The proud person is always at risk of being humbled, whereas the "humble" <note>term: "tznuim" - literally the 'modest' or 'hidden' ones</note> possess wisdom because they are not blinded by their own ego.

**The integrity of the upright**: Integrity acts as a guide. When a person is "perfect" in their heart, their path is clear. The "treacherous," however, are destroyed by their own "crookedness" <note>original: "selef"</note>. Their lack of a straight moral compass leads them into traps of their own making.

**Wealth does not profit**: On the "day of wrath"—which the commentator interprets as the day of death—money is useless. No amount of gold can bribe the Angel of Death. Only "righteousness" <term>tzedakah - which also means 'charity'</term> has the power to deliver the soul and leave a lasting legacy.

<summary>This page covers Proverbs 10:27 to 11:13, contrasting the life-extending and stable nature of righteousness with the self-destructive and fleeting path of the wicked. The commentary emphasizes that moral living is in harmony with the natural and divine order of the world.</summary>
<keywords>Fear of the Lord, integrity, false scales, pride and humility, wealth vs. righteousness, Gersonides, Targum, Masoretic notes</keywords>

# Proverbs 11

### Proverbs 11:14–31

**Aramaic Translation (Targum)** | **Hebrew Source Text**
:--- | :---
Where there is no leader, the people fall; but deliverance comes through an abundance of the kingdom <note>original: "be-sugai de-malkuta"</note>. | Where there is no guidance, a nation falls; but in the multitude of counselors there is safety.
The wicked man does evil at the time when joy arrives—our joy—and he hates those who pray with signs; he hopes for favor <note>The Aramaic here takes a highly interpretive, almost liturgical turn compared to the Hebrew.</note>. | He who is a guarantor for a stranger will surely suffer, but he who hates pledging <note>literally: "striking hands"</note> is secure.
A modest woman shall gain honor, and powerful men shall be strengthened in wealth. | A gracious woman attains honor, and ruthless men attain wealth.
A pious man rewards his own soul, but a cruel man afflicts his own flesh. | The merciful man does good to his own soul, but he who is cruel troubles his own flesh.
A wicked man does a work of falsehood, but for him who sows righteousness, truth is his reward. | The wicked man earns deceptive wages, but he who sows righteousness has a true reward.
Thus, one who does righteousness [tends] toward life, and one who pursues evil [tends] toward death. | As righteousness leads to life, so he who pursues evil leads to his own death.
God distances those of crooked heart, but He desires those who are blameless in their way. | Those of crooked heart are an abomination to the Lord, but those blameless in their way are His delight.
Hand upon hand, he shall not be cleared of evil, but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered. | Hand to hand, the evil man shall not go unpunished; but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.
Like a gold earring <note>original: "chizma"</note> in the snout of a pig, so is a woman who is beautiful but turns away from good sense. | Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout, so is a beautiful woman without discretion.
The desire of the righteous is for good <note>original: "makta," perhaps a scribal error for "tavta"</note>, but the hope of the wicked is for wrath. | The desire of the righteous is only good, but the hope of the wicked is wrath.
There is one who scatters and increases his merit, and one who spares from uprightness and lacks. | There is one who scatters and yet increases more; and one who withholds more than is right, but it leads to poverty.
A soul of blessing shall be made fat, and he who prays shall also learn. | A generous soul <note>literally: "soul of blessing"</note> will be made rich, and he who waters will also be watered himself.
He who hides grain in a time of famine, his children shall leave him; but blessing is upon the head of him who sells it. | The people curse him who withholds grain, but blessing is on the head of him who sells it.
He who brings forward good seeks favor, but for him who seeks evil, it shall come upon him. | He who earnestly seeks good finds favor, but trouble comes to him who seeks evil.
He who trusts in his wealth shall fall, but the righteous shall flourish like a leaf. | He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous will flourish like a leaf.
He who troubles his own house shall inherit the wind, and the fool shall be a servant to the wise. | He who troubles his own house will inherit the wind, and the fool will be servant to the wise of heart.
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and the wise man receives souls. | The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who wins souls is wise.
If the righteous is rewarded on earth, how much more shall the wicked and the sinner be removed from the earth. | If the righteous is recompensed on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner!

<column-break/>

**Where there is no guidance.** Without counsel and thought, a people will fall, but they will be strong in war against their enemies: **And safety.** It comes to them when they trust in the abundance of the counselors' advice.

**He who is a guarantor.** <note>The commentator explains the Hebrew "Ra Yeroa" (will suffer harm).</note> It will be bad for him... <unclear>OCR noise</unclear> ...even if he brings in servants and others to assist him, he will return to his state of lack. 

**A gracious woman.** She attains honor, such as a pious noblewoman who conducts all her affairs with dignity. The text emphasizes "honor" because her life is entwined with her deeds; she does not occupy herself with vanity, but only with that which brings her honor, through which her husband and household are also honored. In contrast, "ruthless men"—those who are arrogant—do not seek honor but only support their wealth, taking by force that which belongs to the wise.

**Rewards his own soul.** He brings good reward to his soul who keeps himself from transgressions. A "pious man" <note>Hebrew: Chasid</note> is one who has mercy on all creatures and sweetens his kindness toward them. **But he who troubles his own flesh.** This refers to one who feeds himself from sacred things <note>Hekdesh</note> or whose actions are destructive to his own wellbeing.

**The wicked man does.** When the wicked sows, he brings only evil and violence. But the reward of the righteous is certain. Sowing righteousness is like planting a crop that will surely yield a "true reward."

**As righteousness leads to life.** Just as righteousness and the "sowing" of charity in the hearts of the wise brings a strengthening reward, **so he who pursues evil leads to his own death.** This is a warning of mortality and ruin. It can also be understood as referring to life in the World to Come, while the wicked man's pursuit of evil leads to his downfall in this world.

**An abomination to the Lord.** Those who bow to arrogance and follow crooked paths in their hearts... even if they appear pleasant, their actions are rebellious.

**Hand to hand.** Even with a strong hand, or from generation to generation <note>interpreting "hand to hand" as a chain of lineage</note>, the wicked will not be cleared of his sin and cunning. **But the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.** They will be saved from the evil that befalls others.

**A gold ring.** Just as a pig would wear a gold ring in its snout <note>an absurd image</note>, falling into the filth, so is a woman who has physical beauty but lacks "taste" or discretion—meaning the wisdom of aging and the dignity of character. 

**The desire.** All the yearnings and desires of the righteous are for the growth of good, which is precious in the eyes of God. **But the hope of the wicked is wrath.** Their hopes turn into anger and decree.

**There is one who scatters.** There are those who "scatter" their wealth by giving to the poor, yet they find that their wealth actually increases through this act of kindness. **But he who withholds more than is right.** One who is stingy with charity, thinking he is saving, will find his resources diminished and his household in want.

**A generous soul.** One who accepts God's will with a blessing will see his wealth "fattened" or increased. **He who waters will also be watered.** This refers to one who teaches others or provides for them; he will be provided for in turn.

**He who withholds grain.** This refers to a person who hoards produce during a time of high prices <note>price gouging during famine</note>. The "nations" (the public) will curse him. But "blessing is on the head of him who sells it"—the one who provides for the needs of the community in their time of distress.

**He who earnestly seeks good.** He seeks the will of God and the benefit of others. **But he who trusts in his riches.** He who trusts only in his wealth will see his heart fall and his strength wither. **But the righteous will flourish like a leaf.** Like a fresh, green leaf that stays moist and connected to the tree, the righteous remain vibrant through their connection to the Divine.

**He who troubles his own house.** One who is miserly or brings strife to his family will inherit only "wind" (nothingness). In the end, the fool will find himself a servant to the wise.

**The fruit of the righteous.** The results of a righteous person's life are like the Tree of Life, providing sustenance to others. **And he who wins souls is wise.** This refers to a teacher who gathers students and teaches them knowledge and the way of understanding.

**If the righteous is recompensed.** If even the righteous person receives his "payment" (punishment for minor errors) on earth, how much more certain is the judgment for the wicked and the sinner! They will be consumed by the troubles they prepared for others.

# Proverbs 12

### Proverbs 12:4–21

**Aramaic Translation (Targum)** | **Hebrew Source Text**
:--- | :---
A virtuous woman <note>original: "eshta kshirta"</note> is a crown to her husband, but a wicked woman is like rot in the bones. | A woman of valor <term>Eshet Chayil: a term for a woman of strength, character, and capability</term> is her husband's crown, but one who brings shame is like rot in his bones.
The thoughts of the righteous are justice and sovereignty <note>Aramaic: "malchuta"</note>; the thoughts of the wicked are like the deceit of the wicked ones. | The thoughts of the righteous are justice; the schemes of the wicked are deceit.
The fruit of the wicked lies in wait for blood, but the mouth of the upright saves them. | The words of the wicked are a blood-ambush, but the mouth of the upright delivers them.
The wicked are overturned and not found, but the house of the righteous shall stand. | Overthrow the wicked and they are no more, but the house of the righteous stands.
A man is praised according to the body of his wisdom, and he who lacks knowledge shall be for foolishness. | A man is praised according to his wisdom, but a warped heart is held in contempt.
Better is he who is lowly and serves himself than he who honors himself and lacks bread. | Better to be lightly esteemed and have a servant <note>or "be a servant to oneself"</note> than to honor oneself and lack bread.
The righteous man knows the soul of his beast, but the mercies of the wicked are cruelty. | A righteous man knows the soul of his beast, but the mercies of the wicked are cruel.
He who works the land shall be sated with bread, but he who pursues vanities lacks reason. | He who tills his land will be sated with bread, but he who pursues vanities lacks heart.
The wicked man desires the evil net, but the root of the righteous shall be established. | The wicked man desires the net of evil ones, but the root of the righteous yields.
In the sin of the lips is an evil snare, but the righteous escapes from trouble. | By the transgression of the lips is an evil snare, but the righteous escapes from trouble.
From the fruit of a man's mouth he is sated with good, and every man is repaid according to the work of his hands. | From the fruit of a man's mouth he is sated with good, and the reward of a man's hands returns to him.
The way of a fool is right in his eyes, but he who listens to counsel is wise. | The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but he who listens to counsel is wise.
The fool makes his anger known on his [first] day, but the shrewd man covers his shame. | A fool's anger is known on the day, but a shrewd man conceals a disgrace.
He who witnesses faithfully speaks righteousness, and a false witness is deceit. | He who breathes truth tells righteousness, but a false witness [tells] deceit.
There are those who speak with "shining" lips <note>Aramaic: "safwata d-shin," likely a corruption or variant meaning sharp speech</note>, and the tongue of the wise is healing. | There is one who speaks like the piercings of a sword, but the tongue of the wise is healing.
The lip of truth is established forever, but the tongue of falsehood is hurried. | The lip of truth is established forever, but a lying tongue is but for a moment.
Deceit is in the heart of those who think evil, but for those who counsel peace, there is joy. | Deceit is in the heart of those who plot evil, but for counselors of peace there is joy.
It is not good for the righteous to have any trouble, but the wicked are full of evil. | No harm shall happen to the righteous, but the wicked are full of evil.

<column-break/>

---

-> **His Interpretations** <-

---

**A woman of valor.** Valor <note>Hebrew: Chayil</note>. Like "and you shall have wealth/valor." A woman of valor is mighty and intelligent; she is a crown to her husband because he is praised through her in all his deeds and commandments, and she publicizes the conduct of the home as a straight and beneficial order. **But like rot in his bones.** Anyone who consumes his actions with foreign breaths and sacrifices for her honor is compared to rot that festers and makes the bones moldy; the marrow will slowly perish. This rot is a dangerous sickness, for in its confidence it strikes him with a cold rot that troubles the wise man to combine sickness and lack in all his deeds. **She who brings shame.** A plot of nullification by removing the enticer.

**The thoughts of the righteous.** The substance [of the matter] is that the thoughts of the righteous are to perform justice and to sustain the state, whereas the wicked will not be sufficient; they will ruin everything and love evil thoughts, <unclear>chaluach</unclear> under schemes all their days to deceive others.

**The words of the wicked.** He expanded on the qualities of the wicked and their actions; the substance of the words of the wicked and their preparation is to ambush and destroy, while the pious ones, with your mouth, will save them from destruction. Do not tell the words of the wicked, for false testimony shall not stand against the righteous, such as those who took money for slandering <note>literally: "walking as a talebearer"</note>, and their mouth will save them from the hand of those who hear false witnesses and find favor.

**The overturning of the wicked and they are no more.** They and their schemes, and at the end their words and their wickedness are sudden. **Overthrow the wicked.** He shall have mercy here on the wicked and overturn them by the name he gave them, giving him strength and mercy... <note>The text here becomes dense with abbreviations and interpretive metaphors</note> ...for the intellect calculates the good for the peace of the house. The wicked one <unclear>chaffs</unclear> all good and speaks a level path of honor and knowledge... it is fitting for him to have rest... and in all this to endure the lament and to be humbled by you and to join the kingdom from the wicked... by his merit and his lament and his knowledge.

**Better to be lightly esteemed.** Like "our hearts are faint." It is better for a person to be humble in his house and acquire everything, wallowing in every purpose of strengthening himself for fatness <note>meaning prosperity</note>, being a servant to himself so that his house is made pious and praised in the eyes of his sickness <note>perhaps meaning his humble state</note>. The wicked one pays with the reward of the kingdom, preparing his honor while he <unclear>chimmar</unclear> lacks bread... And the word "lightly esteemed" <note>Hebrew: nikleh</note> corresponds to "lightness of shame" <note>Hebrew: kalon</note>.

**The righteous knows the soul of his beast.** To rule with the power of his knowledge; he has mercy and pities his own mercies... and likewise for the wise ones... pities his beast and is meticulous in doing good. The substance is that the righteous knows... to give him the knowledge of the "paths" to support the gift and the protection of the wise... the mercies of the wicked are a desecration in the place of mercy... their mercies and their fondness are pities, and they pity the creatures... to pity the wicked and not to kill for his merit as a kindness.

**He who works his land shall be sated with bread.** For he performs labor that is desolate in its qualities. **And he who pursues vanities.** The meaning is a lack of progress by walking with vain things, following the habit of freedom and the evils of man; their thinking is all foolishness and lack of sense. And in the way of the "Crown," anyone who passes through the states... losses that were spoken of in writing... a donkey-like lack of inner naming. **Lacking heart** means he lacks the vessel for the preparation of cleansing the snare of the wicked and their schemes.

**The wicked man desires.** Desires. <unclear>Chas posh</unclear> strong and the matter of wrath. The substance is that the wicked desires the "net" of the wicked for the good of <unclear>latir</unclear> the life of the righteous and covers them. **But the root of the righteous yields.** Meaning, he has mercies... the essence of their money and their strength and of kindness, they are the ones who educate and give life.

**In the sin of the lips.** By the sin of the lips, he increases the honor of the sin and the push of the speech that hides; the sickness of speech that covers with sweetness. And words of abundance open the fruit... **And he shall sprout.** The substance is that my deceit is lacking... the wall of virtues and qualities, whether in speech or in the actions of the hands of the exalted ones, and his words shall be as a strength of goodness. He will exit from the ambush of the heart and the evil of life... also in the reward of the Torah... and also in their actions... he settles his reward for him according to what he is... your hands, etc.

**The way of a fool.** Because of the fool's great folly, he will not examine his affairs at all and will not look at his path... as happens in the life of the wise. The wise man, behold, he listens to counsel... he will not be prevented in the matter, he will tremble in his thoughts and will not look... to nourish the kindness as a species of what will be in the life of the wise, behold he hears counsel that sometimes leads to the straight path.

**A fool's [anger] on the day.** He means the fool on the day of his sinning, who despises drawing near, and his lack of anger will be seen by others, and by this he adds to his shame. The wise man of discipline covers his shame and does not hasten to quarrel, for what benefit is there in his disgrace... to publicize it in a large congregation?

**He who breathes truth.** "Breathes" means he mentions. Anyone who is meticulous in his choice and believes... can testify to lies? For one accustomed to speaking lies establishes the opening of the mouth. **Distances of malice and piercing.** The matters of the response of the sword in the body... a man is meticulous in his words to <unclear>militov</unclear>... in his discipline... like the piercings of a sword because he will cause destruction through his testimony. **The tongue of the wise is healing.** The speech of the testimony... and can... the strengthening of those who die. Or it means he is confident in words... like the piercings of a sword, meaning he pierced him because of his <unclear>chavon dachyu</unclear> since he healed his fellow. If he testified falsely against him, the tongue of the wise will not cause evil to the speaker but will establish for him healing and rest.

**The lip of truth shall be established.** The word "moment" <note>Hebrew: rega</note> means a surplus of speech. The speech of truth will be joined and will exist forever, but the lying tongue can only exist for a moment and the lie has no legs <note>a common Hebrew idiom: "a lie has no legs to stand on"</note>. And it is possible that he means "rest" <note>Hebrew: hargi'ah</note> to establish their words; they will take time... but the masters of lies will not look for a long time... the thing is recognizable, its nature is short-lived and its proof is quick.

**Deceit is in the heart of those who plot [evil].** Plotters <note>Hebrew: chorshei</note>. There are counselors whose wisdom is deceit... they plan this counsel in a way of deceit for their existence, and sometimes evil happens to them... the counselors of peace, the children of deceit will always experience less than the good. It is possible he means that in the heart of those who plot, there is a substance of evil... the matter of deceit... and counselors to others... the counselors of peace will have a second matter... mixed with deceit and the hidden.

**No harm shall happen.** <unclear>Yechuneh</unclear>. Because of the action of the will... they will look to him that the righteous will know the joy of their life... all their actions will die in kindness. **And the wicked are full of evil.** Their words and their actions, for they will always experience the children of iniquity... and the punishment and reward will be clarified... they will not look at these things according to the knowledge... he will be pleased by them. No, to him... and his mouth will contain it from him, and the wicked will be evil in their wickedness.

# Proverbs

### Proverbs 12:22 – 13:14

**Aramaic Translation (Targum)** | **Hebrew Source Text**

Lying lips are distanced <note>original: "merachakateih," literally "distanced" or "removed," where the Hebrew uses "abomination"</note> from the Lord, but those who perform faithfulness find favor with Him. | Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, but those who act faithfully are His delight.
A clever man hides his knowledge, but the heart of fools proclaims folly. | A prudent man conceals knowledge, but the heart of fools shouts folly.

<note>Rabbinic Commentary (Rashi)</note>

**An abomination of the Lord.** Why is the occupation of wisdom placed next to the name of the Lord? Because it is the way of every wise person for their face to be closed and restrained in their house; all their occupation with wisdom is in the fear of Heaven in secret. Therefore, next to this it says "those who act faithfully are His delight." **A prudent man conceals knowledge.** A wise man who conducts business in a place of <unclear>bet</unclear>—meaning, he is bashful and modest, his face is closed and he is beautifully modest. The prudent wise man conceals his knowledge, and his writing is as if lacking in the collection of distant books until the time for his words to come. **But the heart of fools proclaims folly.** He is hurried and impulsive, telling things quickly and openly, etc. **The hand of the diligent shall rule.** Those wise ones who are diligent in seeking wealth especially, etc. "And the deceitful shall be for tribute," etc. **Anxiety in a man's heart bows him down.** It shall worry in his heart, etc. **The righteous is more than his neighbor.** The righteous man exceeds in his surplus, etc. **The deceitful does not roast his prey.** A hunter who hunts an animal with deceit, etc. **In the path of righteousness is life.** etc. **A wise son, the discipline of a father.** etc. **From the fruit of a man's mouth he eats good.** etc. **He who guards his mouth preserves his soul.** etc.

<note>This column break marks the end of the Hebrew verse section and the transition to further rabbinic commentary at the bottom of the page.</note>

<note>Rabbinic Commentary (Ibn Ezra / Ralbag)</note>

**And deceit.** This is because of my important sins. To me, from our hopes, the heat... it will not be enough for you to wander through it, and kindness and they died still and refuge, etc. Deceit is like fat... **More.** A dream of those who act. He will exceed in the dream the deed of his evil and his wisdom, etc. And what they find difficult in taking the matter until they exchange it for the custom of knowledge. # Proverbs

->Page 155<-

**Aramaic Translation (Targum)** | **Hebrew Source Text**
:--- | :---
By goodness and truth, sin is atoned; and by the fear of God, one turns away from evil. | By mercy and truth, iniquity is atoned for; and by the fear of the Lord, men depart from evil.
When God is pleased with the ways of a man, He even brings his enemies to peace with him. | When a man’s ways please the Lord, He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him.
Better is a little for every righteous person than the great abundance of the wicked acquired without justice. | Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues without right.
The heart of a human thinks of his way, but God prepares his path. | A man’s heart plans his way, but the Lord directs his steps.
Divination <note>original: "kosma," referring to a divine-like oracle or insight</note> is on the lips of the king; in judgment, his mouth shall not stumble. | A divine sentence is on the lips of the king; his mouth transgresses not in judgment.
Scales and weights of favor <note>original: "tar'uta," meaning will or pleasure</note> are before God; His works are the pure weights in the bag. | A just weight and balance are the Lord’s; all the weights of the bag are His work.
It is an abomination for kings to commit wickedness, for the throne is established by righteousness. | It is an abomination to kings to commit wickedness, for the throne is established by righteousness.

<column-break/>

**Aramaic Translation (Targum)** | **Hebrew Source Text**
:--- | :---
Brightness of the eyes gladdens the heart, and the best of the best makes the bones healthy. | The light of the eyes rejoices the heart, and a good report makes the bones fat.
The ear that hears the rebuke of life will dwell among the wise. | The ear that hears the reproof of life abides among the wise.
He who lets go of discipline neglects his soul, and he who listens to life-giving rebuke acquires wisdom. | He that refuses instruction despises his own soul, but he that hears reproof gets understanding.
The fear of the Lord is the discipline of wisdom, and before honor is humility. | The fear of the Lord is the instruction of wisdom, and before honor is humility.
Of the human are the arrangements of the heart, and from before the Lord is the speech of the tongue. | To man belong the preparations of the heart, but from the Lord is the answer of the tongue.
All the ways of a man are pure in his own face <note>meaning "in his own sight"</note>, but God prepares the spirits. | All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes, but the Lord weighs the spirits.
Reveal your works to God, and your thoughts will be established. | Commit your works unto the Lord, and your thoughts shall be established.
The Lord created everything to be heard, even the wicked for the evil day. | The Lord has made all things for His purpose; even the wicked for the day of evil.
A distance from God is every one with a high heart; from evil he will not be cleared. | Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to the Lord; though hand join in hand, he shall not be unpunished.

***

**The Lord is far from the wicked:** This means that the Blessed One is "far" from the wicked, not that He physically distances Himself from them or those who seek Him. Rather, it means that they distance themselves from Him through their evil actions, which are the path of distancing. They have directed themselves toward evil and prepared themselves to be far from the actions of the intellect <note>This commentary uses medieval philosophical language, suggesting that sin is a failure of the rational mind</note>. He is then "far" in the sense that when they call, He does not answer because He is "at a distance." Accordingly, this distance is the absence of individual Providence. This Providence is the connection of the overflowing intellect <note>term: "shefa," the divine flow of wisdom or influence</note> to the human soul, according to how much the soul has prepared itself to receive this flow. If there is a lack of perfection in deeds and knowledge, that connection is severed.

**Light of the eyes:** He explains that the Torah and wisdom are like light to the eyes, or like a scent that strengthens the brain. That which is in the soul strengthens the body. This is why it says *it rejoices the heart*, because the intellect is what recognizes the "scent" <note>metaphor for wisdom</note> and it becomes joy in the heart. It then reaches the rest of the body through the natural heat preserved in the blood of the heart, which carries it to all parts of the body.

**A good report:** Hearing the words of the Torah and wisdom, or good deeds that are spoken about a person.

**An ear that hears:** This means someone who is quick to listen and receive the words of the wise and moral discipline, which are the path to life. He will have the intellect to accept the words of the wise.

**He who refuses instruction:** One who leaves or casts away discipline despises his soul, for he does not perceive its flaws nor the loss of its noble side, which is the intellectual portion.

**Fear of the Lord:** The fear of wisdom is required by his preparation in his heart; it will remove from him all pride and self-importance.

**To man belong the preparations of the heart:** It is for the person to prepare his heart so that the words of the intellect come before the words of the tongue. One who is prepared in intellect will speak with wisdom.

**All the ways of a man:** A person will think to himself that all his ways are pure because he does not perceive his own flaws. Therefore, he needs to weigh his spirits against the path of the Torah.

**Commit to the Lord:** This means that whatever revolves around you regarding worldly matters—whether they are good or bad—you should roll <note>The Hebrew "gol" literally means "roll," as in rolling a burden onto someone else</note> them all onto His Blessed will.

**The Lord made all:** For the Blessed Creator created everything for the purpose of perfection.

**Abomination to the Lord:** Behold, every "high heart" <note>proud person</note> is far from the Blessed Creator.

**By grace and truth:** He explains that through acts of kindness and engagement with words of truth, sin is atoned.

**When ways please the Lord:** Behold, when the Blessed Creator is pleased with a man’s deeds because of his goodness and uprightness, He will not allow him to fall into evil.

**Better is a little:** It is better for a man that his sustenance be modest [with righteousness than plenty without it].

**A man's heart:** This means a person thinks of his path according to his own perception—judging evil as evil, or sometimes evil as good.

**A divine sentence on the lips of the king:** He explains that when a king rules with his wisdom and intellect, everything he speaks is weighed with proof.

**A balance and scales:** He informs us here that even these [measures of commerce] are from the Blessed God.

**An abomination to kings:** He informs us here that for great and important kings, [wickedness] is even more distant than it is for the lowly.
